senses.definition: The fruit of the tree Malus domestica, chiefly with a green, red, or yellow skin, cultivated in temperate climates for cidermaking, cooking, and eating.
A fruit of any kind.

Often with a qualifying word: any fruit or vegetable, or any other thing (such as a cone or gall) produced by a plant, especially if from a tree and similar to the fruit of Malus domestica (noun sense 1.1).
Something which resembles the fruit of Malus domestica (noun sense 1.1) in shape (such as a ball, breast, or globe) or colour.
The round, fleshy part of a cheek between the eye and the corner of the mouth when a person is smiling.
The surface of revolution of a circular arc of an angle greater than 180° rotated about the straight line passing through the arc's two endpoints.
In full apple bowl: a round bowl of a tobacco pipe; also, a tobacco pipe with such a bowl.
According to postbiblical Christian tradition, the fruit of the tree of knowledge which was eaten by Adam and Eve despite God commanding them not to do so; the forbidden fruit.
An imaginary diminutive unit of height.
A tree of the genus Malus; especially Malus domestica which is cultivated for its edible fruit; the apple tree.
Synonym of applewood (“the wood of the apple tree”).
A person.
Synonym of CBer (“a CB radio enthusiast”).
An assist.
A Native American or redskinned person who acts or thinks like a white (Caucasian) person.
In full old apple: a baseball.
Synonym of pome (“a type of fruit in which the often edible flesh arises from the swollen base of the flower and not from the carpels”).

senses.definition: A product of fertilization in a plant, specifically
The seed-bearing part of a plant; often edible, colourful, fragrant, and sweet or sour; produced from a floral ovary after fertilization.
An end result, effect, or consequence; advantageous or disadvantageous result.
The spores of cryptogams and their accessory organs.
Any sweet or sour, edible part of a plant that resembles seed-bearing fruit (see former sense) even if it does not develop from a floral ovary.
A sweet or sweetish vegetable, such as the petioles of rhubarb, that resembles a true fruit or is used in cookery as if it was a fruit.
Of, belonging to, related to, or having fruit or its characteristics; (of living things) producing or consuming fruit.
An effeminate man.
A crazy person.
A homosexual man, especially an effeminate one.
Offspring from a sexual union.

senses.definition: The act of preserving, guarding, or protecting; the keeping (of a thing) in a safe or entire state; preservation.

The discipline concerned with protection of biodiversity, the environment, and natural resources

The protection and care of cultural heritage, including artwork and architecture, as well as historical and archaeological artifacts
lack of change in a measurable property of an isolated physical system (conservation of energy, mass, momentum, electric charge, subatomic particles, and fundamental symmetries)

Something which is improved
Increase; growth; progress; advance.

senses.definition: A fundamental assumption, fundamental law or guiding belief.
A rule used to choose among solutions to a problem.
Moral rule or aspect.
A rule or law of nature, or the basic idea on how the laws of nature are applied.
A fundamental essence, particularly one producing a given quality.

A chemical compound within plant or animal tissue that is characteristic of it and more or less peculiar to it, such that it defines the character of that tissue from a human viewpoint (as for example nicotine in tobacco).
A source, or origin; that from which anything proceeds; fundamental substance or energy; primordial substance; ultimate element, or cause.
An original faculty or endowment.
A beginning.

Bringing or being an instance of favourable fortune; apt, felicitous, fortunate, propitious.
Favoring or inclined to use.
Elect or saved after death, blessed.
Dexterous, ready, skilful.

etymology.text: From Middle English happy (“fortunate, happy”), perhaps an alteration of Middle English happyn, happen (“fortunate, happy”), possibly related to or from Old Norse heppinn (“fortunate, happy”); and potentially assimilated to be equivalent to hap (“chance, luck, fortune”) + -y. Compare also Icelandic heppinn (“lucky”), Faroese heppin (“fortunate, lucky, happy”), Norwegian Nynorsk heppen (“lucky”), Scots happin (“fortunate, blessed”). See further at hap.
etymology.native: 「happy」源自中古英語 hapyn 或 happen，意為「幸運、幸福」，可能與古諾斯語 heppinn（意為「幸運」）有關；也可能與 hap（意為「機會、運氣」）+ -y 結合而成。可參照冰島語 heppinn（意為「幸運」）、法羅語 heppin（意為「幸運、幸福」）、挪威語 Nynorsk heppen（意為「幸運」）及蘇格蘭語 happin（意為「幸運、祝福」）。詳見 hap。

etymology.text: From Middle English doun, doune (“down”), from Old English dūne (“down”), aphetic form of adūne (“down, downward”), from earlier ofdūne (“down”, literally “off the hill”), from of (“of, off of”) + dūn (“hill, mount, dune, down”). More at Etymology 2 below. For the development from directional phrases to prepositions, compare Old Frisian dene (“down”, adverb, literally “(to the) floor”), Middle Low German dāle (“down, downwards”, literally “(in/to the) dale/valley”), whence German Low German dal
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（doun），來自古英語（dūne），是（adūne）「向下」的字首省略形式，更早是（ofdūne），字面意思是「從山上下來」，由「從」（of）加「山丘」（dūn）組成。

etymology.text: From Middle English bred, breed, from Old English brēad (“fragment, bit, morsel, crumb", also "bread”), from Proto-West Germanic *braud, from Proto-Germanic *braudą (“bread”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerw-, *bʰrewh₁- (“to boil; to brew”), from *bʰer- (“to bear, carry”). Alternatively, from Proto-Germanic *braudaz, *brauþaz (“broken piece, fragment”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰera- (“to split, beat, hew, struggle”) (see brittle). Perhaps a conflation of the two. Possibly a doublet of broa.
etymology.native: 「bread」源自中世英文的 bred、breed，來自古英文 brēad（意為「碎片、小塊、碎屑」，亦指「麵包」），再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *braud，來自原始日耳曼語 *braudą（意為「麵包」），再往上溯源自原始印歐語 *bʰerw-、*bʰrewh₁-（意為「煮沸、發酵」），而 *bʰer-（意為「承載、攜帶」）。另一說法源自原始日耳曼語 *braudaz、*brauþaz（意為「破碎的片段」），來自原始印歐語 *bʰera-（意為「劈開、敲打、切割」）（見 brittle）。可能為兩者融合而成，也可能為 broa 的同源詞。

She connected the dots.
She bought two pairs of polka dot stockings.
examples.translation: 她買了兩雙波點絲襪。

examples.text: Cities are designated on this map as red dots.
The general meeting began at 9 am on the dot.
examples.translation: 總會在九點整開始了。

relations.native: 橫跨（兩側之間的空隙或空間）
窗戶或門等上的玻璃或其他透明材料單片

etymology.text: From Middle English *dot, dotte, from Old English dott (“a dot, point”), from Proto-West Germanic *dott, from Proto-Germanic *duttaz (“wisp”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Dot, Dotte (“a clump”), Dutch dot (“lump, knot, clod”), Low German Dutte (“a plug”), dialectal Swedish dott (“a little heap, bunch, clump”).

senses.definition: The act of passing over, across, or through something.
The conveyance of people or goods from one place to another, especially on a public transportation system; the vehicles used for such conveyance.
Any form of transport that can be used by a member of public (who usually pays a fare), as opposed to private ownership of e.g. cars; short form of public transit or mass transit
The passage of a celestial body or other object across the observer's meridian, or across the disk of a larger celestial body.
The passage of a celestial body in the horoscope, e.g. through a section or in relation to a specific important point in someone's birth chart.
A surveying instrument rather like a theodolite that measures horizontal and vertical angles.
An imaginary line between two objects whose positions are known. When the navigator sees one object directly in front of the other, the navigator knows that his position is on the transit.
A Ford Transit van, see Transit.
A Ford Transit van.

examples.text: I am here in transit.
I'm in transit.
Public transit is very good in this city.
I listen to the radio while in transit.
Conditions apply for Los Angeles transit passengers.
The rapid transit system is modern and efficient.

etymology.text: From French, from Latin transire (“to go across, pass in, pass through”), from trans (“over”) + ire (“to go”).

senses.definition: An act of transporting; conveyance.
The state of being transported by emotion; rapture.
A vehicle used to transport (passengers, mail, freight, troops etc.)
senses.native: 運輸工具，運送乘客、郵件、貨物或部隊的載具

senses.definition: A tractor-trailer.
The system of transporting passengers, etc. in a particular region; the vehicles used in such a system.
senses.native: 運輸系統，某地區運送乘客的系統與工具

senses.definition: A device that moves recording tape across the read/write heads of a tape recorder or video recorder etc.
senses.native: （錄音、錄影）走帶機構，使磁帶通過讀寫頭的裝置

senses.definition: A deported convict.

examples.text: He's specialized in the transport of cattle.

senses.definition: The act of conveying or removing something from one place, person or thing to another.
An instance of conveying or removing from one place, person or thing to another; a transferal.
An act of exiting one mass transit vehicle and boarding another (typically one belonging to a different line or mode of transportation) to continue a journey.
A paper receipt given to a rider of one bus (and historically also certain elevated or subway lines), allowing free entry onto another bus to continue a journey.
A design conveyed by contact from one surface to another; a heat transfer.
A soldier removed from one troop, or body of troops, and placed in another.
A pathological process by which a unilateral morbid condition on being abolished on one side of the body makes its appearance in the corresponding region upon the other side.
The conveying of genetic material from one cell to another.
A conventional bid which requests partner to bid the next available suit.
A person who transfers or is transferred from one club or team to another.
Of a person with limited mobility: an instance of independent or assisted movement from one stable surface to another.

examples.text: Could you please transfer me to Mr. Smith?
Is it convenient to transfer between the subway and the light rail here?
examples.translation: 在這裡換乘捷運與輕軌方便嗎？

examples.text: Hearing that a transfer student was coming, the class buzzed with excitement.
examples.translation: 聽說要來一個轉校生之後，全班都亂哄哄地活躍起來。

examples.text: We will make the payment by bank transfer.
examples.translation: 我們會用銀行轉帳付款。

examples.text: If you connect your phone to your PC via USB, you can even transfer files and photos.
examples.translation: 您如果透過 USB 將手機連接到電腦，則甚至可以傳輸檔案和照片。

examples.text: "That's an unusual hobby she's got, the transfer student." "She's cute so it's fine with me."
examples.translation: 「她的愛好不尋常啊，這個轉學生。」「她長得可愛，所以對我來說還行。」

etymology.text: From Latin trānsferō (“to bear across”). Distant doublet of translate. See also collate and confer, delate and defer, as well as prelate and prefer among others.

senses.definition: The physical means or contrivances to make something (especially a public service) possible; the required equipment, infrastructure, location etc.
A building or campus specially designed for a specific purpose, such as incarceration, military use, or scientific experimentation.
The fact of being easy, or easily done; absence of difficulty; simplicity.
Dexterity of speech or action; skill, talent.
A toilet.
A condition of mental weakness less than idiocy, but enough to make a person easily persuaded to do something against their better interest.
Affability.

examples.text: Her facility with English is wonderful.
Tom works in a correctional facility.
The unloading facility is in Algiers.
Any member can make use of these facilities.
The common facilities are centrally located.
Are the necessary basic facilities available?

relations.native: 毫不費力、流暢（指工作、能力等）

morphemes.native: 毫不費力、流暢（指工作、能力等）

etymology.text: From Middle English facilite, from Middle French facilité, and its source, Latin facilitās. By surface analysis, facile + -ity. Doublet of faculty.

senses.definition: Physical motion between points in space.
A trend in various fields or social categories, a group of people with a common ideology who try together to achieve certain general goals.
A large division of a larger composition.
A system or mechanism for transmitting motion of a definite character, or for transforming motion, such as the wheelwork of a watch.
The impression of motion in an artwork, painting, novel etc.
Melodic progression, accentual character, tempo or pace.
An instance of an aircraft taking off or landing.
The deviation of a pitch from ballistic flight.
A pattern in which pairs change opponents and boards move from table to table in duplicate bridge.
Motion of the mind or feelings; emotion.

examples.text: The BDS movement is so important.
examples.translation: （BDS）運動非常重要。

examples.text: Has the movement for decolonization started?
examples.translation: 去殖民化運動開始了嗎？

examples.text: Jugurtha carefully studied the Romans' movements.
examples.translation: 朱古達仔細研究羅馬人的動向。

examples.text: I can't control my body's movements anymore.
examples.translation: 我沒辦法控制自己身體的動作了。

examples.text: Each movement of the dancer was perfect.
examples.translation: 這舞者的每一個動作都是完美的。

examples.text: Your son took part in the student movement, I hear.
examples.translation: 聽說你兒子參與了學生運動。

etymology.text: From Middle English mevement, from Old French movement (modern French mouvement), from movoir + -ment; cf. also Medieval Latin movimentum, from Latin movere (“move”). Doublet of moment and momentum. In this sense, displaced native Old English styring, which led to Modern English stirring.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（mevement），來自古法語（movement，現代法語 mouvement），由（movoir）加（-ment）組成；也比較中世紀拉丁語（movimentum），來自拉丁語（movere）「移動」。與（moment）、（momentum）為雙式詞。在此義上取代了古英語原有的（styring），即現代英語（stirring）。

senses.definition: The amount of money levied for a service.
A forceful forward movement.
An official description (by the police or a court) of a crime that somebody may be guilty of.
An electric charge.
The scope of someone's responsibility.
Someone or something entrusted to one's care, such as a child to a babysitter or a student to a teacher.
A load or burden; cargo.
An instruction.
An offensive foul in which the player with the ball moves into a stationary defender.
A measured amount of powder and/or shot in a cartridge.
A measured amount of explosive.
An image displayed on an escutcheon.
A position (of a weapon) fitted for attack.
A sort of plaster or ointment.
An address given at a church service concluding a visitation.
An attack in which combatants rush towards an enemy in an attempt to engage in close combat.
An accusation by a person or organization.
A mortgage.
Cannabis.
Weight; import; value.

examples.text: Who's in charge of this section?
examples.translation: 誰負責這個部門？

examples.text: This pamphlet is free of charge.
examples.translation: 這本小冊子是免費的。

examples.text: The charge for a front row seat is 5 dollars.
examples.translation: 第一排的座位5美元。

examples.text: "Who's in charge here?" "I am." "You wish!"
examples.translation: 「這裡誰是老大？」「我是。」「想得美！」

examples.text: I just talked to the person in charge.
examples.translation: 我剛跟主管人談過。

examples.text: Who's in charge of the sales section?
examples.translation: 誰負責銷售部門？

etymology.text: From Middle English chargen, from Old French chargier, from Late Latin carricō (“to load”), from Latin carrus (“a car, wagon”); see car. Doublet of cargo.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（chargen），來自古法語（chargier），再源自晚期拉丁語（carricō）「裝載」，來自拉丁語（carrus）「車、貨車」；參見（car）。與（cargo）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: The act of connecting.
Coherence; lack of disjointedness.
The point at which two or more things are connected.
A transfer from one transportation vehicle to another in scheduled transportation service.
A physical link between two things or places.
An established communications or transportation link.
A causal relationship between two phenomena; cause and effect.
A relationship between people or groups of people.
A feeling of mutual understanding and ease of communication between two or more people.
A contextual relationship; the commonality between two or more things.
A person or persons related to oneself, through either family or business.
An acquaintance who is useful in a particular scenario, especially in a corrupt or criminal way.

A set of sets that contains the empty set, all one-element sets for any element that is included in any of the sets, and the union of any group of sets that are elements where the intersections of those sets is non-empty.
Sexual intercourse.
A drug dealer.

examples.text: There is no connection between them.
examples.translation: 兩者沒有關聯。

examples.text: My internet connection was cut off.
examples.translation: 我的網路連線被切斷了。

examples.text: We have a special connection.
examples.translation: 我們有特殊聯繫。

examples.text: Why is my Internet connection so slow?
examples.translation: 我的網怎麼會這麼慢？

examples.text: Tell me all you know in connection with this.
There's no connection between the two things.

etymology.text: From Middle English conneccioun, connexioun, conneccyon, conneccion, from Latin connexionem (nominative connexio (“a conclusion, binding together”)), from connectō, an alternative spelling of cōnectō (“to bind together”), from compound of co- (“together”) and nectō (“to bind”).

senses.definition: The quality or state of being independent; lack of dependence; the state of not being reliant on, or controlled by, others.
The state of having sufficient means for a comfortable livelihood.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: India gained independence from Britain in 1947.
examples.translation: 印度於1947年脫離英國獲得獨立。

examples.text: Gandhi is India's iconic independence leader.
examples.translation: 甘地是印度標誌性的獨立領袖。

examples.text: Algeria was granted independence from France.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞從法國獨立。

examples.text: Chechens have inclinations towards independence.
examples.translation: 車臣人傾向獨立。

examples.text: The US declared independence from Great Britain in 1776.
examples.translation: 美利堅合眾國於1776年宣布其獨立於大不列顛王國。

examples.text: Lachin hosted concert marking May 28 – Independence Day.
examples.translation: 拉欽舉辦了一場音樂會，慶祝 5 月 28 日的獨立紀念日。

etymology.text: From French indépendance. Analyzable as in- + de- + pend + -ence or in- + dependence.

senses.definition: A large settlement, bigger than a town; sometimes with a specific legal definition, depending on the place.
The central business district; downtown.
A large amount of something (used after the noun).
A settlement granted special status by royal charter or letters patent; traditionally, a settlement with a cathedral regardless of size.
senses.native: 經皇家特許狀授予特殊地位的城鎮；傳統上指有大教堂的城鎮

examples.text: Because there's pollution in the cities.
examples.translation: 因為有城市公害。

examples.text: So, will this mean healthier cities?
examples.translation: 那麼，這代表更健康的城市嗎？

examples.text: Kyoto and Boston are sister cities.
examples.translation: 京都和波士頓是姐妹城市。

examples.text: Sydney is Australia's largest city.
examples.translation: 雪梨是澳洲最大的城市。

examples.text: Vladivostok is a city in Russia.
examples.translation: 海參崴是俄羅斯的一個城市。

examples.text: Florence is the most beautiful city in Italy.
examples.translation: 佛羅倫薩是義大利最美麗的城市。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English cite, derived from Old French cite, derived from Late Latin cīvitātem (“city”), in Classical Latin "citizenry", derived from cīvis (“fellow-citizen”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱey- (“lie down; settle”). Cognate with Old English hīwan pl (“members of one's household, servants”). See hewe. Doublet of civitas. Mostly displaced native Old English burg, whence Modern English borough.
etymology.native: 承襲自中古英語（cite），來自古法語（cite），再源自晚期拉丁語（cīvitātem）「城市」，古典拉丁語意為「全體公民」，衍生自（cīvis）「同胞公民」，最終來自原始印歐語（*ḱey-）「躺下；定居」。與（civitas）為雙式詞。大多取代了古英語原有的（burg），即現代英語的（borough）。

senses.definition: The state of being free.
The lack of a specific constraint, or of constraints in general; a state of being free, unconstrained.
The right or privilege of unrestricted use or access
Frankness; openness; unreservedness.
Improper familiarity; violation of the rules of decorum.

examples.text: Freedom is very, very important.
examples.translation: 自由非常非常重要。

examples.text: One must pay for freedom.
examples.translation: 自由有價。

examples.text: All I want is my freedom.
examples.translation: 我只要自由。

examples.text: Freedom is not free.
examples.translation: 自由是有代價的。

examples.text: I like freedom.
examples.translation: 我喜歡自由。

examples.text: All kinds of rules made him lose his freedom.
examples.translation: 各種規定讓他失去了自由。

etymology.text: From Middle English fredom, freedom, from Old English frēodōm (“freedom, state of free-will, charter, emancipation, deliverance”), from Proto-West Germanic *frijadōm (“freedom”). Equivalent to free + -dom. Cognate with North Frisian fridoem (“freedom”), Dutch vrijdom (“freedom”), Low German frīdom (“freedom”), Middle High German vrītuom (“freedom”), Norwegian fridom (“freedom”).

senses.definition: The condition or state of having won a battle or competition, or having succeeded in an effort; (countable) an instance of this.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: They congratulated us on our victory.
examples.translation: 他們祝賀我們的勝利。

examples.text: This is your victory.
examples.translation: 這是你們的勝利。

examples.text: It's an easy victory.
examples.translation: 這是一個輕鬆取得的勝利。

examples.text: The victory was won at the cost of many lives.
examples.translation: 勝利是用許多人的性命換來的。

examples.text: The biggest victory is to win over yourself.
examples.translation: 最大的勝利是戰勝自己。

examples.text: In 1958, Brazil won its first World Cup victory.
examples.translation: 在一九五八年，巴西首次奪得了世界盃的冠軍。

etymology.text: The noun is derived from Middle English victory, victori, victorie (“supremacy, victory; a defeat or vanquishing, conquest; superior military force; might, power, strength; triumphal celebration or procession; monument commemorating a defeat; superior position, dominance; mastery; moral victory, vindication; success, triumph; redemption, salvation; resurrection of Jesus; means of achieving spiritual victory; reward for or token of perseverance in a spiritual struggle”) [and other forms], borrowe

senses.definition: The right or condition of self-government; freedom to act or function independently.
A self-governing country or region.
The capacity to make an informed, uncoerced decision.
The capacity of a system to make a decision about its actions without the involvement of another system or operator.
The status of a church whose highest-ranking bishop is appointed by the patriarch of the mother church, but which is self-governing in all other respects. Compare autocephaly.

examples.text: Give your best employees more autonomy.
People would have more autonomy if they had a job.
Autonomy was granted in 1969 and independence in 1979.
Bodily autonomy is a human right.
Mali granted more autonomy to its Tuareg region.
Encouraging autonomy helps people grow and learn.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Ancient Greek αὐτονομῐ́ᾱ (autonomĭ́ā, “freedom to use its own laws, independence”), from αὐτόνομος (autónomos, “living under one's own laws, independent”) + -ῐ́ᾱ (-ĭ́ā, “-y, -ia”, nominal suffix). By surface analysis, auto- (“self”) + -nomy (“a system of rules or laws about a particular field”).

senses.definition: Between or among nations.
Participated in by two or more nations.
Common to, or affecting, two or more nations.
Serving two or more nations.
Of or concerning the association called the International.
Independent of national boundaries; common to all people.
Foreign; of another nation.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: English has become an international language.
examples.translation: 英語成為了一門國際語言。

examples.text: English is an international language.
examples.translation: 英語是國際語言。

examples.text: Happy International Women's Day!
examples.translation: 國際婦女節快樂！

examples.text: March 21 is the International Day of Forests.
examples.translation: 3月21日是國際森林日。

examples.text: Putin will be a pariah on the international stage.
examples.translation: 普丁將成為國際舞台上的棄兒。

examples.text: The drug problem is international.
examples.translation: 毒品是國際性的問題。

etymology.text: From inter- + national. Introduced in modern English by Jeremy Bentham in his An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation, 1780.

senses.definition: Someone who has represented their country in a particular sport.
A game or contest between two or more nations.
A transnational organization of political parties of similar ideology.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: He played as an international for Japan.
examples.translation: 他曾代表日本參加國際賽。

etymology.text: From inter- + national. Introduced in modern English by Jeremy Bentham in his An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation, 1780.

senses.definition: Pertaining to a nation or country, especially as a whole; affecting, shared by, or existing throughout all of a nation; the state.
Belonging to or characteristic of a specific nation or country, as opposed to others.
Nationalistic; patriotic.

examples.text: Estonia has its own national anthem.
examples.translation: 愛沙尼亞有它自己的國歌。

examples.text: Taiwan has nine national parks.
examples.translation: 台灣有九個國家公園。

examples.text: The German national team dismantled Portugal.
examples.translation: 德國國家隊把葡萄牙打得落花流水。

examples.text: The panda is China's national treasure.
examples.translation: 熊貓是中國的國寶。

examples.text: Promoting Mandarin Chinese is China's national plan.
examples.translation: 推行普通話，是中國的國策。

examples.text: A flag is a national symbol.
examples.translation: 旗幟是國家象徵。

etymology.text: From Middle French national, corresponding to nation + -al.
etymology.native: 源自中古法語（national），相當於（nation）加（-al）。

senses.definition: An accessible structure extending from a building, especially outside a window.
An accessible structure overlooking a stage or the like.

examples.text: I ate breakfast on my balcony.
examples.translation: 我在陽臺上吃的早飯。

examples.text: I'm on the balcony.
examples.translation: 我在陽臺上。

examples.text: People were cheering from their balconies.
examples.translation: 人們從陽台歡呼

examples.text: The family eats breakfast on the balcony.
examples.translation: 一家人在陽臺上吃早飯。

examples.text: What are you doing on the balcony?
examples.translation: 你在陽臺上做什麼？

examples.text: Why don't you go out on the balcony and get some sun?
examples.translation: 去陽台上曬曬太陽怎麼樣？

etymology.text: From Italian balcone (“balcony, floor-length window”), from Old Italian balcone (“scaffold”) from Lombardic *balk, *balko (“beam”), from Proto-Germanic *balkô (“beam”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰelǵ- (“beam, pile, prop”). Akin to Old High German balco, balcho (“beam”), Old English balca (“beam, ridge”). More at balk.

senses.definition: A cohesive whole built up of distinct parts.
The underlying shape of a solid.
The overall form or organization of something.
senses.native: 某物的整體形態或組織

senses.definition: A set of rules defining behaviour.
Several pieces of data treated as a unit.
Underwater terrain or objects (such as a dead tree or a submerged car) that tend to attract fish
senses.native: 吸引魚類的海底地形或物體（如沉沒的樹木或汽車）

senses.definition: A body, such as a political party, with a cohesive purpose or outlook.
senses.native: 具有統一目的或觀點的團體，例如政黨

senses.definition: A set along with a collection of finitary functions and relations.
senses.native: 包含有限函數與關係的一套集合

examples.text: I don't get Japanese grammatical structure.
Most proteins are oligomeric in structure.
Morphology studies the structure of words.
The school's tallest structure is that water tower.
examples.translation: 學校最高的建築就是那個水塔。

examples.text: The brain has a complex structure.
examples.translation: 頭腦的結構很複雜。

examples.text: This is the most massive structure I've ever seen.
examples.translation: 這是我所見過的最大型的構造了。

etymology.text: From Middle French structure, from Latin structūra (“a fitting together, adjustment, building, erection, a building, edifice, structure”), from struere, past participle structus (“pile up, arrange, assemble, build”). Compare construct, instruct, destroy, etc.

senses.definition: An institution, building, or room for the exhibition and conservation of important objects, especially works of art.
An establishment that buys, sells, and displays works of art.
The uppermost seating area projecting from the rear or side walls of a theater, concert hall, or auditorium.
The spectators at an event, collectively.
The part of a courtroom, often elevated and in the rear, where seating for the public audience is facilitated during trial.
A roofed promenade, especially one extending along the wall of a building and supported by arches or columns on the outer side.
A browsable collection of images, font styles, etc.
A covered passage cut through the earth or masonry.
A level or drive in a mine.
A channel that carries engine oil to parts of the engine that need lubrication, such as the main bearings.
The production control room.
A part of a light fixture, forming part of its structure and often providing the mounting for the diffuser.
A part of a monocle—a projection off the ring holding the lens—which helps secure the monocle in the eye socket.
The boring trails produced by an insect in wood.

examples.text: On Saturdays, Gustavo visits art galleries.
Do you enjoy visiting art galleries?
We walked through a long gallery.
He managed all the art galleries in the city.
Better drop by his gallery if you have time.
I'm going to have two pieces in her gallery.

etymology.text: From Middle English galery, gallerye, from Middle French galerie, gallerie, from Old French galerie, gallerie (“a long portico, a gallery”), from Medieval Latin galeria (“gallery”), of unknown origin. Perhaps an alteration of Latin galilea (“church porch”), probably from Latin Galilaea, Galilee, region of Israel. More at Galilee.

senses.definition: All the electromagnetic radiation given off by the Sun; especially, that in the visible spectrum and that bathes the Earth.
Brightness, hope; a positive outlook.
Synonym of sunrise.
Synonym of photic (“describing that part of the near-surface ocean in which photosynthesis is possible.”).

examples.text: The hills are bathed in sunlight.
examples.translation: 丘陵沐浴在陽光下。

examples.text: Come and enjoy the sunlight.
examples.translation: 來這享受陽光吧。

examples.text: Sunlight streamed in through the windows.
examples.translation: 陽光從窗戶透進來。

examples.text: Sunlight sparkled on the lake.
examples.translation: 陽光在湖面上閃爍。

examples.text: In the sky, there appeared a ray of sunlight.
examples.translation: 天空中出現了一道陽光。

examples.text: The moon shines because it reflects sunlight.
examples.translation: 月亮發光是因為它反射太陽光。

etymology.text: From Middle English sonnelight, sunneliht, from Old English sunnan lēoht (“sunlight”), equivalent to sun + light. Cognate with Dutch zonlicht (“sunlight”), German Low German Sünnenlücht (“sunlight”), German Sonnenlicht (“sunlight”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 sonnelight、sunneliht，來自古英文 sunnan lēoht（「陽光」），等同於 sun + light。與荷蘭語 zonlicht（「陽光」）、德語低地德文 Sünnenlücht（「陽光」）、德語 Sonnenlicht（「陽光」）同源。

senses.definition: The direct rays, light or warmth of the sun.
A location on which the sun's rays fall.
Geniality or cheerfulness.
A source of cheerfulness or joy.
The effect which the sun has when it lights and warms some place.
A friendly form of address often reserved for juniors.
An ironic form of address directed toward someone perceived as inferior or troublesome.
Used to address someone who has just woken up or is very sleepy.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

senses.definition: A star, especially when seen as the centre of any single solar system.

senses.definition: Sunrise or sunset.
A revolution of the Earth around the Sun; a year.

senses.definition: The thirty-first Lenormand card.

senses.definition: A traditional Japanese unit of length, approximately 30.3 millimetres (1.193 inches).

etymology.text: From Middle English soen, son, sone, sonne, sun, sune, sunna, sunne, sunnæ, synne, zonne, zunne, from Old English sunna, sunne, sunnu (“sun”), from Proto-West Germanic *sunnā, from Proto-Germanic *sunnǭ (“sun”), from heteroclitic inanimate Proto-Indo-European *sh₂wen-, oblique of Proto-Indo-European *sóh₂wl̥ (“sun”).

senses.definition: The feeling of trust, confidence, belief or expectation that something wished for can or will happen.
The actual thing wished for.
A person or thing that is a source of hope.
The virtuous desire for future good.

A sloping plain between mountain ridges.
A small bay; an inlet; a haven.

senses.definition: The morning twilight period immediately before sunrise.
The rising of the sun.
The time when the sun rises.
The earliest phase of something.

A firework made by filling a case with a substance which burns brilliantly with a white or coloured flame.
A window in architecture, carriage design, or motor car design: either the opening itself or the window pane of glass that fills it, if any.
The series of squares reserved for the answer to a crossword clue.
Open view; a visible state or condition; public observation; publicity.
The power of perception by vision: eyesight (sightedness; vision).
The brightness of the eye or eyes.
Electromagnetic radiation in the wavelength range visible to the human eye or in nearby ranges (infrared or ultraviolet radiation).
Electromagnetic radiation of any wavelength.
A lightbulb or similar light-emitting device, regardless of whether it is lit.
A traffic light, or (by extension) an intersection controlled by traffic lights.
Spiritual or mental illumination; enlightenment, useful information.
Facts; pieces of information; ideas, concepts.

etymology.text: From Middle English cutten, of North Germanic origin, from Old Norse *kytja, *kutta, from Proto-Germanic *kutjaną, *kuttaną (“to cut”), of uncertain origin, perhaps related to Proto-Germanic *kwetwą (“meat, flesh”) (compare Old Norse kvett (“meat”)). etymology.text: Adjective and noun from Middle English drye, dryge, drüȝe, from Old English drȳġe (“dry; parched, withered”), from Proto-West Germanic *drūgī, *draugī, from Proto-Germanic *drūgiz, *draugiz (“dry, hard”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰerǵʰ- (“to strengthen; become hard”), from *dʰer- (“to hold, support”). The verb derives from Middle English drien, from Old English drȳġan (“to dry”), from Proto-West Germanic *drūgijan, from Proto-Germanic *drūgiz (“hard, desiccated, dry”), from Proto-Indo-European
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 drye, dryge, drüȝe，來自古英語 drȳġe（「乾的；烤焦的」），源於原始西日耳曼語 *drūgī, *draugī，源於原始日耳曼語 *drūgiz, *draugiz（「乾的、堅硬的」），源於原始印歐語 *dʰerǵʰ-（「加強；變硬」），來自 *dʰer-（「持有、支撐」）。動詞源自中古英語 drien，來自古英語 drȳġan（「乾燥」），源於原始西日耳曼語 *drūgijan，源於原始日耳曼語 *drūgiz（「堅硬、脫水的、乾的」），源於原始印歐語...

etymology.text: From Middle English changen, chaungen, from Old French changier, from Late Latin cambiāre, from Latin cambīre (“to exchange, barter”), derived from the noun cambium (“change”) (whence was loaned the English doublet cambium), from Gaulish cambion, earlier *kambyom (“change”), related to Proto-Celtic *kambos (“twisted, crooked”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ḱh₂(e)mbos, *(s)kh₂(e)mbos (“crooked”). More at skimp, scam; see also Proto-Indo-European *kh₂em-.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（changen），來自古法語（changier），來自後期拉丁語（cambiāre），來自拉丁語（cambīre）「交換、以物易物」，再來自高盧語（cambion）「交換」，可能與原始凱爾特語（*kambos）「彎曲的」有關。

etymology.native: 「park」源自中世紀英語，來源為古法語「parc」，再源自中世紀拉丁語「parcus」或「parricus」，而這些詞又來自古弗蘭克語「*parrik」（意為圍欄或籠子）。與荷蘭語「perk」（意為圍欄或花壇）、古高地德語「pfarrih」或「pferrih」（意為圍欄或籠子）、古英語「pearroc」（意為圍欄，後演變為現代英語「paddock」）、古諾斯語「parrak」或「parak」（意為圍欄或籠子，亦可指困擾或焦慮）、冰島語「parraka」（意為拘束或壓制）同源。另見「parrock」與「paddock」。

senses.definition: To wound or cause physical harm to a living creature.
To damage or impair.
To do injustice to.

senses.definition: Any physical device meant to ease or do a task.
Any piece of equipment used in a profession, such as a craftsman's.
A piece of software used to develop software or hardware, or to perform low-level operations.
Anything that aids someone to perform an operation; an instrument; a means.
A person or group which is used or controlled, usually unwittingly, by another person or group, a pawn.
A particular skill pertaining to baseball (such as hitting, running, etc.).
A handgun.
A penis, notably with a sexual or erotic connotation.
An obnoxious or uptight person.

etymology.text: From Middle English tool, tol, from Old English tōl (“tool, implement, instrument”, literally “that with which one prepares something”), perhaps borrowed from Old Norse tól, but at any rate ultimately from Proto-Germanic *tōlą (“that which is used in preparation, tool”), from Proto-Indo-European *dewh₂- (“to tie to, secure”), equivalent to taw (“to prepare”) + -le (agent suffix). Cognate with Scots tuil (“tool, implement, instrument, device”), Icelandic tól (“tool”), Faroese tól (“tool, instrume

A weighted disk, usually of metal, with a hole in the center for use with a barbell, dumbbell, or exercise machine.
An engraved surface used to transfer an image to paper.
An image or copy.
An illustration in a book, either black and white, or colour, usually on a page of paper of different quality from the text pages.

A material covered with such a layer.
A person's foot.
Home plate.
Plate armor.
An ornamental or food service item coated with silver or gold or otherwise decorated.
senses.native: 鍍金或鍍銀的裝飾或餐具（鍍銀器、鍍金器）（過時）

examples.text: How many plates do we have?
examples.translation: 我們有多少個盤子？

examples.translation: 沒有任何干淨的盤子。

senses.definition: To cover the surface material of an object with a thin coat of another material, usually a metal.

senses.native: 在上菜前把各道菜餚放到用餐者的盤中

senses.definition: To score a run.
To arm or defend with metal plates.
To beat into thin plates.
To specify which airline a ticket will be issued on behalf of.
senses.native: 指定機票應以哪家航空公司開立

senses.definition: To categorize stamps based on their position on the original sheet, in order to reconstruct an entire sheet.
senses.native: 依郵票在原版張上的位置分類，以重建整張郵票版（版位分類）

senses.definition: To identify the printing plate used, particularly with early British stamps.
senses.native: 辨識郵票所用的印版（尤指早期英國郵票）

examples.text: The chefs prepared the feast, plating dishes meticulously in the busy kitchen.
examples.translation: 廚師們在忙碌的廚房裡精心擺盤，準備盛宴。

etymology.text: From Middle English plate, from Old French plate, from Medieval Latin plata, from Vulgar Latin *plat(t)us, from Ancient Greek πλατύς (platús, “broad, flat, wide”). Compare Spanish plato.
etymology.native: 「plate」源自中世紀英語，來源於古法語 plate，再源自中世紀拉丁語 plata，源自通俗拉丁語 *plat(t)us，最終來自古希臘語 πλατύς（platús），意為「寬廣、平坦」。可與西班牙語 plato 相比。

senses.definition: One’s own dwelling place; the house or structure in which one lives; especially the house in which one lives with one's family; the habitual abode of one’s family.

The place (residence, settlement, country, etc.), where a person was born or raised; a childhood or parental home; the home of one’s parents or guardian.
The abiding place of the affections, especially of the domestic affections.
A house that has been made homelike, to suit the comfort of those who live there.

The grave; the final rest; also, the native and eternal dwelling place of the soul.
Anything that serves the functions of a home, as comfort, safety, sense of belonging, etc.
The locality where a thing is usually found, or was first found, or where it is naturally abundant; habitat; seat.
The ultimate point aimed at in a progress; the goal.
Home plate.

examples.translation: 鴿子能靠地球磁場找到回家的路。

senses.definition: Having little depth; significantly less deep than wide.
Extending not far downward.
Concerned mainly with superficial matters.
Lacking interest or substance; flat; one-dimensional.
Not intellectually deep; not penetrating deeply; simple; not wise or knowing.
Not deep in tone.
Not far forward, close to the net.
Not steep; close to horizontal.

examples.text: Tom is shallow.
examples.translation: 湯姆很膚淺。

examples.text: Lake Neusiedl is shallower than Lake Balaton.

examples.text: The river is shallow here. We can walk across.
examples.translation: 河水在這裡很淺，我們可以走過去。

examples.text: Alberto hopped in the shallow end of the pool.

examples.text: Between you and me, he has a shallow way of thinking.
examples.translation: 他思考的方式缺乏深度，這個我們知道就好。

etymology.text: From Middle English schalowe (“not deep, shallow”); apparently related to Middle English schalde, schold, scheld, schealde (“shallow”), from Old English sċeald (“shallow”), from Proto-Germanic *skal-, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kelh₁- (“to parch, dry out”). Related to Low German Scholl (“shallow water”). See also shoal.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語「不深的、淺的」；顯然與中古英語另一組表示「淺」的字有關，來自古英語「淺的」，上溯至原始日耳曼語與原始印歐語「烤乾、使乾」。與低地德語「淺水」有關。另見「淺灘」。

senses.definition: To bring to, or direct toward, a common center; to unite more closely; to gather into one body, mass, or force.
To increase the strength and diminish the bulk of, as of a liquid or an ore; to intensify, by getting rid of useless material; to condense.
To approach or meet in a common center; to consolidate.
To focus one's thought or attention (on).

examples.text: He concentrated on his studies.

examples.text: She couldn't concentrate on the conversation.

examples.text: I think we should concentrate on other things.

examples.text: It is too noisy around here; I can't concentrate.

etymology.text: (early 17th century) From a Romance language, see French concentrer, Italian concentràre, Spanish concentrar; alternatively from Medieval Latin/New Latin concentrō + -ate (verb-forming suffix). Compare also earlier concentre and German konzentrieren. By surface analysis, con- + center (centr- in compounds) + -ate (verb-forming suffix).

senses.definition: To cause to become an element of something; to insert or fill.

senses.definition: To steep in a liquid, so as to extract the soluble constituents (usually medicinal or herbal).

senses.definition: To pull back (an arrow or bowstring) in preparation for shooting the arrow; also, to cause (a bow) to bend by pulling back the bowstring.

To construct (a canal, wall, etc.) from one point to another.

Of a batter: to hit (a ball) from the off side to the leg side, especially with an inclined bat; also, to hit (a short-length ball directed at the leg stump) with an inclined bat so as to deflect the ball between the legs and the wicket.

etymology.text: The verb is derived from Middle English dragen, draghen, draue, drauen, drauhen, drawe, drawen, draȝe, draȝen, draȝhenn (“to drag, pull; to draw (out); to attract; to entice, lure; to lead; to make a drawing; to move, travel; etc.”), from Old English dragan (“to drag, draw”), from Proto-West Germanic *dragan (“to carry, haul”), from Proto-Germanic *draganą (“to carry, draw, pull”); further etymology uncertain, often said to be from Proto-Indo-European *dʰregʰ- (“to drag, pull, run”), but possibl

etymology.text: From Middle English sclise, sklise, from Old French esclice, esclis (“a piece split off”), deverbal of esclicer, esclicier (“to splinter, split up”), from Frankish *slitjan (“to split up”), from Proto-Germanic *slitjaną, from Proto-Germanic *slītaną (“to split, tear apart”), from Proto-Indo-European *sleyd- (“to rend, injure, crumble”). Akin to Old High German sliz, gisliz (“a tear, rip”), Old High German slīȥan (“to tear”), Old English slītan (“to split up”), modern French éclisse. More at slit

etymology.text: From Middle English slitten, from Old English slītan, from Proto-Germanic *slītaną (“to tear apart”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)leyd- (“to tear, rend (cut apart), split apart”). Possibly cognate with Latin laed- (“to strike, hurt, injure”). Doublet of slite; also related to slice through French borrowing. Apparently unrelated to English slot, whose etymology, however, is uncertain.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 slitten，再追溯至古英語的 slītan，來自日耳曼語族的 *slītaną（撕裂），最終源自印歐語系的 *(s)leyd-（撕裂、割開）。可能與拉丁語的 laed-（打擊、傷害）同源。它是 slite 的同源詞，也與從法語借來的 slice 有關。似乎與英語的 slot 無關，後者的詞源尚不確定。

etymology.text: From Middle English casten, from Old Norse kasta (“to throw, cast, overturn”), from Proto-Germanic *kastōną (“to throw, cast”), of unknown origin.

senses.definition: Pertaining to the world as understood through the senses rather than the mind, having to do with the material world.
In accordance with the laws of nature; now specifically, pertaining to physics.
Denoting a map showing natural features of the landscape (compare political).
Having to do with the body as opposed to the mind; corporeal, bodily.
Sexual, carnal.
Involving bodily force or contact; vigorous, aggressive.
Of a piece of media, existing as a tangible object instead of being digital.
Pertaining to the field of medicine; medical.
That practises medicine; pertaining to doctors, physicianly.
Medicinal; good for the health, curative, therapeutic.

Scientists deal mainly with physical matters.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Late Latin physicālis, from Latin physica (“study of nature”), from Ancient Greek φυσική (phusikḗ), feminine singular of φυσικός (phusikós, “natural; physical”), from φύσις (phúsis, “origin, birth; nature, quality; form, shape; type, kind”), from φῠ́ω (phŭ́ō, “grow”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuH- (“to appear, become, rise up”).

senses.definition: According to norms or rules or to a regular pattern.
In whose representation in a given base b ≥ 2, for every positive integer n, the bⁿ possible strings of n digits follow a uniform distribution.
With cosets which form a group.
Which is the splitting field of a family of polynomials in K.
Which has a very specific bell curve shape; that is or has the qualities of a normal distribution.
Which is pre-compact.
Which is strictly monotonically increasing and continuous with respect to the order topology.
Which commutes with its conjugate transpose.
Which commutes with its adjoint.
Which is the kernel or cokernel of some morphism, respectively.
Which contains only normal morphisms.
In which disjoint closed sets can be separated by disjoint neighborhoods.
Integrally closed: equal its own integral closure in its field of fractions.
Such that all of its localizations at prime ideals are integrally closed domains.
Such that the local ring at every point is an integrally closed domain.
Usual, healthy; not sick or ill or unlike oneself.
Teaching teachers how to teach; teaching teachers the norms of education.
Of, relating to, or being a solution containing one equivalent weight of solute per litre of solution.
Describing a straight chain isomer of an aliphatic hydrocarbon, or an aliphatic compound in which a substituent is in the 1- position of such a hydrocarbon.
Fervently interested in a subject; obsessed.

senses.definition: Self-directed; happening or acting without external cause or instigation; proceeding from natural feeling, temperament, or momentary impulse.

Produced without being planted or without human cultivation or labor.

senses.definition: Of high or especially quick cognitive capacity, bright.
Well thought-out, well considered.
Characterized by thoughtful interaction.
Having at least a similar level of brain power to humankind.
Having an environment-sensing automatically-invoked built-in computer capability.

senses.definition: The early part of the day, especially from midnight to noon.

etymology.text: From Middle English houre, hour, oure, from Old French houre, from Latin hōra (“hour”), from Ancient Greek ὥρα (hṓra, “any time or period, whether of the year, month, or day”), from Proto-Indo-European *yóh₁r̥ (“year, season”). Akin to Old English ġēar (“year”). Doublet of hora and year. Compare horary.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（houre、hour），來自古法語（houre），再源自拉丁語（hōra），來自古希臘語（ὥρα）「時期、時節」，最終來自原始印歐語（*yóh₁r̥）「年、季節」。與古英語（ġēar）「年」同源。與（hora）、（year）為雙式詞。

etymology.native: 源自中古英語（nighte、night、niȝt），來自古英語（niht），再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*nahts），最終來自原始印歐語（*nókʷts）「夜」。

senses.definition: The time of day between afternoon and night.

A party or gathering held in the evening.

senses.definition: Any disturbed state of the atmosphere causing destructive or unpleasant weather, especially one affecting the earth's surface involving strong winds (leading to high waves at sea) and usually lightning, thunder, and precipitation.

Synonym of cyclone (“a weather phenomenon consisting of a system of winds rotating around a centre of low atmospheric pressure”).

A disturbed state of the atmosphere between a severe or strong gale and a hurricane on the modern Beaufort scale, with a wind speed of between 89 and 102 kilometres per hour (55–63 miles per hour; 10 on the scale, known as a "storm" or whole gale), or of between 103 and 117 kilometres per hour (64–72 miles per hour; 11 on the scale, known as a "violent storm").
A heavy expulsion or fall of things (as blows, objects which are thrown, etc.).
A violent agitation of human society; a domestic, civil, or political commotion.
A violent commotion or outbreak of sounds, speech, thoughts, etc.; also, an outpouring of emotion.
Chiefly with a qualifying word: a violent attack of diease, pain, physiological reactions, symptoms, etc.; a paroxysm.
A period of frosty and/or snowy weather.
A violent assault on a fortified position or stronghold.

examples.text: I resolved to keep a diary this year.

etymology.text: From Middle English resolven, from Old French resolver, a learned borrowing of Latin resolvō (“loosen, thaw, melt, resolve”), equivalent to re- + solve. Piecewise doublet of re-solve.

senses.definition: To make distinctions.

senses.definition: To set apart as being different; to mark as different; to separate from another by discerning differences; to distinguish.

examples.text: I don't discriminate.
examples.translation: 我不歧視人。

examples.text: Most of women are discriminated.
examples.translation: 大多數女性受到歧視。

etymology.text: First attested in 1615; borrowed from Latin discrīminātus, perfect passive participle of discrīminō (“to divide, separate, distinguish”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from discrīmen (“a space between, division, separation, distinction”), from discernō (“to divide, separate, distinguish, discern”). By surface analysis, dis- + criminate.
etymology.native: 最早見於 1615 年；借自拉丁語 discrīminātus，動詞 discrīminō（「分開、分離、區分」）的完成被動分詞。

senses.definition: To oxidize or discolor due to oxidation.

examples.text: Old love does not tarnish.

examples.text: Those photos—which experts say could have been created as early as 1850—were tarnished so badly they were unrecognizable.
examples.translation: 那些照片據專家稱可能早在 1850 年就已拍攝，因受損嚴重而無法辨認。

examples.text: People on the website engage in a disgraceful behavior of bullying Antonio, tarnishing the online community's reputation.

relations.native: 因灑漏或其他接觸液體或物質而變色

etymology.text: From Middle English ternysshen, from Old French terniss-, stem of ternir (“to make dim, make wan”), borrowed from Old High German *ternen, tarnen, from Proto-West Germanic *darnijan (“to conceal”). Doublet of dern and darn.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 ternysshen，來自舊法語 terniss-，源自 ternir（使變暗、使蒼白），借自舊高地德語 *ternen 及 tarnen。

senses.definition: To mark with speckles.

examples.text: I have a black and white speckled dog.

senses.definition: A flat fold; a doubling, as of cloth; a pleat.
A braid, as of hair or straw; a plat.

etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 pleit，來自盎格魯-諾曼語 pleit（對照古法語 ploit），源自拉丁語 plectō，與古挪威語 flétta（丹麥語 flette）、俄語 плести́（plestí）相近，亦與古英語 fleohtan 相似，此詞已取代它。是 plight（「編織、摺疊」）的同源詞。

To interweave the strands or locks of; to braid

examples.text: He plaited her hair for her.

etymology.text: From Middle English pleit, from Anglo-Norman pleit (compare Old French ploit), from Latin plectō, which is akin to Old Norse flétta (Danish flette), Russian плести́ (plestí) and also to Old English fleohtan, which it displaced. Doublet of plight (“plait, fold”) and pleat.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 pleit，來自盎格魯-諾曼語 pleit（對照古法語 ploit），源自拉丁語 plectō，與古挪威語 flétta（丹麥語 flette）、俄語 плести́（plestí）相近，亦與古英語 fleohtan 相似，此詞已取代它。是 plight（「編織、摺疊」）的同源詞。

Anything twisted, or the act of twisting.
senses.native: 扭轉、扭曲，或扭轉的動作

The degree of stress or strain when twisted.
A type of thread made from two filaments twisted together.
senses.native: 絞線，兩股絲線絞合而成的線

senses.definition: A sudden bend (or short series of bends) in a road, path, etc.

senses.definition: An unexpected turn in a story, tale, etc.

senses.native: 扭扭舞，1950 年代末至 1960 年代流行於西方的舞蹈

A twig.
A girl, a woman.
A beverage made of brandy and gin.

senses.definition: An act of folding.

A layer, such as of of folded or wrapped cloth.
A clasp, embrace.
A coil of a snake’s body.
One of the doorleaves of a folding door.
A gentle curve of the ground; gentle hill or valley.
senses.native: 地面的緩坡；小山丘或山谷

senses.native: 原為平面的沉積岩層等因塑性變形而彎曲或褶皺

senses.definition: Any of a family of higher-order functions that process a data structure recursively to build up a value.

Home, family.

etymology.text: The verb is from Middle English folden, from Old English fealdan, from Proto-West Germanic *falþan, from Proto-Germanic *falþaną (“to fold”), from Proto-Indo-European *pel- (“to fold”).
etymology.native: 此詞源於中古英語的 folden，來自古英語 fealdan，再源自原始日耳曼語 *falþaną（「摺疊」），最終追溯至原始印歐語 *pel-（「摺疊」）。

senses.definition: To form something by passing lengths or strands of material over and under one another.

examples.text: Spiders like to weave webs.

Food, especially snack food.

The beat of a drum.

etymology.text: From Middle English tuken, touken (“to torment, to stretch (cloth)”), from Old English tūcian (“to torment, vex”) and Middle Dutch tucken (“to tuck”), both from Proto-Germanic *teuh-, *teug- (“to draw, pull”) (compare also *tukkōną), from Proto-Indo-European *dewk- (“to pull”). examples.text: We don't need any more. We already have ample.
examples.translation: 我們不需要更多了，我們已經夠了。

Ridiculous, absurd, outrageous, preposterous, especially in a galling, hypocritical, or brazen way.
Pornographic; titillating.

To live one's life according to (religion, teachings, etc).
To understand, to pay attention to.
To watch, to keep track of (reports of) some event or person.
To be a supporter of (a sports team).
To walk in, as a road or course; to attend upon closely, as a profession or calling.
senses.native: 從事（某職業）；沿著（道路）走

examples.text: The lion followed the trainer's commands.
examples.translation: 獅子聽從馴獸師的指揮。

examples.text: Please follow the nurse's directions.
examples.translation: 請遵循護士的指導。

examples.text: Don't ask questions. Just follow me.
examples.translation: 別問問題。跟著我就行。

examples.text: Dan was disfigured following a car accident.
examples.translation: 丹在一場車禍後毀容了。

examples.text: Xiao Wang followed my advice and quit smoking.
examples.translation: 小王聽從了我的勸告，把煙戒了！

examples.text: Tom wanted to follow in his father's footsteps.
examples.translation: 湯姆想追隨他父親的腳步。

relations.native: 制酥點用的擀成極薄層的生面
碎片；殘片；脫離的不完整部分

etymology.text: From Middle English folwen, folȝen, folgen, from Old English folgian (“to follow, pursue”), from Proto-West Germanic *folgēn, from Proto-Germanic *fulgāną (“to follow”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（folwen），來自古英語（folgian）「跟隨、追趕」，經原始日耳曼語（*fulgāną）「跟隨」。

senses.definition: To survey; to look broadly over.
To write a critical evaluation of a new art work etc.; to write a review.
To look back over in order to correct or edit; to revise.
To look over again (something previously written or learned), especially in preparation for an examination.
To view or see again; to look back on.
To retrace; to go over again.

examples.text: The doctors reviewed their containment procedures.
examples.translation: 醫生們檢討了他們的防疫程序。

examples.text: Tom and Mary are reviewing all their options.
examples.translation: 湯姆和瑪麗正在檢視他們所有的選項。

examples.text: I'll keep the meeting notes to review them before the next session.
examples.translation: 我會記會議筆記，下次會議前可以回顧一下。

examples.text: He advised us to review the lesson thoroughly.
examples.translation: 他建議我們徹底複習這一課。

examples.text: He reviewed the footage frame by frame.
examples.translation: 他一格一格地檢視那段影片。

examples.text: Before I tackle the question directly, I must briefly review historical approaches to the problem.

etymology.text: From Middle English revewe, reveue, from Old French reveüe, revue (Modern French: revue), feminine form of reveü, past participle of reveoir (French: revoir), from Latin revideō, from re- +videō (“see, observe”) (English: video). Equivalent to re- + view. Compare retrospect. Doublet of revue.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（revewe、reveue），來自古法語（reveüe、revue，現代法語 revue），是（reveoir，法語 revoir）過去分詞（reveü）的陰性形式，源自拉丁語（revideō），由（re-）加（videō）「看」組成（英語 video）。相當於（re-）加（view）。比較（retrospect）。與（revue）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: The sense or faculty by which objects are perceived through the agency of light; the sense by which we see.
Something seen.
Something worth seeing; a spectacle, either good or bad.
A device used in aiming a projectile, through which the person aiming looks at the intended target; see also in one's sights.
An act, instance, opportunity or possibility of seeing; the perception of objects by the eye; view (see also idiomatic expressions such as in sight, out of sight, catch sight of, etc.)
senses.native: 看見、視察；眼睛感知物體的能力；景象

senses.definition: A small aperture through which objects are to be seen, and by which their direction is settled or ascertained.
senses.native: 用於觀察物體並確定其方向的狹小孔洞

senses.definition: a great deal, a lot; frequently used to intensify a comparative.
senses.native: 很多、許多；常用於加強比較級語氣

senses.definition: In a drawing, picture, etc., that part of the surface, as of paper or canvas, which is within the frame or the border or margin. In a frame, the open space, the opening.
senses.native: 畫作或紙張上位於邊框內的部分；相框中的開口

senses.definition: Mental view; opinion; judgment.
The instrument of seeing; the eye.

examples.text: The bird disappeared from my sight.
examples.translation: 鳥兒從我的視線中消失了。

examples.text: She attracted me at first sight.
examples.translation: 我對她一見鐘情。

examples.text: Switzerland boasts many sights.
examples.translation: 瑞士有很多景點。

examples.text: There's still no end in sight.
examples.translation: 還是看不見盡頭。

examples.text: There's not a cloud in sight.
examples.translation: 連一個雲朵都沒有。

examples.text: Did you fall in love with her at first sight?
examples.translation: 你對她是不是一見鍾情？

etymology.text: From Middle English sighte, from Old English sihþ (“something seen; vision”), from Proto-West Germanic *sihti (“seeing, sight”), equivalent to see + -t.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 sighte，來自古英語 sihþ（「所見之物；視覺」），等同於 see 加上 -t 詞綴。

senses.definition: A summary or synopsis.
A summary or account of education and employment experiences and qualifications; a curriculum vitae (often for presentation to a potential future employer when applying for a job).

examples.text: I don't worry so much about my resume.
examples.translation: 我對自己的履歷不那麼在意。

examples.text: I asked the company for his resume.
examples.translation: 我向他公司詢問了他的經歷。

examples.text: I've seen your resume and am very impressed.
He advised the job applicant to redo her resume.

etymology.text: From Anglo-Norman resumer, Middle French resumer, from Latin resumere, from re- + sumere (“to take”).

senses.definition: A rapidly executed freehand drawing that is not intended as a finished work, often consisting of a multitude of overlapping lines.
A brief musical composition or theme, especially for the piano.
A rough design, plan, or draft, as a rough draft of a book.
senses.native: 粗略的草圖、計畫或草稿，例如書稿的初稿

senses.definition: A brief description of a person or account of an incident; a general presentation or outline.
senses.native: 對人物的簡短描述或事件經過的敘述；一般性的介紹或大綱

senses.definition: A brief, light, or informal literary composition, such as an essay or short story.
senses.native: 一篇輕盈、隨意或非正式的文學作品，例如散文或短篇小說

senses.definition: An amusing person.
A lookout; vigilant watch for something.
senses.native: 警戒者；對某事的警惕監視

senses.definition: A humorous newspaper article summarizing political events, making heavy use of metaphor, paraphrase and caricature.
senses.native: 一篇幽默的新聞文章，總結政治事件，大量運用比喻、改寫和漫畫風格

senses.definition: A formal specification of a mathematical structure or a data type described in terms of a graph and diagrams (and cones (and cocones)) on it. It can be implemented by means of “models”, which are functors which are graph homomorphisms from the formal specification to categories such that the diagrams become commutative, the cones become limiting (i.e., products), the cocones become colimiting (i.e., sums).
senses.native: 一種數學結構或資料類型的正式規格，以圖形和圖表（以及錐體與反錐體）描述之；可透過函子實現，使圖形成為可交換、錐體成為極限積、反錐體成為極限餘

examples.text: Jiro made a sketch of Mt. Fuji.
examples.translation: 次郎畫了一幅富士山的素描。

examples.text: This sketch is representative of Tom's style.
Tom ripped a page out of his sketch book.
examples.translation: 湯姆從他的繪畫本上撕下了一頁。

examples.text: I have to write a character sketch for a novel study.

etymology.text: From Dutch schets or German Skizze, from Italian schizzo, from Latin schedium, from Ancient Greek σχέδιος (skhédios, “made suddenly, off-hand”), from σχεδόν (skhedón, “near, nearby”), from ἔχω (ékhō, “to hold”). Compare scheme.

senses.definition: The action of looking; an attempt to see.
Physical appearance, visual impression.
A facial expression.

examples.text: Judging from the look of the sky, it is likely to rain.
examples.translation: 看看天的樣子，要下雨了。

senses.definition: An abstract or a condensed presentation of the substance of a body of material.

examples.text: He translated the summary into Berber.
Tom wrote down a summary.
The following is a summary of the President's speech.
examples.translation: 下面是總統講話的概要。

examples.text: Your summary leaves nothing to be desired.
If you like, I can send you a half-page summary.
A summary contains the essence of a text.

etymology.text: From Middle English summary, from Medieval Latin summārius, from Latin summa (“total, sum”) + -ārius (suffix forming adjectives).

senses.definition: The act of examining.
Particularly, an inspection by a medical professional to establish the extent and nature of any sickness or injury.

A formal test involving answering written or oral questions under a time constraint and usually without access to textbooks; typically, a large, written test administered to high school and college students covering course material studied in a semester.
Interrogation, particularly by a lawyer in court or during discovery.

examples.text: They failed in the examination.
examples.translation: 他們考試失敗了。

examples.text: The following persons passed the examination.
Your examination results are excellent.
Work hard, and you will pass the examination.
examples.translation: 好好努力，你就能透過考試。

examples.text: He was happy to have passed the examination.
examples.translation: 他為考試及格感到高興。

examples.text: I have to take the entrance examination today.
examples.translation: 我今天要參加入學試。

etymology.text: From Middle English examinacioun, from Old French examinacion, from Latin exāminātiō. Morphologically examine + -ation.

senses.definition: To observe carefully or critically to learn about someone or something.
To check the health or condition of something or someone.
To determine the aptitude, skills or qualifications of someone by subjecting them to an examination.
To interrogate.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: The doctor examined the patients.
examples.translation: 醫生檢查了病人。

examples.text: The doctor examined Boldi very carefully.
examples.translation: 醫生非常仔細地為博爾迪做了檢查。

examples.text: The scientists examined dendrochronological records.
examples.translation: 科學家們檢視了樹輪年代的紀錄。

examples.text: The doctor used X-rays to examine my stomach.
examples.translation: 醫生用放射線照片檢查我的胃。

examples.text: Dentists take X-rays to examine your teeth.
examples.translation: 牙醫用放射線照片檢查你的牙齒。

examples.text: I had my teeth examined at the dentist's.
examples.translation: 我在牙醫那兒檢查了牙齒。

relations.native: 仔細檢視，尋找隱藏或隱晦的瑕疵

etymology.text: From Middle English examinen, examenen, from Old French examiner, from Latin exāmināre.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語，來自古法語，來自拉丁語「檢驗、衡量」。

senses.definition: To notice or view, especially carefully or with attention to detail.
To follow or obey the custom, practice, or rules (especially of a religion).
To take note of and celebrate (a holiday or similar occurrence), to keep; to follow (a type of time or calendar reckoning).
senses.native: 遵守、慶祝（節日）；遵行（某種曆法）

senses.definition: To comment on something; to make an observation.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: They will observe it.
examples.translation: 他們會觀察它。

senses.definition: To follow urgently, originally with intent to capture or harm; to chase.
To follow, travel down (a particular way, course of action etc.).
To aim for, go after (a specified objective, situation etc.).
To participate in (an activity, business etc.); to practise, follow (a profession).
To urge (someone or something) to act in a particular way.
To act as a legal prosecutor.
To continue; to carry on.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Some people pursue only pleasure.
examples.translation: 有些人只追求快樂。

examples.text: Michael never really pursued anyone before.
Elias pursued Sandra and caught her.
The police will pursue her for a long time.
examples.translation: 警察會追捕她很長時間。

examples.text: She especially likes to pursue questions till the very end.
examples.translation: 她呢就是喜歡打破沙鍋問到底。

examples.text: The police and the FBI pursued several leads.

etymology.text: From Middle English pursuen, from Anglo-Norman pursure, poursuire etc., from Latin prōsequor (though influenced by persequor). Doublet of prosecute.

senses.definition: To deliberately not listen or pay attention to.
To pretend to not notice someone or something.
Fail to notice.
Not to know.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: He ignored all of our warnings.
examples.translation: 他不顧我們的一再勸告。

examples.text: She ignored all my warnings.
examples.translation: 她忽視了我所有的警告。

examples.text: The warnings were ignored.
examples.translation: 警告被忽視。

examples.text: Why are you ignoring me?
examples.translation: 為什麼你不理我？

examples.text: I have a feeling I'm being ignored.
examples.translation: 我有一種我被忽略了的感覺。

examples.text: If I were you, I would ignore it.
examples.translation: 如果我是你，我就忽略它。

etymology.text: From French ignorer, from Latin ignōrō (“to have no knowledge of, mistake, take no notice of, ignore”), from ignārus (“not knowing”), from in- (“not”) + gnārus (“knowing”), from gnōscō, nōscō; see know.

senses.definition: To sell at a reduced price.
To disregard or regard as unimportant.
To lend money upon, deducting the discount or allowance for interest.
To take into consideration beforehand; to anticipate and form conclusions concerning (an event).
To believe, or act as though one believes, that one's own feelings are more important than the reality of a situation.
To deduct from an account, debt, charge, etc.

examples.text: Can the price be discounted?
examples.translation: 價錢可以打折嗎？

examples.text: Owing to his reputation, they discounted his comments.
The company's directors were chagrined to learn that banks were suddenly refusing to discount its notes.
Merchants sometimes discount five or six per cent for prompt payment of bills.

etymology.text: Alteration of French descompte, décompte, from Old French disconter, desconter (“reckon off, account back, discount”), from Medieval Latin discomputō (“to deduct, discount”), from Latin dis- (“away”) + computō (“to reckon, count”). By surface analysis, dis- + count.

senses.definition: To discharge; to end the employment or service of.
To order to leave.
To dispel; to rid one’s mind of.
To reject; to refuse to accept.
To invalidate; to treat as unworthy of serious consideration.
senses.native: 駁回；視為不值得認真考慮

senses.definition: To send or put away, to discard with disregard, contempt or disdain. (sometimes followed by as).
To get a batsman out.
To give someone a red card; to send off.

examples.text: Lucy dismissed what Mary was saying.
examples.translation: 露西不理會瑪麗所說的話。

examples.text: They were dismissed from their jobs.
examples.translation: 他們被從工作中解僱了。

examples.text: He was dismissed by the boss of the factory.
examples.translation: 他被工廠的老闆解僱。

examples.text: The secretary was dismissed.
examples.translation: 秘書被炒了。

examples.text: Henry was dismissed by reason of his old age.
examples.translation: 亨利因年事已高而被解僱。

examples.text: The possibility of a lack of connection between the events can be dismissed immediately.
examples.translation: 可以立即排除事件之間缺乏關聯的可能性

relations.native: 點燃（某物，通常是建築物）

etymology.text: Middle English, from Latin dimissus (“sent away, dismissed, banished”), perfect passive participle of dīmittō (“send away, dismiss”), from dis- + mittere (“to send”).
etymology.native: 源於拉丁語，意為「被遣送」，由前綴 dis- 與動詞 mittere（發送）組成。

senses.definition: To ignore; to pay no attention to.

examples.text: Donald disregarded Jessica's recommendations.
examples.translation: 唐納德忽略賈絲貝拉的建議。

examples.text: He disregarded his father's advice.
examples.translation: 他不顧他父親的忠告。

examples.text: He disregarded my advice.
examples.translation: 他不顧我的忠告。

examples.text: Disregarding the "No Entry" sign, she pushed open the door and walked inside.
examples.translation: 無視於「 禁止進入」 的牌子，她推開了門走進去。

examples.text: How do we decide which social norms are good and which ones we should disregard?
examples.translation: 我們如何決定哪些社會規範是好的，哪些應該忽略？

etymology.text: From dis- + regard. Compare misregard.
etymology.native: 由 dis- 與 regard 組成。可與 misregard 相比。

senses.definition: To become aware of; to observe.
To be noticeable; to show.
To perceive Jewish influence or responsibility.
senses.native: （反猶陰謀論用語）察覺猶太人的影響

senses.definition: To remark upon; to mention.
To lavish attention upon; to treat (someone) favourably.

examples.text: Mary said she's noticed the difference.
examples.translation: 瑪麗說她察覺到了區別。

examples.text: He will notice sooner or later.
examples.translation: 他遲早會發現的。

examples.text: I noticed that Tom was smiling.
examples.translation: 我注意到湯姆在笑。

examples.text: The ladies don't notice him.
examples.translation: 女人們不注意他。

examples.text: I noticed that she was wearing new glasses.
examples.translation: 我注意到她戴著新眼鏡。

examples.text: Walking along the fence he noticed a mouse.
examples.translation: 沿著柵欄走時, 他看到了一隻老鼠。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French notice, from the Latin nōtitia. Doublet of notitia.
etymology.native: 借自中古法語（notice），來自拉丁語（nōtitia）。與（notitia）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: To perceive the truth or factuality of; to be certain of; to be certain that.
To be acquainted or familiar with; to have encountered.
To have knowledge; to have information, be informed.
To be or become aware or cognizant.
To be aware of; to be cognizant of.
To experience.
To understand or have a grasp of through experience or study.
To be able to distinguish, to discern, particularly by contrast or comparison; to recognize the nature of.
To recognize as the same (as someone or something previously encountered) after an absence or change.
To be able to play or perform (a song or other piece of music).
senses.native: 會彈奏或演唱（某首曲子）

senses.definition: To have indexed and have information about within one's database.
senses.native: 在資料庫中索引並擁有資訊

senses.definition: To maintain (a belief, a position) subject to a given philosophical definition of knowledge; to hold a justified true belief.
senses.native: 依據特定哲學定義維持信念或立場；持有經證實的真實信念

senses.definition: To be acquainted (with another person).
To have sexual relations with. This meaning normally specified in modern English as e.g. to ‘know someone in the biblical sense’ or to ‘know biblically’.

examples.text: Don't you know what happened yesterday?
examples.translation: 你不知道昨天發生什麼事嗎？

examples.text: They don't know that I'm Japanese.
examples.translation: 他們不知道我是日本人。

examples.text: I don't know where we'll arrive.
examples.translation: 我不知道我們會到達哪裡。

examples.text: You know where the problem lies.
examples.translation: 你知道問題在哪裡。

examples.text: Do you know how high the television tower is?
examples.translation: 你知道那座電視塔有多高嗎？

examples.text: Do you know when the musician will come here?
examples.translation: 你知道音樂傢什麼時候來這兒嗎？

etymology.text: From Middle English knowen, from Old English cnāwan (“to know, perceive, recognise”), from Proto-West Germanic *knāan, from Proto-Germanic *knēaną (“to know”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵneh₃- (“to know”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（knowen），來自古英語（cnāwan）「知道、察覺、認出」，經原始日耳曼語（*knēaną），上溯至原始印歐語（*ǵneh₃-）「知道」。

senses.definition: To look at, see, or view for a period of time.
To observe over a period of time; to notice or pay attention.
To mind, attend, or guard.
To be wary or cautious of.
To attend to dangers to or regarding.
To remain awake with a sick or dying person; to maintain a vigil.
senses.native: 陪伴病人或垂死者，徹夜守候（守夜）

senses.definition: To be vigilant or on one's guard.
To act as a lookout.
To serve the purpose of a watchman by floating properly in its place.
senses.native: （浮標）適當浮於定位，發揮標示作用

senses.definition: To be awake.
To be on the lookout for; to wait for expectantly.

examples.text: My little brother is watching television.
examples.translation: 我弟弟在看電視。

examples.text: We enjoyed watching the baseball game.
examples.translation: 我們喜歡看棒球比賽。

examples.text: Because they're watching television.
examples.translation: 因為他們正在看電視。

examples.text: Have you watched television tonight?
examples.translation: 你今晚看電視了嗎？

examples.text: I feel like everybody's watching me.
examples.translation: 我感覺大家都在關注我。

examples.text: I want to watch the concert of Kylie Minogue.
examples.translation: 我想看凱莉米洛的演唱會。

etymology.text: As a noun, from Middle English wacche, from Old English wæċċe. See below for verb form.

senses.definition: To negotiate, discuss terms, bargain (for or with).
To handle, deal with or behave towards in a specific way.
To entertain with food or drink, especially at one's own expense; to show hospitality to; to pay for as celebration or reward.
To care for medicinally or surgically; to apply medical care to.
To discourse; to handle a subject in writing or speaking; to conduct a discussion.
To discourse on; to represent or deal with in a particular way, in writing or speaking.
To commit the offence of providing food, drink, entertainment or provision to corruptly influence a voter.
To subject to a chemical or other action; to act upon with a specific scientific result in mind.
To provide (someone) with something special and pleasant.
To entreat or beseech (someone).

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: They were treated for hypothermia.
examples.translation: 醫生治療了他們的降低體溫。

examples.text: You yourself need to be treated!
examples.translation: 應該接受治療的是你自己!

examples.text: Mary treated her wounded knee.
examples.translation: 瑪麗處理了膝蓋的傷口。

examples.text: She treated him very well.
examples.translation: 她對他很好。

examples.text: It would be unfair if we treated him so badly.
examples.translation: 我們這樣待他，好像不是太好。

examples.text: He is our boss, and must be treated as such.
examples.translation: 他是我們的老闆，所以一定要受到這樣的禮待。

relations.native: 陳腐的；因使用過多而變得普通、無趣或過時的

etymology.text: From Middle English treten, from Anglo-Norman treter, Old French tretier, traiter, from Latin tractāre (“to pull", "to manage”), from the past participle stem of trahere (“to draw", "to pull”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（treten），來自英法語（treter）、古法語（tretier、traiter），再源自拉丁語（tractāre）「拉、處理」，來自（trahere）「拉」的過去分詞詞幹。

senses.definition: To refuse to accept; to forswear.
To block a shot, especially if it sends the ball off the court.
To refuse a romantic advance.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: He rejected her advances.

A software program designed to perform a single task or a small range of tasks, often to help manage and tune computer hardware, an operating system, or application software.

etymology.text: From Middle English qualite, from Old French qualité, from Latin quālitās, quālitātem, from quālis (“of what kind”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷo- (“who, how”). Cicero coined qualitas as a calque to translate the Ancient Greek word ποιότης (poiótēs, “quality”), coined by Plato from ποῖος (poîos, “of what nature, of what kind”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（qualite），來自古法語（qualité），再源自拉丁語（quālitās），來自（quālis）「何種的」，最終源自原始印歐語（*kʷo-）「誰、如何」。西塞羅造出（qualitas）一詞，用來仿譯柏拉圖所造的古希臘語（ποιότης）「性質」。

Displaced native Middle English sothen (“to prove”), from Old English sōþian (“to prove”). Doublet of probe. More at
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（proven），來自古英語（prōfian）「尊重、顯示、試驗、證明」與古法語（prover）「證明」，兩者皆源自拉丁語（probō）「試驗、檢查、認可、證明」，來自（probus）「好的、正直的」，最終源自原始印歐語。取代了中古英語原有的（sothen）「證明」。與（probe）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: An effort, process, or operation designed to establish or discover a fact or truth; an act of testing; a test; a trial.

The degree of evidence which convinces the mind of any truth or fact, and produces belief; a test by facts or arguments which induce, or tend to induce, certainty of the judgment; conclusive evidence; demonstration.
The quality or state of having been proved or tried; firmness or hardness which resists impression, or does not yield to force; impenetrability of physical bodies.
A proof sheet; a trial impression, as from type, taken for correction or examination.
A limited-run high-quality strike of a particular coin, originally as a test run, although nowadays mostly for collectors' sets.

A sequence of statements consisting of axioms, assumptions, statements already demonstrated in another proof, and statements that logically follow from previous statements in the sequence, and which concludes with a statement that is the object of the proof.
A process for testing the accuracy of an operation performed. Compare prove, transitive verb, 5.

A measure of the alcohol content of liquor. Originally, in Britain, 100 proof was defined as 57.1% by volume (no longer used). In the US, 100 proof means that the alcohol content is 50% of the total volume of the liquid; thus, perfectly pure absolute alcohol would be 200 proof.
Experience of something.
Firmness of mind; stability not to be shaken.
Armour of excellent or tried quality, and deemed impenetrable; properly, armour of proof.
