etymology.text: From Middle English proof, from Old French prove, from Late Latin proba (“a proof”), from Latin probō (“to prove”); see prove; compare also the doublet probe.

senses.definition: A fact or statement used to support a proposition; a reason.
A series of propositions organized so that the final proposition is a conclusion which is intended to follow logically from the preceding propositions, which function as premises.
A process of reasoning; argumentation.

An abstract or summary of the content of a literary work such as a book, a poem or a major section such as a chapter, included in the work before the content itself; (figuratively) the contents themselves.
A verbal dispute; a quarrel.
Any of the phrases that bear a syntactic connection to the verb of a clause.
The independent variable of a function.
The phase of a complex number.
A quantity on which the calculation of another quantity depends.
A value, or a reference to a value, passed to a function.
A parameter at a function call; an actual parameter, as opposed to a formal parameter.
Any dispute, altercation, or collision.
a fact or assertion offered as evidence that something is true
a contentious speech act; a dispute where there is strong disagreement
a discussion in which reasons are advanced for and against some proposition or proposal
a summary of the subject or plot of a literary work or play or movie
(computer science) a reference or value that is passed to a function, procedure, subroutine, command, or program
A matter in question; a business in hand.
The subject matter of an artistic representation, discourse, or writing; a theme or topic.
Evidence, proof; (countable) an item of such evidence or proof.

etymology.text: From Middle English argument, from Anglo-Norman and Old French arguement, from Latin argumentum. The English word is analysable as argue + -ment. Doublet of argumentum.

senses.definition: Having a (specified) intention.
Expressing some intention or significance; meaningful.

examples.text: I can't understand this sign's meaning.

etymology.text: From Middle English mening, menyng, equivalent to mean + -ing. Cognate with Scots mening (“intent, purpose, sense, meaning”), West Frisian miening (“opinion, mind”), Dutch mening (“view, opinion, judgement”), German Meinung (“opinion, view, mind, idea”), Danish and Swedish mening (“meaning, sense, sentence, opinion”), Icelandic meining (“meaning”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 mening、menyng，意為 mean + -ing。與蘇格蘭語 mening（意為「意圖、目的、意義」）、西弗里斯蘭語 miening（意為「意見、心思」）、荷蘭語 mening（意為「觀點、意見、判斷」）、德語 Meinung（意為「意見、觀點、心思、想法」）、丹麥語與瑞典語 mening（意為「意義、語意、句子、意見」）、冰島語 meining（意為「意義」）同源。

senses.definition: Signifying something; carrying meaning.
Having a noticeable or major effect.
Reasonably large in number or amount.
Having a covert or hidden meaning.
Having a low probability of occurring by chance (for example, having high correlation and thus likely to be related).
Of a digit or figure, see significant figure.

etymology.text: From Latin significans, present participle of significare, from signum (“sign”) + ficare (“do, make”), variant of facere.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語（significans），是（significare）的現在分詞，由（signum）「記號」加（ficare，facere 的變體）「做」組成。

senses.definition: The extent to which something matters; importance
Meaning.

examples.text: Did that have any special significance?

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English significaunce, from Middle French significance, from Old French significance, from Latin significantia. Doublet of signifiance.

senses.definition: Physical matter; material.
A form of matter that has constant chemical composition and characteristic properties.
The essential part of anything; the most vital part.
Substantiality; solidity; firmness.
Material possessions; estate; property; resources.
Drugs (illegal narcotics)
Ousia, essence; underlying reality or hypostasis in the philosophical sense.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English substance, from Old French substance, from Latin substantia (“substance, essence”), from substāns, present active participle of substō (“exist”, literally “stand under”), from sub + stō (“stand”). Displaced native Old English andweorc.

senses.definition: Something brought in from an exterior source, especially for sale or trade.
The practice of importing.
A foreigner playing in a sports league.
Significance, importance
The meaning of a term, statement, etc.

senses.definition: An abstract archetype of a given thing, compared to which real-life examples are seen as imperfect approximations; pure essence, as opposed to actual examples.
An image of an object that is formed in the mind or recalled by the memory.
A conception in the mind of something to be done; a plan for doing something, an intention.
More generally, any result of mental activity; a thought, a notion; a way of thinking.
A purposeful aim or goal; intent.
A vague or fanciful notion; a feeling or hunch; an impression.
A musical theme or melodic subject.
The conception of someone or something as representing a perfect example; an ideal.
The form or shape of something; a quintessential aspect or characteristic.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin idea (“a (Platonic) idea; archetype”), from Ancient Greek ἰδέα (idéa, “notion, pattern”), from εἴδω (eídō, “to see”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *weyd- (“to know; see”). Cognate with French idée. Doublet of idée. Related to idol, idolum, and eidolon.
etymology.native: 借自拉丁語（idea）「（柏拉圖式的）理念；原型」，來自古希臘語（ἰδέα）「概念、形態」，再源自（εἴδω）「看」，最終來自原始印歐語（*weyd-）「知道、看」。與法語（idée）同源。與（idol）、（eidolon）有關。

senses.definition: A communication, or what is communicated; any concept or information conveyed.
An errand.
An errand to a shop, a shopping expedition; an item of shopping; (in plural) groceries.
An underlying theme or conclusion to be drawn from something.

Perception through the intellect; apprehension; awareness.
The meaning, reason, or value of something.
A meaning of a term (word or expression), among its various meanings.
Sound practical or moral judgment.
A single conventional use of a word; one of the entries or definitions for a word in a dictionary.

etymology.text: From Middle English sense, from Old French sens, sen, san (“sense, perception, direction”); partly from Latin sēnsus (“sensation, feeling, meaning”), from sentiō (“feel, perceive”); partly of Germanic origin (whence also Occitan sen, Italian senno), from Vulgar Latin *sennus (“sense, reason, way”), from Frankish *sinn ("reason, judgement, mental faculty, way, direction"; whence also Dutch zin, German Sinn, Swedish sinne, Norwegian sinn). Both Latin and Germanic from Proto-Indo-European *sent- (“

senses.definition: A measurement one can compare (some other measurement) to.
Information about a person, provided by someone (a referee) with whom they are well acquainted.
A person who provides this information; a referee.
A reference work.
The act of referring: a submitting for information or decision.
A relation between objects in which one object designates, or acts as a means by which to connect to or link to, another object.
A short written identification of a previously published work which is used as a source for a text.
A previously published written work thus indicated; a source.
An object containing information which refers to data stored elsewhere, as opposed to containing the data itself.
A special sequence used to represent complex characters in markup languages, such as ™ for the ™ symbol.
A relationship or relation (to something).
Appeal.

senses.definition: Having meaning, significant.

A prison cell.
A cell used for solitary confinement.
A coffin.
The television.
A computer, or the case in which it is housed.
A gym dedicated to the CrossFit exercise program.

Impact.

etymology.text: From Middle English chayere, chayer, chayre, from Old French chaiere, chaere, from Latin cathedra (“seat”), from Ancient Greek καθέδρα (kathédra), from κατά (katá, “down”) + ἕδρα (hédra, “seat”). Partially displaced native stool and settle, which now have more specialised senses. Doublet of cathedra and chaise.

etymology.text: From Middle English chayere, chayer, chayre, from Old French chaiere, chaere, from Latin cathedra (“seat”), from Ancient Greek καθέδρα (kathédra), from κατά (katá, “down”) + ἕδρα (hédra, “seat”). Partially displaced native stool and settle, which now have more specialised senses. Doublet of cathedra and chaise.

A person presiding over a corporation, usually an executive overseeing daily operations under a chief executive officer but sometimes a separate position held by a CEO.
A person presiding over a meeting.
A person presiding over a dinner or similar informal conversation.
An honorific for the head of state of a republic.

etymology.text: From Old French president, from Latin praesidēns (“presiding over; president, leader”) (accusative: praesidentem). The Latin word is the substantivized present active participle of the verb praesideō (“preside over”). The verb is composed from prae (“before”) and sedeō (“sit”). The original meaning of the verb is 'to sit before' in the sense of presiding at a meeting. A secondary meaning of the verb is 'to command, to govern'. So praesidēns means 'the presiding one on a meeting' or 'governor, co
etymology.native: 源自古法語（president），來自拉丁語（praesidēns）「主持、會長、領袖」（受格 praesidentem），是動詞（praesideō）「主持」的現在主動分詞的名詞化。該動詞由（prae）「在前」加（sedeō）「坐」組成，原義是「坐在前面」主持會議，引申為「指揮、統治」。

senses.definition: To serve as chairman.

examples.text: In the interim, I will serve as chairman.

etymology.text: From chair + -man.

senses.definition: To reduce the excessiveness of (something).
To become less excessive.
To preside over (something) as a moderator.
To act as a moderator; to assist in bringing to compromise.
To supply with a moderator (substance that decreases the speed of neutrons in a nuclear reactor and hence increases likelihood of fission).

examples.text: He used to be an extremist but moderated later in life.
We need more users to volunteer to moderate the comment section of our forum.
John moderated the discussion.

etymology.text: From Middle English moderat(e) (“moderate, temperate”), borrowed from Latin moderātus, perfect active participle of moderor (“to regulate, to restrain, to moderate”) (see -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from moder-, modes-, a stem appearing also in modestus (“moderate, discreet, modest”), from modus (“a measure”); see mode and modest. Doublet of moderato. Displaced native Old English ġemetlīċ (“moderate”) and metegian (“to moderate”). Cognate with French modéré.

senses.definition: A chairman or chairwoman, someone who presides over a meeting, board, etc.

etymology.text: Borrowed from French sofa, ultimately from Arabic صُفَّة (ṣuffa, “a long seat made of stone or brick, covered with rich carpets and cushions and used for sitting”). Cognate with Aramaic צפא/Classical Syriac ܨܦܬܐ (ṣipā’, ṣeppəṯā, “mat, matting”). The word may have entered European languages via Muslim Iberia or through Turkish.
etymology.native: 「sofa」源自法語，最終來自阿拉伯語 صُفَّة (ṣuffa)，意為「用石或磚製成的長椅，鋪有絨毯與靠墊」。此詞亦與阿拉姆語 צפא 及古典敘利亞語 ܨܦܬܐ (ṣipā’, ṣeppəṯā) 同源，意為「墊子」。此詞可能經穆斯林伊比里亞半島或土耳其傳入歐洲語言。

etymology.text: From Middle English separaten (“to separate”), from separat (“separated”) + -en, from Latin sēparātus, perfect passive participle of sēparō (“to separate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from sē- (“apart”) + parō (“prepare”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *per- (“produce, procure, bring forward, bring forth”). Displaced Middle English scheden, from Old English scēadan (whence English shed).

senses.definition: To apply violent force to someone or something.
To aggressively challenge a person, idea, etc., with words (particularly in newspaper headlines, because it typesets into less space than "criticize" or similar).
(Of a chemical species) To approach a chemical species or bond in order to form a bond with it.
To begin to affect; to act upon injuriously or destructively; to begin to decompose or waste.
To deal with something in a direct way; to set to work upon.
To aim balls at the batsman’s wicket.

To bat aggressively, so as to score runs quickly.

To accelerate quickly in an attempt to get ahead of the other riders.

etymology.text: Borrowed from French attaque, derived from the verb attaquer, from Italian attaccare (“to join, attach”) (used in attaccare battaglia (“to join battle”)), from Frankish *stakkijan (“to stick, stick to, attach”). Doublet of attach. Displaced native Middle English onresen, from Old English onrǣsan (“to attack”); and Middle English resinge (“an assault, attack”) (compare Old English onrǣs (“an attack”)).
etymology.native: 借自法語（attaque），源自動詞（attaquer），來自義大利語（attaccare）「連接、附著」（用於 attaccare battaglia「開戰」），再源自法蘭克語（*stakkijan）「黏、附著」。與（attach）為雙式詞。取代了中古英語原有的（onresen，源自古英語 onrǣsan「攻擊」）與（resinge）「襲擊」。

senses.definition: The act of someone who lounges; idle reclining.

A place where one can lounge; an area, establishment, house etc. where loungers gather and where one can relax and be at ease.
A couch.

examples.text: Stefan went to the teachers' lounge.

Expected or scheduled to take place in the future.
Advanced beyond the usual degree; advanced for the season; precocious.
Without customary restraint or modesty; bold, cheeky, pert, presumptuous or pushy.
Prominent, emphasized (or, in combinations, emphasizing).
Ready; prompt; ardently inclined; in a bad sense, eager or hasty.

examples.text: The forward battalion took a hammering.
examples.translation: 前線營遭受重創。

examples.text: My forward vision is fine, but my peripheral vision is poor.
examples.translation: 我的正前方視力很好，但周邊視力很差。

examples.text: This is an important forward step for the country.
examples.translation: 這是國家向前邁出的重要一步。

examples.text: The price for forward delivery is presently higher than the spot price.
examples.translation: 目前遠期交貨的價格高於現貨價。

examples.text: The grass is forward, or forward for the season. We have a forward spring.
examples.translation: 草長得早，以這個季節來說算早。今年春天來得早。

relations.native: （故事的）未來場景；倒敘的反向

etymology.text: From Middle English foreward, from Old English foreweard (“forward, inclined to the front, fore, early, former”), from Proto-Germanic *fura- (“fore-”), *warþaz (“turned”), equivalent to fore + -ward. Cognate with Dutch voorwaarts (“forward”), German vorwärts (“forward”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（foreward），來自古英語（foreweard）「向前、在前、早期、以前」，由原始日耳曼語（*fura-）「前」加（*warþaz）「轉向」組成，相當於（fore）加（-ward）。與荷蘭語（voorwaarts）、德語（vorwärts）同源。

senses.definition: A device that generates light, heat, or other electromagnetic radiation. Especially an electric light bulb.
A device containing oil, burnt through a wick for illumination; an oil lamp.
A piece of furniture holding one or more electric light sockets.
An eye.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: She turned off her desk lamp.
examples.translation: 她關掉了她的檯燈。

examples.text: Are you selling these lamps?
examples.translation: 你在賣這些燈嗎？

examples.text: I bought an old lamp.
examples.translation: 我買了一盞很舊的燈。

examples.text: The lamp was suspended from the branch of a tree.
examples.translation: 燈籠在樹枝上吊著。

examples.text: Edison invented the electric lamp.
examples.translation: 愛迪生發明了電燈。

examples.text: I'd like to turn off the reading lamp, is that OK?
examples.translation: 我想把閱讀燈關了，行嗎？

etymology.text: From Middle English laumpe, lampe, from Old French lampe (“lamp, light”), from Latin lampas (“torch, lamp, light”), from Ancient Greek λαμπάς (lampás, “torch, lamp, beacon, light, meteor”), from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂p- (“to shine”). Cognate with Lithuanian lópė (“light”), Welsh llachar (“bright”). Displaced native Old English lēohtfæt (literally “light-vat”).

senses.definition: To hunt at night using a lamp, during which bright lights are used to dazzle the hunted animal or to attract insects for capture.
To make (something, such as a vase or urn) into a table lamp.
To hit, clout, belt, wallop.
To hang out or chill; to do nothing in particular.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: I do not like a big desk lamp.

etymology.text: From Middle English laumpe, lampe, from Old French lampe (“lamp, light”), from Latin lampas (“torch, lamp, light”), from Ancient Greek λαμπάς (lampás, “torch, lamp, beacon, light, meteor”), from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂p- (“to shine”). Cognate with Lithuanian lópė (“light”), Welsh llachar (“bright”). Displaced native Old English lēohtfæt (literally “light-vat”).

senses.definition: A sudden, short, temporary burst of light.
A very short amount of time.
A sudden and brilliant burst, as of genius or wit.
Pizzazz, razzle-dazzle.
Material left around the edge of a moulded part at the parting line of the mould.
The strips of bright cloth or buttons worn around the collars of market traders.
A pattern where each prop is thrown and caught only once.
A language, created by a minority to maintain cultural identity, that cannot be understood by the ruling class.
A form of military insignia.
Any of various lycaenid butterflies of the genera Artipe, Deudorix and Rapala.
A flashlight; an electric torch.
A tattoo flash (example design on paper to give an idea of a possible tattoo).
The sudden sensation of being "high" after taking a recreational drug.
Synonym of flashback (“recurrence of the effects of a hallucinogenic drug”).
A brief exposure or making visible (of a smile, badge, etc).
The (intentional or unintentional) exposure of an intimate body part or undergarment in public.
A pool of water, in some areas especially one that is marshy, and/or one formed by subsidence of the ground due to mining. (Compare flush (“marsh; pool”).)
senses.native: 沼澤池；因採礦形成的水坑

senses.definition: A reservoir and sluiceway beside a navigable stream, just above a shoal, so that the stream may pour in water as boats pass, and thus bear them over the shoal.
A preparation of capsicum, burnt sugar, etc., for colouring liquor to make it look stronger.
A newsflash.

examples.text: Jonas started noticing the flashes again.
I left your flash drive at home.
examples.translation: 我把你的優盤忘在家裡了。

examples.text: I saw a flash of lightning far in the distance.
He had a flash of intuition.

etymology.text: In some senses, from Middle English flasshen, a variant of flasken, flaskien (“to sprinkle, splash”), which was likely of imitative origin; in other senses probably of North Germanic origin akin to Swedish dialectal flasa (“to burn brightly, blaze”), related to flare. Compare also Icelandic flasa (“to rush, go hastily”).

senses.definition: A collection of sheets of paper bound together to hinge at one edge, containing printed or written material, pictures, etc.
A record of betting (from the use of a notebook to record what each person has bet).
A list of all players who have been booked (received a warning) in a game.
The list of mares that a stallion will breed in a given season.
A list of the races that a jockey is scheduled to ride in.
The twenty-sixth Lenormand card.
Any source of instruction.
The accumulated body of knowledge passed down among black pimps.
The sum of chess knowledge in the opening or endgame.
A long work fit for publication, typically prose, such as a novel or textbook, and typically published as such a bound collection of sheets, but now sometimes electronically as an e-book.
A major division of a long work.
A bookmaker (a person who takes bets on sporting events and similar); bookie; turf accountant.
A convenient collection, in a form resembling a book, of small paper items for individual use.
The script of a musical or opera.
Records of the accounts of a business.
A book award, a recognition for receiving the highest grade in a class (traditionally an actual book, but recently more likely a letter or certificate acknowledging the achievement).
Six tricks taken by one side.
Four of a kind.
A document, held by the referee, of the incidents that happened in a game.
senses.native: （比賽中由裁判持有的）記錄單（記錄比賽事件）

senses.definition: A portfolio of one's previous work in the industry.

examples.text: This book contains forty photographs.
examples.translation: 這本書裡面有四十張照片。

examples.text: Are you reading an interesting book?
examples.translation: 你在讀有趣的的書嗎?

examples.text: Have you finished reading the book?
examples.translation: 你讀完這本書了嗎？

examples.text: This book isn't interesting at all.
examples.translation: 這本書一點也不有趣。

examples.text: I ordered those books from Germany.
examples.translation: 我從德國訂購了那些書。

examples.text: I have to give back the book before Saturday.
examples.translation: 我必須在禮拜六之前把書還回去。

etymology.text: From Middle English bok, book, from Old English bōc, from Proto-West Germanic *bōk, from Proto-Germanic *bōks. Bookmaker sense by clipping.
etymology.native: 「book」源自中世英文 bok，來自古英文 bōc，再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *bōk，更上溯至原始日耳曼語 *bōks。其「賭博」義項則由剪切形成。

senses.definition: To reserve (something) for future use.
To write down, to register or record in a book or as in a book.
senses.native: 登記、記錄（於簿冊或類似的紀錄中）

senses.definition: To add a name to the list of people who are participating in something.
To record the name and other details of a suspected offender and the offence for later judicial action.
senses.native: 記錄嫌疑人的姓名、資料及違法事由，以供日後司法追訴

senses.definition: To issue a caution to, usually a yellow card, or a red card if a yellow card has already been issued.
senses.native: 對（球員）出示警告（通常為黃牌，若已有黃牌則出示紅牌）

senses.definition: To travel very fast.
To record bets as bookmaker.
To receive the highest grade in a class.
To move or leave, often hurriedly and abruptly.

examples.text: The policeman booked her when she tried to solicit a man.
examples.translation: 警察在她試圖勾引男子時將她逮捕。

etymology.text: From Middle English bok, book, from Old English bōc, from Proto-West Germanic *bōk, from Proto-Germanic *bōks. Bookmaker sense by clipping.
etymology.native: 「book」源自中世英文 bok，來自古英文 bōc，再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *bōk，更上溯至原始日耳曼語 *bōks。其「賭博」義項則由剪切形成。

senses.definition: Something actual as opposed to invented.
Something concrete used as a basis for further interpretation.
An objective consensus on a fundamental reality that has been agreed upon by a substantial number of experts.
Information about a particular subject, especially actual conditions and/or circumstances.
Something which is real.
An individual value or measurement at the lowest level of granularity in a data warehouse.
A wrongful or criminal deed.
Action; the realm of action.
A feat or meritorious deed.

examples.text: We have overlooked this important fact.
examples.translation: 我們看漏了這件重要的事。

examples.text: There is no denying the fact.
examples.translation: 這是無可否認的事實。

examples.text: This story is based on facts.
examples.translation: 這個故事是根據真人真事寫成的。

examples.text: Are you sure of your facts?
examples.translation: 你確定你的資料屬實嗎？

examples.text: We want to know the facts.
examples.translation: 我們想知道真相。

examples.text: I don't really like him, in fact, I hate him.
examples.translation: 我不太喜歡他，其實我討厭他。

etymology.text: From Old French fact, from Latin factum (“an act, deed, feat, etc.”); also Medieval Latin for “state, condition, circumstance”; neuter of factus (“done or made”), perfect passive participle of faciō (“do, make”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to put, place, set”). Old/Middle French later evolved it into faict and fait. Doublet of feat.
etymology.native: 源自古法語（fact），來自拉丁語（factum）「行為、事蹟」，是（faciō）「做」的完成被動分詞中性形式，上溯至原始印歐語（*dʰeh₁-）「放、置」。與（feat）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: A set of items or amount of material procured, gathered or presented together.
A set of pitch classes used by a composer.
The activity of collecting.
A set of sets; used because such a thing is in general too large to comply with the formal definition of a set.
A gathering of money for charitable or other purposes, as by passing a contribution box for donations.
Debt collection.
The jurisdiction of a collector of excise.
A set of college exams generally taken at the start of the term.
The quality of being collected; calm composure.
The act of inferring or concluding from premises or observed facts; also, that which is inferred.

examples.text: The flat front trouser was a staple of that fashion designer's collections.
The attic contains a remarkable collection of antiques, oddities, and random junk.
The asteroid belt consists of a collection of dust, rubble, and minor planets.
This year's Summer Collection will include a wide range of evening wear.
He has a big collection of stamps.
He has a superb coin collection.

etymology.text: From Middle English colleccioun, collection, from Old French collection, from Latin collēctiō, collēctiōnem, from collēctus, from colligō (“collect together”), composed of con- + legō (“bring together, gather, collect”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *leǵ- (“to gather, collect”). Equivalent to collect + -ion.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語，經古法語來自拉丁語「收集」，由「一起」加「採集」組成，最終來自原始印歐語「採集」的字根。相當於「收集」加名詞字尾。

senses.definition: A task.
An economic role for which a person is paid.
A person who shows remarkable patience, especially in the face of great misfortune.
Plastic surgery.
A sex act.
A task, or series of tasks, carried out in batch mode (especially on a mainframe computer).
A public transaction done for private profit; something performed ostensibly as a part of official duty, but really for private gain; a corrupt official business.
senses.native: 假公濟私的勾當；營私舞弊

senses.definition: A robbery or heist.
Any affair or event which affects one, whether fortunately or unfortunately.
A thing or whatsit (often used in a vague way to refer to something whose name one cannot recall).
The police as a profession, act of policing, or an individual police officer.
A sudden thrust or stab; a jab or punch.
Synonym of penis.

examples.text: They hope to be able to find a well-paid job.
examples.translation: 他們希望會找到一份報酬優厚的工作。

examples.text: I'm looking for a part-time job on weekends.
examples.translation: 我在找一份週末的零工。

examples.text: You must get the job done before the deadline.
examples.translation: 你必須在到期前完成這項工作。

examples.text: He was tired out by an awfully tough job.
examples.translation: 他被一件辛苦的工作累壞了。

examples.text: Calling them “silver tongued pundits,” Kenner says their job is to simplify and manipulate arcane scientific data for public consumption.
examples.translation: 肯納稱他們為「銀舌專家」，說他們的工作是將複雜的科學數據簡化並操控以供大眾消費。

etymology.text: From the phrase jobbe of work (“piece of work”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from a variant of Middle English gobbe (“mass, lump”); or perhaps related to Middle English jobben (“to jab, thrust, peck”), or Middle English choppe (“piece, bargain”). More at gob, jab, chop.
etymology.native: 源自片語（jobbe of work）「一件工作」，來源不明。可能是中古英語（gobbe）「團、塊」的變體，或與中古英語（jobben）「戳、啄」或（choppe）「一塊、交易」有關。參見（gob）、（jab）、（chop）。

senses.definition: A book specially designed to keep photographs, stamps, or autographs.
A collection, especially of literary items.
A phonograph record that is composed of several tracks.
A jacket or cover for such a phonograph record.
A group of audio recordings, on any medium, intended for distribution as a group.
In Ancient Rome, a white tablet or register on which the praetor's edicts and other public notices were recorded.

examples.text: They add pictures to their album.
examples.translation: 他們在相簿裡面加了些圖片。

examples.text: She showed her album to me.
examples.translation: 她給我看她的相簿。

examples.translation: 湯姆買了新專輯。

examples.text: Will you show me your photo album?
examples.translation: 你能讓我看看你的相簿嗎？

examples.text: He showed me his photograph album.
examples.translation: 他給我看了他的影集。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin album (“blank white writing tablet”), from albus (“white”).

senses.definition: A playing card.

A resource or argument, used to achieve a purpose. (See play the something card.)
Any flat, normally rectangular piece of stiff paper, plastic, etc.
Any of a set of pages or forms that the user can navigate between, and fill with data, in certain user interfaces.
A greeting card.
A business card.

A test card.
In formal debating, a verbatim citation used as evidence for a point.
A perforated pasteboard or sheet-metal plate for warp threads, making part of the Jacquard apparatus of a loom.
A graph formed from a given graph by deleting one vertex.
An indicator card.
A bank card.
Any electronic payment (rather than a cash payment using notes, bills or coins).
Paper that is thicker and more durable than normal writing or printing paper, but thinner and more flexible than paperboard, used for postcards, playing cards, etc.; card stock.
An amusing or entertaining person, often slightly eccentric.

A tabular presentation of the key statistics of an innings or match: batsmen’s scores and how they were dismissed, extras, total score and bowling figures.
A removable electronic device that may be inserted into a powered electronic device to provide additional capability.
senses.native: 可插入電子裝置以擴充功能的可拆卸元件（卡）

examples.text: Please shuffle the cards carefully.

examples.text: Playing cards is very interesting.
examples.translation: 打牌很有意思。

examples.text: George sent me a birthday card.
examples.translation: 喬治給我寄了一張生日卡片。

examples.text: Look, this is my business card.
examples.translation: 看，這是我的名片。

examples.text: They eat sunflower seeds while playing cards.
examples.translation: 他們一邊嗑香瓜子，一邊打牌。

examples.text: Tom sent Christmas cards to all his friends.
examples.translation: 湯姆將聖誕節賀卡送給所有的朋友們。

etymology.native: 源自中古英語 carde（紙牌），來自舊法式 carte，再來自拉丁語 charta，最終源於古希臘 χάρτης（khártēs，「紙張、莎草紙」）。與 carte 和 chart 同源。

senses.definition: A writing consisting of multiple glyphs, characters, symbols or sentences.
A verse or passage of Scripture, especially one chosen as the subject of a sermon, or in proof of a doctrine.
A book, tome or other set of writings.
Anything chosen as the subject of an argument, literary composition, etc.
senses.native: 論述、文學作品等的主題

senses.native: 可解讀為人類可讀文字之資料

senses.definition: A style of writing in large characters; also, a kind of type used in printing.
senses.native: 大字的書寫風格；亦指印刷用字體之一種

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Tom sent me an interesting text.
examples.translation: 湯姆給我發了一條有趣的簡訊。

examples.text: Do we already have that text?
examples.translation: 我們已經有那篇課文了嗎？

examples.text: She sent a text.
examples.translation: 她發了一條簡訊。

examples.text: Please use British English in your text.
examples.translation: 請你這篇文章用英式英語。

examples.translation: 說話就如過眼雲煙，文字卻能流傳千古。

examples.translation: 沒有上下文就沒有詞義。

etymology.text: From Middle English text, from Old French texte, from Medieval Latin textus, from Latin textus (“style or texture of a work”), perfect passive participle of texō (“to weave”). Cognate to texture.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 text，來自舊法語 texte，來自中世紀拉丁語 textus，來自拉丁語 textus（作品之風格或紋理），texō（編織）的完成被動分詞。與 texture 同源。”},{

senses.definition: A three-dimensional measure of space that comprises a length, a width and a height. It is measured in units of cubic centimeters in metric, cubic inches or cubic feet in English measurement.
Strength of sound: how loud it is.
The issues of a periodical over a period of one year.
A bound book.
A single book of a publication issued in multi-book format, such as an encyclopedia.
A great amount (of meaning) about something.
Quantity.
A rounded mass or convolution.
The total supply of money in circulation or, less frequently, total amount of credit extended, within a specified national market or worldwide.
An accessible storage area with a single file system, typically resident on a single partition of a hard disk.
A modular foothold attached to a climbing wall used for gripping, often in triangular, pyramidal, or angular shapes.
The sum of the degrees of a set of vertices.

A green/blue-screen chromakey visual effects (“VFX”) sound stage surrounded by a multitude of filming cameras, to allow for virtual camera changes in post production, by filming the whole 3-D volume of a chromakey film set.

A sound stage film set that has walls of video monitors, substituting for an actual background, set structures, providing a changeable video matte painting. A set with a form of projected background, similar to legacy traditional rear projection and front projection sets.
A roll or scroll, which was the form of ancient books.
The total of weight worked by a muscle in one training session, the weight of every single repetition summed up.
senses.native: 一次訓練中，肌肉所舉起的總重量（每組每次重量的總和）（訓練量）

examples.text: This library has more than 50,000 volumes.

examples.translation: 音量調節在哪裡？

examples.text: What's the largest lake in Algeria by volume?

etymology.text: From Middle English volume, from Old French volume, from Latin volūmen (“book, roll”), from volvō (“roll, turn about”).

senses.definition: An original or official paper used as the basis, proof, or support of anything else, including any writing, book, or other instrument conveying information pertinent to such proof or support.
A file that contains text.
Any material substance on which the information is represented by writing.
senses.native: 文件，以文字記錄資訊的實體材料

senses.definition: An object conveying information by whatever means, capable of being indexed alongside other similar objects.
senses.native: 資料，以任何方式傳遞資訊、可與同類物件一併索引的物件

senses.definition: That which is taught or authoritatively set forth; precept; instruction; dogma.

senses.native: 借鏡，用來教導或警示的實例

examples.text: Tom translated the document into French.
examples.translation: 湯姆把文件譯成法語。

examples.text: I signed the document.
examples.translation: 我簽了文件。

examples.text: Where should these documents be submitted?
examples.translation: 這些文件應該提交到哪裡？

examples.text: This is the pen that he signed the document with.
examples.translation: 這就是他用來簽署那份文件的筆了。

senses.definition: A roll of paper or parchment; a writing formed into a roll.
An ornament formed of undulations giving off spirals or sprays, usually suggestive of plant form. Roman architectural ornament is largely of some scroll pattern.
Spirals or sprays in the shape of an actual plant.
A mark or flourish added to a person's signature, intended to represent a seal, and in some States allowed as a substitute for a seal. [U.S.] Alexander Mansfield Burrill.
The carved end of a violin, viola, cello or other stringed instrument, most commonly scroll-shaped but occasionally in the form of a human or animal head.
A skew surface.
A kind of sweet roll baked in a somewhat spiral shape.
The incremental movement of graphics on a screen, removing one portion to show the next.
A spiral waterway placed round a turbine to regulate the flow.
A turbinate bone.
The act of scrolling.
A rough draft of anything.

examples.text: Some of the best scrolls contain unicorns and space.
Archaeologists found a papyrus scroll in the ruins.
Scroll compressors consist of two scrolls to pressurize refrigerant.
I ordered a glass of lemonade and a coffee scroll.
I gave the terms and conditions a quick scroll before signing up to the website.

etymology.text: From Middle English scrowle, scrolle, from earlier scrowe, scrouwe (influenced by Middle English rolle), from Old French escroe, escrowe, escrouwe (“scroll, strip of parchment”), from Frankish *skrōda (“a shred”), from Proto-Germanic *skraudō, from *skrew- (“to cut; cutting tool”), extension of *(s)ker- (“to cut”). Doublet of shred and escrow.

Cognate with Scots landskape, landskep, landskip (“landscape”), West Frisian lânskip (“landscape”), Low German landschop (“l
etymology.native: 此詞源自荷蘭語 landschap 的變體，而 landschap 又來自中世紀荷蘭語 landscap、lantscap，源自古荷蘭語 *landskepi、*landskapi，意為「地區、區域」；亦可追溯至古英語 landsċipe、landsċeap，意為「地區、區域」；在部分語義上亦與蘇格蘭語 landskape、landskep、landskip、弗里斯蘭語 lânskip、低德語 landschop 相關。

senses.definition: A telecommunication device which converts data or sounds (usually speech) into electrical signals which are then transmitted to enable two or more people to communicate with each other over a distance; now usually a device having a dial or keypad with numerals for entering a number, etc., to connect with a person, and means (such as a sound or vibration) for alerting one to an incoming call or transmission; also, the handset or receiver of such a device.
A means of communicating information from one person to another or others.

Synonym of Chinese whispers (“a game for several players in which a phrase, whispered by each person in turn to their neighbour, is often unwittingly misunderstood as it is transferred, to humorous effect by the time it reaches the last person and is compared with the original phrase; (figurative) a situation where something is changed or misunderstood as a result of passing through successive people or processes”).
Now chiefly preceded by a descriptive word: a simple communication device which converts sounds (usually speech) into mechanical vibrations along a string, wire, etc.
A type of foghorn used for sending signals in the form of loud tones or musical notes, especially one invented in the 19th century by John Taylor, a captain in the British Royal Navy.

A communication device consisting of two aligned gutta-percha speaking tubes connected to parabolic reflectors which allows speech spoken into one tube to be sent through the air to the other one, invented in the 19th century by the British engineer Francis Whishaw (1804–1856); also, a speaking tube of such a device.
A system of communication using musical notes, also known as Solresol, invented in 1828 by the French composer Jean-François Sudre (1787–1862).

etymology.text: The noun is derived from tele- (prefix meaning ‘from a distance’) + -phone (suffix denoting a device which makes a sound), modelled after German Telephon (“early apparatus converting sound into electrical signals”) (dated) (now German Telefon). The word was first used to refer to the modern device in 1876 by the Scottish-born Canadian-American engineer Alexander Graham Bell (1847–1922).
etymology.native: 這個名詞源自 tele-（表示「從遠處」的前綴）＋ -phone（表示「發出聲音的裝置」的後綴），仿照德語 Telephon（「早期將聲音轉換為電信號的裝置」）（舊用語）（現為德語 Telefon）。1876年，蘇格蘭出生的加拿大裔美國工程師亞歷山大·格雷厄姆·貝爾（1847–1922）首次用此詞指稱現代裝置。

etymology.native: 「香蕉」來自葡萄牙語或西班牙語的 banana，源自西非剛果語族中幾內亞地區的語言，具體來源不明。可能的祖先或同源語言包括 Wolof 的 banaana、東部 Maninkakan 的 banana，以及 Vai 的 ꕒꘌꕯ (ɓaana) 或 ꕒꕌꕯ (ɓaana)，可能源自阿拉伯語 بَنَان (banān，意為「指尖、香蕉」)。然而，Ay Baati Wolof（Munro & Gaye, 1997）認為 Wolof 的 banaana 本身源自葡萄牙語的 banana。

etymology.text: First appears c. 1655, in the English translation Álvaro Semedo’s writings. From Dutch thee, from Hokkien 茶 (tê) (Amoy dialect), from Old Chinese, ultimately from Proto-Sino-Tibetan *s-la (「leaf, tea」). Introduced to English and other Western European languages by the Dutch East India Company, who sourced their tea in Amoy; compare Malay teh along the same trade route. Doublet of chai and cha (and, distantly, the first element of lahpet), from same Proto-Sino-Tibetan root; see discussion of cogn
etymology.native: 最早出現於1655年左右，源自荷蘭人譯本Álvaro Semedo的著作。來自荷蘭語thee，源自 Hokkien 茶（tê）（同安腔），源自古漢語，最終源自原始漢藏語 *s-la（「葉，茶」）。由荷蘭東印度公司引入英文及其他西歐語言，他們從同安供應茶葉；可與馬來語teh 比較，沿同一貿易路線。與chai及cha為同源詞（且遠源與lahpet之首字同源），詳見相關詞源討論。

To move the camera lens angle while continuing to expose the film, enabling a contiguous view and enrichment of context. The resulting image may extend a short distance laterally or as great as 360° from the point where the film first began to be exposed.
senses.native: 攝影機鏡頭角度移動的同時持續曝光，以取得連續畫面（橫搖；靜態合照時鏡頭或底片架橫向移動，成像可延伸至最遠 360°）

senses.definition: To clean with water.
To carry away or erode by the force of water in motion.
To be eroded or carried away by the action of water.
To clean oneself with water.
To cover with water or any liquid; to wet; to fall on and moisten.
To move with a lapping or swashing sound; to lap or splash.

To pass or extract (a gas or gaseous mixture) through or over a liquid for the purpose of purifying it, especially by removing soluble constituents.
To separate valuable material (such as gold) from worthless material by the action of flowing water.
To cause dephosphorization of (molten pig iron) by adding substances containing iron oxide, and sometimes manganese oxide.
To mix up tiles (before a new game) to make them random; to shuffle.

examples.text: She is going to wash the bike this afternoon.

senses.definition: A flat-bottomed vessel (usually metal) used for cooking food, possibly excluding saucepans (see usage notes).

Any of various traditional units of volume notionally based on the capacity of a pot.
An iron hat with a broad brim worn as a helmet.
A pot-shaped non-conducting (usually ceramic) stand that supports an electrified rail while insulating it from the ground.

That which happens without human design or forethought.
Anything (as a die, pebble, ball, or slip of paper) used in determining a question by chance, or without human choice or will.
The part, or fate, that falls to one, as it were, by chance, or without one's planning.

Allotment; lottery.
All members of a set; everything.
An old unit of weight used in many European countries from the Middle Ages, often defined as 1/30 or 1/32 of a (local) pound.

etymology.text: From Middle English del, dele, from Old English dǣl (“part, share, portion”), from Proto-West Germanic *daili, from Proto-Germanic *dailiz (“part, deal”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰ(h₁)-oy-lo- (“part, watershed”). Cognate with Scots dele (“part, portion”), West Frisian diel (“part, share”), Dutch deel (“part, share, portion”), German Teil (“part, portion, section”), Danish, Slovene, and Swedish del (“part”), Icelandic deila (“division, contention”), Gothic 𐌳𐌰𐌹𐌻𐍃 (dails, “portion”). Related to

A large quantity; a sum.
Bulk; magnitude; body; size.
The principal part; the main body.

Usually regarded as a borrowing of Late Latin catīllus (“small bowl”), diminutive of Latin catinus (“deep bowl, vessel for cooking up or serving food”), however, the word may be Germanic confused with the Latin: compare Old English cete (“cooking pot”)
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 ketel，亦作 chetel，來自古英語 ċietel（「鍋、大鍋」），中古英語時可能受古諾斯語 ketill 影響，皆源自原始日耳曼語 *katilaz（「鍋、桶、容器」），起源與構成不明。通常認為是拉丁語 catīllus（「小碗」）的借詞，此詞為拉丁語 catinus（「深碗、烹煮或盛食之器」）之縮小形，但此詞也可能因德語與拉丁語混淆而產生；可參照古英語 cete（「烹煮鍋」）

etymology.native: 源自中古英語（nere、ner），來自古英語（nēar）「較近」，是（nēah）「近」的比較級（最高級後來成為 next），受古諾斯語（nær）「近」影響，兩者均源自原始日耳曼語（*nēhwiz）「較近」，最終來自原始印歐語（*h₂neḱ-）「到達」。

etymology.text: First attested in c. 1646 in a publication by Thomas Browne. From New Latin ēlectricus (“electrical; of amber”), from ēlectr(um) (“amber”) + -icus (“adjectival suffix”); from Ancient Greek ἤλεκτρον (ḗlektron, “amber”); related to ἠλέκτωρ (ēléktōr, “shining sun”), of unknown origin (see which for more). The Latin term was apparently used first with the sense electrical in 1600 by the English physician and scientist William Gilbert in his work De Magnete.

"Main" refers to the mainmast, whereas a truck on another mast may be called (on the mizzenmast, for example) "mizzen-truck".

examples.translation: 人固有一死。

examples.text: Tatoeba: Let the 'mortal translation' begin!
examples.translation: Tatoeba：讓「致命翻譯」開始吧！

examples.text: We know that all men are mortal.
examples.translation: 我們知道人皆難免一死。

examples.text: How can you, a mere mortal, dare criticise Tom?
examples.translation: 你如何敢於，身為一個凡夫俗子，批評 Tom？

etymology.text: From Middle English mortal, mortel, from Old French mortal, and their source Latin mortālis, from mors (“death”). In this sense, displaced native deadly, from Old English dēadlīċ.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 mortal 或 mortel，來自舊法語的 mortal，其根源為拉丁語 mortālis，源自 mors（死亡）。在此意義上，取代了本土的 deadly，來自古英語 dēadlīċ。

senses.definition: A large or dense piece of something.
An attractive man, especially one who is muscular.
senses.native: 一位有魅力的男子，特別是指肌肉結實者

senses.definition: A record of differences between almost contiguous portions of two files (or other sources of information). Differences that are widely separated by areas which are identical in both files would not be part of a single hunk. Differences that are separated by small regions which are identical in both files may comprise a single hunk. Patches are made up of hunks.
senses.native: 兩個幾乎相鄰的文件（或其他資訊來源）之間差異的記錄。若兩文件間存在大量相同區域，則相隔甚遠的差異不會屬於同一塊；若相隔區域較小且內容相同，則可能構成單一區塊。修補檔由多個區塊組成

senses.definition: A honyock.
A material object considered purely as extended stuff without identity criteria.
senses.native: 僅視為具有延展性的物質，而不考慮其身份標準的實體物件

senses.definition: A goal or base in children's games.
senses.native: 兒童遊戲中的目標或基地

examples.text: The teacher gave us a large hunk of bread to share.
examples.translation: 老師給我們一大片麵包分享。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: That dense hunk of fog obscured the distant mountain peaks.
examples.translation: 那團濃密的霧氣遮擋了遠處的山巒。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: You're a hunk.
examples.translation: 你真是個帥哥。

examples.text: Tom is a hunk.
examples.translation: 湯姆是個帥哥。

examples.text: He's a hunk.
examples.translation: 他真帥氣。

examples.text: We won't get very far with this hunk of junk.
examples.translation: 我們拿這堆破東西是辦不到什麼大事的。

etymology.text: Probably borrowed from West Flemish hunke (“hunk; chunk”), of obscure origin. Probably from an earlier *humke, *humpke, a diminutive related to Dutch homp (“hunk; lump”), English hump, equivalent to hump + -kin. The sense of an attractive man is recorded in Australian slang in 1941, in jive talk in 1945.
etymology.native: 可能源自西弗蘭芒語的 hunke（意為「塊狀物；碎塊」），其起源不明確。可能來自更早的 *humke 或 *humpke，這是與荷蘭語 homp（意為「塊狀物；疙瘩」）、英語 hump 相關的貶稱詞，相當於 hump + -kin。形容有魅力的男子一義始見於 1941 年的澳洲俚語，至 1945 年才出現在 jive talk 中。

senses.definition: To extend beyond a surface.
To cast (an image or shadow) upon a surface; to throw or cast forward; to shoot forth.
To make plans for; to forecast.
To extend (a protrusion or appendage) outward.
To present (oneself), to convey a certain impression, usually in a good way.
senses.native: 展現（自己）；給人某種印象

senses.definition: To assume qualities or mindsets in others based on one's own personality.
To change the projection (or coordinate system) of spatial data with another projection.
To draw straight lines from a fixed point through every point of any body or figure, and let these fall upon a surface so as to form the points of a new figure.
(of a neuron or group of neurons) to have axon(s) extending to and therefore able to influence a remote location
To cause (one's voice or words) to be heard at a great distance.
To speak or sing in such a way that one can be heard at a great distance.
senses.native: 大聲說或唱以讓遠處聽得到

senses.definition: To extend to reach a point.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Their common aim was to make the project successful.
examples.translation: 這些人共同的目標是把這個專案做成功。

examples.text: NASA has recently unveiled a new project.
examples.translation: 美國太空總署最近公布了一項新計畫。

examples.text: The Edinburgh Waterfront project could be about to change all that.
examples.translation: 愛丁堡的水邊地工程可能會把諸如此類的事情改變。

etymology.text: From Latin prōiectus, perfect passive participle of prōiciō (“throw forth, extend; expel”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語（prōiectus），是（prōiciō）「擲出、伸出、驅逐」的完成式被動分詞。

senses.definition: To grasp and pull with the fingers or fingernails.
To harvest a fruit or vegetable for consumption by removing it from the plant to which it is attached; to harvest an entire plant by removing it from the ground.
To steal; to pilfer.
To separate or open by means of a sharp point or points.
To screen.
To pull apart or away, especially with the fingers; to pluck.
To take up; especially, to gather from here and there; to collect; to bring together.
To remove something from somewhere with a pointed instrument, with the fingers, or with the teeth.
To decide upon, from a set of options; to select.
To seek (a fight or quarrel) where the opportunity arises.
To recognise the type of ball being bowled by a bowler by studying the position of the hand and arm as the ball is released.
To pluck the individual strings of a musical instrument or to play such an instrument.
To open (a lock) with a wire, lock pick, etc.
To eat slowly, sparingly, or by morsels; to nibble.
To do anything fastidiously or carefully, or by attending to small things; to select something with care.
To throw; to pitch.
To peck at, as a bird with its beak; to strike at with anything pointed; to act upon with a pointed instrument; to pierce; to prick, as with a pin.
To intercept a pass from the offense as a defensive player.

examples.text: The boy is picking yellow flowers.
examples.translation: 男孩在摘黃色的花。

examples.text: She picked flowers in the garden.
examples.translation: 她在花園裡摘花。

examples.text: The kids are picking flowers in the garden.
examples.translation: 孩子們正在花園裡摘花。

examples.text: The child has picked a hole in his new jumper.
examples.translation: 孩子的新毛衣上勾了一個洞。

examples.text: I've found a way to overcome my habit of always picking fault with others.
examples.translation: 我想辦法克服了對別人吹毛求疵的毛病。

examples.text: A well-used creel might better not be picked as a picnic hamper.
examples.translation: 用舊的魚簍最好別拿來當野餐籃。

etymology.text: From Middle English piken, picken, pikken, from Old English *piccian, *pīcian (attested in pīcung (“a pricking”)), and pīcan, pȳcan (“to pick, prick, pluck”), both from Proto-West Germanic *pikkōn, from Proto-Germanic *pikkōną (“to pick, peck, prick, knock”), from Proto-Indo-European *bew-, *bu- (“to make a dull, hollow sound”). Doublet of pitch and peck.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（piken、picken），來自古英語（*piccian、*pīcian）及（pīcan、pȳcan）「挑、刺、拔」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*pikkōną）「挑、啄、刺、敲」，最終來自原始印歐語（*bew-）「發出沉悶聲」。與（pitch）、（peck）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: To care for (someone requiring attention); specifically, of a doctor, nurse, etc.: to provide professional care to (someone).

To wait on (someone or their instructions) as an attendant, servant, etc.; also (specifically of a gentleman-in-waiting or lady-in-waiting to a member of royalty), to accompany (someone) in order to assist or wait upon them; to escort.
To be present at (an event or place) in order to take part in some action or proceedings; also, to regularly go to (an event or place).
To take action with respect to (someone, or something such as a concern, problem, or task); to deal with, to handle.
Of a (chiefly immaterial) thing: to be consequent to or present with (someone or something); to accompany.
Followed by to: to look after someone or something.
To be ready to wait upon someone or their instructions as an attendant, servant, etc.; also (followed by on or upon), to accompany someone in order to assist or wait upon them.
Followed by at: to go to and be present at a place for some purpose; also (obsolete), followed by on: to be present at and take part in an event.
Followed by to: to take action with respect to someone or something; to deal with.
Followed by on or upon: of a (chiefly immaterial) thing: to be consequent on or present with.
Often followed by to, upon, or with: to give consideration; to pay attention.
To look after (someone or something); to tend.
To listen to (something or someone).
To give consideration to (someone or something); to heed, to pay attention, to regard.
Followed by to or unto: to listen.
To look out or wait for (someone, or something such as a decision or event); to await.
To expect or look forward to (someone or something).
Of a thing: to be in store or lie in wait for (someone or something); to await.
To remain and wait; to abide.
Followed by for: to expect or look forward.

examples.text: You should've attended the meeting.
examples.translation: 你應該參加這個會議的。

examples.text: I attended the meeting yesterday.
examples.translation: 昨天我出席了會議。

examples.text: Many people attended his concert.
examples.translation: 很多人前來參加他的演唱會。

examples.text: Where do you attend high school?
examples.translation: 你在哪裡唸高中?

examples.text: How many different schools have you attended?
examples.translation: 你上了幾所學校？

examples.text: Children of six and above should attend school.
examples.translation: 六歲及以上的小孩應該上學。

etymology.text: From Middle English attenden, atenden (“to devote oneself (to a task, etc.); to pay attention to (something), to look after; to consider (something); to expect or look forward to (something); to intend to do (something); to help or serve (someone), attend upon; to take care of (something)”), from Old French atendre (“to await, wait for; to expect; to intend”), from Latin attendere, adtendere (“to pay attention to, attend; to direct or turn toward”), from ad- (“prefix meaning ‘to, towards’”) + te

senses.definition: To wait for.
To expect.
To be in store for; to be ready or in waiting for.
To serve or attend; to wait on, wait upon.
To watch, observe.
To wait; to stay in waiting.

examples.text: No one knew what awaited us.
examples.translation: 沒人知道等待我們的是什麼。

examples.text: I await updates.
examples.translation: 我等待更新。

examples.text: Dozens of letters are awaiting you.
No one knows what awaits Boldi in the future.
Go over there, and await further instructions.
What punishment awaits him?
examples.translation: 他將面臨什麼樣的懲罰？

etymology.text: From Middle English awaiten, from Old Northern French awaitier (“to lie in wait for, watch, observe”), originally especially with a hostile sense; itself from a- (“to”) + waitier (“to watch”). More at English wait.

senses.definition: To lower into a liquid.
To immerse oneself; to become plunged in a liquid; to sink.
(of a value or rate) To decrease slightly.
To lower a light's beam.
senses.native: 降低（燈光）的光束（改用近光）

senses.definition: To lower (a flag), particularly a national ensign, to a partially hoisted position in order to render or to return a salute. While lowered, the flag is said to be “at the dip.” A flag being carried on a staff may be dipped by leaning it forward at an approximate angle of 45 degrees.
senses.native: 降下（旗幟，尤指國旗）致敬，升至半旗位置；此時稱旗幟「在致敬位置」

senses.definition: To treat cattle or sheep by immersion in chemical solution.
senses.native: 以化學藥液浸泡（牛或羊）以消毒或防治寄生蟲

senses.definition: To use a dip stick to check oil level in an engine.
senses.native: 以量油尺檢查引擎機油油位

senses.definition: To consume snuff by placing a pinch behind the lip or under the tongue in order to absorb the desired chemical constituents.
senses.native: 將鼻菸放在唇下或舌下吸收其成分

senses.definition: To immerse for baptism.
To wet, as if by immersing; to moisten.
To plunge or engage thoroughly in any affair.
senses.native: 全心投入或深入參與某事

senses.definition: To take out, by dipping a dipper, ladle, or other receptacle, into a fluid and removing a part; often with out.
senses.native: 以勺子或容器從液體中舀取部分；常與副詞連用（dip out）

senses.definition: To perform the action of plunging a dipper, ladle. etc. into a liquid or soft substance and removing a part.
To engage as a pledge; to mortgage.
To perform (a bow or curtsey) by inclining the body.
To sink, drop, or slope downwards.
To incline downward from the plane of the horizon.
To perform a dip dance move (often phrased with the leader as the subject noun and the follower as the subject noun being dipped)
To briefly lower the body by bending the knees while keeping the body in an upright position, usually in rhythm, as when singing or dancing.
To leave; to quit or abandon.

examples.text: The ball dipped and swerved unpredictably.
Tom likes dipping cookies in milk.
The children were skinny dipping.
He dipped his spoon into the soup.
examples.translation: 他把他的湯匙浸入湯裡。

examples.text: Tom dipped his french fries into the ketchup.
He dipped his head underwater to take a look.

etymology.text: From Middle English dippen, from Old English dyppan, from Proto-West Germanic *duppjan, from Proto-Germanic *dupjaną; see *daupijaną (“to dip”). Related to deep.

senses.definition: To fall away gradually; to subside.
To fall or pass from one proprietor to another, or from the original destination, by the omission, negligence, or failure of somebody, such as a patron or legatee.
To fall into error or heresy.
To slip into a bad habit that one is trying to avoid.
senses.native: 滑入試圖避免的不良習慣

senses.definition: To become void.

examples.text: Tom lapsed into silence.
examples.translation: 湯姆陷入了沉默。

examples.text: He lapsed into despair after that accident.
examples.translation: 那場事故後，他陷入了絕望。

examples.text: Tom began to lapse in and out of consciousness.
examples.translation: 湯姆開始意識清醒與昏迷之間交替。

examples.text: Tom lapsed into a coma and didn't regain consciousness.
examples.translation: 湯姆陷入了昏迷，未能恢復意識。

examples.text: The correspondence lapsed.
examples.translation: 通訊中斷了。

etymology.text: From Middle French laps, from Latin lāpsus, from lābī (“to slip”). Doublet of lapsus.
etymology.native: 源於中古法語 laps，來自拉丁語 lāpsus，意為「滑動」。與 lapsus 同源詞。

senses.definition: A hollow or pit into which liquid drains, such as a cesspool, cesspit or sink.
The lowest part of a mineshaft into which water drains.
senses.native: 礦坑的最低處，水會在此匯集

senses.definition: A completely flooded cave passage, sometimes passable by diving.
senses.native: 完全被水淹沒的洞穴通道，有時可潛水通行

senses.definition: The crankcase or oil reservoir of an internal combustion engine.
senses.native: 內燃機的曲軸箱或油槽

senses.definition: The pit at the lowest point in a circulating or drainage system (FM 55-501).
senses.native: 循環或排水系統中最低點的坑洞（FM 55-501）

senses.definition: An intentional depression around a drain or scupper that promotes drainage.
senses.native: 排水口或溢流口周圍有意設計的凹陷，促進排水

senses.definition: A sudden or heavy fall of rain; a deluge.
senses.native: 突發性或強烈的降雨；傾盆大雨

examples.text: Architects designed a complex sump network to handle peak storm runoff.
examples.translation: 建築師設計了複雜的水坑網路，以處理高峰期的暴雨徑流。

examples.text: The derelict sump, long abandoned by civilization, now serves as a breeding ground for mold.

relations.native: 廢棄物堆放處；焚化灰場；垃圾填埋場

etymology.text: From Middle English sompe, either from Middle Dutch somp, sump or Middle Low German sump from Old Saxon *sump, from Proto-West Germanic *sump, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *sumpaz. Doublet of swamp.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 sompe，可能來自中古荷蘭語 somp 或中低地德語 sump，最終源自原始日耳曼語 *sumpaz，與 swamp 同源。

senses.definition: To bring down the size, quantity, quality, value or intensity of something; to diminish, to lower.
To add electrons / hydrogen or to remove oxygen.
To convert to written form. (Usage note: this verb almost always appears as “reduce to writing”.)
To perform a reduction; to restore a fracture or dislocation to the correct alignment.
To reform a line or column from (a square).
To strike off the payroll.
To annul by legal means.
To pronounce (a sound or word) with less effort.
To lose weight.
To bring to an inferior rank; to degrade, to demote.
To humble; to conquer; to subdue; to capture.
To bring to an inferior state or condition.
To be forced by circumstances (into something one considers unworthy).
To decrease the liquid content of (a food) by boiling much of its water off.
To produce metal from ore by removing nonmetallic elements in a smelter.
To simplify an equation or formula without changing its value.
To express the solution of a problem in terms of another (known) algorithm.
To convert a syllogism to a clearer or simpler form.
senses.native: （邏輯）把三段論化為更簡單的形式

senses.definition: To translate (a book, document, etc.).

examples.text: The snow was reducing visibility.
examples.translation: 大雪降低了能見度。

examples.text: Our school was reduced to ashes.
examples.translation: 我們的學校被燒成了灰燼。

examples.text: Algeria needs to massively reduce tariffs.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞需要大幅削減關稅。

examples.text: The big fire reduced the whole town to ashes.
examples.translation: 那場大火把整個小鎮燒成了灰燼。

examples.text: I have to reduce my expenses this month.
examples.translation: 我這個月要減少開支。

examples.text: The fire reduced the house to ashes.
examples.translation: 房子被大火燒成了灰燼。

etymology.text: From Middle English reducen, from Old French reduire, from Latin redūcō (“reduce”); from re- (“back”) + dūcō (“lead”). See duke, and compare with redoubt.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（reducen），來自古法語（reduire），再源自拉丁語（redūcō）「帶回、減少」，由（re-）「回」加（dūcō）「引導」組成。參見（duke），並比較（redoubt）。

senses.definition: To die.
To lapse and become invalid.
To come to an end; to conclude.
To exhale; to breathe out.
To give forth insensibly or gently, as a fluid or vapour; to emit in minute particles.
To bring to a close; to terminate.
To cause to lapse; to invalidate.

examples.text: The card expires in January of 2006.
Your vacation days have expired.
Tom's library card is expired.
My ID card has expired, what should I do?
examples.translation: 我的身份證過期了，我該怎麼辦？

examples.text: Your driver's license has expired.
examples.translation: 你的駕駛執照已經過期了。

examples.text: Tom's driver's license will expire next month.

etymology.text: From Middle English expire, from Middle French expirer, from Latin expīrō, exspīrō, from ex- (“out”) + spīrō (“breathe, be alive”).

senses.definition: A small amount of something.
A piece of metal placed in a horse's mouth and connected to the reins to direct the animal.
A unit of currency worth one eighth of a dollar, originally of a Spanish dollar but later also US or Canadian; also, a coin with this value, in particular the silver Spanish real.
Synonym of microbitcoin.
A portion of something.
Somewhat; something, but not very great; also used like jot and whit to express the smallest degree. See also a bit.
A replaceable tip for a hand tool or power tool, comprising the portion that drives a fastener.
An excerpt of material making up part of a show, comedy routine, etc.
The part of a key which enters the lock and acts upon the bolt and tumblers.
The cutting iron of a plane.
The bevelled front edge of an axehead along which the cutting edge runs.
A gag of a style similar to a bridle.
A rotary cutting tool, fitted to a drill, brace, or router, used to bore or drill holes or to remove material from the profile of the workpiece.

A unit of currency and coin of the British West Indies worth six black dogs, originally equal to one-eighth of a Spanish dollar but later increasingly debased to one tenth, one eleventh, one twelfth, etc.
senses.native: 英屬西印度群島的貨幣單位及硬幣

senses.definition: A unit of currency of the Dutch West Indies in the early 20th century, worth one fifth of a cent.
senses.native: 二十世紀初荷屬西印度群島的貨幣單位，值五分之一分

senses.definition: Specifically, a small amount of time.
A small fraction above a whole number.
Fractions of a second.
A prison sentence, especially a short one.
A gag or put-on; a humorous conceit, especially when insistently presented as true.

examples.text: He collected bits of information.
examples.translation: 他收集了一些訊息。

examples.text: I know a bit about calligraphy.
examples.translation: 我對書法略知一二。

examples.text: Tom's dog bit him playfully.
examples.translation: 湯姆的狗咬他玩。

examples.text: Tom tore the ticket to bits.
