examples.text: I'll open the window a bit.
examples.translation: 我把窗戶開啟一點。

examples.text: You've got a bit of a fever today, don't you?
examples.translation: 你今天有點發燒，是吧？

etymology.text: From Middle English bitte, bite, from Old English bita (“bit; fragment; morsel”) and bite (“a bite; cut”), from Proto-Germanic *bitô and *bitiz; both from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeyd- (“to split”). More at bite.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（bitte、bite），來自古英語（bita）「一點；碎片；一口」與（bite）「咬；切口」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語，最終來自原始印歐語（*bʰeyd-）「劈開」。參見（bite）。

senses.definition: An allocated amount.
That which is divided off or separated, as a part from a whole; a separated part of anything.
One's fate; lot.
The part of an estate given or falling to a child or heir; an inheritance.
A wife's fortune; a dowry.

examples.text: The portions are ginormous.
examples.translation: 這些份量太大了

examples.text: I swallowed a portion of couscous.
We have small and large portions.
He finished the steak, then ordered another portion.
examples.translation: 他吃完排骨又點了一份。

examples.text: Mary bought a large portion of a cream tart.
He complained about getting a small portion.

etymology.text: English portion From Middle English porcioun, borrowed from Old French porcion, accusative of Latin portiōnem (“a share, part, portion, relation, proportion”), from portiō, akin to pars (“part”); see part. Compare proportion.

senses.definition: Something which clips or grasps; a device for attaching one object to another.
An unspecified, but normally understood as rapid, speed or pace.
A frame containing a number of rounds of ammunition which is intended to be inserted into an internal magazine of a firearm to allow for rapid reloading.
A projecting flange on the upper edge of a horseshoe, turned up so as to embrace the lower part of the hoof; a toe clip or beak.
A gaff or hook for landing the fish, as in salmon fishing.
A removable magazine of a firearm.
Something which has been clipped from a larger whole
The product of a single shearing of sheep.
A season's crop of wool.
A section of video taken from a film, broadcast, or other longer video.
A short piece of audio (shortened version of audio clip, or alternatively clipping of audio).
A newspaper clipping.
An act of clipping, such as a haircut.
The condition of something, its state.
A blow with the hand (often in the set phrase clip round the ear)
An embrace.

examples.text: Tap on a clip to paste it in the text box.
The video clip contains images from the fairy tale movie.
How can I extract the audio from a video clip?
Jonas found a paper clip under his desk.
A note was attached to the document with a paper clip.
This clip runs viral in Twitter.

etymology.text: From Middle English clippen, cleppen, clüppen, from Old English clyppan (“to hug, embrace, cherish, clasp”), from Proto-Germanic *klumpijaną, from Proto-Indo-European *glemb-, *glembʰ- (“lump, clump, clod, clamp”). Cognate with Old Frisian kleppa, klippa (“to hug, embrace”), Middle High German klimpen, klimpfen (“to contract tightly, constrict, squeeze”).

senses.definition: A part broken off; a small, detached portion; an imperfect part, either physically or not.
A sentence not containing a subject or a predicate; a sentence fragment.
senses.native: 主詞或謂語皆缺失的句子；句子片段

senses.definition: An incomplete portion of code.
senses.native: 程式碼中不完整的一段

senses.definition: A portion of a URL referring to a subordinate resource or anchor (such as a specific point on a web page), introduced by the # sign.
senses.native: 網址中指向從屬資源或錨點（如網頁特定位置）的部分，以「#」符號引入

senses.definition: A split piece of an organism that has undergone the asexual reproduction process where the organism splits into one or more pieces, then those pieces become new individuals.
senses.native: 生物體經過無性繁殖分裂成一個或多個部分，這些部分再變成新個體的片段

examples.text: The vase broke into fragments.
I can only remember fragments.
Donald went to clean up the mirror fragments.
examples.translation: 唐納德去清理鏡子碎片。

examples.text: It's hard to splice the two fragments together.
Fragments of the mirror were scattered on the floor.
A few fragments of dead leaves floated on the pond.
examples.translation: 池塘裡漂浮著零星的幾片落葉。

relations.native: 由碎片組成；斷裂的；散亂的

etymology.text: From Late Middle English fragment, from Latin fragmentum (“a fragment, remnant”), from frangō (“to break”) + -mentum.

senses.definition: A loose filmy mass or a thin chiplike layer of anything
A scale of a fish or similar animal
A prehistoric tool chipped out of stone.
A person who is impractical, flighty, unreliable, or inconsistent; especially with maintaining a living.
A carnation with only two colours in the flower, the petals having large stripes.
A flat turn or tier of rope.
A corrupt arrest, e.g. to extort money for release or merely to fulfil a quota.
A wire rack for drying fish.
Dogfish.
The meat of the gummy shark.
A platform of hurdles, or small sticks made fast or interwoven, supported by stanchions, for drying codfish and other things.
A small stage hung over a vessel's side, for workmen to stand on while calking, etc.
A paling; a hurdle.

examples.text: It's a flake covered in chocolate!
examples.translation: 這是一塊沾滿巧克力的脆片！

examples.text: Tom likes corn chips, but hates corn flakes.
examples.translation: 湯姆喜歡玉米片，卻討厭玉米脆片。

examples.text: Corn flakes and milk certainly go well together.
examples.translation: 玉米脆片配牛奶，搭配得非常完美。

examples.text: Dandruff is made of small flakes of dead skin.
examples.translation: 頭皮屑是由脫落的死皮細小碎片組成。

examples.text: He can finish ten boxes of corn flakes in one sitting.
examples.translation: 他一次能吃完十盒玉米脆片。

examples.text: He likes to sprinkle coconut flakes on top of his cupcakes.
examples.translation: 他喜歡在紙杯蛋糕上撒椰子脆片。

etymology.text: From Middle English flake (“a flake of snow”), from Old English flacca and/or Old Norse flak (“loose or torn piece”) (compare Old Norse flakna (“to flake or chip”)), from Proto-Germanic *flaką (“something flat”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat, broad, plain”). Cognate with Norwegian flak (“slice, sliver”, literally “piece torn off”), Swedish flak (“a thin slice”), Danish flage (“flake”), German Flocke (“flake”), Dutch vlak (“smooth surface, plain”) and vlok (“flake”), as well as with La
etymology.native: 「flake」源自中世英文 flake（雪片），來自古英語 flacca 和／或古諾斯語 flak（鬆散或撕裂的碎片），又源自原始日耳曼語 *flaką（扁平之物），再溯源自原始印歐語 *pleh₂-（平坦、寬廣）。與挪威語 flak（切片、薄片，字面為「撕下的碎片」）、瑞典語 flak（薄片）、丹麥語 flage（碎屑）、德語 Flocke（碎屑）、荷蘭語 vlak（平滑表面）及 vlok（碎屑）同源，亦與拉丁語相關。

senses.definition: A small part of something, such as a song or fabric; sample.
A text file containing a relatively small amount of code, useless by itself, along with instructions for inserting that code into a larger codebase.
senses.native: 一段包含少量程式碼的檔案，本身無用，但附有將該程式碼插入較大程式碼庫的說明

examples.text: She gave me a snippet of information which is top secret.
examples.translation: 她給我一段機密至極的資訊片段。

examples.text: I collect snippets of information from a variety of sources.
examples.translation: 我從各種來源收集資訊片段。

examples.text: And miraculously, he lifted his own violin and started playing, by ear, certain snippets of violin concertos.
examples.translation: 神蹟般地，他拿起自己的小提琴開始演奏，憑耳聽，彈奏某些小提琴協奏曲的片段。

examples.text: From the snippet I heard of their rehearsal, they sound pretty good.
examples.translation: 從我聽到的他們彩排片段來看，他們的聲音還不錯。

examples.text: This is just a tiny snippet of the whole song.
examples.translation: 這只是整首歌的一小段片段。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: She cut a small snippet from the old fabric.
examples.translation: 她從舊布料上剪下一小塊。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

relations.native: 浸在肉汁裡的一小塊烤麵包

etymology.text: From snip + -et. Compare snippock.
etymology.native: 由「剪」加上後綴「-et」組成。可與「snippock」相比。

senses.definition: The selection of one thing or person over others (with the main adposition being "for" in relation to the thing or person, but possibly also "of")
The option to so select, and the one selected.
The state of being preferred over others.
A strong liking or personal valuation.
A preferential bias; partiality; discrimination.
Preferans, a card game, principally played in Eastern Europe.

examples.text: It's a matter of personal preference.
Everyone has their own preferences.
I don't really have a preference.
My preferences are very dissimilar to yours.
It can be customized to suit your preferences.
Music preferences vary from person to person.

etymology.text: From Middle French preference, from Medieval Latin preferentia. Doublet of preferans. Morphologically prefer + -ence.

senses.definition: A taste, liking, or inclination for (something).
A card game resembling bezique.
senses.native: 類似貝齊克的紙牌遊戲

senses.definition: In the game of penchant, any queen and jack of different suits held at the same time.
senses.native: 在筆欽遊戲中，同時持有的不同花色的王后與傑克

examples.text: He has a penchant for fine wine.
examples.translation: 他非常喜愛優質葡萄酒。

examples.text: Women have a natural penchant for the mysterious.
examples.translation: 女性天生對神秘事物有著天然的興趣。

examples.text: He plays a wily detective with a penchant for disguises.
examples.translation: 他扮演一位擅長變裝的狡猾偵探。

examples.text: He has a penchant for whistling at pretty ladies he sees on the street.
examples.translation: 他喜歡在街上對漂亮女士吹口哨。

examples.text: The Irish have a penchant for blarney.
examples.translation: 愛爾蘭人擅長說花言巧語。

examples.text: I have a real penchant for collecting old stamps.
examples.translation: 我真的很喜歡收集舊郵票。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

relations.native: 易受影響的狀態；脆弱性

etymology.text: Unadapted borrowing from French penchant, present participle of pencher (“to tilt, to lean”), from Middle French, from Old French pengier (“to tilt, be out of line”), from Vulgar Latin *pendicāre, a derivative of Latin pendere (“to hang”).
etymology.native: 此詞源自法語筆欽，意為傾斜或倚靠，其源頭可追溯至古法語及拉丁語的「懸掛」之意。

senses.definition: To label (something).
To mark (something) with one's graffiti tag.
senses.native: 以塗鴉簽名（tag）標記某物（塗鴉）

senses.definition: To remove dung tags from a sheep.
senses.native: 去除羊隻身上的糞便結塊（剪糞尾）

senses.definition: To put a runner out by touching them with the ball or the ball in a gloved hand.
senses.native: 以球或持球的手套碰觸跑者，使其出局（觸殺）

senses.definition: To mark with a tag (metadata for classification).
senses.native: 以標籤（用於分類的元資料）標記

senses.definition: To attach the name of (a user) to a posted message so that they are linked from the post and possibly sent a notification.
senses.native: 在貼文中標註使用者名稱，使其與該貼文連結並可能收到通知（標記）

senses.definition: To follow closely, accompany, tag along.
To catch and touch (a player in the game of tag).
senses.native: （抓人遊戲中）抓到並碰觸（某位玩家）

senses.definition: To fit with, or as if with, a tag or tags.
senses.native: 為……裝上標籤（或類似標籤）

senses.definition: To fasten; to attach.
To repeat (the ending of a song); to play a tag
To hit the ball hard.
To make contact with an enemy, usually by attacking it before other players do, to establish exclusive or partial eligibility for loot, experience points achievements, etc.
to have sex with someone (especially a man of a woman)
senses.native: （俚，粗俗）與某人（尤指男性與女性）發生性行為

examples.text: Claudio tagged Isabella in a picture.
examples.translation: 克勞迪奧在照片中標記了伊莎貝拉。

examples.text: Are you sure you don't mind me tagging along?
examples.translation: 你確定不介意我跟著一起嗎？

examples.text: You should tag that sentence as ambiguous.
examples.translation: 你應該將該句子標記為有歧義。

examples.text: The snail tagged along with the turtle.
examples.translation: 田螺跟著烏龜一起前行。

examples.text: In the first paragraph, she describes the labels she was tagged with, which have a negative connotation.
examples.translation: 在第一段中，她描述了被她標記的標籤，這些標籤帶有負面含義。

etymology.text: From Middle English tagge (“small piece hanging from a garment”), probably of North Germanic origin. Compare Norwegian tagg (“point; prong; barb; tag”), Swedish tagg (“thorn; prickle; tine”), Icelandic tág (“a willow-twig”). Compare also tack.
etymology.native: 此詞源於中古英語的 tagge，意指掛在衣服上的小塊物體。

senses.definition: To hold by the end; said of a timber when it rests upon a wall or other support; with in or into
To swing with the stern in a certain direction; said of a vessel at anchor.
senses.native: （停泊的船）以船尾擺向某方向（擺船）

senses.definition: To follow or hang to, like a tail; to be attached closely to, as that which can not be evaded.
senses.native: 如尾巴般緊跟；緊緊黏著，無法擺脫

senses.definition: To follow and observe surreptitiously.
To pull or draw by the tail.

examples.text: I can't make head or tail of those directions.

etymology.text: From Middle English tail, taile, taille, tayil, tayl, tayle, tayll, teil, tæȝel, from Old English tæġel, tæġl (“tail”), from Proto-West Germanic *tagl, from Proto-Germanic *taglą (“hair, fiber; hair of a tail”), from Proto-Indo-European *doḱ- (“hair of the tail”), from Proto-Indo-European *deḱ- (“to tear, fray, shred”).

senses.definition: To cause someone to become annoyed or angry.
To bring about a reaction.
To appeal.

examples.text: Don't provoke me.
examples.translation: 別惹我了。

examples.text: Tom seems to enjoy provoking arguments.
This could provoke riots in Algeria.
It was his fault. He kept provoking everyone.
Don't let yourself be provoked into a fight.
The cat will scratch you if you provoke it.

relations.native: 持續不斷地騷擾、煩擾或使某人感到煩惱

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French provoquer, from Old French, from Latin prōvocāre. Doublet of provocate.

senses.definition: To provoke someone to do wrong, especially by promising a reward; to entice.
To attract; to allure.
To provoke something; to court.

examples.text: I didn't mean to tempt you.
examples.translation: 我沒想誘惑你。

examples.text: That sounds very tempting.
examples.translation: 聽起來很誘人

examples.text: The snake tempted Eve.
examples.translation: 蛇誘惑了夏娃。

examples.text: The sight of the money tempted him into stealing.
examples.translation: 看到這筆錢使他被誘惑偷東西。

examples.text: Can I tempt you to try another piece of cake?
I think Tom could've been tempted to do that.

etymology.text: From Middle English tempten, from Old French tempter (French: tenter), from Latin temptare, from tentare (“to handle, touch, try, test, tempt”), frequentative of tendere (“to stretch”). Displaced native English costning (“temptation”).

senses.definition: To detect with the senses, especially with the eyes.
To perceive, recognize, or comprehend with the mind; to descry.
senses.native: 心智感知、辨識或理解；詳察

senses.definition: To distinguish something as being different from something else; to differentiate or discriminate.
senses.native: 辨別某物與他物之不同；區分或鑑別

senses.definition: To perceive differences.

examples.text: He just talks; he doesn't discern.
examples.translation: 他只會說話，無法辨別。

examples.text: This man discerns well.
examples.translation: 此人辨識力極佳。

examples.text: It is hard to discern between true and false.
examples.translation: 分辨真偽頗為困難。

examples.text: He can't discern fact from fiction.
examples.translation: 他無法分辨事實與虛構。

examples.text: Carlos needs to discern reality from fiction.
examples.translation: 卡洛斯需辨別現實與虛構。

examples.text: Comedy too can sometimes discern what is right.
examples.translation: 喜劇有時也能辨明何者正確。

etymology.text: From Middle English discernen, from Old French discerner, from Latin discernere (“to separate, divide, distinguish, discern”), from dis- (“apart”) + cernere (“to distinguish”); see certain.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 discernen，來自舊法式 discerner，再源自拉丁語 discernere（分開、區分、辨識），由 dis-（分開）與 cernere（辨識）組成；參見 certain。

senses.definition: To spoil the appearance of.
To tarnish (reputation, character, etc.); to defame.
senses.native: 使（名譽、品格等）蒙汙；誣蔑

examples.text: Her beauty was blemished by the scar.
examples.translation: 她的美麗因那道傷疤而受損。

examples.text: Her face was blemished.
examples.translation: 她的臉上有瑕疵。

etymology.text: From Middle English blemisshen, blemissen, from Old French blemiss-, stem of Old French blemir, blesmir (“make pale, injure, wound, bruise”) (French blêmir), from Old Frankish *blesmijan, *blasmijan (“to make pale”), from Old Frankish *blasmī (“pale”), from Proto-Germanic *blasaz (“white, pale”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel- (“to shine”). Cognate with Dutch bles (“white spot”), German blass (“pale”), Old English āblered (“bare, uncovered, bald, shaven”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 blemisshen，來自舊法語 blemir（使變淡、傷害、受傷），再追溯至原始日耳曼語 *blasaz（白色、蒼白），最終源自原始印歐語 *bʰel-（發光）。

senses.definition: High in price; expensive.
Loved; lovable.
Lovely; kind.
Loving, affectionate, heartfelt
Precious to or greatly valued by someone.
A formal way to start (possibly after my) addressing somebody at the beginning of a letter, memo etc.
A formal way to start (often after my) addressing somebody one likes or regards kindly.
An ironic way to start (often after my) addressing an inferior or someone one dislikes.
Severe, or severely affected; sore.
Noble.
Fierce.

examples.text: You captivated me, dear.
examples.translation: 親愛的，你把我迷住了。

examples.text: Dog food is dear.
examples.translation: 狗糧很貴。

examples.text: My dear mother.
examples.translation: 我親愛的媽媽

examples.text: Dear Santa, I want a girlfriend for Christmas.
examples.translation: 聖誕老人，我想要一個女朋友當聖誕禮物。

examples.text: I was aided by a dear friend.
examples.translation: 我獲得了好友的幫助。

examples.text: I'm so glad to see you, dear.
examples.translation: 親愛的, 我很高興看到你。

etymology.text: From Middle English dere, from Old English dēore, dīere, dīore, dȳre (“of great value or excellence, expensive, beloved”), from Proto-West Germanic *diurī, from Proto-Germanic *diurijaz (“dear, precious; expensive”), probably from Proto-Indo-European *dʰegʷʰ- (“to burn; hot, warm”).

senses.definition: Ex-, former, previously but no longer.
My algebra II teacher's dad is an ex PE teacher at the same school.
the place the train originated from or called at prior to the present location.
expensive, dear

examples.text: It's too ex.

etymology.text: From Latin ex.

senses.definition: Having a high price or cost.
Taking a lot of system time or resources.
Having a high economy rate.
Given to expending a lot of money; profligate, lavish.

examples.text: The reporter rented an expensive room.
examples.translation: 記者租了間很貴的房。

examples.text: Vegetables are getting more expensive.
examples.translation: 蔬菜越來越貴了。

examples.text: These blueberries were too expensive.
examples.translation: 這兒的藍莓也太貴了。

examples.text: What she bought was very expensive.
examples.translation: 她買的東西很昂貴。

examples.text: She always buys expensive clothes.
examples.translation: 她總是買昂貴的衣服。

examples.text: Visiting a foreign country must be expensive.
examples.translation: 到外國一定很貴。

etymology.text: From Latin *expēnsīvus, from expendō (“to weigh out (money), to pay out”) (whence English expend). By surface analysis, expense + -ive. In the sense of "high-priced" has largely displaced dear.

senses.definition: To attest to (a fact) as the truth.
To authenticate or verify in writing.
To attest that a product, service, organization, or person has met an official standard.
To inform; to tell (a person) that something is true.
To assure (oneself) of something; to ascertain.

examples.text: This building is LEED Platinum certified.
Bruno is board certified in psychiatry.
examples.translation: 布魯諾是委員會認證的精神科專家。

examples.text: The check will be certified.
examples.translation: 我們會認證支票。

examples.text: The Canadian Million Dollar Coin was certified by the Guinness World Records as the world's largest gold coin.
Records certify that Bob passed his driving test.
But I have a note from a renowned psychiatrist certifying that my brain functions completely normally.

relations.native: 證明 所支款額超出存款額

etymology.text: From Old French certefier (“confirm, assure, make certain”). Compare French certifier.

senses.definition: The region which the eye overlooks at one time; a view; a scene; an outlook.
A picturesque or panoramic view; a landscape; hence, a sketch of a landscape.
A position affording a fine view; a lookout.
A relative position of the front of a building or other structure; a face; a relative aspect.
The act of looking forward; foresight; anticipation.
The potential things that may come to pass, often favorable.
A hope; a hopeful.
Any player whose rights are owned by a top-level professional team, but who has yet to play a game for said team.
A potential client or customer.
The façade of an organ.

examples.text: Tom sounded excited by the prospect.
The prospects aren't very bright.
The hotel has a good prospect.
This year's prospects are looking good so far.
I am excited at the prospect of seeing her.
I'm excited at the prospect of meeting Tom.

etymology.text: From Middle English prospecte, from Latin prōspectus (“view, sight, prospect; panorama”), from prōspiciō (“to look forward”) + -tus (suffix forming action nouns), from pro (“before, forward”) + speciō, spiciō (“to look, to see”). By surface analysis, pro- + -spect. Doublet of prospectus and prospekt. The verb is from the noun.

senses.definition: To thrive or grow well.
To be known to have been alive at a particular time or in a particular period, where one's birth and death dates are not known; to have been active during a specified period; floruit.
To prosper or fare well.
To be in a period of greatest influence.
To develop; to make thrive; to expand.
To make bold, sweeping movements with.
To make bold and sweeping, fanciful, or wanton movements, by way of ornament, parade, bravado, etc.; to play with fantastic and irregular motion.
senses.native: 做出大膽、華麗或任性的動作，作為裝飾、炫耀等；玩弄奇幻且不規則的動作

senses.definition: To use florid language; to indulge in rhetorical figures and lofty expressions.
senses.native: 使用華麗的文辭；沉溺於修辭手法和高遠的表達方式

senses.definition: To make ornamental strokes with the pen; to write graceful, decorative figures.
senses.native: 用筆寫出裝飾性的筆畫；寫出優雅、裝飾性的字體

senses.definition: To adorn with beautiful figures or rhetoric; to ornament with anything showy; to embellish.
senses.native: 以美麗的字句或修辭裝飾；以任何炫耀之物裝飾；美化

senses.definition: To execute an irregular or fanciful strain of music, by way of ornament or prelude.
senses.native: 演奏不規則或奇幻的樂曲，作為裝飾或前奏

senses.definition: To boast; to vaunt; to brag.
To brandish (a weapon).

examples.text: Mary really flourished after leaving Tom.
examples.translation: 瑪麗在離開湯姆後真的過得非常好。

examples.text: Your business is flourishing, I hear.
examples.translation: 聽聞你的生意興旺。

etymology.native: 源自中古英語（side），來自古英語（sīde）「側邊、腰側」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*sīdǭ）「側面、邊緣、岸」，可能最終來自原始印歐語（*seh₁-）「長的」。與荷蘭語（zijde）、德語（Seite）、瑞典語（sida）同源。

examples.text: Please replace the empty ink cartridge in the printer.
examples.translation: 請把印表機裡面的空的墨粉鼓換掉。

etymology.text: From Middle English ynke, from Old French enque, from Latin encaustum (“purple ink used by Roman emperors to sign documents”), from Ancient Greek ἔγκαυστον (énkauston, “burned-in”), from ἐν (en, “in”) + καίω (kaíō, “burn”). In this sense, displaced native Old English blæc (“ink”, literally “black”).

senses.definition: Of, belonging or relating to music, or to its performance or notation.
Pleasing to the ear; sounding agreeably; having the qualities of music; melodious; harmonious.
Fond of music; discriminating with regard to music; gifted or skilled in music.
Pertaining to a class of games in which players move while music plays, but have to take a fixed position when it stops; by extension, any situation where people repeatedly change positions.

examples.text: Can you play any musical instruments?
examples.translation: 你會樂器嗎?

examples.text: Some learned to play musical instruments.
What's your favorite Broadway musical?
Mozart: one of the great musical prodigies of all time.
examples.translation: 莫札特: 一個永遠的音樂奇才

examples.text: My favourite musical instrument is the electric guitar.
examples.translation: 我最喜歡的樂器是電吉他。

examples.text: Is mayonnaise a musical instrument?
examples.translation: 美乃滋是一種樂器嗎？

etymology.text: From Middle English musical, from Old French [Term?], from Medieval Latin mūsicālis, from Latin mūsica (“music”) + -ālis (suffix forming adjectives); equivalent to music + -al.

senses.definition: That can be disposed of.
That is designed to be discarded rather than reused, refilled or repaired.
Available to be used; at one's disposal.

examples.text: Volunteers distributed tea in disposable cups.
These microfiber towels are disposable.
His work was anything but disposable.
The call came from a disposable phone.
Tom was drinking coffee in a disposable styrofoam cup.
My disposable income is as low as it gets.

relations.native: 合意、合乎願望的、令人滿意的

etymology.text: From dispos(e) + -able.

senses.definition: A container.
The part of the flower stalk (peduncle or pedicel) to which the floral parts are attached; a thalamus, a torus.
senses.native: 花莖上附著花部的部位；花托或花梗

senses.definition: A condensed rachis of a capitate or umbellate inflorescence at the end of the peduncle, to which all of the florets or pedicels are attached.
senses.native: 頂生於花莖末端、所有小花或花梗均附著其上的縮短花軸

senses.definition: A structure at the end of a branch of an alga containing conceptacles (reproductive organs).
senses.native: 藻類枝條末端包含生殖器官（概念囊）的結構

senses.definition: An organ that receives and holds a secretion.
senses.native: 接收並儲存分泌物的器官

senses.definition: A contact device installed at an outlet for the connection of an attachment plug (typically by receiving the plug's prongs) to supply portable appliances or equipment.
senses.native: 安裝於插座以連接插頭（通常接收插腳）供電給可攜式設備的接觸裝置

examples.text: The eye socket is the bone receptacle in which the eye fits.
examples.translation: 眼窩是裝載眼球的花托骨。

examples.text: The waterskin is a sheepskin or goat skin sewn in the shape of a bag and serving as a receptacle.
examples.translation: 水囊是用羊皮或牛皮縫製成袋狀，作為容器的皮囊。

examples.text: Thus, one of the loveliest of earthly paradises was doomed to be a receptacle for the very worst of malefactors.
examples.translation: 因此，這世上最美麗的樂園之一，注定要成為最惡劣罪犯的收容所。

examples.text: Maria Montessori invented the sorting box after observing that children enjoy fitting objects through receptacles of a similar shape.
examples.translation: 瑪麗亞·蒙台梭利觀察到兒童喜歡將物件放入形狀相似的容器中後，發明了分類盒。

examples.text: The old vase served as a unique receptacle for flowers.
examples.translation: 那隻舊花瓶被用作存放花朵的獨特容器。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The antique urn functioned as an elegant receptacle for ceremonial offerings.
examples.translation: 那座古董壺被用作盛放儀式供品的優雅容器。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Middle English receptacle, from Anglo-Norman receptacle and Middle French receptacle (“organ containing a fluid; gathering place; water basin”) (modern French réceptacle), from Latin receptāculum (“animal enclosure, container, place of refuge, receptacle, repository, reservoir, shelter”), from receptāre (“to harbour, to receive, to shelter”) or receptō (“to receive back or again, to recover”), frequentative of recipiō (“to receive; to hold back, to reserve”) (from re- (“back, again”) + capi
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 receptacle，來自盎格魯諾曼語和中古法語（意為「含液體的器官；聚集處；水盆」），現代法語 réceptacle 則來自拉丁語 receptāculum。

senses.definition: That serves to decorate
That has no functional purpose.

examples.text: The bed is adorned with decorative pillows.
examples.translation: 床鋪上擺著裝飾性枕頭。

examples.text: In some cultures, antlers are used for decorative or ceremonial purposes.
examples.translation: 在某些文化中，鹿角被用於裝飾或儀式用途。

examples.text: There was a decorative pilaster to either side of the building's entrance.
examples.translation: 建築入口兩側各有一個裝飾性壁柱。

examples.text: To spice up the design, he added some decorative shapes with a dingbat font.
examples.translation: 為了增添設計感，他用了一種標點字體加入一些裝飾性圖形。

examples.text: Today Mary is wearing elegant decorative glasses.
examples.translation: 今天瑪麗戴著精緻的裝飾眼鏡。

examples.text: Tessellations have been used to create decorative motifs in both textiles and architecture since ancient times.
examples.translation: 自古以來，馬賽克圖案就被用於紡織品與建築的裝飾紋樣。

etymology.text: From Latin decorātus + -ive. Cognate with French décoratif.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 decorātus 加 -ive。與法語 décoratif 同源。

senses.definition: Imparting or improving beauty, particularly the beauty of the complexion.
External or superficial; pertaining only to the surface or appearance of something.

examples.text: Fortunately, the damage to the house was mostly cosmetic and a bit of paint covered it nicely.

relations.native: 裝飾性的、觀賞性的、觀賞的
裝飾性的、觀賞性的、觀賞的

etymology.text: From French cosmétique, from Ancient Greek κοσμητική (kosmētikḗ, “the art of dress and ornament”), κοσμητικός (kosmētikós), from κοσμητής (kosmētḗs, “orderer, director, decorator”), from κοσμέω (kosméō, “to order, to arrange, to rule, to adorn, to equip, to dress, to embellish”), from κόσμος (kósmos, “order”). By surface analysis, cosmos + -etic.

senses.definition: Any of a number of chemical elements in the periodic table that form a metallic bond with other metal atoms; generally shiny, somewhat malleable and hard, often a conductor of heat and electricity.
Any material with similar physical properties as those chemical elements, especially as a combination of several of them, such as an alloy.
A category of rock music encompassing a number of genres (including thrash metal, death metal, etc.) characterized by strong drumbeats and distorted guitars.
An element which was not directly created after the Big Bang but instead formed through nuclear reactions; any element other than hydrogen and helium.
Crushed rock, stones etc. used to make a road.
The ore from which a metal is derived.
A mine from which ores are taken.
A light tincture used in a coat of arms, specifically argent (white or silver) and or (gold).
Molten glass that is to be blown or moulded to form objects.
The substance that constitutes something or someone; matter; hence, character or temper.
The effective power or calibre of guns carried by a vessel of war.
senses.native: 戰艦上火砲的有效威力或口徑（火力）

senses.definition: The rails of a railway.
The actual airline operating a flight, rather than any of the codeshare operators.

examples.text: Coins are made of metal.
examples.translation: 硬幣是金屬做的。

examples.text: I have a metal table.
examples.translation: 我有一張金屬桌子。

examples.text: Why did you think that Tom liked heavy metal?
examples.translation: 你為什麼覺得湯姆喜歡重金屬樂隊？

examples.text: Nickel is a hard metal with a silvery luster.
examples.translation: 鎳是一種堅硬、銀光閃閃的金屬。

examples.text: Acids react chemically with metals.
examples.translation: 酸會和金屬物質起化學反應。

examples.text: The value of a coin depends on the weight of the metal used.
examples.translation: 錢幣的價值取決於所使用的金屬的重量。

etymology.text: From Middle English metal, a borrowing from Old French metal, from Latin metallum (“metal, mine, quarry, mineral”), itself a borrowing from Ancient Greek μέταλλον (métallon, “mine, quarry, metal”).

senses.definition: Characterized by strong drum-beats and distorted guitars.
Having the emotional or social characteristics associated with metal music; brash, bold, frank, unyielding, etc.
senses.native: 具有重金屬音樂相關情感或社會特質的（直率、大膽、堅定不移等）

examples.text: This ladder is metal.

etymology.text: From Middle English metal, a borrowing from Old French metal, from Latin metallum (“metal, mine, quarry, mineral”), itself a borrowing from Ancient Greek μέταλλον (métallon, “mine, quarry, metal”).

senses.definition: Of, relating to, or characteristic of metal.
Made of or containing metal.
senses.native: 由金屬製成或含有金屬的

senses.definition: Harsh, as if coming from two metals striking one another.
senses.native: 刺耳，如同兩塊金屬相互碰撞的聲音

senses.definition: Having the appearance of being of polished metal.

examples.text: My bicycle was painted metallic blue.
examples.translation: 我的腳踏車塗成了金屬藍色。

examples.text: Tom's new bicycle is metallic red.
examples.translation: 湯姆的新腳踏車是金屬紅色。

examples.text: It has a metallic luster.
examples.translation: 它具有金屬光澤。

examples.text: The moon shines with a metallic light.
examples.translation: 月亮散發出金屬般的光芒。

examples.text: A metallic note sounded in his voice.
examples.translation: 他的聲音中傳來一種金屬般的音符聲。

examples.text: He heard some sort of a metallic buzz.
examples.translation: 他聽到某種金屬嗡嗡聲。

etymology.text: From Latin metallicus, from metallum (“metal”), from Ancient Greek μέταλλον (métallon). Equivalent to metal + -ic.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 metallicus，來自 metallum（金屬），源自古希臘語 μέταλλον。等同於 metal 加上 -ic 詞尾。

senses.definition: Made of bronze metal.
Having a reddish-brown colour.
Tanned; darkened as a result of exposure to the sun.

examples.text: The 5 yen coin is made from brass and the 10 yen coin is made from bronze.
examples.translation: 5元硬幣是黃銅做的，10元硬幣是青銅做的。

etymology.text: From French bronze (1511); from Italian bronzo (13th c.), of uncertain origin (q.v.). First use appears c. 1721 in the writings of Matthew Prior (for which, see citation below).
etymology.native: 源自法語 bronze（1511 年）；來自義大利語 bronzo（13 世紀），起源不明。首次使用約於 1721 年，見馬修·普爾的文集。

senses.definition: A small ticket or sign giving information about something to which it is attached or intended to be attached.
A non-interactive control or widget displaying text, often used to describe the purpose of another control.
A name given to something or someone to categorise them as part of a particular social group.
A company that sells records.
A user-defined alias for a numerical designation, the reverse of an enumeration.
A named place in source code that can be jumped to using a GOTO or equivalent construct.
A charge resembling the strap crossing the horse’s chest from which pendants are hung.
A tassel.
A small strip, especially of paper or parchment (or of some material attached to parchment to carry the seal), but also of iron, brass, land, etc.
A piece of writing added to something, such as a codicil appended to a will.
A brass rule with sights, formerly used with a circumferentor to take altitudes.
The projecting moulding by the sides, and over the tops, of openings in mediaeval architecture.
In mediaeval and later art, a representation of a band or scroll containing an inscription.
senses.native: （中世紀及以後的藝術）表示銘文的飄帶或卷軸圖形

examples.text: The contents of the box are listed on the label.
examples.translation: 箱子的內容在標籤上面寫著。

examples.text: Tom picked up the jar and read the label.
examples.translation: 湯姆拿起罐子讀標籤。

examples.text: Use a marker on the case label, not the disc.
examples.translation: 請在盒蓋標籤上使用記號筆，不要用在碟片上。

examples.text: He attached a "Fragile" label to the package.
examples.translation: 他把「易碎」標籤貼在包裝上。

examples.text: Observers note that animals don't conform to human labels.
examples.translation: 觀察者注意到動物不符合人類的標籤。

examples.text: In the first paragraph, she describes the labels she was tagged with, which have a negative connotation.
examples.translation: 在第一段中，她描述了自己被貼上的標籤，這些標籤具有負面含義。

etymology.text: From Middle English label (“narrow band, strip of cloth”), from Old French label, lambel (Modern French lambeau), from Frankish *lappā (“torn piece of cloth”), from Proto-Germanic *lappǭ, *lappô (“cloth stuff, rag, scraps, flap, dewlap, lobe, rabbit ear”), from Proto-Indo-European *leb- (“blade”). Cognate with Old High German lappa (“rag, piece of cloth”), Old English læppa (“skirt, flap of a garment”). More at lap.
etymology.native: 「label」源自中世英文，意為「窄帶、布條」，來源於古法文 label、lambel（現代法文 lambeau），再溯源自古弗蘭克語 *lappā（意為「撕裂的布片」），而古德語 *lappǭ、*lappô（意為「布料、碎布、翻邊、下垂的皮毛、耳廓」），源自印歐語系 *leb-（意為「刀片」）。與古高地德語 lappa（意為「布頭、布片」）、古英語 læppa（意為「裙襬、衣物的翻邊」）同源。詳見 lap。

senses.definition: To put a label (a ticket or sign) on (something).
To give (a label) to (someone or something) in order to categorise that person or thing.
senses.native: 為（某人或某物）貼上標籤，以分類

senses.definition: To replace specific atoms by their isotope in order to track the presence or movement of this isotope through a reaction, metabolic pathway or cell.
senses.native: 以同位素取代特定原子，以追蹤其在反應、代謝途徑或細胞中的分布（標記）

senses.definition: To add a detectable substance, either transiently or permanently, to a biological substance in order to track the presence of the label-substance combination either in situ or in vitro
senses.native: 加入可偵測物質（暫時或永久）於生物物質中，以追蹤其在原位或試管中的存在（標記）

examples.text: I soon came across a box labeled Terry Tate.
examples.translation: 我很快便發現了一個標有「特里·泰特」字樣的盒子。

examples.text: Oleg is always labeled as naive.
examples.translation: 奧列格總被標籤為天真。

examples.text: They labeled him deviant simply because he thought differently.
examples.translation: 他們僅因他想法不同，便將他標籤為異類。

examples.text: The shop assistant labeled all the products in the shop.
examples.translation: 店員將店內所有商品標上價格。

examples.text: Trump labeled Vietnam a currency manipulator.
examples.translation: 特朗普將越南標籤為貨幣操控者。

etymology.text: From Middle English label (“narrow band, strip of cloth”), from Old French label, lambel (Modern French lambeau), from Frankish *lappā (“torn piece of cloth”), from Proto-Germanic *lappǭ, *lappô (“cloth stuff, rag, scraps, flap, dewlap, lobe, rabbit ear”), from Proto-Indo-European *leb- (“blade”). Cognate with Old High German lappa (“rag, piece of cloth”), Old English læppa (“skirt, flap of a garment”). More at lap.
etymology.native: 「label」源自中世英文，意為「窄帶、布條」，來源於古法文 label、lambel（現代法文 lambeau），再溯源自古弗蘭克語 *lappā（意為「撕裂的布片」），而古德語 *lappǭ、*lappô（意為「布料、碎布、翻邊、下垂的皮毛、耳廓」），源自印歐語系 *leb-（意為「刀片」）。與古高地德語 lappa（意為「布頭、布片」）、古英語 læppa（意為「裙襬、衣物的翻邊」）同源。詳見 lap。

senses.definition: To sit in judgment on; to pass sentence on (a person or matter).
To sit in judgment, to act as judge.
To judicially rule or determine.
To form an opinion on; to appraise.
To arbitrate; to pass opinion on something, especially to settle a dispute etc.
To have as an opinion; to consider, suppose.
To form an opinion; to infer.
To criticize or label another person or thing; to be judgmental toward.
To govern as biblical judge or shophet (over some jurisdiction).
To sentence to punishment, to judicially condemn.
To award judicially; to adjudge.
To constitute a fitting appraisal or criterion of; to provide a basis for forming an opinion on.

examples.text: We should judge him according to his actions.
examples.translation: 我們應該根據他的作為來評判他。

examples.text: You shouldn't judge a man by his appearance.
examples.translation: 你不應該以貌取人。

examples.text: Do not judge so that you will not be judged.
examples.translation: 不要做評判，這樣您自己才不會被人評判。

examples.text: Don't judge other people's traditional culture.
examples.translation: 你不要隨意評判別人的傳統文化。

examples.text: Don't judge people from the way they look.
examples.translation: 不要以貌取人。

examples.text: Judging from the look of the sky, it is likely to rain.
examples.translation: 看看天的樣子，要下雨了。

etymology.text: From Middle English juge, jugge, from Old French juge, from Latin iūdex. Displaced native Middle English deme (from Old English dēma (“judge”)) and demere (from Old English dēmere (“judge”)), see also deemer, deemster.

senses.definition: To declare formally, officially or ceremoniously.
To declare authoritatively, or as a formal expert opinion.
To pronounce dead.
To pass judgment.
To sound out (a word or phrase); to articulate.
To sound like.
To produce the components of speech.
To read aloud.
To emphasize, highlight.

examples.text: This word is difficult to pronounce.
examples.translation: 這個字很難發音。

examples.text: How do you pronounce this word?
examples.translation: 你們怎麼讀這個詞？

examples.text: How do you pronounce your name?
examples.translation: 你怎麼唸你的名字？

examples.text: Can anyone pronounce this word?
examples.translation: 有人能發這個詞的音嗎？

examples.text: I am pronouncing Chinese words.
examples.translation: 我正在讀漢字。

examples.text: Is there anyone who can pronounce this word?
examples.translation: 有人可以唸這個字嗎？

etymology.text: Recorded since c.1330 as Middle English pronouncen (“to utter, declare officially”), from Old French prononcier, from Latin prōnūntiō, itself from prō- (“forth, out, in public”) + nūntiō (“to announce”) from nūntius (“messenger”).

senses.definition: A group, often named or numbered, to which items are assigned based on similarity or defined criteria.

A collection of objects, together with a transitively closed collection of composable arrows between them, such that every object has an identity arrow, and such that arrow composition is associative.

examples.text: Irma is a category 5 hurricane.
How many categories are there?
This is a different category.
You need to create two new categories.
examples.translation: 需新建兩個分類。

examples.text: I put that in the category about memorabilia.
Should I pick a category, or do you want to?

etymology.text: Late Middle English, borrowed from French catégorie, from Middle French categorie, from Late Latin catēgoria (“class of predicables”), from Ancient Greek κατηγορία (katēgoría, “head of predicables”). Doublet of categoria.

senses.definition: A sketch or account of anything in words; a portraiture or representation in language; an enumeration of the essential qualities of a thing or species.
The act of describing; a delineation by marks or signs.
A set of characteristics by which someone or something can be recognized.
A scientific documentation of a taxon for the purpose of introducing it to science.
The act or practice of recording and describing actual language usage in a given speech community, as opposed to prescription, i.e. laying down norms of language usage.
A descriptive linguistic survey.

examples.text: The man matches the description.
examples.translation: 此人與描述相符。

examples.text: The scenery was beautiful beyond description.
examples.translation: 這風景美得無法形容。

examples.text: The beauty of the scene was beyond description.
examples.translation: 那裡的景色美得無法以筆墨形容。

examples.text: I don't know anyone who meets that description.
examples.translation: 我不認識符合條件的人。

examples.text: The beauty of that country is beyond description.
examples.translation: 那個國家的美是語言無法形容的。

examples.text: This description is too abstract.
examples.translation: 這個描述太抽象了。

etymology.text: From Middle English descripcioun, from Old French description and its etymon, Latin dēscrīptiō, noun of action of dēscrībō (“to describe”). Equivalent to describe + -tion.

senses.definition: A felt-tipped pen, a marker pen.
A scorekeeper, especially one who tallies billiard scores.
A device that fires a paintball.
Someone or something used to mark a position or amount, particularly
A real or virtual objective, something to be aimed for.
A location on a stage or set where an actor is to stand or move to during a scene, usually indicated by a small X design placed on the floor.
A direction issued by a camera operator for actors to be on their locations in readiness for a take.
A free or bound morpheme indicating a grammatical function.
A gene or DNA sequence with a known location on a chromosome that can be used to identify individuals or species.
A substance used as an indicator for diagnosis or other analysis, a biomarker.
The soldier who forms the pilot of a wheeling column or marks the direction of an alignment.
A sewing machine attachment that creases the fabric to mark a line
A counter, especially one used in card games or backgammon.
Any of various objects that mark a place on the landscape, such as a milepost, blaze, or surveyor's cairn.
Someone who assigns marks on tests, examinations, etc.; a grader.
A personal favor owed to someone, whether written or not.

A formal certification that a company was the first to approach a competition authority to reveal the existence of a cartel, generally entitling it to greater leniency during the cartel's dissolution and punishment.
A player on defense used to mark one or more offensive players.
Synonym of IOU, an informal record of a debt.
The ink marks or residue of a felt-tipped pen.

examples.text: Where are all the blue markers?
James gave them all markers.
That's a marker, not a pen.
The pencil case was full of dry-erase markers.
Hey, where's the markers we just bought?
Me and my mother have eleven markers.

etymology.text: From mark + -er.

senses.definition: To give a name to.
To mention, specify.
To identify as relevant or important
To publicly implicate by name.
To disclose the name of.
To designate for a role.
To initiate a process to temporarily remove a member of parliament who is breaking the rules of conduct.

examples.text: She was named Kate after her mother.
examples.translation: 她以她母親的名字被取名為凱特。

etymology.text: From Middle English name, nome, from Old English nama, noma, from Proto-West Germanic *namō, from Proto-Germanic *namô (“name”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁nómn̥ (“name”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（name），來自古英語（nama），經原始日耳曼語（*namô）「名字」，上溯至原始印歐語（*h₁nómn̥）「名字」。

senses.definition: To write software programs.
To add codes to (a data set).
To categorise by assigning identifiers from a schedule, for example CPT coding for medical insurance purposes.
To encode.
To encode a protein.
To call a hospital emergency code.
Of a patient, to suffer a sudden medical emergency (a code blue) such as cardiac arrest.

etymology.text: From Middle English adressen (“to raise erect, adorn”), from Old French adrecier (“to straighten, address”) (modern French adresser), from Proto-Romance *addīrēctiāre, from ad- (“to; towards”) + *dīrēctiāre (“to guide; to direct”), from Latin dīrēctus (“straight; right”), from dīrigō (“to lay straight; to direct”), itself from regō (“to govern, to rule”). Cognate with Scots sairie (“sad, grieved”), Saterland Frisian seerich (“sore, inflamed”), West Frisian searich (“sad, sorry”), Low German serig (“sick, scabby”), German dialectal sehrig (“sore, sad, painful”), Swedish sårig. etymology.native: 源自中古英語（sory），來自古英語（sāriġ）「悲傷的、難過的、哀痛的」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*sairagaz）「悲傷的」，最終來自原始印歐語（*seh₂yro）「硬的、粗糙的、痛的」。與蘇格蘭語（sairie）、西弗里斯語（searich）同源。

etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 fom、foom，來自古英語 fām，源自原始西日耳曼語 *faim，再源自原始德語 *faimaz，來自原始印歐語 *(s)poHy-m-os，源自 *(s)poH(y)-（意為「泡沫」）。與德語 Feim（泡沫）、拉丁語 spūma（泡沫）、拉丁語 pūmex（火山岩）、梵語 फेन (phéna，意為「泡沫」）同源，可能也與庫爾德語 fê（意為「癲癇」）有關。

senses.definition: To form or emit foam.
To spew saliva as foam; to foam at the mouth.
To coat or cover with foam.

examples.text: He was foaming at the mouth.
examples.translation: 他嘴裡泡沫滿溢。

examples.text: James was practically foaming at the mouth.
examples.translation: 詹姆斯幾乎嘴裡泡沫滿溢。

examples.text: The river was foaming.

Cognate with German Feim (“foam”), Latin spūma (“foam”), Latin pūmex (“pumice”), Sanskrit फेन (phéna, “foam”), possibly Northern Kurdish fê (“epilepsy”).

senses.definition: A fine, gentle, dispersed mist of liquid.
A pressurized container; an atomizer.
Something resembling a spray of liquid.
Any of numerous commercial products, including paints, cosmetics, and insecticides, that are dispensed from containers in this manner.
A jet of fine medicated vapour, used either as an application to a diseased part or to charge the air of a room with a disinfectant or a deodorizer.
A side channel or branch of the runner of a flask, made to distribute the metal to all parts of the mold.
A group of castings made in the same mold and connected by sprues formed in the runner and its branches.
The allocation and filling of blocks of memory with the same byte sequence, hoping to establish that sequence in a certain predetermined location as part of an exploit.
A loud scolding or reprimand, usually delivered by a sports coach or similar figure.
A small branch of flowers or berries.
A collective body of small branches.
Branches and twigs collectively; foliage.
An orchard.
An ornament or design that resembles a branch.

examples.text: Spray Cookie with the water bottle.
examples.translation: 用水瓶噴餅乾。

examples.text: I saw Tom spray painting something on the wall.
examples.translation: 我看到湯姆在牆上噴漆畫東西。

examples.text: Mary carries pepper spray in her purse.
examples.translation: 瑪麗的包裡有辣椒噴霧。

examples.text: I only use environmentally friendly sprays.
examples.translation: 我只用環保噴劑。

examples.text: The smell of skunk spray can cause people to vomit.
examples.translation: 臭鼬噴出的氣味會讓人嘔吐。

examples.text: I knew we should've packed bug spray.
examples.translation: 我就知道我們應該帶防蚊液。

etymology.text: From Middle Dutch sprāien, sprayen, spraeyen (“to spray, sprinkle, spread”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *sprēwijaną (“to spray, sprinkle”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)per- (“to sow, scatter”).
etymology.native: 源自中古荷蘭語「噴灑、撒、散布」，最終上溯至原始日耳曼語「噴灑、撒」，來自原始印歐語「播種、散布」。

senses.definition: Of a liquid or other substance, or a container holding it: to be boiled (vigorously); to become boiling hot.
Of a liquid, vapor, etc., or a container holding it: to foam or froth in an agitated manner, as if boiling.
Of a person: to be in an agitated or angry mental state, often in a way that is not obvious to others.
Of a place: to be filled with many people or things moving about actively; to buzz with activity; also, of people or things: to move about actively in a crowd or group.
Of a place: to have inhabitants in an angry or disaffected mood; to be in a state of unrest.
To overboil (something) so that it loses its flavour or texture; hence (figurative), to cause (the body, the mind, the spirit, etc.) to become dull through too much alcoholic drink or heat.
To soak (something) in a liquid; to drench, to steep.
To boil (something); especially, to cook (food) by boiling or stewing; also, to keep (something) boiling.
Of the stomach: to digest (food).

examples.text: The square was seething with people.
examples.translation: 廣場裡人聲鼎沸。

examples.text: He talks to me, I seethe inside.
examples.translation: 他跟我說話，我內心憤怒煩躁。

examples.text: The country seethed over the issue of national defense.
examples.translation: 國家對國防議題民怨沸騰。

examples.text: Mary is seething with rage she feels unable to express.
examples.translation: 瑪麗怒火中燒卻無法表達。

examples.text: Rodrigo was seething in anger.
examples.translation: 羅德里戈怒氣沖沖。

examples.text: When the scandal broke, the Congressman's constituents were seething.
examples.translation: 丑聞曝光後，眾議員的選民們民怨沸騰。

relations.native: 滾動的行為、結果或狀態

etymology.text: The verb is derived from Middle English sethen, seeth (“to boil, seethe; to cook; etc.”) [and other forms], from Old English sēoþan (“to boil, seethe; to cook; etc.”), from Proto-West Germanic *seuþan, from Proto-Germanic *seuþaną (“to boil, seethe”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂sewt-, *h₂sew-, *h₂sut- (“to move about, roil, seethe”).
etymology.native: 此動詞源於中古英語 sethen 與古英語 sēoþan，皆來自日耳曼語系中表示「沸騰」的詞根。

senses.definition: To fit, as for a specific end or purpose; make suitable or comfortable; adapt; adjust.
To construct by fitting together or uniting various parts; fabricate by union of constituent parts.
To bring or put into form or order; adjust the parts or elements of; compose; contrive; plan; devise.
To put together the structural elements of (a constructed object such as a building).
To place (a picture such as a painting or photograph) inside a decorative border.
To position visually within a fixed boundary.
To construct in words so as to establish a context for understanding or interpretation.
Conspire to falsely incriminate an innocent person.
To wash ore with the aid of a frame.
To move.
To proceed; to go.
To hit (the ball) with the frame of the racquet rather than the strings (normally a mishit).
senses.native: 以球拍框架（非線面）擊球（通常為失誤）

senses.definition: To strengthen; refresh; support.
To execute; perform.
To cause; to bring about; to produce.
To profit; avail.
To fit; accord.
To succeed in doing or trying to do something; manage.

examples.text: He was framed by his wife.
examples.translation: 他被妻子誣陷了。

examples.text: This will be framed and hung up on the wall.
examples.translation: 這件作品將被裝裱好掛在牆上。

examples.text: All have sworn him an oath that they should frame his will on earth.
examples.translation: 所有人都向他起誓，要依照他的意志在世上行事。

examples.text: The frame itself is worth more than the picture.
examples.translation: 畫框比畫還值錢。

examples.text: Are you trying to frame me?
examples.translation: 你是在試圖陷害我嗎？

examples.text: Once we finish framing the house, we'll hang tin on the roof.
examples.translation: 等我們完成房屋的裝裱，就該在屋頂鋪鐵皮了。

etymology.text: From Middle English framen, fremen, fremmen (“to construct, build, strengthen, refresh, perform, execute, profit, avail”), from Old English framian, fremian, fremman (“to profit, avail, advance”), from Proto-West Germanic *frammjan, from Proto-Germanic *framjaną (“to further, promote, perform”), from Proto-Indo-European *promo- (“front, forward”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 framen, fremen, fremmen（意為「建造、強化、更新、執行、獲益」），來自古英語 framian, fremian, fremman（意為「獲益、前進」），再溯源自古西日耳曼語 *frammjan，再溯源自古德語 *framjaną（意為「推進、執行」），最終源自印歐語系 *promo-（意為「前進、向前」）。

senses.definition: The structural elements of a building or other constructed object.
The outer decorated portion of a stamp's image, often repeated on several issues although the inner picture may change.
The outer circle of a cancellation mark.
A division of time on a multimedia timeline, such as 1/30 or 1/60 of a second.
An individually scrollable rectangular region of a web page, forming part of a frameset.
Anything composed of parts fitted and united together; a fabric; a structure.
senses.native: 由零件拼合而成的任何物品；織物；結構

senses.definition: A human body or the structure thereof; the size, shape, sturdiness etc. of a person's body as described in a certain way; one's build.

senses.native: 用於裝裱紙張、畫布等軟性材料的硬質框架

senses.definition: A piece of photographic film containing an image.

senses.native: 理解或詮釋的脈絡（架構）

senses.definition: A conspiracy to falsely incriminate an innocent person.
senses.native: 偽造罪證、陷害無辜者的陰謀（栽贓）

senses.definition: A set of balls whose results are added together for scoring purposes. Usually two balls, but only one ball in the case of a strike, and three balls in the case of a strike or a spare in the last frame of a game.
senses.native: 保齡球的一局（一格）中用來計分的一組球（通常為兩球；全倒時僅一球；最後一格全倒或補中時為三球）

senses.definition: The complete set of pins to be knocked down in their starting configuration.
senses.native: 保齡球開局時整組球瓶的擺放位置（全瓶）

senses.native: 用於栽培或遮蔽植物的可移動結構（框架、苗床罩）

senses.definition: An inning.
Any of certain machines built upon or within framework.
Frame of mind; disposition.
Contrivance; the act of devising or scheming.

senses.definition: A drawing or diagram conveying information.
A human figure, which dress or corset must fit to; the shape of a human body.
A numeral.

senses.native: （美術）人像、形象，任何形體的描繪，尤指人體

Distinguished appearance; magnificence; conspicuous representation; splendour; show.

examples.text: He has a soccer-player physique.

senses.definition: An individual who has been granted personhood; usually a human being.
A character or part, as in a play; a specific kind or manifestation of individual character, whether in real life, or in literary or dramatic representation; an assumed character.
A human of unspecified gender (in terms usually constructed with man or woman).
The physical body of a being seen as distinct from the mind, character, etc.
Any individual or formal organization with standing before the courts.
A linguistic category used to distinguish between the speaker of an utterance and those to whom or about whom they are speaking. See grammatical person.
A soulmate; someone, especially a romantic partner, with whom one is exceptionally compatible and connected.
Any one of the three hypostases of the Holy Trinity: the Father, Son, or Holy Spirit.
Any sapient or socially intelligent being.
Someone who likes or has an affinity for (a specified thing).
A worker in a specified function or specialty.
The human genitalia; specifically, the penis.
A shoot or bud of a plant; a polyp or zooid of the compound Hydrozoa, Anthozoa, etc.; also, an individual, in the narrowest sense, among the higher animals.
senses.native: 植物的芽；水螅綱等複合動物中的多胚或體狀；在狹義上，高等動物中的個體

examples.text: People established churches and schools there.
examples.translation: 人們在那裡建立了教堂和學校。

examples.text: The Japanese are an industrious people.

examples.text: I'm always forgetting people's names.

examples.text: He liberated the people from bondage.

examples.text: People who will lie for you, will lie to you.
examples.translation: 會為你說謊的人，就會對你說謊。

etymology.text: From Middle English persoun, personne et al., from Anglo-Norman parsone, persoun et al. (Old French persone (“human being”), French personne), and its source Latin persōna (“mask used by actor; role, part, character”), perhaps a loanword from Etruscan 𐌘𐌄𐌓𐌔𐌖 (φersu, “mask”). In this sense, displaced native man, which came to mean primarily "adult male" in Middle English; see Old English mann. Displaced native Old English hād (“person, individual”). Doublet of parson and persona.
etymology.native: 「人」一詞源於中古英語的 persoun，其後可追溯至盎格魯 - 諾曼語的 parsone 與 persoone，再源自古法語 personne（意為「人類」）及現代法語 personne。

senses.definition: A hard earthen substance that can form rocks; especially, such substance when regarded as a building material.
A piece of such material: a block of stone, rock or a pebble.
A hard, stone-like deposit.
A stand or table with a smooth, flat top of stone, commonly marble, on which to arrange the pages of a book, newspaper, etc. before printing.
A gemstone, a jewel, especially a diamond.
A unit of weight equal to 14 pounds (≈6.3503 kilograms), formerly used for various commodities (wool, cheese, etc.), but now principally used for personal weight. Abbreviated as st.
The central part of some fruits, particularly drupes; consisting of the seed and a hard endocarp layer.
A playing piece made of any hard material, used in various board games such as backgammon and go.
A dull light grey or beige, like that of some stones.
A 42-pound, precisely shaped piece of granite with a handle attached, which is bowled down the ice.
A monument to the dead; a gravestone or tombstone.
senses.native: 紀念亡者的紀念碑；墓碑

senses.definition: A mirror, or its glass.
A testicle.

An area at a racetrack used for refueling and repairing the vehicles during a race.

senses.native: 行進樂隊中演奏大鼓等打擊樂器的前排樂團；也可指這些樂器放置的旁側區域

senses.definition: A mine.

A hole or trench in the ground, excavated according to grid coordinates, so that the provenance of any feature observed and any specimen or artifact revealed may be established by precise measurement.
senses.native: 依照網格座標挖掘的地面孔洞或溝槽，用以精確測定所觀察到的特徵、樣本或文物的來源

senses.definition: A trading pit.
An armpit.
A luggage hold.
A small surface hole or depression, a fossa.
senses.native: 小型表面孔洞或凹陷，即窪地

senses.definition: The indented mark left by a pustule, as in smallpox.
senses.native: 膿包留下的凹痕，如天花病變處

senses.definition: The grave, underworld or Hell.
An enclosed area into which gamecocks, dogs, and other animals are brought to fight, or where dogs are trained to kill rats.
senses.native: 供鬥雞、鬥狗等動物相鬥的圍場，或訓練狗捕鼠的場地（鬥坑）

senses.definition: Only used in the pits.
A mosh pit.
The emergency department of a hospital.
A bed.

examples.text: Kalman was watching the fire pit.
examples.translation: 卡爾曼正注視著那個火坑。

examples.text: He fell into the bottomless pit.
examples.translation: 他掉進了無底的深淵。

examples.text: That family really is the pits!
examples.translation: 那家人簡直糟糕透頂！

examples.text: As a man, no a human being, you're the pits!
examples.translation: 身為人類，你簡直糟透了！

examples.text: I dug a huge pit with my shovel in just one day.
examples.translation: 我只用一天就用鏟子挖了一個大坑。

examples.text: He who digs a pit for his brother falls into it.
examples.translation: 誰若為兄弟挖坑，自己也會掉進去。

relations.native: 拋棄或放棄；停止與某人交往

etymology.text: From Middle English pit, pet, püt, from Old English pytt, from Proto-West Germanic *puti, from Latin puteus (“trench, pit, well”), although there are phonetic difficulties.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 pit、pet 或 püt，再追溯至古英語 pytt，來自日耳曼語族原初詞 *puti，意即拉丁語 puteus（溝渠、坑洞或井），儘管存在音韻上的困難。

senses.definition: Any formal system in which symbolic expressions are manipulated according to fixed rules.
Differential calculus and integral calculus considered as a single subject.
A stony concretion that forms in a bodily organ.
Deposits of calcium phosphate salts on teeth.
A decision-making method, especially one appropriate for a specialised realm.
Calculation; computation.

examples.text: Tom's favourite subject is calculus.
Claudio was in calculus class.
Last year I was a TA for calculus.
examples.translation: 去年我是一個微積分學助教。

examples.text: Does anyone know where my calculus book went?
What calculus book is used at your university?
Calculus just did not appeal to Mary.

etymology.text: * Borrowed from Latin calculus (“a pebble or stone used as reckoning counters in abacus”), diminutive of calx (“limestone”) + -ulus.

senses.definition: To put to death; to extinguish the life of.
To use up or to waste.
To succeed with an audience, especially in comedy.
To disconnect (a user) involuntarily from the network.
To deadmelt.
To render inoperative.
To stop, cease, or render void; to terminate.
To amaze, exceed, stun, or otherwise incapacitate.
To cause great pain, discomfort, or distress to; to hurt.
To produce feelings of dissatisfaction or revulsion in.
To overpower, overwhelm, or defeat.
To force a company out of business.
To punish severely.
To strike (a ball, etc.) with such force and placement as to make a shot that is impossible to defend against, usually winning a point.
To cause (a ball, etc.) to be out of play, resulting in a stoppage of gameplay.
To cause to assume the value zero.
To sexually penetrate in a skillful way.
To exert oneself to an excessive degree.

examples.text: No fewer than 50 passengers were killed.
examples.translation: 不下50個乘客死了。

examples.text: Tom admitted that he'd killed Mary.
examples.translation: 湯姆承認他殺死了瑪麗。

examples.text: It was Alister who killed Barbara.
examples.translation: 是阿里斯特殺了芭芭拉。

examples.text: They're plotting to kill the king.
examples.translation: 他們正密謀要殺害國王。

examples.text: Tom was killed three years later.
examples.translation: 湯姆在三年之後被殺了。

examples.text: My brother was killed in a traffic accident.
examples.translation: 我哥哥在一次交通意外中喪生了。

etymology.text: From Middle English killen, kyllen, cüllen (“to strike, beat, cut”), of obscure origin. Cognate with Scots kele, keil (“to kill”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（killen、kyllen、cüllen）「打、擊、砍」，來源不明。與蘇格蘭語（kele、keil）「殺」同源。

senses.definition: The cavity or mold in which anything is formed.
The metaphorical place where something is made, formed, or given birth.
The material or tissue in which more specialized structures are embedded.
An extracellular matrix, the material or tissue between the cells of animals or plants.
Part of the mitochondrion.
The medium in which bacteria are cultured.
A table of data.

A rectangular arrangement of numbers or terms having various uses such as transforming coordinates in geometry, solving systems of linear equations in linear algebra and representing graphs in graph theory.
A two-dimensional array.
A grid-like arrangement of electronic components, especially one intended for information coding, decoding or storage.
A geological matrix.
The sediment surrounding and including the artifacts, features, and other materials at a site.
The environment from which a given sample is taken.
In hot metal typesetting, a mold for casting a letter.
In printmaking, the plate or block used, with ink, to hold the image that makes up the print.
The five simple colours (black, white, blue, red, and yellow) from which all the others are formed.
A binding agent of composite materials, e.g. resin in fibreglass.
Matrix clause is a clause that has another (subordinate) clause embedded within it.
The womb.

examples.text: Show that the matrix is diagonalisable.

The matrix consisted of five rows and seven columns.
The inverse of a non-square matrix is a dangerous thing.
examples.translation: 非方矩陣的逆陣是一個危險的東西。

examples.text: Tom has a dot matrix printer.
We live in a media matrix.

etymology.text: From Middle English matris, matrice, matrix, from Old French matrice (“pregnant animal”), or from Latin mātrīx (“dam, womb”), both ultimately from māter (“mother”). Doublet of mother from Indo-European ancestor.

senses.definition: A stone milepost (or by extension in other materials), one of a series of numbered markers placed along a road at regular intervals, typically at the side of the road or in a median.

examples.text: We have reached an important milestone.
It's an important milestone for her.
We passed a milestone again.
Another milestone has been passed.
The US releases centennial coins to celebrate different milestones.
She sees the service award as a milestone in her career.

etymology.text: From mile + stone. Compare Dutch mijlsteen (“milestone”), German Low German Mielensteen (“milestone”), German Meilenstein (“milestone”), Swedish milsten (“milestone”).

senses.definition: The act of reflecting or the state of being reflected.
The property of a propagated wave being thrown back from a surface (such as a mirror).
Something, such as an image, that is reflected.
Careful thought or consideration.
A representative manifestation or outcome of a condition, trend or trait.
Used to make an implied criticism.
The process or mechanism of determining the capabilities of an object at run-time.
The folding of a part; a fold.

examples.text: Spirituality begins with self-reflection.
examples.translation: 靈性從自我反省開始。

examples.text: Mary is looking at her reflection.
examples.translation: 瑪麗正看著自己的倒影。

examples.text: Reflections could be seen in the puddles.
examples.translation: 水窪裡可以看見倒影。

examples.text: A little reflection will show you that you are wrong.
examples.translation: 只要你細心想一想，就會明白自己的錯處了。

examples.text: My cat peers bemusedly at her reflection in the water.
examples.translation: 我的貓兒一臉迷惘地盯著自己在水中的倒影。

examples.text: I saw my reflection in the window.
examples.translation: 我在窗戶上看見了我的映像。

etymology.text: From Middle English refleccion, refleccioun, refleccioune, reflection, from Middle French reflection, reflexion, and its source Late Latin reflexiō, from the participle stem of reflectō. The current spelling is influenced by reflect. Equivalent to reflect + -ion.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 refleccion、refleccioun、refleccioune，來源為中世紀法文 reflection、reflexion，再源自拉丁文 reflexiō，出自 reflectō 的分詞語幹。現行拼寫受 reflect 影響，等同 reflect + -ion。

senses.definition: The action of expressing thoughts, ideas, feelings, etc.

A colloquialism or idiom.
A facial appearance usually associated with an emotion.
An arrangement of symbols denoting values, operations performed on them, and grouping symbols.
The process of translating a gene into a protein.
A piece of code in a high-level language that returns a value.
A specific blend of whisky.
The act of pressing or squeezing out.
The tone of voice or sound in music.
Emotional involvement or engagement in a text read aloud rendered by the voice of the reciter or the reader.

examples.text: This expression is very Chinese.
examples.translation: 這種表達方式很中國化。

examples.text: He saw my expression change.
examples.translation: 他看到我臉色變了。

examples.translation: 那種表達方式已經過時了。

examples.translation: 英語的「別在意」這個說法在多語例句庫上有四百四十四種翻譯。

examples.translation: 她臉上的表情讓我很困惑。

etymology.native: 借自中古法語，來自後期拉丁語「壓出」。

senses.definition: The act of contemplating; being highly concentrated in thought; musing.

examples.text: He watches the world in quiet contemplation.
examples.translation: 他靜心沉思著世界。

examples.text: Wisdom grows through contemplation.
examples.translation: 智慧透過沉思而增長。

examples.translation: 埃及的紀念碑令人難以沉思。

examples.translation: 你在進行什麼嚴肅的沉思？

examples.text: Silent contemplation is pleasant.
examples.translation: 靜心沉思令人愉悅。

examples.text: The young man was completely absorbed in the contemplation of her beauty.
examples.translation: 那年輕人完全沉浸在對她美貌的沉思中。

etymology.text: From Middle English contemplacioun, from Old French contemplation, from Latin contemplatio. By surface analysis, contemplate + -ion.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 contemplacioun，來自舊法語 contemplation，拉丁語 contemplatio。字面分析為 contemplate 加上 -ion。

examples.translation: 我仔細地考慮了這個問題。

examples.text: We should've taken the schedule into consideration.
examples.translation: 我們本該考慮一下行程。

examples.translation: 你應該考慮的第一件事是時間。

senses.definition: A reflected sound that is heard again by its initial observer.

Something that reflects or hearkens back to an earlier thing.

examples.text: He echoes his wife in everything.

examples.translation: 我們聽見自己說話的回音從山谷的另一邊傳了回來。

examples.text: In retrospect, I think you were right.
examples.translation: 回顧來說，我認為你是對的。

examples.translation: 回顧來說，這令人尷尬。

examples.translation: 回顧來說，湯姆希望自己花更多時間學習。

examples.translation: 回顧來說，那個決定是個錯誤。

examples.translation: 回顧來說，我本應對她更尊重。

examples.translation: 回顧來說，也許我不該在部落格貼那張照片。

etymology.native: 此詞源自拉丁語 retrōspectum，由 retrōspicio（「回顧」）組成，等同 retro- 加上 -spect。可與 review 相比。

examples.text: He returned from abroad yesterday.
examples.translation: 他昨天從國外回來。

examples.text: My brother wants to study abroad.
examples.translation: 我哥哥要出國唸書。

examples.text: Many people go abroad during summer vacation.
examples.translation: 許多年輕人在暑假時出國。

etymology.text: First attested in mid 13th century. From Middle English abrood (“broadly widely scattered”), from a- (“on, in”) + brood (“broad”). Equivalent to a- + broad.

senses.definition: A submicroscopic, non-cellular structure that consists of a core of DNA or RNA surrounded by a protein coat, that requires a living host cell to replicate, and that sometimes causes disease in the host organism (such agents are often classed as nonliving infectious particles and less often as microorganisms).

Any type of malware.
Any malicious or dangerous entity that spreads from one place or person to another.
A disease caused by such an infectious agent; a viral illness.
Venom, as produced by a poisonous animal etc.

examples.translation: 病毒開始變異了。

examples.translation: 那台電腦中毒了。

Paul created a deadlier variant of the virus.
The virus cut down many elephants in Africa.

examples.translation: 湯姆在可疑的網站上看影片的時候中了電腦病毒。

relations.native: 乳頭多瘤空泡病毒組病毒

senses.definition: Cause, interest or account.
Purpose or end; reason.
The benefit or regard of someone or something.
Contention, strife; guilt, sin, accusation or charge.

examples.text: Tofu goes well with good sake.
examples.translation: 豆腐配清酒很合適。

examples.text: I stopped smoking for the sake of my health.
examples.translation: 為了健康，我不再抽菸。

examples.text: I gave up smoking for the sake of my health.
examples.translation: 為健康戒了煙。

examples.translation: 他為了健康，戒菸了。

examples.text: They fought for the sake of their country.
examples.translation: 他們為祖國而戰鬥。

etymology.text: From Middle English sake (“sake, cause”), from Old English sacu (“cause, lawsuit, legal action, complaint, issue, dispute”), from Proto-West Germanic *saku, from Proto-Germanic *sakō (“affair, thing, charge, accusation, matter”), from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂g- (“to investigate”).

examples.text: May I borrow your garden hose?
examples.translation: 我可以借你的園藝水龍頭嗎？

examples.translation: 湯姆用園藝水龍頭澆花園。

examples.text: Tom drank the water as it came out the hose.
examples.translation: 湯姆喝著從水龍頭流出的水。

examples.text: He played a hose on the burning hotel.
examples.translation: 他用水龍頭對著著火的飯店噴水。

examples.text: The water stopped running because the hose has a kink in it.
examples.translation: 水停了，因為水龍頭彎曲了。

examples.translation: 他把橡膠水龍頭接在排氣管上。

etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 hose（意為「褲管、緊身褲」），來自古英文 hose, hosa（意為「褲子、緊身褲」），源自原始西日耳曼語 *hosā，再源自原始德語 *husǭ（意為「覆蓋物、緊身褲、長褲」），最終源自原始印歐語 *(s)kewH-（意為「覆蓋」）

examples.translation: 鞋子、拖鞋和涼鞋屬於鞋類。

examples.translation: 我現在有能力裝腔作勢地自以為是了。

examples.translation: 你們要是用刀劍刺向我們，我們難道不會流血嗎？

examples.translation: 玫瑰的刺讓我手上有細小的刺痛。

etymology.text: From Middle English prik, prikke, from Old English prica, pricu (“a sharp point, minute mark, spot, dot, small portion, prick”), from Proto-West Germanic *prikō, *priku, from Proto-Germanic *prikô, *prikō (“a prick, point”), of uncertain origin, perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *breyǵ- (“to scrape, scratch, rub, prickle, chap”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 prik、prikke，來自古英語 prica、pricu（意為「尖銳的點、細小的標記、斑點、小部分」），源自原始西日耳曼語 *prikō、*priku，再源自原始德語 *prikô、*prikō（意為「刺、尖點」），起源不明，可能來自原始印歐語 *breyǵ-（意為「刮、抓、摩擦、刺」）

senses.definition: To pierce or puncture slightly.
To drive a nail into (a horse's foot), so as to cause lameness.
senses.native: 將釘子釘入（馬蹄）使其跛足

senses.definition: To shoot without killing.
To form by piercing or puncturing.
To mark the surface of (something) with pricks or dots; especially, to trace a ship’s course on (a chart).
senses.native: 在（某物）表面刺點或作記號；尤指在海圖上標出船隻航線

senses.definition: To fix by the point; to attach or hang by puncturing.
senses.native: 以尖端固定；以刺穿方式懸掛或附著

senses.definition: To make or become sharp; to erect into a point; to raise, as something pointed; said especially of the ears of an animal, such as a horse or dog; and usually followed by up.
senses.native: 使（如馬或狗的耳朵）豎立、尖起（常接 up）

senses.definition: Usually in the form prick out: to plant (seeds or seedlings) in holes made in soil at regular intervals.
senses.native: （常作 prick out）將種子或幼苗栽入等距的土孔中

senses.definition: To incite, stimulate, goad.
To affect with sharp pain; to sting, as with remorse.
To make acidic or pungent.
To become sharp or acid; to turn sour, as wine.
To aim at a point or mark.
To mark or denote by a puncture; to designate by pricking; to choose; to mark.
To run a middle seam through the cloth of a sail.
To be punctured; to suffer or feel a sharp pain, as by puncture.
senses.native: 被刺穿；因刺痛而感到劇痛（過時）

senses.definition: To urge one's horse on; to ride quickly.
to dress or adorn; to prink.

examples.text: If you want roses, you're going to get pricked.
examples.translation: 想要玫瑰，就得被刺到。

examples.text: Tom pricked Mary's bum with a cactus.
examples.translation: 湯姆用仙人掌刺了瑪麗的屁股。

examples.translation: 約翰幾乎沒感覺到針刺進手臂，護士正抽血。

etymology.text: From Middle English prik, prikke, from Old English prica, pricu (“a sharp point, minute mark, spot, dot, small portion, prick”), from Proto-West Germanic *prikō, *priku, from Proto-Germanic *prikô, *prikō (“a prick, point”), of uncertain origin, perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *breyǵ- (“to scrape, scratch, rub, prickle, chap”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 prik、prikke，來自古英語 prica、pricu（意為「尖銳的點、細小的標記、斑點、小部分」），源自原始西日耳曼語 *prikō、*priku，再源自原始德語 *prikô、*prikō（意為「刺、尖點」），起源不明，可能來自原始印歐語 *breyǵ-（意為「刮、抓、摩擦、刺」）

senses.definition: To hurt, usually by introducing poison or a sharp point, or both.
To puncture with the stinger.
To hurt, to be in pain (physically or emotionally).
senses.native: （身體或情感上）感到疼痛、刺痛

senses.definition: To cause harm or pain to.

examples.text: Why do bees die after stinging?
examples.translation: 蜜蜂蜇人後為什麼會死去呢？

etymology.text: From Middle English styng, sting, stynge, stenge, from Old English sting, stincg (“a sting, stab, thrust made with a pointed instrument; the wound made by a stab or sting”), from Proto-Germanic *stingaz; possibly also from Old English stynġ, from Proto-Germanic *stungiz.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 styng，後者來自古英語 sting，意指用尖銳工具刺擊或造成的傷口；可能也源自古英語 stynġ。

senses.definition: A jet or current of water or vapour directed upon some part of the body to benefit it medicinally; in particular, such a jet directed at the vagina for irrigation.
senses.native: 用於醫療目的噴射於身體某部位的水流或氣流；特指用於沖洗陰道的噴射

senses.definition: Something that produces the jet or current in the previous sense, such as a syringe.
A jet or spray of any liquid.
senses.native: 任何液體的噴射或噴霧

examples.text: Rodrigo's friend was a douche.
examples.translation: 羅德里戈的朋友是個混蛋。

etymology.text: From Middle English suffren, from Anglo-Norman suffrir, from Latin sufferre (“to offer, hold up, bear, suffer”), from sub- (“up, under”) + ferō (“to carry”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰer- (“to bear, carry”). Displaced native Old English þrōwian.

To create a hole in the skin for the purpose of inserting jewelry.
to break or interrupt abruptly

etymology.text: From Middle English perce, from conjugated forms of Old French percier such as (jeo) pierce (“I pierce”), probably from Vulgar Latin *pertūsiō, from Latin pertūsus, past participle of pertundō (“thrust or bore through”), from per- (“through”) + tundō (“beat, pound”). Displaced native Old English þȳrlian (literally “to hole”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 perce，來自古法語 percier 的變位形式，可能源自通俗拉丁語 *pertūsiō，來自拉丁語 pertūsus（pertundō 的過去分詞），由前綴 per-「透過」加上動詞 tundō「敲打、捶打」組成。此詞取代了古英語本土詞 þȳrlian（字面意義為「穿孔」）。

senses.definition: The total number of goals, points, runs, etc. earned by a participant in a game.
A subject.
An account; a reason; a motive; a sake; a behalf.

An account or reckoning; account of dues; bill; debt.

Twenty pounds sterling.

etymology.text: From Middle English score, skore, schore, from Old English scoru (“notch; tally; score”), from Old Norse skor, from Proto-Germanic *skurō (“incision; tear; rift”), which is related to *skeraną (“to cut”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“cut”). Cognate with Icelandic skora, Swedish skåra, Danish skår. Related to shear.

etymology.text: Recorded since 1577, probably a rebracketing of an otch, from Middle French oche (“notch”), itself from the Old French verb ochier (“to notch”), of uncertain origin, but possibly related to French hocher and English nick (“small cut, notch”).
etymology.native: 自1577年開始記錄，可能是將「otch」重新分類，源自中世紀法語「oche」（意為「凹口」），而該詞又來自古法語動詞「ochier」（意為「做凹口」），起源不明，但可能與法語「hocher」及英文「nick」（意為「小切口」）有關。

etymology.native: 源自新拉丁語 ephemerus，來自古希臘語 ἐφήμερος，意為「僅活一天」或「短暫的」。
