examples.text: The situation there was critical.
examples.translation: 那裡的情況很危急。

etymology.text: From Latin criticus + English -al.

senses.definition: A class or school for young schoolboys.
An outbuilding used as a lavatory; an outhouse, a privy.
A little schoolboy, either in grade or size.

etymology.text: The adjective is derived from Middle English peti, pety (“little, small; minor”) [and other forms], from Anglo-Norman petit, Middle French petit, and Old French peti, petit, pitet (“young; little, small; inferior; insignificant”) (modern French petit), ultimately of imitative origin. It is no longer thought that the word is derived from Celtic. Doublet of petit and petite.

senses.definition: The condition of being vindictive; a malevolent desire for revenge.

examples.text: We never ought to allow our instincts of justice to degenerate into mere vindictiveness.
examples.translation: 我們絕不應該讓我們的正義感淪為單純的報復心。

etymology.text: From vindictive + -ness.
etymology.native: 此詞由「報復的」加上表示狀態的後綴構成。

senses.definition: To add sauce to; to season.
To cause to relish anything, as if with a sauce; to tickle or gratify, as the palate; to please; to stimulate.
To make poignant; to give zest, flavour or interest to; to set off; to vary and render attractive.
To treat with bitter, pert, or tart language; to be impudent or saucy to.
To send or hand over.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

etymology.text: From Middle English sauce, from Old French sause, from Vulgar Latin *salsa, noun use of the feminine of Latin salsus (“salted”), past participle of saliō (“to salt”), from sal. Doublet of salsa.
etymology.native: 「sauce」源自中世紀英文，來源為古法文 sause，再源自通俗拉丁文 *salsa，是拉丁文 salsus（意為「鹽味的」）的女性名詞用法，為 saliō（意為「鹽製」）的過去分詞，而 saliō 又來自 sal（鹽）。此詞與 salsa 為同源詞。

senses.definition: The act or process of irrigating, or the state of being irrigated; especially, the operation of causing water to flow over lands, for nourishing plants.

etymology.native: 源自中世紀法語的灌溉，來自拉丁語 irrigatio。

senses.definition: An item of goods or supplies, especially food, obtained for future use.
The act of providing, or making previous preparation.
Money set aside for a future event.
A liability or contra account to recognise likely future adverse events associated with current transactions.

Regular induction into a benefice, comprehending nomination, collation, and installation.
A nomination by the pope to a benefice before it became vacant, depriving the patron of his right of presentation.

A downward wind.

etymology.native: 由「灑」加表示工具的字尾組成。

senses.definition: The probability of a negative outcome to a decision or event.

The magnitude of possible loss consequent to a decision or event.

A thing (from the perspective of how likely or unlikely it is to cause an adverse effect).
A borrower (such as a mortgage-holder or person with a credit card).
A financial product (typically an investment).
An entity insured by an insurer.

senses.definition: A period of unusually low rainfall, longer and more severe than a dry spell.

dryness, aridness, dry heat

More at food, fodder.

Any habitual intake or consumption.
A council or assembly of leaders; a formal deliberative assembly.
A session of exams.
A criminal proceeding in court.
A clerical or ecclesiastical function in Scotland.

senses.definition: The art or science of cultivating the ground, including the growing and harvesting of crops, and the rearing and management of livestock.

The central dark part of an ocellated spot.
An orphan who is a minor and under the protection of the state.

senses.definition: One who audits bookkeeping accounts.

One who audits an academic course; who attends the lectures but does not earn academic credit.
One trained to perform spiritual guidance procedures.
One who listens, typically as a member of an audience.

examples.text: Universities have classrooms and dormitories.

senses.definition: A knot, knob, protuberance or swelling.

The point where the orbit of a planet, as viewed from the Sun, intersects the ecliptic. The ascending and descending nodes refer respectively to the points where the planet moves from South to North and N to S; their respective symbols are ☊ and ☋.
A leaf node.
A computer or other device attached to a network.
The point at which the lines of a funicular machine meet from different angular directions.
The point at which a curve crosses itself, being a double point of the curve. See crunode and acnode.
A similar point on a surface, where there is more than one tangent-plane.
A vertex or a leaf in a graph of a network, or other element in a data structure.
A hard concretion or incrustation which forms upon bones attacked with rheumatism, gout, or syphilis; sometimes also, a swelling in the neighborhood of a joint.
A point along a standing wave where the wave has minimal amplitude.
A hole in the gnomon of a sundial, through which passes the ray of light which marks the hour of the day, the parallels of the Sun's declination, its place in the ecliptic, etc.
The word of interest in a KWIC, surrounded by left and right cotexts.
A region of an electric circuit connected only by (ideal) wires (i.e. the voltage between any two points on the same node must be zero).
A point in a parse tree that can be assigned a syntactic category label.
A point in a cladogram from which two clades branch, representing the presumed ancestor.
The knot, intrigue, or plot of a dramatic work.

senses.definition: A proposition antecedently supposed or proved; something previously stated or assumed as the basis of further argument; a condition; a supposition.
Any of the first propositions of a syllogism, from which the conclusion is deduced.

Matters previously stated or set forth; especially, that part in the beginning of a deed, the office of which is to express the grantor and grantee, and the land or thing granted or conveyed, and all that precedes the habendum; the thing demised or granted.
A piece of real estate; a building and its adjuncts.
The fundamental concept that drives the plot of a film or other story.

examples.text: Smoking is prohibited on hospital premises.
We entered the school premises.
These premises need a makeover.
I don't see anything wrong with your premise.
I don't agree with the premise of your argument.
It is forbidden to smoke on school premises.

etymology.text: From Middle English premise, premisse, from Old French premisse, from Medieval Latin premissa (“set before”) (premissa propositio (“the proposition set before”)), feminine past participle of Latin praemittere (“to send or put before”), from prae- (“before”) + mittere (“to send”).

senses.definition: The formation of something complex or coherent by combining simpler things.
Creation of a complex waveform by summation of simpler waveforms.
The reaction of elements or compounds to form more complex compounds.
A deduction from the general to the particular, by applying the rules of logic to a premise.
The combination of thesis and antithesis.
In intelligence usage, the examining and combining of processed information with other information and intelligence for final interpretation.
An apt arrangement of elements of a text, especially for euphony.
The uniting of ideas into a sentence.
The reunion of parts that have been divided.
An Ancient Roman dining-garment.

examples.text: His work is a synthesis of several ideas.
Phosphorylation is an important step in the synthesis of ATP.
With synthesis, you have to be objective.
The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the organelle responsible for lipid synthesis.
Love, in fact, is the agent of universal synthesis.
Ribosomes are the organelles responsible for protein synthesis.

relations.native: 人口普查、人口調查、戶口檢查

etymology.text: From Latin synthesis, from Ancient Greek σύνθεσις (súnthesis, “a putting together; composition”), from συντίθημι (suntíthēmi, “put together, combine”), from συν- (sun-, “together”) + τίθημι (títhēmi, “set, place”). Doublet of sandhi.

senses.definition: US standard form of aluminium foil.

senses.definition: A very thin sheet of metal.
A very thin sheet of plastic.
Thin aluminium/aluminum (or, formerly, tin) used for wrapping food.
A thin layer of metal put between a jewel and its setting to make it seem more brilliant.

In literature, theatre/theater, etc., a character who helps emphasize the traits of the main character and who usually acts as an opponent or antagonist, but can also serve as the sidekick of the protagonist.
Anything that acts by contrast to emphasise the characteristics of something.
A very thin sword with a blunted (or foiled) tip.
A thin, transparent plastic material on which marks are made and projected for the purposes of presentation. See transparency.
A premium trading card with a glossy finish.
A stylized flower or leaf.
Failure when on the point of attainment; defeat; frustration; miscarriage.

senses.definition: One of the incorrect answers presented in a multiple-choice test.
senses.native: （選擇題中的）錯誤選項（干擾選項）

senses.definition: The track of an animal.
A small arc in the tracery of a window, etc.

etymology.text: From Middle English foyle, from Middle French fueille, from Old French fueille (“plant leaf”), from Late Latin folia, the plural of folium, mistaken as a singular feminine.
etymology.native: 來源於中古英語 foyle，源自中古法語 fueille，再源自古法語 fueille（意為「植物葉子」），又源自拉丁語 folia（folium 的複數形式），被誤認為單數陰性形式。

senses.definition: Having little thickness or extent from one surface to its opposite.
Very narrow in all diameters; having a cross section that is small in all directions.
Having little body fat or flesh; slim; slender; lean; gaunt.
Of low viscosity or low specific gravity.
Scarce; not close, crowded, or numerous; not filling the space.
Describing a poorly played golf shot where the ball is struck by the bottom part of the club head. See fat, shank, toe.
Lacking body or volume; small; feeble; not full.
Slight; small; slender; flimsy; superficial; inadequate; not sufficient for a covering.
Of a route: relatively little used.
Poor; scanty; without money or success.

examples.text: This woman is very thin.
examples.translation: 這個女人很瘦。

examples.text: His body is too thin.

etymology.text: From Middle English thinne, thünne, thenne, from Old English þynne, from Proto-West Germanic *þunnī, from Proto-Germanic *þunnuz (“thin”) – compare *þanjaną (“to stretch, spread out”) – from Proto-Indo-European *ténh₂us (“thin”), from *ten- (“to stretch”).

senses.definition: of or relating to a barbarian; uncivilized, uncultured or uncouth

examples.text: Israel's barbaric actions are indefensible.
examples.translation: 以色列的殘暴行徑難以辯護。

examples.text: That's a barbaric practice.
examples.translation: 那是一種殘暴的行為。

examples.text: Algeria is a modern nation, not a barbaric country.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞是現代國家，不是殘暴的國家。

examples.text: Is Islamic law barbaric?
examples.translation: 伊斯蘭法是殘暴的嗎？

examples.text: The US invasion of Iraq was a barbaric attack.
examples.translation: 美國入侵伊拉克是一場殘暴的攻擊。

examples.text: Bullfighting is so cruel and barbaric.
examples.translation: 鬥牛如此殘忍且殘暴。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English barbarik, from Old French barbarique (“barbarous”), from Latin barbaricus, from Ancient Greek βαρβαρικός (barbarikós, “barbaric, savage, fierce”), from βάρβαρος (bárbaros, “barbarian”) + -ικός (-ikós, adjective suffix). See βάρβαρος (bárbaros) for more.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 barbarik，來源於古法文 barbarique，再源自拉丁文 barbaricus，源自古希臘文 βαρβαρικός（barbarikós，意為「野蠻、凶猛」），由 βάρβαρος（bárbaros，意為「野蠻人」）+ -ικός（-ikós，形容詞後綴）構成。詳見 βάρβαρος（bárbaros）以獲更多資訊。

senses.definition: Exceedingly violent, severe, ferocious, cruel or savage.
Resolute or strenuously active.
Threatening in appearance or demeanor.
Of exceptional quality, exhibiting boldness or chutzpah.
Excellent, very good.

examples.text: Gabriel's boat endured fierce storms.

etymology.text: From Middle English fers, fiers, borrowed from Old French fers (“wild", "ferocious”), nominative of fer, from Latin ferus (“wild", "untamed”).

senses.definition: Occurring quickly with little or no warning or expectation; instantly.
Hastily prepared or employed; quick; rapid.
Hasty; violent; rash; precipitate.

examples.text: I wouldn't make any sudden moves.
The change in weather was sudden.
Don't make any sudden movements.
I was surprised at the news of his sudden death.
examples.translation: 他突然過世的訊息讓我感到驚訝。

examples.text: All of a sudden the sky became overcast.
examples.translation: 天突然轉陰了。

examples.text: His sudden appearance surprised us all.
examples.translation: 他的突然出現，讓我們都感到驚訝。

etymology.text: From Middle English sodeyn, sodain, from Anglo-Norman sodein, from Old French sodain, subdain (“immediate, sudden”), from Vulgar Latin *subitānus (“sudden”), from Latin subitāneus (“sudden”), from subitus (“sudden", literally, "that which has come stealthily”), originally the past participle of subīre (“to come or go stealthily”), from sub (“under”) + īre (“go”). Doublet of subitaneous. Displaced native Old English fǣrlīċ.

senses.definition: Not pleasant.

examples.text: Don't be so unpleasant with your sister, Tom.

senses.definition: A yelp or bark.
Loud or coarse talk.

examples.text: I sound my barbaric yawp over the roofs of the world. - Walt Whitman

etymology.text: From Middle English yolpen, of imitative origin.

senses.definition: To express feelings of pain, dissatisfaction, or resentment.
To state the presence of something negative; to indicate that one is suffering from something; to report (e.g.) a symptom.
To make a formal accusation or bring a formal charge.
To creak or squeak, as a timber or wheel.

etymology.text: From Middle English complaynen, from Old French complaindre, from Medieval Latin complangere (“to bewail, complain”), from Latin com- (“together”) + plangere (“to strike, beat, as the breast in extreme grief, bewail”); see plain, plaint.

senses.definition: To use up.
To eat.
To completely occupy the thoughts or attention of.
To destroy completely.

examples.text: Weasels consume rodents in large quantities.

senses.definition: To expel (as exhaust).

etymology.native: 源於拉丁語 exhaustus，為 exhaurīre 的過去分詞（「抽出、喝乾、倒空、耗盡」），由 ex（「外」）加上 haurīre（「抽水、排水」）組成。

senses.definition: To oxidize, especially of iron or steel.
become destroyed by water, air, or a corrosive such as an acid
cause to deteriorate due to the action of water, air, or an acid

To touch repeatedly; to fiddle with.
To strangle.

etymology.text: From Middle English enquery, from the Old French verb enquerre, from Latin inquīrō, composed of in- (“in, at, on; into”) + quaerō (“to seek, look for”), of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-Italic *kʷaizeō, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷeh₂- (“to acquire”). The alternative form inquiry was subsequently respelled to conform to the original Latin spelling, as opposed to the Old French spelling.

First attested 1530. Compare English scapegrace, scapegallows.

etymology.text: From Old English port, borrowed from Latin portus (“port, harbour”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pértus (“crossing”) (and thus a distant doublet of ford). Doublet of fjard, fjord, firth, ford, and Portus.

examples.translation: 你能說出多少種會冬眠的動物？

examples.text: Bears aren't the only animals that hibernate.
examples.translation: 熊不是唯一會冬眠的動物。

examples.text: The bat hibernates during the winter months.
examples.translation: 蝙蝠在冬季月份裡會冬眠。

examples.text: I thought only bears hibernated, but my teacher said that turtles do, too.
examples.translation: 我以為只有熊會冬眠，但老師說烏龜也會。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin hībernātus, perfect passive participle of hībernō (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from hībernus (“wintry”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 hībernātus，為 hībernō 的完成時被動分詞，來自 hībernus（冬季的）。

senses.definition: An imaginary place inhabited by those who are asleep; (by extension) the state of slumber.

examples.text: I dream about a magical land called Slumberland every night.
examples.translation: 我每晚都夢見一個名叫夢境的魔法世界。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: My parents say they live in Slumberland while they sleep.
examples.translation: 父母說他們睡覺時住在夢境裡。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The book tells stories from the wonderful world of Slumberland.
examples.translation: 這本書講述了夢境這個奇妙世界的故事。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: In Slumberland, people can fly and talk to animals easily.
examples.translation: 在夢境裡，人們可以輕鬆飛翔並與動物交談。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: She wrote a story about her adventures in the land of Slumberland.
examples.translation: 她寫了一篇關於她在夢境冒險的故事。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Many children believe that Slumberland is a real place for dreaming.
examples.translation: 許多孩子相信夢境是一個真實的夢幻之地。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From slumber + -land.
etymology.native: 由「睡眠」加上表示地方的後綴組成。

senses.definition: Sleepy, drowsy.
Sleep-inducing.

examples.text: A slumberous June morning.
examples.translation: 一個嗜睡的六月清晨。

examples.text: Slumberous (or slumbrous) eyes.
examples.translation: 一副嗜睡的眼睛。

examples.text: My little brother is very slumberous after lunch.
examples.translation: 我弟弟午餐後非常嗜睡。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: She looks slumberous because she hasn't slept well.
examples.translation: 她看起來很嗜睡，因為昨晚睡得不好。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The baby was so slumberous that he fell asleep.
examples.translation: 嬰兒太嗜睡了，直接就睡著了。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: He felt slumberous and wanted to take a short nap.
examples.translation: 他覺得很嗜睡，決定讀本書小憩一下。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From slumber + -ous.
etymology.native: 源自「睡眠」加上表示形容詞的後綴。

senses.definition: To fire (pottery) in a kiln, without a ceramic glaze.
To take part in the sport of tubing, riding down a river on an inner tube.
senses.native: 乘坐內胎順流而下（管狀滑水）

examples.text: A rusk is a kind of hard biscuit or bread.

etymology.text: From earlier bisket, from Middle English bisquyte, from Old French bescuit (French biscuit); doublet of biscotto.
etymology.native: 源自早期的 bisket，來自中世紀英文 bisquyte，源自古法文 bescuit（法文 biscuit）；是 biscotto 的同源詞。

senses.definition: A small nail with a flat head.
That which is attached; a supplement; an appendix.
A thumbtack.
A loose seam used to temporarily fasten pieces of cloth.
The lower corner on the leading edge of a sail relative to the direction of the wind.
A course or heading that enables a sailing vessel to head upwind.
A direction or course of action, especially a new one; a method or approach to solving a problem.
The maneuver by which a sailing vessel turns its bow through the wind so that the wind changes from one side to the other.
The distance a sailing vessel runs between these maneuvers when working to windward; a board.
A rope used to hold in place the foremost lower corners of the courses when the vessel is close-hauled; also, a rope employed to pull the lower corner of a studding sail to the boom.
Any of the various equipment and accessories worn by horses in the course of their use as domesticated animals.
The stickiness of a compound, related to its cohesive and adhesive properties.
Food generally; fare, especially of the hard bread or breadlike kind.
senses.native: 食物（泛指）；伙食，尤指硬麵包或類似麵包的食物

senses.definition: A stain; a tache.
That which is tacky; something cheap and gaudy.
A contract by which the use of a thing is set, or let, for hire; a lease.
Confidence; reliance.
A peculiar flavour or taint.

examples.text: I decided to take a different tack with my students.
examples.translation: 我決定對學生採取不同的方法。

examples.text: Why don't you try a different tack?
examples.translation: 你何不試試不同的方法？

examples.text: Only a solitary tack prevented the entire wooden panel from collapsing under its weight.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Restoring the antique required finding the original tack that once secured the delicate panel.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: He stuck the notice on the board with tacks.
examples.translation: 他用釘子把告示釘在公告欄上。

examples.text: The laminate adhesive has very aggressive tack and is hard to move once in place.
examples.translation: 這種層壓膠黏劑的粘性非常強，一旦貼上就難以移動。

etymology.text: From Middle English tak, takke (“hook; staple; nail”), from Old Northern French taque (“nail, pin, peg”), from Frankish *takkō (“twig, branch, shoot”), of unknown origin, but possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dHgʰ-n-, from the root *déHgʰ- (“to pinch; to tear, rip, fray”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Takke (“bough; branch; twig”), West Frisian takke (“branch”), tûk (“branch, smart, sharp”), Dutch tak (“twig; branch; limb”), German Zacke (“jag; prong; spike; tooth; peak”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 tak，後經古北法語演化，可能源自日耳曼語族詞根，意為「捏、撕」，與荷蘭語及德語相關詞彙同源。

senses.definition: Any of various evergreen trees from the family Palmae or Arecaceae, which are mainly found in the tropics.
A branch or leaf of the palm, anciently borne or worn as a symbol of victory or rejoicing.
senses.native: 棕櫚枝，古時象徵勝利或歡慶

senses.definition: Triumph; victory.
Any of the twenty-three awards that can be earned after obtaining the Eagle Scout rank, but generally only before turning eighteen years old.
senses.native: （童軍）獎章，鷹級童軍後可獲得的二十三項獎章之一

senses.definition: The inner and somewhat concave part of the human hand or other primate hand that extends from the wrist to the bases of the fingers.
The corresponding part of the forefoot of a nonprimate mammal.
senses.native: （動物）掌，非靈長類哺乳動物前足的對應部位

senses.definition: A metallic disk attached to a strap and worn in the palm of the hand; used to push the needle through the canvas, in sewing sails, etc.
senses.native: （縫帆）頂針，套在手掌上的金屬圓盤，用來推針穿過帆布

senses.definition: The broad flattened part of an antler, as of a full-grown fallow deer; so called as resembling the palm of the hand with its protruding fingers.
senses.native: （鹿角）掌狀部，成年黇鹿鹿角寬扁的部分

senses.definition: The flat inner face of an anchor fluke.
Synonym of hand, any of various units of length notionally derived from the breadth of the palm, formalized in England as 4 inches and now chiefly used for the height of horses
senses.native: 掌（長度單位），源自手掌寬度，英制定為四英寸，今主要用於量馬高

senses.definition: Any of various units of length notionally derived from the length of the palm from the wrist to the base of the fingers.
senses.native: （長度單位）掌，源自手掌長度的各種單位

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: I'm interested in palm reading.
examples.translation: 我對掌上閱讀很感興趣。

examples.text: Palm trees are excellent for landscaping.
How tall do most palm trees grow?
examples.translation: 棕櫚樹最高是多高？

examples.text: An A6 notebook is just a little bigger than a palm.
examples.translation: 一個A6的本子大概就比巴掌大一點。

examples.text: I can place the palms of my hands on the floor without bending my knees.
examples.translation: 我不彎膝也能把手掌平放在地上。

examples.text: Palm oil production is the leading cause of deforestation in Indonesia.
examples.translation: 棕櫚油製造是導致印度尼西亞森林砍伐的主要原因。

etymology.text: From Middle English palme, from Old English palm, palma (“palm-tree, palm-branch”), from Latin palma (“palm-tree, palm-branch, palm of the hand”), from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₂meh₂, *pl̥h₂emeh₂ (“palm of the hand”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat”). Cognate with Dutch palm, German Palme, Danish palme, Icelandic pálmur (“palm”).

senses.definition: A fanciful impulse, or sudden change of idea.
A large capstan or vertical drum turned by horse power or steam power, for raising ore or water, etc., from mines, or for other purposes.
A bird, the Eurasian wigeon.

examples.text: He indulges all her whims.
examples.translation: 他滿足她所有的任性。

examples.text: It's just a whim of yours.
examples.translation: 這只是你的任性。

examples.text: He can't make decisions like that on a whim.
examples.translation: 他不能隨便就做這種決定。

examples.text: At work they are at the whim of the boss.
examples.translation: 在公司裡，他們完全聽從主管的安排。

examples.text: This is not a whim; it’s a deep, personal choice.
examples.translation: 這不是任性；這是深層的個人選擇。

examples.text: On a whim, he learnt the periodic table off by heart.
examples.translation: 他隨便一想，就把週期表背熟了。

etymology.text: Clipping of whim-wham.
etymology.native: whim-wham 的縮略形式。

senses.definition: Mental apprehension of whatever may be known, thought, or imagined; idea, concept.
A sentiment; an opinion.
Any small article used in sewing and haberdashery, either for attachment to garments or as a tool, such as a button, zipper, or thimble.
An invention; an ingenious device; a knickknack.
Inclination; intention; predisposition; disposition.
Pretentiousness or overambition.
Sense; mind.

examples.text: Futurology includes notions of probabilities.
It challenged my preconceived notions.
He has some pretty strange notions.
His notion is that planes are safer than cars.
What on earth put such a notion into your head?
We had no notion of leaving our hometown.

etymology.text: From Latin nōtiō (“a becoming acquainted, a taking cognizance, an examination, an investigation, a conception, idea, notion”), from nōscō (“to know”). Compare French notion. See know.

senses.definition: A thrust; a push; a sudden force that impels.
A wish or urge, particularly a sudden one prompting action.
The integral of force over time.

examples.text: Discernment prevails over impulse.
She bought the dress on impulse.
I learned it on impulse.
He told his wife not to buy on impulse.
examples.translation: 他叫自己的妻子不要衝動購物。

examples.text: On a sudden impulse, I returned to my home town.
He went out, yielding to a sudden impulse.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French impulser, from Latin impulsus.

senses.definition: Something to play with, especially as intended for use by a child.
A thing of little importance or value; a trifle.
A simple, light piece of music, written especially for the virginal.
An inferior graffiti artist.
A gun.
Love play, amorous dalliance; fondling.
A vague fancy, a ridiculous idea or notion; a whim.
An old story; a silly tale.
A headdress of linen or wool that hangs down over the shoulders, worn by elderly women of the lower classes.
The penis.
The vagina.
A watch.
A small jar (about an inch across) used to hold prepared opium.
A small ball of opium (about the size of a pea).

examples.text: The children are playing with toys.
examples.translation: 小孩們在玩玩具。

examples.text: This toy car runs on batteries.
examples.translation: 這個玩具汽車是裝電池的。

examples.text: He gathered his toys together.
examples.translation: 他收起了他的玩具。

examples.text: This factory produces toys.
examples.translation: 這個工廠製造玩具。

examples.text: He deprived my little sister of all her toys.
examples.translation: 他把我妹妹的玩具都搶走了。

examples.text: It was her little sister that broke her toy.
examples.translation: 她的玩具是被她妹妹弄壞的。

relations.native: 非他也非她者；生物；被非人化的存在

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English toye (“amorous play, piece of fun or entertainment”), probably from Middle Dutch toy, tuyg (“tools, apparatus, utensil, ornament”) as in Dutch speel-tuig (“plaything, toy”), from Old Dutch *tiug, from Proto-West Germanic *tiugī̆, *teug, from Proto-Germanic *teugą (“stuff, matter, device, gear, lever”, literally “that which is drawn or pulled”), from Proto-Germanic *teuhaną (“to lead, bring, pull”), from Proto-Indo-European *dewk- (“to pull, lead”).

senses.definition: A playful activity that may be unstructured; an amusement or pastime.
A particular instance of playing a game.
Wild animals hunted for food.
An activity described by a set of rules, especially for the purpose of entertainment, often competitive or having an explicit goal.
A school subject during which sports are practised.
Part of a set during which one player continuously serves (at least four rallies must be won to win a game, at least six games must be won to win the set).
That which is gained, such as the stake in a game.
The number of points necessary to win a game.
In some games, a point awarded to the player whose cards add up to the largest sum.
The equipment that enables such activity, particularly as packaged under a title.
One's manner, style, or performance in playing a game.
A field of gainful activity, as an industry or profession.
The music industry.
Something that resembles a game with rules, despite not being designed.
An exercise simulating warfare, whether computerized or involving human participants.
A questionable or unethical practice in pursuit of a goal.
A flock of swans, especially as kept for hunting purposes (or, originally, a group of any animals kept for such purpose).
The ability to seduce or woo someone, usually by strategy.
Prostitution. (Now chiefly in on the game.)
Lovemaking, flirtation.

examples.text: We enjoyed watching the baseball game.
examples.translation: 我們喜歡看棒球比賽。

examples.text: Tom is always playing video games.
examples.translation: 湯姆總是在玩電視遊樂器。

examples.text: Everybody plays the game of love.
examples.translation: 大家都玩愛情遊戲。

examples.text: Which game are you talking about?
examples.translation: 你在說哪個遊戲？

examples.text: The baseball game was called off due to rain.
examples.translation: 棒球比賽因為天雨取消了。

examples.text: Whatever game I play with you, you never win.
examples.translation: 無論我和你玩甚麼遊戲，你也總是輸。

etymology.text: From Middle English game, gamen, gammen, from Old English gamen (“sport, joy, mirth, pastime, game, amusement, pleasure”), from Proto-West Germanic *gaman, from Proto-Germanic *gamaną (“amusement, pleasure, game", literally "participation, communion, people together”), from *ga- (collective prefix) + *mann- (“man”); or alternatively from *ga- + a root from Proto-Indo-European *men- (“to think, have in mind”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（game、gamen），來自古英語（gamen）「運動、歡樂、消遣、遊戲」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*gamaną）「娛樂、遊戲」，字面意為「參與、共處」，由集合字首（*ga-）加（*mann-）「人」組成；或另說來自原始印歐語（*men-）「想」。

senses.definition: A state of being pleased or contented; gratification.
A person, thing or action that causes enjoyment.
Sexual enjoyment.
One's preference.
The will or desire of someone or some agency in power.

examples.text: He lives for nothing but pleasure.
examples.translation: 他生活除了享樂之外沒別的了。

examples.text: Reading gives me great pleasure.
examples.translation: 閱讀帶給我巨大的快樂。

examples.text: It's our pleasure.
examples.translation: 這是我們的榮幸。

examples.text: Few things give us as much pleasure as music.
examples.translation: 很少有東西像音樂一樣帶給我們這麼多的快樂。

examples.text: Is your coming to Guangdong a pleasure trip?
examples.translation: 來廣東玩嗎

examples.text: It has always been a pleasure to work with you.
examples.translation: 跟你共事總是很愉快。

etymology.text: From Early Modern English pleasur, plesur, alteration (with ending accommodated to -ure) of Middle English plaisir (“pleasure”), from Old French plesir, plaisir (“to please”), infinitive used as a noun, conjugated form of plaisir or plaire, from Latin placeō (“to please, to seem good”), from the Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂-k- (“wide and flat”). Related to Dutch plezier (“pleasure, fun”). More at please.

senses.definition: Violent derangement of mind; madness; insanity.
Excessive or unreasonable desire; insane passion affecting one or many people; fanaticism.
The state of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, arousal, and/or energy levels.
senses.native: 異常亢奮、易怒的情緒、興奮或能量狀態

examples.text: Manias can be alarming.
examples.translation: 狂躁症可能令人擔憂。

examples.text: Something about big cities triggers mania in me.
examples.translation: 某些關於大城市的因素會在我身上引發狂躁。

examples.text: I don't understand all the soccer mania.
examples.translation: 我不完全明白所有的足球狂熱。

examples.text: He has mania for sports cars.
examples.translation: 他對賽車車的狂熱令人印象深刻。

examples.text: I get hypomanic, but rarely does this become full-blown mania.
examples.translation: 我會有輕度躁鬱，但這很少發展成完全發作的狂躁症。

examples.text: This is pure and sterile mania of protagonism for its own sake.
examples.translation: 這是純粹且無菌的、為本身而存在的 protagonism 狂熱。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin mania, from Ancient Greek μανία (manía, “madness”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 mania，來自古希臘語 μανία（madness）。

senses.definition: The quality of being discreet.
The ability to make wise choices or decisions.
The freedom to make one's own judgements.
The authority to exercise one's own judgement in making decisions that have effect.

examples.text: This plan has discretion advised.
examples.translation: 此計劃建議謹慎行事。

examples.text: What is required here is discretion.
This plan needs discretion.
Discretion is the better part of valour.
He has attained to years of discretion.
Parental discretion is advised.

etymology.text: From Middle English discrecioun, from Old French discretion, from Late Latin discrētiō, from Latin discerno. Equivalent to discreet + -ion.

senses.definition: An activity that one enjoys doing in one's spare time.
An extinct breed of horse native to the British Isles, also known as the Irish Hobby.
Synonym of hobby horse (“a favorite topic”).
Painting and building miniatures (as opposed to playing the game)
Any of four species of small falcons in the genus Falco, especially Falco subbuteo.

examples.text: His hobby is painting pictures of flowers.
examples.translation: 他的愛好是畫有花的圖。

examples.text: My hobbies are not only wide-ranging but also useful.
examples.translation: 我的愛好不但廣泛而且有用。

examples.text: My hobbies are driving and playing the guitar.
examples.translation: 我的愛好是開車和彈吉他。

examples.text: I like to collect stamps from different countries as a hobby.
I'm more into the competitive part than the hobby part of this game.

etymology.text: From Middle English hoby (“small horse, pony”), a variant or alteration of hobyn (“a small ambling horse”), of uncertain and disputed origin. According to one theory the term is derived from Hobin, a pet name of Robert or Robin, at the time frequently used as a proper name for a workhorse (compare dobbin).

senses.definition: A contract which binds a person to work for another, under specified conditions, for a specified time (often as an apprentice).
A contract relating to lending (typically for issuing a bond), a real estate transaction, or a bankruptcy that imposes additional conditions on one or both parties.
A document, written as duplicates separated by indentations, specifying either of the above contracts.
An indentation; a recess.

examples.text: The indenture required me to work 40 hours weekly for a year.
examples.translation: 此契約規定我須每周工作四十小時，持續一年。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The indenture specifies my duties, hours, and end date clearly.
examples.translation: 契約明確列明我的職責、時數與終止日期。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: I must follow the indenture’s terms or face penalties.
examples.translation: 我必須遵守契約條款，否則將面臨懲罰。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The indenture binds me to work under specific conditions for a year.
examples.translation: 契約約束我於特定條件下服役一年。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: This indenture includes clauses on pay, hours, and termination.
examples.translation: 此契約包含薪資、時數與終止條款。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The indenture is legally binding and enforceable in court.
examples.translation: 契約具法律效力，可於法院執行。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Anglo-Norman endenture, from Old French endenteure, from endenter (“to dent”). The name of the contract derives from the irregular dent-shaped cut (indentation) used to prove the authenticity of the two parts, similar to a chirograph.
etymology.native: 此詞源自盎格魯-諾曼語 endenture，來源於古法語 endenteure，又源自 endenter（意為「齒狀凹陷」）。合約之名來自於用不規則的齒狀凹陷（凹痕）來證明兩部分真實性，類似於手寫契約。

senses.definition: To bind a person under such a contract.
To indent; to make hollows, notches, or wrinkles in; to furrow.

examples.text: Though age may creep on, and indenture the brow.
examples.translation: 雖年歲漸長，亦不免契約刻皺眉間。

etymology.text: From Anglo-Norman endenture, from Old French endenteure, from endenter (“to dent”). The name of the contract derives from the irregular dent-shaped cut (indentation) used to prove the authenticity of the two parts, similar to a chirograph.
etymology.native: 此詞源自盎格魯-諾曼語 endenture，來源於古法語 endenteure，又源自 endenter（意為「齒狀凹陷」）。合約之名來自於用不規則的齒狀凹陷（凹痕）來證明兩部分真實性，類似於手寫契約。

senses.definition: To constrain someone by force or by social, moral or legal means.
To do (someone) a service or favour (hence, originally, creating an obligation).
To cause somebody to feel indebted.

examples.text: Tom obliges us with almost everything.
Thank you very much! Much obliged.
You're not obliged to thank me.
She was obliged to work to support five children.

senses.definition: Confidence in or reliance on some person or quality.

Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *deru- (“be firm, hard, solid”).

etymology.text: From Middle English schitten, schetten, from Old English sċyttan (“to cause rapid movement, shoot a bolt, shut, bolt”), from Proto-West Germanic *skuttjan, from Proto-Germanic *skutjaną, *skuttijaną (“to bar, bolt”), from Proto-Germanic *skuttą, *skuttjō (“bar, bolt, shed”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewd- (“to drive, fall upon, rush”). The Modern English word was originally a dialect form; the Old English word would have normally merged with shit.

senses.definition: To notch, as a sword or knife.
To make an opening in; to breach.
To check the size of a gap.
To fall or spill open so as to leave a gap.
Of an electric train, to be positioned, or to cause to be positioned, between electrical pickup points, causing loss of power.
To surpass (someone or something) by a considerable margin.
To leave suddenly.
To stare or gape.

examples.text: Please mind the gap between the train and the platform.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English gap /gappe, from Old Norse gap (“an empty space, gap, chasm”), from gapa (“to gape, scream”), from Proto-Germanic *gapōną, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₂- (“to open wide, gape”). Related to Danish gab (“an expanse, space, gap”), Old English ġeap (“open space, expanse”). Doublet of gape.

senses.definition: Able to be known or seen by everyone; happening without concealment; open to general view.
Open to all members of a community, as opposed to only a segment of it; especially, provided by national or local authorities and supported by money from taxes.
Pertaining to the people as a whole, as opposed to a group of people; concerning the whole community or country.

senses.definition: Pertaining to nations collectively, or to nations regarded as civilized; international, supernational.

Of or pertaining to the human race as a whole; common, universal.

etymology.text: From casual, from Middle French casuel, from Medieval Latin casualitas and Late Latin cāsuālis (“happening by chance”), from Latin cāsus (“event”) (English case), from cadere (“to fall”). Originally meaning “a chance event” (compare casual, as in “casual encounter”), it developed a negative meaning as “an unfortunate event”, especially the loss of a person.
etymology.native: 源於 casual，來自中古法語 casuel，源自中世紀拉丁語 casualitas 和晚拉丁語 cāsuālis（「偶然發生之事」），來自拉丁語 cāsus（事件）（英語 case），來自 cadere（「落下」）。原意指「偶然事件」（比較 casual，如「casual encounter」），後發展出負面含義，指「不幸的事件」，特別是人員喪失。

etymology.text: From Middle English hayl, haul, from Old English hæġl, hæġel, hagol (“hail”), from Proto-West Germanic *hagl, from Proto-Germanic *haglaz, of uncertain origin. Either from Proto-Indo-European *kagʰlos (“pebble”); or alternatively from *ḱoḱló-, a reduplication of *ḱel- (“cold”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Hail (“hail”), West Frisian heil (“hail”), Low German Hagel (“hail”), German Hagel (“hail”), Dutch and Swedish hagel (“hail”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Icelandic hagl
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 hayl、haul，來自古英語 hæġl、hæġel、hagol（「冰雹」），源自西日耳曼語 *hagl，源自原始日耳曼語 *haglaz，起源不明。可能源自原始印歐語 *kagʰlos（「卵石」）；或來自 *ḱoḱló-，*ḱel-（「寒冷」）的疊音詞。與薩特蘭弗里斯蘭語 Hail（「冰雹」）、西弗里斯蘭語 heil（「冰雹」）、低地德語 Hagel（「冰雹」）、德語 Hagel（「冰雹」）、荷蘭語和瑞典語 hagel（「冰雹」）、丹麥語、挪威語 Bokmål、挪威語 Nynorsk 及冰島語 hagl 同源。

Cognate with dialectal Danish and Norn drit (“excrement”), Norwegian dritt (“excrement”), dialectal Swedish dret (“shit”), Faroese and Icelandic drit (“bird excrement”), Dutch drijten (“to defecate”), drits (“dirt, mud, filth”), drijt and dreet (“excrement”), Low German drieten (“to defecate”), Driet (“shit”

etymology.text: Borrowed from French mannequin, derived from Old French [Term?] (“little man, figurine”), derived from Middle Dutch mannekin (“little man”) or mannekijn (see English manikin), diminutive of man (“man”). etymology.native: 從法語「mannequin」借來，源自古法語[詞源不明]（意為「小人、塑像」），源自中世紀荷蘭語「mannekin」（意為「小人」）或「mannekijn」（見英文「manikin」），是「man」的縮小形式。表面構成為「man + -kin」。可與「ramequin/ramekin」比較。為「manakin」與「manikin」的同源詞。

etymology.text: From Middle English buket, boket, partly from Old English bucc ("bucket, pitcher"; mod. dialectal buck), equivalent to bouk + -et; and partly from Anglo-Norman buket, buquet (“tub; pail”) (compare Norman boutchet, Norman bouquet), diminutive of Old French buc (“abdomen; object with a cavity”), from Vulgar Latin *būcus (compare Occitan and Catalan buc, Italian buco, buca (“hole, gap”)), from Frankish *būk (“belly, stomach”). Both the Old English and Frankish terms derive from Proto-Germanic *būka
etymology.native: 來自中古英語 buket、boket，部分源自古英語 bucc（「桶、水壺」；現代方言 buck），等於 bouk + -et；另一部分源自盎格魯-諾曼語 buket、buquet（「桶；桶狀物」），是古法語 buc（「腹部；有空腔的物體」）的縮小形式，源自 Vulgar Latin *būcus（比較奧克語與加泰羅尼亞語 buc、義大利語 buco、buca（「洞、空隙」）），而古英語與弗蘭克語詞源皆來自原始日耳曼語 *būka。

senses.definition: To go fast.
To exceed the speed limit.
To increase the rate at which something occurs.
To cause to make haste; to dispatch with celerity; to drive at full speed; hence, to hasten; to hurry.
To hasten to a conclusion; to expedite.
To be under the influence of stimulant drugs, especially amphetamines.
To succeed; to prosper, be lucky.
To help someone, to give them fortune; to aid or favour.
To be expedient.
To hurry to destruction; to put an end to; to ruin.
To wish success or good fortune to, in any undertaking, especially in setting out upon a journey.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Don't exceed the speed limit.
examples.translation: 不要超速。

examples.text: He was driving the car at full speed.
examples.translation: 他全速駕駛著。

examples.text: The driver was charged with speeding.
examples.translation: 司機被控超速駕駛。

examples.text: Ken was fined 7,000 yen for speeding.
examples.translation: 肯因超速被罰款7000日元。

examples.text: The policeman arrested him for speeding.
examples.translation: 他超速駕駛，被警察逮捕了。

examples.text: The car continued to put on speed.
examples.translation: 車子繼續加速。

etymology.text: From Middle English sped (“prosperity, good luck, quickness, success”), from Old English spēd (“success”), from Proto-West Germanic *spōdi (“prosperity, success”), from Proto-West Germanic *spōan, from Proto-Germanic *spōaną (“to prosper, succeed, be happy”), from Proto-Indo-European *speh₁- (“to prosper, turn out well”).

senses.definition: Something or someone that has been ruined.
The remains of something that has been severely damaged or worn down.
An event in which something is damaged through collision.
A shipwreck: an event in which a ship is heavily damaged or destroyed.
senses.native: 船難：船舶遭受嚴重損壞或毀滅的事件

senses.definition: Goods, etc. cast ashore by the sea after a shipwreck.
senses.native: 因船難而隨海浪沖上岸的貨物等

senses.definition: A large number of birds that have been brought to the ground, injured or dead, by extremely adverse weather.
senses.native: 因極端惡劣天氣而被擊落、受傷或死亡的鳥群

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: This car looks like a wreck.
examples.translation: 這輛車看起來像廢船一樣。

examples.text: My life has become a wreck.
examples.translation: 我的生活已變成一片混亂。

examples.text: A hundred people were hurt in a train wreck.
examples.translation: 一百多個人在一個火車事故中受了傷。

examples.text: A stewardess was rescued from the wreck.
examples.translation: 一名空姐從飛機殘骸中被救出來了。

examples.text: Driving on a slippery road can lead to a car wreck.
examples.translation: 在光滑的路上開車會導致車禍。

examples.text: The car was a rusty wreck.
examples.translation: 那輛車已經爛得不成樣子了。

etymology.text: From Middle English wrek, from Anglo-Norman wrek, from Old Norse *wrek (whence Norwegian rek, Icelandic rek, Swedish vrak, Danish vrag), from Proto-Germanic *wrekaną (“to pursue”, whence Old English wrecan (English wreak), Old Saxon wrekan, Old High German rëhhan, Gothic 𐍅𐍂𐌹𐌺𐌰𐌽 (wrikan)), from Proto-Indo-European *wreg- (“to track; to hunt; to follow”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 wrek，來自盎格魯諾曼語 wrek，再源自古諾斯語 *wrek（由此衍生出挪威語 rek、冰島語 rek、瑞典語 vrak、丹麥語 vrag），來自日耳曼語族原語 *wrekaną（「追趕」，由此衍生出古英語 wrecan、古薩克森語 wrekan、古高地德語 rëhhan、哥特語 𐍅𐍂𐌹𐌺𐌰𐌽），最終源自印歐語原語 *wreg-（「追蹤；獵捕；跟隨」）。

senses.definition: An act of stamping the foot, paw or hoof.
An indentation, imprint, or mark made by stamping.
A device for imprinting designs.
A small piece of paper, with a design and a face value, used to prepay postage or other dues such as tax or licence fees.
A small piece of paper bearing a design on one side and adhesive on the other, used to decorate letters or craft work.
A kind of heavy pestle, raised by water or steam power, for crushing ores.
Cast; form; character; distinguishing mark or sign; evidence.
A tattoo.
A single dose of lysergic acid diethylamide.

examples.text: Yoko is interested in collecting stamps.
examples.translation: 洋子有收集郵票的興趣。

examples.text: Her only hobby is collecting stamps.
examples.translation: 她唯一的興趣是集郵。

examples.text: His hobby is collecting old stamps.
examples.translation: 他的興趣愛好是收集舊郵票。

examples.text: My brother likes to collect stamps.
examples.translation: 我的兄弟喜歡集郵。

examples.text: John likes to trade stamps with his friends.
examples.translation: 約翰喜歡和朋友交換郵票。

examples.text: Don't forget to put a stamp on your letter.
examples.translation: 別忘了在你的信上貼張郵票。

etymology.text: From Middle English stampen (“to pound, crush”), from assumed Old English *stampian, variant of Old English stempan (“to crush, pound, pound in mortar, stamp”), from Proto-West Germanic *stampōn, *stampijan, from Proto-Germanic *stampōną, *stampijaną (“to trample, beat”), from Proto-Indo-European *stemb- (“to trample down”).

senses.definition: A fixed verse form of Italian origin consisting of fourteen lines that are typically five-foot iambics and rhyme according to one of a few prescribed schemes.

examples.text: You should read Shakespeare's sonnets.
examples.translation: 你應該讀莎士比亞的十四行詩。

examples.text: Mary wasn't interested in Tom's sonnet.
examples.translation: 瑪麗對湯姆的十四行詩不感興趣。

examples.text: Writing a haiku is easier than writing a sonnet.
examples.translation: 寫一首俳句比寫一首十四行詩容易。

examples.text: Shakespeare knew how to write a sonnet.
examples.translation: 莎士比亞懂得寫十四行詩。

examples.text: Tom invented his own form of sonnet.
examples.translation: 湯姆創作了他自己的十四行詩形式。

examples.text: A sonnet is framed poetry. It has beauty in form and expression.
examples.translation: 十四行詩是框構詩體，形式與表達皆具美感。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French sonnet, from Italian sonetto, from Old Occitan sonet (“a song”), diminutive of son (“song, sound”), from Latin sonus (“sound”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀法語sonnet，來自義大利sonetto，源自古奧克語sonet（「一首歌」），是son（「歌、聲音」）的縮小形式，來自拉丁語sonus（「聲音」）。

senses.definition: Quantity of countable things.
An abstract entity used to describe quantity.
A numeral: a symbol for a non-negative integer.
An element of one of several sets: natural numbers, integers, rational numbers, real numbers, complex numbers, and sometimes extensions such as hypercomplex numbers, etc.

Indicating the position of something in a list or sequence. Abbreviations: No or No., no or no. (in each case, sometimes written with a superscript "o", like Nº or №). The symbol "#" is also used in this manner.
A sequence of digits and letters used to register people, automobiles, and various other items.
Of a word or phrase, the state of being singular, dual or plural, shown by inflection.
A performance; especially, a single song or song and dance routine within a larger show.
A telephone number.
A group of people.
A person.
An outfit, particularly a stylish one.
A marijuana cigarette, or joint; also, a quantity of marijuana bought from a dealer.
A large amount, in contrast to a smaller amount; numerical preponderance.
An activity; assignment; job, as in cushy number.
Something that numbs.
Poetic metres; verses, rhymes.
An issue of a periodical publication.

examples.text: Number 26 is already reserved, sorry.
examples.translation: 26號已經有預約了。很抱歉。

examples.text: A number of famous artists live in Australia.
examples.translation: 許多著名的畫家居住在澳洲。

examples.text: What number bus do I take to get to Waikiki?
examples.translation: 我乘幾路車去懷基基？

examples.text: The tomato is subject to a number of diseases.
examples.translation: 番茄容易遭受很多病害。

examples.text: Could you tell me your name and your number?
examples.translation: 你能告訴我你的姓名和手機號碼嗎？

examples.text: A great number of citizens went into the army.
examples.translation: 許多老百姓加入了軍隊。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English number, nombre, numbre, noumbre, from Anglo-Norman noumbre, Old French nombre, from Latin numerus (“number”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *nem- (“to distribute, to give, to take”). Compare Saterland Frisian Nummer, Nuumer, West Frisian nûmer, Dutch nummer (“number”), German Nummer (“number”), Danish nummer (“number”), Swedish nummer (“number”), Icelandic númer (“number”). Displaced Middle English ȝetæl and rime; more at tell, tale and rhyme. Distantly relate
etymology.native: 承襲自中古英語（number、nombre），來自英法語（noumbre）、古法語（nombre），來自拉丁語（numerus）「數」，上溯至原始印歐語（*nem-）「分配」。與荷蘭語（nummer）、德語（Nummer）同源。

senses.definition: The act of storing goods; the state of being stored.
An object or place in which something is stored.
Any computer device, including such as a disk, on which data is stored for a longer term than main memory.
The price charged for storing goods.

examples.text: Your laptop's storage is almost full.
examples.translation: 你的筆記型電腦儲存空間幾乎滿了。

examples.text: Lukas was in the storage room.
examples.translation: 盧卡斯在儲藏室。

examples.text: My phone needs to have enough storage for my apps.
examples.translation: 我的手機需要足夠存儲空間來下載 App。

examples.text: William took Sandra to the food storage room.
examples.translation: 威廉帶桑德拉去食物儲藏室。

examples.text: There was no network inside the storage unit.
examples.translation: 儲藏單位內沒有網路。

examples.text: Where is the nuclear waste storage facility?
examples.translation: 核廢料儲存設施在哪裡？

etymology.text: From store + -age.
etymology.native: 來自 store + -age。

senses.definition: To put into storage; to store.

examples.text: Don't forget to take my things out of storage!

etymology.text: From store + -age.
etymology.native: 來自 store + -age。

senses.definition: The ability of the brain to record information or impressions with the facility of recalling them later, usually at will.
A record of a thing or an event stored and available for later use by an organism.
The part of a computer that stores variable executable code or data (RAM) or unalterable executable code or default data (ROM).
The time within which past events can be or are remembered.
Of a material, which returns to its original shape when heated.
Synonym of pelmanism (“memory card game”).
A memorial.
A term of venery for a social group of elephants, normally called a herd.

examples.text: He wishes to erase bad memories.
examples.translation: 他希望抹去不好的記憶。

examples.text: Liars must have a good memory.
examples.translation: 騙子們必須有好記性。

examples.text: You have a very good memory.
examples.translation: 你記性很好。

examples.text: Thank you for the memories.
examples.translation: 感謝那些回憶。

examples.text: Your memory isn't too good.
examples.translation: 您記性不太好。

examples.text: I'd like to find a way to improve my memory.
examples.translation: 我想找一種提升記憶力的方法。

etymology.text: From Anglo-Norman memorie, Old French memoire etc., from Latin memoria (“the faculty of remembering, remembrance, memory, a historical account”), from memor (“mindful, remembering”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)mer- (to remember), related to Ancient Greek μνήμη (mnḗmē, “memory”) μέρμερος (mérmeros, “anxious”), μέριμνα (mérimna, “care, thought”), Old English ġemimor (“mindful, remembering”). More at mimmer. Doublet of memoir and memoria. Displaced native Old English myne (whence English min) and

senses.definition: Fixtures, equipment, fasteners, tools, and devices used for general-purpose construction and repair of a structure or object. Also such equipment as sold as stock by a store of the same name, e.g. hardware store.
The part of a computer that is fixed and cannot be altered without replacement or physical modification; motherboard, expansion cards, etc.
Electronic equipment.
Metal implements.
Equipment.
A firearm.
Medals or trophies.

examples.text: He'll never find that hardware store.
Santiago visited the hardware store.
Hardware stores are open on Sundays.
He went to the hardware store to get a shovel.
There is a hardware store not far from here.
Apple tried hard to design beautiful hardware.

etymology.text: From Middle English hardware; equivalent to hard + -ware; attested since the mid-15th century.

senses.definition: Anything that raises or uplifts.
A permanent construction with a built-in platform or cab that can be raised and lowered, used to transport people and goods, as between different floors of a building.
A silo used for storing wheat, corn or other grain (grain elevator).
A control surface of an aircraft responsible for controlling the pitching motion of the machine.
A dental instrument used to pry up ("elevate") teeth in difficult extractions, or depressed portions of bone.
Any muscle that serves to raise a part of the body, such as the leg or the eye.
A type of shoe having an insert lift to make the wearer appear taller.

examples.text: Smoking isn't allowed inside the elevator.
examples.translation: 電梯內不准吸煙。

examples.text: I smell smoke in the elevator.
examples.translation: 我在電梯裡嗅到煙味。

examples.text: Our new home has an elevator.
examples.translation: 我們的新家有一臺電梯。

examples.text: Tom never takes the elevator.
examples.translation: 湯姆從不坐電梯。

examples.text: The elevator's out again.
examples.translation: 電梯又壞了。

examples.text: No worries, I will send you to the elevator.
examples.translation: 沒關係，送你到電梯口。

etymology.text: From elevate + -or.

senses.definition: Alternative spelling of savour.

examples.text: Every morning I make coffee and savor its aroma.
examples.translation: 每天早晨我煮咖啡，品味它的香氣。

examples.text: Savor the soup.
examples.translation: 品嚐這碗湯。

examples.text: Savor the rich aroma of freshly baked bread.
examples.translation: 品嚐剛烤好的麵包濃郁香氣。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Savor the quiet moments before bedtime.
examples.translation: 享受睡前那寧靜的片刻。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Savor the taste of your favorite dessert.
examples.translation: 品嚐你最愛甜點的滋味。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Savor the delicate fragrance of jasmine tea.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

senses.definition: Alternative spelling of savour.

examples.text: You should savor this moment.
examples.translation: 你應該好好享受這一刻。

examples.text: I like to savor raspberry ice cream.
examples.translation: 我喜歡慢慢品嚐樹莓冰淇淋。

examples.text: They sipped their tea slowly, savoring the moment.

senses.definition: To receive pleasure or satisfaction from something.
To have the use or benefit of something.
To be satisfied or receive pleasure; to have fun.
To have sexual intercourse with.

examples.text: Robert enjoyed talking with his girlfriend.
examples.translation: 羅伯特喜歡和他的女朋友談話。

examples.text: We enjoyed watching the baseball game.
examples.translation: 我們喜歡看棒球比賽。

examples.text: Please enjoy yourself at the dance.
examples.translation: 請盡情地跳舞。

examples.text: The boy enjoyed painting a picture.
examples.translation: 這個男孩喜歡繪畫。

examples.text: Did you enjoy your winter holidays?
examples.translation: 你寒假過得愉快嗎？

examples.text: My brother seems to enjoy himself at college.
examples.translation: 我弟弟似乎在大學過得很愉快。

etymology.text: From Middle English enjoyen, from Old French enjoier, anjoier, enjoer (“to give joy, receive with joy, rejoice”), equivalent to en- + joy.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（enjoyen），來自古法語（enjoier、enjoer）「使喜悅、欣然接受」，相當於（en-）加（joy）。

senses.definition: To bathe in warmth; to be exposed to pleasant heat.
To expose oneself to heat, especially sunlight, in order to raise body temperature, as a form of thermoregulation.
senses.native: 在陽光下曝曬以提升體溫，作為一種體溫調節方式

senses.definition: To take great pleasure or satisfaction; to feel warmth or happiness.
senses.native: 感到極大的快樂或滿足；感到溫暖或幸福

examples.text: The turtles basked in the sun.
examples.translation: 烏龜們在陽光下曬太陽。

examples.text: Mary is basking in the sun.
examples.translation: 瑪麗正沐浴在陽光中。

examples.text: I cannot bask in the sun. It's too hot now.
examples.translation: 我無法在陽光下曝曬，現在太熱了。

examples.text: David basked in the sun, enjoying the view.
examples.translation: 戴維德沐浴在陽光中，欣賞著景色。

examples.text: We lay blissfully basking on the beach.
examples.translation: 我們愉悅地躺在海灘上曬太陽。

examples.text: Have you ever basked in the sun of the Sahara desert?
examples.translation: 你曾經沐浴過撒哈拉沙漠的陽光嗎？

relations.native: 沐浴於溫暖之中；暴露在宜人的熱度下

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English basken, from Old Norse baðask (“to take a bath”, literally “to bathe oneself”), mediopassive form from underlying baða (“to bathe”) + sik (“oneself”), from Proto-Germanic *baþōną and *sek. Doublet of English bathe.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 basken，來自古諾斯語 baðask（「洗澡」，字面意義為「自我沐浴」），是介動詞形式，由底層詞根 baða（「洗澡」）加上 sik（「自己」）組成。

senses.definition: Any tropical climbing orchid of the genus Vanilla (especially Vanilla planifolia), bearing podlike fruit yielding an extract used in flavoring food or in perfumes.
The fruit or bean of the vanilla plant.
The extract of the fruit of the vanilla plant.
The distinctive fragrant flavour/flavor characteristic of vanilla extract.
Any artificially produced homologue of vanilla extract, principally vanillin produced from lignin from the paper industry or from petrochemicals.
A yellowish-white colour, like that of vanilla ice cream.
Someone who is not into fetishism.
An unmodded version of a game.
A white person.

examples.text: Sugar-free vanilla latte for Angie.
I'd like two vanilla ice creams.
I'd like some vanilla ice cream.
She made a vanilla chocolate cake for four people.
examples.translation: 她做了一個四人份的巧克力香草蛋糕。

examples.text: Do you prefer vanilla or chocolate ice cream?
The vanilla in my chicken soup is sickening.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Spanish vainilla, a diminutive form of vaina (“pod”). "Plain" senses derive from the perceived plainness of vanilla ice cream.

senses.definition: To acquire, or attempt to acquire knowledge or an ability to do something.
To attend a course or other educational activity.
To gain knowledge from a bad experience so as to improve.
To study.
To come to know; to become informed of; to find out.
To teach.

examples.text: Beginners should learn spoken English first.
examples.translation: 初學者應先學習口說英語。

examples.text: Learning a foreign language is difficult.
examples.translation: 學習外語是困難的。

examples.text: Learning English well is not difficult.
examples.translation: 學好英文不難。

examples.text: You should learn to restrain yourself.
examples.translation: 你應該學習控制自己的情緒。

examples.text: The students are all learning English.
examples.translation: 同學們都在學英文。

examples.text: We must learn to live in harmony with nature.
examples.translation: 我們必須學會與自然和諧共處。

etymology.text: From Middle English lernen (“to learn", also, "to teach"”), from Old English leornian (“to learn", rarely also, "to teach”), from Proto-West Germanic *liʀnōn, from Proto-Germanic *lizaną, from Proto-Indo-European *(le-)lóys-e, stative from the root *leys- (“track, furrow, trace, trail”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（lernen）「學習；也指教」，來自古英語（leornian），再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*lizaną），最終來自原始印歐語詞根（*leys-）「軌跡、溝痕」。

senses.definition: To look at on all sides or in all its aspects; to view or consider with continued attention; to regard with deliberate care; to meditate on; to study, ponder, or consider.
To consider as a possibility.

examples.text: She will contemplate the painting for hours.
examples.translation: 她會凝視那幅畫好幾個小時。

senses.definition: A small group of individuals in very close proximity to one another.
A session in which a group of journalists assemble in an informal, dense cluster to question a person of interest.
A brief meeting of all the players from one team that are on the field with the purpose of planning the following play.
A hesitation during play to think about one's next move.
A dense and disorderly crowd.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Penguins often huddle together to keep warm.
examples.translation: 企鵝們常聚在一起保暖。

examples.text: A huddle of frightened women.
examples.translation: 一群驚慌失措的女性。

examples.text: Let's huddle together — it's cold!
examples.translation: 我們一起緊緊靠在一起吧——太冷了！

etymology.text: From Middle English *hudelen, alteration (due to hudels, hidels (“hiding place”), see hiddle) of *huderen, hoderen (“to cover; press together; huddle”), a frequentative form of Middle English huden, hiden (“to hide”), equivalent to hide + -le and/or hide + -er. Compare Low German huderken (“to brood; coddle; nurse; lull children to sleep”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 *hudelen，是 *huderen、hoderen（意為「覆蓋；壓近；聚攏」）的變體，源自中古英語 huden、hiden（意為「隱藏」）的頻繁形式，等同於 hide + -le 和/或 hide + -er。可與低德語 huderken（意為「孵育；撫育；哄睡孩子」）相比。

senses.definition: To crowd together.
To curl one's legs up to the chest and keep one's arms close to the torso; to crouch; to assume a position similar to that of an embryo in the womb.
To get together and discuss a topic.
To form a huddle.
To crowd (things) together; to mingle confusedly; to assemble without order or system.
To do, make, or put, in haste or roughly; hence, to do imperfectly; usually with a following preposition or adverb (huddle on, huddle up, huddle together).
To hesitate during play while thinking about one's next move.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: We huddled together and talked about all sorts of things into the wee hours of the night.
examples.translation: 我們緊緊靠在一起，聊著各種話，聊到深夜。

examples.text: The sheep huddled together seeking warmth.
examples.translation: 羊們聚在一起尋求溫暖。

etymology.text: From Middle English *hudelen, alteration (due to hudels, hidels (“hiding place”), see hiddle) of *huderen, hoderen (“to cover; press together; huddle”), a frequentative form of Middle English huden, hiden (“to hide”), equivalent to hide + -le and/or hide + -er. Compare Low German huderken (“to brood; coddle; nurse; lull children to sleep”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 *hudelen，是 *huderen、hoderen（意為「覆蓋；壓近；聚攏」）的變體，源自中古英語 huden、hiden（意為「隱藏」）的頻繁形式，等同於 hide + -le 和/或 hide + -er。可與低德語 huderken（意為「孵育；撫育；哄睡孩子」）相比。

senses.definition: The act of consulting together formally; serious conversation or discussion; interchange of views.
A multilateral diplomatic negotiation.
A formal event where scientists or other scholars present their research results in speeches, workshops, posters or by other means.
An event organized by a for-profit or non-profit organization to discuss a pressing issue, such as a new product, market trend or government regulation, with a range of speakers.
A group of sports teams that play each other on a regular basis.
A constituent tournament of a sports league in a given season.
A stated meeting of preachers and others, invested with authority to take cognizance of ecclesiastical matters.
A voluntary association of Congregational churches of a district; the district in which such churches are.
A talk or lecture, (Catholicism) especially when given as part of a retreat.
An autumn cultivar of the European pear Pyrus communis.
The act of comparing two or more things together; comparison.

examples.text: The conference will end tomorrow.
examples.translation: 會議明天就結束了。

examples.text: The conference closed at five.
examples.translation: 會議在五點鐘結束。

examples.text: He is in conference.
examples.translation: 他正在開會。

examples.text: He represented our company at the conference.
examples.translation: 他代表我們公司出席了會議。

examples.text: Tom is waiting for you in the conference room.
examples.translation: 湯姆在會議室等你。

examples.text: Everyone chose him to speak at the conference.
examples.translation: 大家推舉他到大會發言。

etymology.text: From Middle French conférence, from Medieval Latin cōnferentia, from Latin cōnferēns, omitting several steps, from con- + ferō.

senses.definition: The act of mixing cards or mah-jong tiles so as to randomize them.
The act of reordering anything, such as music tracks in a media player.
senses.native: 任意事物的重新排列，例如媒體播放器中的音樂曲目

senses.definition: An instance of walking without lifting one's feet.
senses.native: 不抬起腳走路的一次動作

senses.definition: A rhythm commonly used in blues music, consisting of a series of triplet notes with the middle note missing, so that it sounds like a long note followed by a short note, and suggests a walker dragging one foot.
senses.native: 藍調音樂中常見的一種節奏，由一系列缺少中間音符的三連音組成，聽起來像長音符後跟短音符，並暗示著拖著一隻腳行走的人

senses.definition: A dance move in which the foot is scuffed back and forth across the floor.
senses.native: 一種舞蹈動作，將腳在地板上前後摩擦移動

senses.definition: A trick; an artifice; an evasion.
senses.native: 一個花招；一種手段；一種迴避

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Please shuffle the cards carefully.
examples.translation: 請仔細洗牌。

examples.text: He made a real mess of the last shuffle.
examples.translation: 他把最後一次洗牌弄得一團糟。

examples.text: The sad young girl left with a tired shuffle.
examples.translation: 那個悲傷的少女帶著疲憊的拖曳步離開了。

examples.text: The gambler's artful shuffle randomized the deck, rendering any previous sequence utterly futile.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

relations.native: 兩種或兩種以上物質混合後的結果；混合物

etymology.text: Originally the same word as scuffle, and properly a frequentative of shove.
etymology.native: 原本與「scuffle」是同一個詞，本意是「shove」的頻繁動作形式。

senses.definition: A rush or hurry, especially making use of the limbs against a surface.
An emergency defensive air force mission to intercept attacking enemy aircraft.
senses.native: 空軍緊急攔截敵機的任務（緊急起飛）

senses.definition: A motocross race.
Any frantic period of competitive activity.
senses.native: 任何激烈的競爭活動時期（混戰）

senses.definition: An impromptu maneuver or run by a quarterback, attempting to gain yardage or avoid being tackled behind the line of scrimmage.
senses.native: 四分衛臨時跑動或突破，以爭取碼數或避開擒抱（自由跑動）

senses.definition: A statistic used in assessing a player's short game, consisting of a chip or putt from under 50 yards away that results in requiring one putt or less on the green.
senses.native: 衡量短桿技術的統計：距離果嶺 50 碼內的切球或推桿，一桿或更少推進洞（短桿救球）

senses.definition: A variant of golf in which each player in a team tees off on each hole, and the players decide which shot was best. Every player then plays their second shot from within a club length of where the best ball has come to rest, and the procedure is repeated until the hole is finished.
senses.native: 高爾夫球變化賽制：每隊員每洞都開球，選出最佳球後，其餘人自該球附近一桿竿長內擊球，循環至完成該洞（最佳球）

senses.definition: A dish (meal) involving scrambled eggs and a hodgepodge of complementary ingredients, usually closer to a casserole than to an omelette.
senses.native: 炒蛋與多種配料混合的菜餚，比較接近砂鍋而非歐姆蛋（炒蛋燉菜）

senses.definition: A venue where enslaved people were auctioned during the Atlantic slave trade.
senses.native: 大西洋奴隸貿易中拍賣奴隸的場所（奴隸市場）

examples.text: The scramble for Africa was the last wave of colonialism.
examples.translation: 對非洲的爭奪戰是殖民主義的最後一波浪潮。

etymology.text: Origin uncertain. Perhaps from earlier dialectal scramble, scrammel (“to collect or rake together with the hands”), from scramb (“to pull or scrape together with the hands”) + -le (frequentative suffix) (compare Dutch schrammen (“to graze, brush, scratch”)); or alternatively from a nasalised form of scrabble (“to scrape or scratch quickly”).
etymology.native: 起源不明，或許來自早期方言 scramble 或 scrammel（用手收集或耙起），由 scramb（用手拉或刮）加上 -le（表示動作頻繁的詞綴）組成；或另從 scrabble 的鼻化形式而來。

senses.definition: Conveying color, as opposed to shades of gray.

examples.text: Gold is similar in color to brass.
examples.translation: 金的顏色和黃銅很相似。

etymology.text: From Middle English colour, color, borrowed from Anglo-Norman colur, from Old French colour, color, from Latin color. Doublet of couleur.
etymology.native: 來自中古英語 colour，源自盎格魯-諾曼語 colur，來自古法語 couleur，源自拉丁語 color。是 couleur 的同義詞。

senses.definition: To give something color.
To cause (a pipe, especially a meerschaum) to take on a brown or black color, by smoking.
senses.native: （美）（吸菸）使（菸斗，尤指海泡石菸斗）燻成棕黑色

senses.definition: To apply colors to the areas within the boundaries of a line drawing using colored markers or crayons.
senses.native: （美）用彩色筆或蠟筆為線條圍成的區域上色

senses.definition: To become red through increased blood flow.
To affect without completely changing.
senses.native: （美）在不完全改變的情況下產生影響

senses.definition: To attribute a quality to; to portray (as).
To assign colors to the vertices of a graph (or the regions of a map) so that no two vertices connected by an edge (regions sharing a border) have the same color.
senses.native: 為圖的頂點（或地圖的區域）著色，使相鄰者顏色不同

senses.definition: To affect the quality of a speech sound, especially a vowel.
senses.native: （美）影響語音（尤指元音）的音質

examples.text: Meg colored the picture.
examples.translation: 瑪格為圖畫上色。

etymology.text: From Middle English colour, color, borrowed from Anglo-Norman colur, from Old French colour, color, from Latin color. Doublet of couleur.
etymology.native: 來自中古英語 colour，源自盎格魯-諾曼語 colur，來自古法語 couleur，源自拉丁語 color。是 couleur 的同義詞。

senses.definition: To bring something out of shape, to misshape.
To become misshapen.
To give a false or misleading account of; pervert.

examples.text: The pictures were getting more distorted.
Some newspapers distorted the news.
I never distorted anyone's words.
He has a habit of distorting the facts a bit.
Tom talked into the fan to distort his voice.
Get the facts first. You can distort them later.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin distortum, past participle of distorqueō (“to twist, torture, distort”).

senses.definition: To have an effect on by using gentle or subtle action; to exert an influence upon; to modify, bias, or sway; to persuade or induce.
To exert, make use of one's influence.
To cause to flow in or into; infuse; instill.

examples.text: Such toys have a bad influence on children.
examples.translation: 這種玩具會對小孩子帶來不良的影響。

examples.text: Such magazines have a great influence on children.
examples.translation: 這些雜誌對小孩的影響很大。

examples.text: Many TV programs have a bad influence on children.
examples.translation: 許多電視節目對兒童有不良的影響。

examples.text: She's highly influenced by current trends.
examples.translation: 她對當下的流行很敏感。

examples.text: I think my living with you has influenced your way of living.
examples.translation: 我覺得我和你一起住影響了你生活的方式。

examples.text: A good programmer will influence everyone around him.
examples.translation: 一個好的程式設計師會影響他身邊的每一個人。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English influence, from Old French influence, borrowed from Medieval Latin īnfluentia, from Latin īnfluēns + -ia. Doublet of influenza.
etymology.native: 承襲自中古英語（influence），來自古法語（influence），借自中世紀拉丁語（īnfluentia），由拉丁語（īnfluēns）加（-ia）組成。與（influenza）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: To colour with dye, or as if with dye.

examples.text: The cloth was dyed bright red.
examples.translation: 布被染成鮮紅。

examples.text: Tom dyed his hair brown.
examples.translation: 湯姆把他的頭髮染成了褐色。

examples.text: At dusk, the sky was dyed with purple light.
examples.translation: 黃昏時分，天空染上了紫色的光。

examples.text: It's become a hassle to keep on dyeing my hair.
examples.translation: 一直染髮太麻煩了。

examples.text: My boyfriend wants to dye his hair purple.
examples.translation: 我的男朋友想把頭發染紫。

examples.text: Mary prefers to dye her hair blonde.
examples.translation: 瑪麗更想把頭髮染成金色。

relations.native: 因灑漏或其他接觸液體或物質而變色

etymology.text: From Middle English deye, from Old English dēah, dēag (“color, hue, dye”), from Proto-West Germanic *daugu (“color, shade”), from *daugan (“to conceal, be dark”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewh₂- (“to smoke, raise dust, camouflage”).

senses.definition: Alternative form of black and white (when used attributively).

examples.text: Black-and-white TVs are obsolete.
It's a black-and-white picture.
Will black-and-white work?
Rodrigo was watching a black-and-white movie.
Tom has a black-and-white television.
They were watching an old black-and-white movie on TV.

senses.definition: A great attention and concern from someone or something; intellectual curiosity.
The price paid for obtaining, or price received for providing, money or goods in a credit transaction, calculated as a fraction of the amount or value of what was borrowed.
An involvement, claim, right, share, stake in or link with a financial, business, or other undertaking or endeavor.
Any excess over and above an exact equivalent
Attention that is given to or received from someone or something.
Advantage, welfare, or something that serves it.
Something which, or someone whom, one is interested in.
Condition or quality of exciting concern or being of importance.
The persons and companies interested in any particular business or measure, taken collectively.
A genre of factual short films, generally more amusing than informative, especially those not covered by a more specific genre label.
Injury, or compensation for injury; damages.

examples.text: Tom has lost his interest in studying French.
examples.translation: 湯姆已經失去學習法語的興趣。

examples.text: What is your field of study, your domain of inquiry, your major interest?
examples.translation: 你的研究領域、探究範疇、主要興趣是什麼？

examples.text: Accountability is in the interest of the Government and the citizenry alike.
examples.translation: 問責制度對政府和人民都有好處。

examples.text: Our bank offers borrowers an annual interest of 5%.
examples.translation: 本行提供借款人年利率百分之五。

examples.text: She has an interest in the proceedings, and all stakeholders' interests must be protected.
examples.translation: 她和這些訴訟有利害關係，所有利害關係人的權益都必須受到保護。

examples.text: If economic globalization is inevitable, it should primarily serve humanity rather than the interests of trans-national corporations.
examples.translation: 如果全球化無法避免，應該首先為人服務而不是為跨國公司的利益服務。

etymology.text: From Middle English interest, from Old French interesse and interest (French intérêt), from Medieval Latin interesse, from Latin interesse.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（interest），來自古法語（interesse、interest），來自中世紀拉丁語（interesse），再來自拉丁語（interesse）「在中間、有關係」。

senses.definition: The outer protective layer of the body of any animal, including of a human.
The skin and fur of an individual animal used by humans for clothing, upholstery, etc.
A set of resources that modifies the appearance and/or layout of the graphical user interface of a computer program.
The outer surface covering much of the wings and fuselage of an aircraft.
A drink of whisky served hot.
A member of the team not wearing shirts, in a shirts and skins game.
The outer protective layer of the fruit of a plant.
A congealed layer on the surface of a liquid.
An alternate appearance (texture map or geometry) for a character model in a video game.
senses.native: （遊戲）造型，角色模型的替代外觀

senses.definition: Rolling paper for cigarettes.
A subgroup of Australian aboriginal people.
senses.native: （澳洲原住民）皮族，親屬分類的一支

senses.definition: Bare flesh, particularly bare breasts.
A vessel made of skin, used for holding liquids.
senses.native: 皮囊，用皮革做成、盛裝液體的容器

senses.definition: That part of a sail, when furled, which remains on the outside and covers the whole.
senses.native: （帆船）帆面，收帆時位於外側、覆蓋整個帆的部分

senses.definition: The covering, as of planking or iron plates, outside the framing, forming the sides and bottom of a vessel; the shell; also, a lining inside the framing.
senses.native: 船殼的外層覆蓋（如木板或鐵板），構成船的兩側與底部；亦指骨架內側的襯板

senses.definition: A person; chap.
A purse.
