examples.text: The skin of peaches bruises easily.
examples.translation: 桃子的皮很容易破。

senses.definition: An aristocrat; one of aristocratic blood.
A medieval gold coin of England in the 14th and 15th centuries, usually valued at 6s 8d.

examples.text: He springs from a noble family.
examples.translation: 他出身於名門望族。

examples.text: They should have a noble mind.
examples.translation: 他們應具備高尚的品格。

examples.text: Giraffes are noble herbivores.
examples.translation: 長頸鹿是高貴的植食性動物。

examples.text: She looks as noble as if she were a princess.
examples.translation: 她看起來像公主般高貴。

examples.text: You speak in a very noble and courteous way.
examples.translation: 你說話方式非常禮貌且莊重。

examples.text: Your sister looks as noble as if she were a princess.
examples.translation: 你妹妹看上去那麼高貴，就像是個公主一樣。

etymology.text: From Middle English noble, from Old French noble, borrowed from Latin nōbilis (“knowable, known, well-known, famous, celebrated, high-born, of noble birth, excellent”), from nōscere, gnōscere (“to know”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 noble，來自古法文 noble，借自拉丁文 nōbilis（意為「可被知曉、知名、著名、受人推崇、出身貴族、卓越」），源自拉丁文 nōscere、gnōscere（意為「知道」）

senses.definition: Having honorable qualities; having moral eminence and freedom from anything petty, mean or dubious in conduct and character.
Grand; stately; magnificent; splendid.
Of exalted rank; of or relating to the nobility; distinguished from the masses by birth, station, or title; highborn.
Of an element, unreactive.

Belonging to a class of grape cultivars traditionally considered most favorable for winemaking, usually encompassing the six: Merlot, Pinot Noir, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon blanc, Chardonnay, and Riesling.
Both isohedral and isogonal.

examples.text: He made a noble effort.
examples.translation: 他做出了高貴的努力。

examples.text: He is a noble man who would never put his family in jeopardy.

etymology.text: From Middle English noble, from Old French noble, borrowed from Latin nōbilis (“knowable, known, well-known, famous, celebrated, high-born, of noble birth, excellent”), from nōscere, gnōscere (“to know”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 noble，來自古法文 noble，借自拉丁文 nōbilis（意為「可被知曉、知名、著名、受人推崇、出身貴族、卓越」），源自拉丁文 nōscere、gnōscere（意為「知道」）

senses.definition: A peer; an aristocrat; ranks range from baron to king to emperor.

examples.text: He's a nobleman.
examples.translation: 他是一位貴族。

examples.text: A count is a nobleman, a marquess too.
examples.translation: 伯爵也是貴族，侯爵亦然。

examples.text: I see a nobleman and a noblewoman.
examples.translation: 我見到一位貴族和一位貴婦。

examples.text: A canopy is a roof, while a marquess is a nobleman.
examples.translation: 天篷是屋頂，侯爵則是貴族。

examples.text: But these jovial sounds fell sadly on the ear of the ruined nobleman.
examples.translation: 但這歡愉的聲音卻令那位破落貴族聽來倍感悲傷。

examples.text: I know that my young nobleman will perfectly imitate the grace, voice, bearing, and gestures of a noblewoman.
examples.translation: 我知道我那年輕的貴族將完美地模仿貴婦的風度、嗓音、儀態與肢體動作。

etymology.text: From noble + man.
etymology.native: 此詞由「尊貴」與「男子」組合而成。

senses.definition: Lower in rank, status, or quality.
Of low rank, standard or quality.
senses.native: 等級、標準或品質較低的

senses.definition: (of a court or tribunal) Susceptible to having its decisions overturned by a higher court.
senses.native: （法庭）判決可能被上級法院推翻的

senses.definition: Denoting goods or services which are in greater demand during a recession than in a boom, for example second-hand clothes.
senses.native: （經濟）低檔的，衰退時需求高於繁榮時期的商品，如二手衣物

senses.definition: Situated further below (another part of the body), a direction that in humans corresponds to caudad.
senses.native: （解剖）位於另一部位下方的，人體中對應尾側的方向

senses.definition: Situated in a relatively low posterior or ventral position in a quadrupedal body.
senses.native: （四足動物）位於較低的後方或腹側位置的

senses.definition: Situated below some other organ (said of a calyx when free from the ovary, and therefore below it, or of an ovary with an adherent and therefore inferior calyx).
On the side of a flower which is next to the bract.
Printed in subscript.
Below the horizon.
Nearer to the Sun than the Earth is.
senses.native: （天文）內行星的，比地球更接近太陽的

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: You think that your language is inferior.

Causing physical or mental repulsion; horrid; disgusting.
senses.native: 令人作嘔的、卑劣可惡的

examples.text: What Gustavo was doing was vile.
That's a vile falsehood.
He shares the most vile things on Facebook.
You know, Tom, that's really a vile thing!
The vile lizard wants to eat your eyes and ears!
Wisdom and goodness to the vile seem vile.

etymology.text: From Middle English vile, vyle, vyl, from Anglo-Norman ville, Old French vil, vile, from Latin vīlis.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語，來自盎格魯諾曼語與古法語「卑賤的」，來自拉丁語「廉價的、卑劣的」。

senses.definition: Having worth, merit, or value.
Admirable or honourable.
Deserving, or having sufficient worth.
Suited; suitable; befitting.

examples.text: Rome is worthy of a visit.
Tom isn't worthy of you.
I am not worthy of this.
From hand to mouth will never make a worthy man.
The problem is worthy of being remembered.
Your proposal is worthy of being considered.
examples.translation: 你的建議值得考慮。

etymology.text: From Middle English worthy, wurthi, from Old English *weorþiġ (“worthy”), equivalent to worth + -y. Cognate with Dutch waardig (“worthy”), Middle Low German werdig (“worthy”), German würdig (“worthy”), Swedish värdig (“worthy”), Icelandic verðugur (“worthy”).

senses.definition: See-through, clear; having the property that light passes through it almost undisturbed, such that one can see through it clearly.
Open, public; having the property that theories and practices are publicly visible, thereby reducing the chance of corruption.
Obvious; readily apparent; easy to see or understand.
Of a graphical image or animated GIF, having parts that allow the background to show through.
Having the property of transparency, i.e. sufficiently accurate that the compressed result is perceptually indistinguishable from the uncompressed input.
Not noticeable because it happens automatically or in the background; invisible.

examples.text: Algerian banks have to be transparent.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞銀行必須透明。

examples.text: The glass is fragile and transparent.
examples.translation: 這玻璃易碎且透明。

examples.text: Algeria needs a transparent electoral system.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞需要透明的選舉制度。

examples.text: It's my goal to be as transparent as possible.
examples.translation: 我目標是盡可能透明。

examples.text: Algeria's leadership needs to be transparent.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞的領導層必須透明。

examples.text: Many fish have evolved to have transparent skin.
examples.translation: 許多魚演化出透明皮膚。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Medieval Latin trānspārēns, trānspārēntis (“transparent”), present participle of transpareō, from Latin trans + pareō. Displaced native Old English þurhsīene.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Medieval Latin trānspārēns, trānspārēntis (“transparent”), present participle of transpareō, from Latin trans + pareō. Displaced native Old English þurhsīene.
etymology.native: 此詞源自中世紀拉丁語 trānspārēns，為 transpareō 的現在分詞，來自拉丁語 trans + pareō；原為古英語 þurhsīene。

senses.definition: Calm, peaceful, unruffled.
Without worry or anxiety; unaffected by disturbance.

senses.native: 清澈透明（如天空）；明朗；無遮蔽

examples.text: Ah! How serene is this temple!
examples.translation: 啊！這座廟宇真寧靜啊！

examples.text: The weather is serene.
examples.translation: 天氣很寧靜。

examples.text: The sky is serene.
examples.translation: 天空很寧靜。

examples.text: There's no denying that he's a serene child.
examples.translation: 無法否認他是一個非常安詳的孩子。

examples.text: Greetings and may your morning be serene!
examples.translation: 問候您，祝您早晨寧靜美好！

examples.text: The night was serene, the sky a sea of velvety black.
examples.translation: 夜晚寧靜，天空如絲絨般的漆黑大海。

etymology.text: From Middle English, borrowed from Latin serēnus (“clear, cloudless, untroubled”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語，借自拉丁語 serēnus（「清澈、無雲、安寧」）。

senses.definition: Allowing light to pass through, but diffusing it.
Clear, lucid, or transparent.

examples.text: The teacup was almost translucent.
examples.translation: 那個茶杯幾乎是半透明的。

examples.text: This teacup is almost translucent.

examples.translation: 持續攪拌，直到溶液變成半透明為止。

etymology.text: From Latin trānslūcentem, accusative of trānslūcēns, present participle of trānslūcēre.
etymology.native: 源於拉丁語 trānslūcentem，trānslūcēre 的現在分詞。

senses.definition: Of an event, situation, etc.: to appear or happen again, especially repeatedly.
Of a disease or symptom: to happen again, especially repeatedly or after a remission or an apparent recovery.
Of a memory, thought, etc.: to come to the mind again.
Synonym of recurse (“to execute a procedure recursively”).
Often in the form recurring following a number: of a numeral or group of numerals in a decimal fraction: to repeat indefinitely.
To speak, think, or write about something again; to go back or return to a memory, a subject, etc.
Followed by to, or (Scotland, obsolete) on or upon: to have recourse to someone or something for assistance, support, etc.; to appeal, to resort, to turn to.
Followed by into or to: to go to a place again; to return.
Followed by into or to: To go back to doing an activity, or to using a thing; to return.
Followed by to: to go to a place; to resort.
Followed by from: to move or run back from something; to recede, to withdraw.

examples.text: Tom had recurring nightmares about it.
examples.translation: 湯姆經常做關於它的惡夢。

examples.text: I have recurring nightmares about it.
examples.translation: 我經常做關於它的惡夢。

examples.text: I have recurring dreams about Tom.
examples.translation: 我經常做關於湯姆的夢。

examples.text: Did you ever have a recurring dream?
examples.translation: 你有過一個你會重複做的夢嗎？

examples.text: Dan has been troubled by recurring nightmares.
examples.translation: 丹經常被惡夢困擾。

examples.text: This is a recurring issue in many projects.
examples.translation: 這在許多專案中都是持續出現的問題。

etymology.text: Learned borrowing from Latin recurrō (“to hurry or run back; to return, revert”), from re- (prefix meaning ‘back, backwards’) + currō (“to hasten, hurry; to move, travel; to run”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱers- (“to run”)).
etymology.native: 「回」是從拉丁語 recurrō 借來的，意思是「急著跑回去」或「返回」，由 re-（表示「往回」）+ currō（意思是「急著跑」或「奔跑」）組成，而 currō 最初源自印歐語系的 *ḱers-（意思是「奔跑」）。

senses.definition: To do or say again (and again).
To refill (a prescription).
To happen again; recur.
To echo the words of (a person).
To strike the hours, as a watch does.
To repay or refund (an excess received).
To call in a previous artillery fire mission with the same ammunition and method either on the coordinates or adjusted either because destruction of the target was insufficient or missed.
To commit fraud in an election by voting more than once for the same candidate.
To make trial of again; to undergo or encounter again.

examples.text: Excuse me, could you repeat that?
examples.translation: 不好意思，您可以再說一遍嗎？

examples.text: Could you repeat that, please?
examples.translation: 能不能請你重複一下？

examples.text: The teacher made me repeat the sentence.
examples.translation: 老師讓我重複了這句話。

examples.text: I'm repeating it for you one last time.
examples.translation: 我再給你重複最後一遍。

etymology.text: From Middle English repeten, from Old French repeter, from Latin repetō, from the prefix re- (“again”) + petō (“to attack, beseech”).

senses.definition: To step or turn aside; to deviate; to swerve; especially, to turn aside from the main subject of attention, or course of argument, in writing or speaking.
To turn aside from the right path; to transgress; to offend.

examples.text: I'm sorry, I digress.
examples.translation: 抱歉，我跑題了。

examples.text: But I digress.
examples.translation: 但我跑題了。

examples.text: After digressing, he returned to the subject.

examples.translation: 你容易跑題。

examples.translation: Tom 幾次都跑離了主題。

examples.text: Resist the temptation to digress.
examples.translation: 不要有跑題的念頭。

etymology.text: From Latin digressum, past participle of digredi.
etymology.native: 此詞源於拉丁語的 digressum，是動詞 digredi 的分詞形式。

senses.definition: To occur or take place.
To do or occur by chance or unexpectedly.
To encounter by chance.
To become popular or trendy.
To happen to; to befall.

examples.text: There is always something happening here.
examples.translation: 這裡總有一些事情在發生。

examples.text: Don't you know what happened yesterday?
examples.translation: 你不知道昨天發生了甚麼事嗎？

examples.text: I can't change what happened yesterday.
examples.translation: 我沒法改變昨天發生的事情。

examples.text: Let's forget about what happened today.
examples.translation: 忘了今天的事兒吧。

examples.text: What happened? The car's slowing down.
examples.translation: 發生了什麼事？車子慢下來了。

examples.text: I'll always love you, no matter what happens.
examples.translation: 不論發生了什麼事，我會永遠愛你。

relations.native: 碎片；殘片；脫離的不完整部分

etymology.text: From Middle English happenen, hapnen, augmented from Middle English happen (“to come to pass, happen”), perhaps from Old English hæppan (“to move accidentally, slip”) and/or from Old Norse *happa, *heppa, from Proto-Germanic *hampijaną (“to fit in, be fitting”). Equivalent to hap (“a chance, occurrence, byfall”) + -en (verbal suffix).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（happenen、hapnen），由中古英語（happen）「發生」擴充而來，可能源自古英語（hæppan）「意外移動、滑」及／或古諾斯語（*happa），再上溯至原始日耳曼語。相當於（hap）「機運」加動詞字尾（-en）。

senses.definition: To say or do (something) for a second time, such as for emphasis.
To say or do (something) repeatedly.
To say (something) for a second time, but word it differently.
senses.native: 再次說出（某事），但用不同的說法

examples.text: We're reiterating the same promises.
examples.translation: 我們正在重複相同的承諾。

examples.text: Let me reiterate what I've said.
examples.translation: 讓我再說一次我剛才講過的話。

examples.text: Tom reiterated that concern.

examples.text: The press office later reiterated the point.

examples.text: He reiterated this advice several more times during the meeting.
examples.translation: 他在會議中多次重申這項建議。

etymology.text: Early 15th century, from Late Latin reiteratus, past participle of reiterare (“to repeat”) from re- (“again”) + iterare (“to repeat”) from iterum (“again”).
etymology.native: 約 15 世紀初，源自晚拉丁語 reiteratus（reiterare 的過去分詞），由 re-（「再次」）加上 iterare（「重複」，來自 iterum「再次」）組成。

senses.definition: To make a copy of.
To do repeatedly; to do again.
To produce something equal to.

examples.text: Don't duplicate this floppy.

Can you duplicate this kind of key?
He found it hard to duplicate the skills of his wife.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin duplicātus, perfect passive participle of duplicō, see -ate.

senses.definition: To proceed with (doing an activity); to prolong (an activity).
To resume.
To make last; to prolong.
To retain (someone or something) in a given state, position, etc.
senses.native: 使保持（某種狀態或職位）

senses.definition: To remain in a given place or condition; to remain in connection with; to abide; to stay.
senses.native: 留在；保持（某處或某狀態）

senses.definition: To adjourn, prorogue, put off.
To make a continuation bet.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Her mother will continue to work.

etymology.text: From Middle English continuen, from Old French continuer, from Latin continuō. Displaced native Middle English thurghwonen, from Old English þurhwunian.

senses.definition: The recoil of an object bouncing off another.
A return to health or well-being; a recovery.
An effort to recover from a setback.
The strike of the ball after it has bounced off a defending player or the crossbar or goalpost.
An instance of catching the ball after it has hit the rim or backboard without a basket being scored, generally credited to a particular player.
The period of getting over a recently ended romantic relationship.
A romantic partner with whom one begins a relationship (or the relationship one begins) for the sake of getting over a previous, recently ended romantic relationship.

examples.text: She went out with her on the rebound.

etymology.text: From Old French rebondir.

senses.definition: To wonder, think of deeply.
To consider (something) carefully and thoroughly.
To weigh.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: There are bigger questions to ponder.
examples.translation: 還有更重大的問題值得深思。

examples.text: Let's ponder that for a moment.
examples.translation: 讓我們稍作沉思。

examples.text: I'll have to ponder this one.
examples.translation: 我必須再好好想想這件事。

etymology.text: From Middle English ponderen, from Old French ponderer (“to weigh, balance, ponder”) from Latin ponderāre (“to weigh, ponder”), from pondus (“weight”), from pendere (“to weigh”); see pendent and pound.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 ponderen，來自舊法式 ponderer（「衡量、平衡、深思」），源自拉丁語 ponderāre（「衡量、深思」），詞根為 pondus（重量），來自 pendere（「衡量」）；參見 pendent 與 pound。

senses.definition: To point out; to discover; to direct to a knowledge of; to show; to make known.
To show or manifest by symptoms.
To point to as the proper remedies.
To signal in a vehicle the desire to turn right or left.
To investigate the condition or power of, as of steam engine, by means of an indicator.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Smiles do not always indicate pleasure.
examples.translation: 微笑並不一定表示高興。

examples.text: The speedometer was indicating 95 mph.

examples.translation: 她臉上的笑容，代表她已經原諒我了。

examples.text: The strong wind indicates that a storm is coming.

examples.text: The different colored strings indicate different fillings.
examples.translation: 不同顏色的繩子表示不同的餡料。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin indicātus, perfect passive participle of indicō (“to point out, indicate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from in- (“in, to”) + dicō (“to declare, (originally) to point”). See also diction and index.

senses.definition: To cause (oneself or someone, or their mind, etc.) to feel confused or mystified because they cannot understand a complicated matter, a problem, etc.; to confuse, to mystify, to perplex.
To use (one's brain or mind) to try to work out a complicated matter, a problem, etc.; also, to try to work out (a complicated matter, a problem, etc.).
Often followed by about, over, or upon: to feel confused or mystified because one cannot understand a complicated matter, a problem, etc.
Often followed by about, over, or or upon: to think deeply in bewilderment to try to work out a complicated matter, a problem, etc.
To search in a confused or mystified manner.
Followed by through: to solve a complicated matter, a problem, etc., by working through confusing or difficult matters.
To (intentionally) make (something) complicated or confused, and so difficult to resolve or understand; to confuse, to complicate.
To cause (someone) to not know what to do due to some problem, situation, etc.; to bewilder, to confound, to perplex.

examples.text: Tom said that I looked puzzled.
examples.translation: 湯姆說我看起來很困惑。

examples.text: She told me that she's puzzled.
examples.translation: 她告訴了我她很迷惑的。

examples.text: Tom was a bit puzzled by Mary's answer.
examples.translation: 湯姆對瑪麗的回答有困惑。

examples.text: I was puzzled about what to do next.
examples.translation: 我對以後做什麼很迷茫。

examples.text: Tom was puzzled by what Mary said.
examples.translation: 湯姆被瑪麗說的話給難倒了。

examples.text: I suspect that Tom and Mary are a bit puzzled.

etymology.text: The verb, of uncertain origin, is attested first. Apparently cognate with Scots pousle, pouzle, poozle (“to trifle; poke or potter around aimlessly; search about with uncertainty”), Saterland Frisian puzelje (“to work hard and continuously”), West Frisian peuzelje (“to trifle, work slowly; eat slowly and daintifully, snack”), Dutch peuzelen (“to perform insignificant work, dawdle; pick at, eat with relish in small pieces, snack”), German Low German pusseln (“to tinker, fiddle; trifle”) and pösel

senses.definition: To make prominent; emphasize.

To dye (part of the hair) a different color than the rest.
To seek the attention of (a user) on IRC by mentioning their name in a message, causing that message to appear highlighted on their screen.

examples.text: You should highlight this sentence here.

senses.definition: To paint or draw the likeness of.
To play a role; to depict a character, person, situation, or event.
To represent by an image or look.
senses.native: 描繪、刻畫（以圖像或外貌呈現）

senses.definition: To describe in words; to convey.
To adorn.

examples.text: The artist will portray the queen in oil.

senses.definition: That reflects, or redirects back to the source.

senses.definition: That reveals or shows; revealing; indicative of.
senses.native: 反映出的、表示的、象徵的

senses.definition: Involving reflection.
By means of reflection.
Reciprocal.

examples.text: Wear your reflective tape so you can be seen.

One of several similar units of a song, consisting of several lines, generally rhymed.
Poetic form in general.
A small section of a holy book (Bible, Quran etc.)
A portion of an anthem to be performed by a single voice to each part.

examples.translation: 不是每句話都能寫成詩歌。

etymology.text: From Middle English vers, from a mixture of Old English fers and Old French vers; both from Latin versus (“a line in writing, and in poetry a verse; (originally) row, furrow”), from vertō (“to turn around”).
etymology.native: 源自中世英文的 vers，由古英語 fers 與古法文 vers 混合而成；二者皆源自拉丁文 versus（意為「文字或詩歌中的一行」，原指「行、溝」），來自 vertō（意為「轉向」）

senses.definition: To tell in verse, or poetry.
to educate about, to teach about.
To oppose, to compete against.
To compose verses.

A poet's literary production.
An artistic quality that appeals to or evokes the emotions, in any medium; something having such a quality.

examples.translation: 中國詩歌以李白的詩最為有名。

examples.text: They referred to Chaucer as the father of English poetry.
examples.translation: 他們視喬叟為英詩之父。

examples.text: Wine is poetry in bottles.

To record data mechanically or electronically.
To sell (an option or other derivative).
To paint a religious icon or a pysanka egg.
To be the author of (a book, article, poem, etc.).

To compose and send (written information or a written message, e.g. a letter) to.

A bishop's council.
An administrative division of an organization, usually local to a specific area.
An organized branch of some society or fraternity, such as the Freemasons.

A chapter house
A sequence (of events), especially when presumed related and likely to continue.
A prescribed reading at one of the canonical hours.
A location or compartment.

A straggling, haphazard growth, especially of housing on the edge of a city.
senses.native: 散亂、無序的成長，特別是指城市邊緣的住宅區

senses.definition: A defensive technique that is done in response to certain takedown attempts, where one scoots the legs backwards so as to land on the upper back of the opponent.
senses.native: 針對特定過肩摔嘗試所採取的防禦技術，將腿向後滑動以落在對手背部上方

examples.text: Urban sprawl is environmentally damaging.
examples.translation: 城市擴張會對環境造成破壞。

examples.text: Urban sprawl and chaos create many planning problems.
examples.translation: 城市蔓延與混亂造成許多規劃問題。

examples.text: Planning experts and local officials say suburban sprawl has negative impacts on the environment.
examples.translation: 規劃專家與地方官員表示，郊區蔓延對環境有負面影響。

examples.text: The city sprawls between a chain of mountains and a big river.
examples.translation: 城市在連綿的山脈與大河之間延伸。

etymology.text: From Middle English spraulen, from Old English spreawlian (“move convulsively”), ultimately through a Proto-Germanic form cognate with *spreutaną (“to sprout”) from Proto-Indo-European *sper- (“to strew”). Compare North Frisian spraweli, Norwegian sprala, Swedish sprala.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 spraulen，來自古英語 spreawlian（「劇烈移動」），最終源自日耳曼語族共同祖語 *spreutaną（「發芽」），再追溯至印歐語系 *sper-（「播撒」）。可對比北弗里斯蘭語 spraweli、挪威語 sprala 及瑞典語 sprala。

senses.definition: To endeavor to gain someone's affection or support.
Often of a man, to try to persuade (someone) to be in an amorous relationship with.
To court solicitously; to invite with importunity; to solicit in love.

examples.text: They're trying to woo the customers back with this new mobile plan.
examples.translation: 他們正試圖用這個新手機套餐把顧客爭回來。

etymology.text: From Middle English wowen, woȝen, from Old English wōgian (“to woo, court, marry”), of uncertain origin. Cognate with Scots wow (“to woo”). Perhaps related to Old English wōg, wōh (“bending, crookedness”), in the specific sense of "bend or incline (some)one toward oneself". If so, then derived from Proto-Germanic *wanhō (“a bend, angle”), from Proto-Indo-European *wonk- (“crooked, bent”), from Proto-Indo-European *wā- (“to bend, twist, turn”); related to Old Norse vá (“corner, angle”).
etymology.native: 此詞源自中古英語 wowen, woȝen，來自古英語 wōgian（意為「追求、迎娶」），起源不明。與蘇格蘭語 wow（意為「追求」）同源。可能與古英語 wōg, wōh（意為「彎曲、曲折」）有關，特指「使某人傾向於自己」。若如此，則源自原始日耳曼語 *wanhō（意為「彎曲、角度」），再源自原始印歐語 *wonk-（意為「彎曲、彎折」），而原始印歐語 *wā-（意為「彎曲、扭轉、轉向」）；亦與古諾斯語 vá（意為「角落、角度」）相關。

senses.definition: Alternative spelling of whoo, expressing joy or excitement.

examples.text: "I got you a new cell phone." "Woo, that's great!"
examples.translation: "我幫你買了新手機。" "哇，太棒了！"

etymology.text: From Middle English wowen, woȝen, from Old English wōgian (“to woo, court, marry”), of uncertain origin. Cognate with Scots wow (“to woo”). Perhaps related to Old English wōg, wōh (“bending, crookedness”), in the specific sense of "bend or incline (some)one toward oneself". If so, then derived from Proto-Germanic *wanhō (“a bend, angle”), from Proto-Indo-European *wonk- (“crooked, bent”), from Proto-Indo-European *wā- (“to bend, twist, turn”); related to Old Norse vá (“corner, angle”).
etymology.native: 此詞源自中古英語 wowen, woȝen，來自古英語 wōgian（意為「追求、迎娶」），起源不明。與蘇格蘭語 wow（意為「追求」）同源。可能與古英語 wōg, wōh（意為「彎曲、曲折」）有關，特指「使某人傾向於自己」。若如此，則源自原始日耳曼語 *wanhō（意為「彎曲、角度」），再源自原始印歐語 *wonk-（意為「彎曲、彎折」），而原始印歐語 *wā-（意為「彎曲、扭轉、轉向」）；亦與古諾斯語 vá（意為「角落、角度」）相關。

senses.definition: Alternative form of woo woo (“esoteric, pseudoscientific phenomena”).

examples.text: Quantum physics has spawned a large amount of woo.

etymology.text: From Middle English wowen, woȝen, from Old English wōgian (“to woo, court, marry”), of uncertain origin. Cognate with Scots wow (“to woo”). Perhaps related to Old English wōg, wōh (“bending, crookedness”), in the specific sense of "bend or incline (some)one toward oneself". If so, then derived from Proto-Germanic *wanhō (“a bend, angle”), from Proto-Indo-European *wonk- (“crooked, bent”), from Proto-Indo-European *wā- (“to bend, twist, turn”); related to Old Norse vá (“corner, angle”).
etymology.native: 此詞源自中古英語 wowen, woȝen，來自古英語 wōgian（意為「追求、迎娶」），起源不明。與蘇格蘭語 wow（意為「追求」）同源。可能與古英語 wōg, wōh（意為「彎曲、曲折」）有關，特指「使某人傾向於自己」。若如此，則源自原始日耳曼語 *wanhō（意為「彎曲、角度」），再源自原始印歐語 *wonk-（意為「彎曲、彎折」），而原始印歐語 *wā-（意為「彎曲、扭轉、轉向」）；亦與古諾斯語 vá（意為「角落、角度」）相關。

senses.definition: To successfully convince (someone) to agree to, accept, or do something, usually through reasoning and verbal influence.
To convince of by argument, or by reasons offered or suggested from reflection, etc.; to cause to believe (something).
To urge, plead; to try to convince (someone to do something).

examples.text: Tom failed to persuade Mary.
examples.translation: 湯姆沒能說服瑪麗。

examples.text: We tried to persuade him.
examples.translation: 我們試著勸了他。

examples.text: She attempted to persuade her father.
You tried to persuade Tom to do that, didn't you?
examples.translation: 你之前試著勸過湯姆去做那件事，對吧？

examples.text: I don't see any point in persuading him.
examples.translation: 我認為沒有必要游說他。

examples.text: I persuaded him to give up the idea.
examples.translation: 我說服他放棄了這個主意。

etymology.text: From Latin persuādeō (“to persuade”). Cognate to for, sweet.

senses.definition: The fruit of the oak, being an oval nut growing in a woody cup or cupule.
A cone-shaped piece of wood on the point of the spindle above the vane, on the mast-head.
See acorn-shell.
The glans penis.
A testicle.

examples.text: Great oaks from little acorns grow.
examples.translation: 高大的橡樹是從一顆小小的橡子成長而來的。

examples.text: A hungry pig dreams of acorns.
examples.translation: 飢餓的豬夢到橡樹子。

examples.text: The squirrels were searching for acorns.
examples.translation: 松鼠在找橡子。

examples.text: From a small acorn grows a tall oak tree.
examples.translation: 一粒小小的橡實可以長成一棵高大的橡樹。

examples.text: Acorns are excellent food to fatten pigs.
examples.translation: 橡子是讓豬長肥的好食物。

examples.text: The centipede twirled around the fallen acorns.
examples.translation: 蜈蚣在倒下的橡子旁轉圈。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English acorn, an alteration (after corn) of earlier *akern, from Old English æcern (“acorn, oak-mast”), from Proto-West Germanic *akarn, from Proto-Germanic *akraną (“fruit; acorn, nut”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂égrō (“berry”).
etymology.native: 「橡果」源自中世紀英文 acorn，是 earlier *akern 的變體（源自 corn），而 *akern 又來自古英語 æcern（意為「橡果、橡樹果實」），再往上溯源自古西德語 *akarn，而 *akarn 則來自原始印歐語 *h₂égrō（意為「漿果」）

senses.definition: A specialized cell, group of cells, or organ of endothelial origin in the human or animal body that synthesizes a chemical substance, such as hormones or breast milk, and releases it, often into the bloodstream (endocrine gland) or into cavities inside the body or its outer surface (exocrine gland).
A structure resembling a gland, especially a lymph node.
A secretory structure on the surface of an organ.
A stuffing box used to seal a rotating or reciprocating shaft against a fluid.

A compressable cylindrical case and its contents around a shaft where it passes through a barrier, intended to prevent the passage of a fluid past the barrier, used for example around a ship’s propeller shaft or around a tap, valve or faucet.

examples.text: The adrenal glands secrete adrenalin.
examples.translation: 副交感神經系統分泌腎上腺素。

examples.text: The pineal gland secretes melatonin.
examples.translation: 松果體分泌褪黑激素。

examples.text: The thyroid is an endocrine gland.
examples.translation: 甲狀腺是一種內分泌腺。

examples.text: There's something wrong with her thyroid gland.
examples.translation: 她的甲狀腺有異常。

examples.text: Glands secrete chemical substances into the body.
examples.translation: 腺體會將化學物質分泌至體內。

examples.text: There's a problem with her thyroid gland.
examples.translation: 她的甲狀腺有問題。

etymology.text: Late 17th century borrowing from French glande, alteration of Old French glandre, from Latin glandulae (“throat glands, tonsils”), plural of glandula (“a little acorn”), from glāns (“an acorn”) + -ula (diminutive nominal suffix).
etymology.native: 17世紀末從法文 glande 借入，源自古法文 glandre，來自拉丁文 glandulae（「喉嚨腺體、扁桃體」），為 glandula（「小橡果」）的複數形式，由 glāns（「橡果」）+ -ula（縮小名詞後綴）構成。

senses.definition: A roving motion; course without definite direction; lack of rule or method; chance.
The direction of a rake-vein.
A frame for composing type.
An undefined, unknown or unimportant person; a person of no consequence.
Speed, full speed; impetuosity, force.
The full range of a bullet or other projectile; hence, the angle at which a weapon is tilted to allow the greatest range.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Your random firing will scare away the prey.
examples.translation: 你胡亂打槍，會嚇跑獵物的。

examples.text: The party was boring. It was full of randoms.

etymology.text: From earlier randon, from Middle English randoun, raundon, from Old French randon, from randir (“to run, gallop”) (whence French randonnée (“long walk, hike”)), from Frankish *randiju (“a run, race”) or Old Norse rend (“a run, race”), both from Proto-Germanic *randijō, from *rinnaną (“run”, verb), from Proto-Indo-European *(H)r̥-nw- (“to flow, move, run”). Cognate with Middle Low German uprinden (“to jump up”), Danish rende (“to run”). See run.

senses.definition: Any member of Caninae, the only living subfamily of Canidae.
Any of certain extant canids regarded as similar to the dog or wolf (including coyotes, jackals, etc.) but distinguished from the vulpines, which are regarded as fox-like.
senses.native: 犬科動物（含郊狼、狐犬等）

senses.definition: Synonym of cuspid, the pointed tooth between the incisors and premolars in heterodont mammals.
A king and a nine as a starting hand in Texas hold 'em due to phonetic similarity.

examples.text: A wolf is a canine.
examples.translation: 狼是犬科動物。

etymology.text: From Latin canīnus (“of dogs, doglike, dogtooth”), from canis (“dog”). Compare French canin.
etymology.native: 來自拉丁語 canīnus（意為「狗的、像狗的、狗牙的」），源自 canis（狗）。可與法語 canin 相比。

senses.definition: A hard, calcareous structure present in the mouth of many vertebrate animals, generally used for biting and chewing food.
A projection or point in other parts of the body resembling the tooth of a vertebrate animal.
A sharp projection on the blade of a saw or similar implement.
A projection on the edge of a gear that meshes with similar projections on adjacent gears, or on the circumference of a cog that engages with a chain.
The property of resisting slippage when knotted.
A pointed projection from the margin of a leaf.
The rough surface of some kinds of cel or other films that allows better adhesion of artwork.
Liking, fondness (compare toothsome).
An irreducible component of a comb that intersects the handle in exactly one point, that point being distinct from the unique point of intersection for any other tooth of the comb.

examples.text: You've got something in your teeth.
examples.translation: 牙齒卡了點東西。

examples.text: He is lying through his teeth.
examples.translation: 他明顯在撒謊。

examples.text: Your tooth must be extracted.
examples.translation: 您的牙要拔掉。

examples.text: My son is brushing his teeth.
examples.translation: 我兒子在刷牙。

examples.text: Remember to brush your teeth.
examples.translation: 別忘了刷牙。

examples.text: These are my grandmother's artificial teeth.
examples.translation: 這是我外婆的假牙。

etymology.text: From Middle English toth, tothe, tooth, from Old English tōþ, from Proto-West Germanic *tanþ, from Proto-Germanic *tanþs, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃dónts (“tooth”). Doublet of dent, dens, tind, and tine. Related to tusk.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語，來自古英語「牙」，上溯至原始西日耳曼語與原始日耳曼語「牙」，來自原始印歐語「牙」。與「齒（法語）」、「尖齒」、「叉齒」為同源異形詞，並與「獠牙」有關。

senses.definition: An organism that feeds chiefly on animals; an animal that feeds on meat as the main part of its diet.
A mammal belonging to the order Carnivora.
A person who is not a vegetarian.
A follower of the carnivore diet.

examples.text: That animal is a carnivore.
examples.translation: 那隻動物是食肉動物。

examples.text: Crocodiles are carnivores.
examples.translation: 鱷魚都是食肉動物。

examples.text: Cows are herbivores, while dogs are carnivores.
examples.translation: 牛是草食動物，而狗則是食肉動物。

examples.text: That's because there weren't any large carnivores in New Guinea.
examples.translation: 這是因為新幾內亞沒有大型食肉動物。

examples.text: Some animals are herbivores, whereas other ones are carnivores or omnivores.
examples.translation: 有些動物是草食動物，而其他則是食肉動物或雜食動物。

examples.text: The pike and the perch are carnivores.
examples.translation: 鱸魚和比目魚都是食肉動物。

relations.native: 以動物為食的生物；主要以肉類為食的動物

etymology.text: Borrowed from French carnivore, from Latin carnivorus. In the zoological sense, coined by William Whewell in 1840 as an adaptation of Cuvier's coinage, French carnivore.
etymology.native: 此詞源自法語，再源自拉丁語。生物學家威廉·惠威爾於 1840 年將其作為庫維爾的用法進行改編而造出。

senses.definition: Canis lupus; the largest wild member of the canine subfamily.
Any of several related canines that resemble Canis lupus in appearance, especially those of the genus Canis.
A man who makes amorous advances to many women.
A wolf tone or wolf note.
Any very ravenous, rapacious, or destructive person or thing; especially, want; starvation.
One of the destructive, and usually hairy, larvae of several species of beetles and grain moths.
A white worm which infests granaries, the larva of Nemapogon granella, a tineid moth.
A wolf spider (Lycosidae spp.).
A willying machine, that uses willow twigs to cleanse wool.
An eating ulcer or sore. See lupus.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: I saw wolves in the Appennines.
examples.translation: 我在亞平寧山脈看到了狼。

examples.text: Tom doesn't know anything about wolves.
examples.translation: 湯姆對狼完全不了解。

examples.text: Tom shot his own dog, thinking it was a wolf.
examples.translation: 湯姆把他的狗認成狼了，所以把它斃了。

examples.text: Lions, wolves, elephants, and horses are all animals.
examples.translation: 獅子，狼，大象，馬，這些都是動物。

examples.text: One day she met a wolf in the woods.
examples.translation: 有一天，她在森林裡遇到一頭狼。

examples.text: Wolves won't usually attack people.
examples.translation: 一般來說，狼不會攻擊人。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English wolf, from Old English wulf, ƿulf, from Proto-West Germanic *wulf, from Proto-Germanic *wulfaz, from Proto-Indo-European *wĺ̥kʷos. Doublet of lobo and lupus.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 wolf，來自古英語 wulf、ƿulf，源自古西日耳曼語 *wulf，再溯自古德語 *wulfaz，最終來自印歐語系 *wĺ̥kʷos。為 lobo 與 lupus 的同源詞。

senses.definition: A long, pointed canine tooth used for biting and tearing flesh.
A long, pointed tooth in snakes, used for injecting venom.
A pointed extension of the chelicera in spiders, used for injecting venom.
Synonym of tooth, particularly in humans.
Either of the two factors that make a number a vampire number.
Synonym of root, the part of a tooth embedded in the gums.
Synonym of spike or prong, any sharp projection.
Synonym of tang, the projection of a piece of metal intended to be driven into a shaft for holding.
The valve of a pump-box.
Synonym of mandible, the long mouthpart of insects and other invertebrates.
A grasping; capture; the act or power of seizing; hold.
That which is seized or carried off; booty; spoils; stolen goods.
Synonym of trap or noose.
Synonym of root, a major projection of a plant's root system.
Synonym of claw or talon.
Synonym of vang, a line extended from the end of a gaff to control its position.
A channel cut or pipe set for the purpose of carrying fresh air to working miners.
Catches on which a coalmining cage rests while cars are being moved on and off.

examples.text: No, I am Fang Ning.
examples.translation: 不，我是方寧。

examples.text: Which snake has the longest fangs?
examples.translation: 哪種蛇的牙最長？

examples.text: Boldi had really long fangs.
examples.translation: Boldi 的牙真的非常長。

examples.text: My dog was barking and showing its fangs.
examples.translation: 我的狗在吠叫並露出牙。

examples.text: Read the lessons in "Spoken Hokkien" by Meili Fang.
examples.translation: 閱讀方美莉所著的《 spoken Hokkien 》課文。

examples.text: The snake hissed and bared its fangs.
examples.translation: 蛇嘶鳴著並張開牙。

etymology.text: From clipping of fangtooth, from Middle English *fangtooth, *fengtooth, from Old English fengtōþ (“molar tooth”), from feng, preterite of fōn (“to catch, take, seize”). Cognate with German Fangzahn (“fang”, literally “catch-tooth”) and Dutch vangtand. See also related senses of Etymology 3 below.
etymology.native: 「fangtooth」源自中古英語 *fangtooth、*fengtooth，來自古英語 fengtōþ（意為「磨牙」），源自 feng（意為「抓住、攫取」的過去式）。與德語 Fangzahn（「catch-tooth」）及荷蘭語 vangtand 同源。另見下方「Etymology 3」相關義項。

senses.definition: Of or pertaining to a particular person; relating to, or affecting, an individual, or each of many individuals
Pertaining to persons (human beings as opposed to things or animals).
Dealing with subjects about which one wishes (or people usually wish) to maintain privacy or discretion; not for public view; sensitive, intimate.
Intended for sexual use.
Pertaining to the external or bodily appearance; corporeal; bodily.
Done in person; without an intermediary.
Relating to an individual, their character, conduct, motives, or private affairs, in an invidious and offensive manner
senses.native: 針對個人的；人身攻擊的

senses.definition: Of a noun or pronoun, having reference particular to humans and other entities having personality such as a named animal, a deity, a personification, etc.
Related to grammatical first, second, etc. persons.
Denoting ownership.

examples.text: Personal computers are of great use.
examples.translation: 箇人電腦非常有用。

examples.text: Will you take a personal check?
examples.translation: 你收私人支票嗎?

examples.text: I have to make money to buy a personal computer.
examples.translation: 必須要賺錢才能買一台個人計算機。

examples.text: She got her daughter a personal computer.
examples.translation: 她給她的女兒買了一台個人電腦。

examples.text: I avoid discussing personal subjects with my boss.
examples.translation: 我避免跟老闆討論箇人話題。

examples.text: The whole plan is only based on his personal opinions.
examples.translation: 整個計劃只是基於他的個人看法。

etymology.text: From Middle English personal, personele, from Anglo-Norman personel, personal, personell, Old French personal, personel, from Late Latin persōnālis (“of a person, personly”), equivalent to person + -al. Doublet of personnel.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（personal、personele），來自英法語（personel、personal）、古法語（personal），再源自晚期拉丁語（persōnālis）「個人的」，相當於（person）加（-al）。與（personnel）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: Cleaning and polishing of an animal's teeth.
A dental sound.

examples.text: How much do dental assistants make?
examples.translation: 牙科助理的薪水有多少？

examples.text: Use dental floss after each meal.
examples.translation: 每餐飯後使用牙線。

examples.text: He opened his own dental office.
examples.translation: 他開了自己的牙科診所。

examples.text: When was your most recent dental appointment?
examples.translation: 你最近一次看牙是什麼時候？

examples.text: I didn't know that Tom was a dental assistant.
examples.translation: 我不知道湯姆是牙科助理。

examples.text: How much will I pay for NHS dental treatment?
examples.translation: 英國健保的牙科治療我要付多少錢？

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French dental or Late Latin dentālis, from dēns (“a tooth”) + -ālis (“-al”, adjectival suffix).
etymology.native: 借自中古法語或後期拉丁語「牙齒的」，由「牙齒」加形容詞字尾組成。

senses.definition: An overseer of congregations: either any such overseer, generally speaking, or (in Eastern Orthodoxy, Catholicism, Anglicanism, etc.) an official in the church hierarchy (actively or nominally) governing a diocese, supervising the church's priests, deacons, and property in its territory.
The chess piece denoted ♗ or ♝ which moves along diagonal lines and developed from the shatranj alfil ("elephant") and was originally known as the aufil or archer in English.
A chief of the Festival of Fools or St. Nicholas Day.
Any of various African birds of the genus Euplectes; a kind of weaverbird closely related to the widowbirds.
A flowering plant of the genus Bifora.
A sweet drink made from wine, usually with oranges, lemons, and sugar; mulled and spiced port.
A similar official or chief priest in another religion.
The holder of the Greek or Roman position of episcopus, supervisor over the public dole of grain, etc.
Any watchman, inspector, or overlooker.
A ladybug or ladybird, beetles of the family Coccinellidae.
A bustle.
A children's smock or pinafore.

Cognate with all European terms for the position in various Christian churches; compare also Middle English

etymology.text: Shortened from gooney, from obsolete gony (“simpleton”), used circa 1580, of unknown origin. Perhaps a familiar term derived from Middle English gone, a variant of gome (“man, person”). Gony was applied by sailors to the albatross and similar big, clumsy birds (circa 1839). The term goon first carried the meaning "stupid person" (circa 1921). Compare Scots goni, guni (“a bogey, bugbear, hobgoblin”), dialectal Swedish gonnar (“elves, goblins”, plural).
etymology.native: 「gooney」源自已廢棄的「gony」（意為「傻瓜」），約在1580年使用，起源不明。可能源自中古英格蘭的「gone」，為「gome」（意為「人」）的變體。 sailors 約在1839年用「gony」形容鴨嘴鳥等笨重的大鳥。直到1921年，「goon」才開始指「愚蠢的人」。可與蘇格蘭語「goni」、「guni」（意為「惡魔、妖怪」）及瑞典方言「gonnar」（意為「精靈、小妖」）相對照。

senses.definition: Mental focus.

senses.definition: The sense or ability of sight.
Something seen; an object perceived visually.
Something imaginary one thinks one sees.
Something unreal or imaginary; a creation of fancy.
A perceived potential future event or occurrence.
An ideal or a goal toward which one aspires.
General aspiration; forward-thinkingness.
A religious or mystical experience of a supernatural appearance.
A person or thing of extraordinary beauty.
Pre-recorded film or tape; footage.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Wearing glasses should correct your vision.
examples.translation: 戴眼鏡應該能糾正你的視力。

examples.text: There are no real visions.

examples.text: Please check my vision.

etymology.text: From Middle English visioun, from Anglo-Norman visioun, from Old French vision, from Latin vīsiō (“vision, seeing”), noun of action from the perfect passive participle visus (“that which is seen”), from the verb videō (“to see”) + action noun suffix -iō.

senses.definition: Related to or affecting the vision.
That can be seen; visible.

examples.text: The lesson was visual.
examples.translation: 這堂課以視覺教學為主。

etymology.text: From Middle English visual, from French visuel, visual and directly from Late Latin vīsuālis (“of sight”), from vīsus (“sight, vision”) + -ālis (“adjective suffix”), from vidēre (“to see, perceive; look (at)”); see visage. By surface analysis, Latin vīsus + -ual.

senses.definition: An ardent enthusiast or admirer.
A believer in a particular religion or god.
A person (almost exclusively a man) with a sexual attraction for people with physical disabilities, especially amputees.

examples.text: Tom is a BTS devotee.
examples.translation: 湯姆是BTS的狂熱粉絲。

examples.text: Devotees of science fiction will enjoy this new film.
examples.translation: 科幻電影的粉絲會喜歡這部新片。

examples.text: The devotees witnessed the miracle with their own eyes.
examples.translation: 粉絲親眼見證了這項奇蹟。

examples.text: The devotees of Vishnu are called Vaishnavas; the devotees of Shiva are Shaivites.
examples.translation: 維濕努的信徒稱為維濕努派；濕婆的信徒稱為濕婆派。

examples.text: He was a staunch devotee who had unflinching faith.
examples.translation: 他是一位堅定的信徒，信仰毫不動搖。

examples.text: The syncretist, the mystic, the devotee, the puritan, would find a congenial climate in these regions of Asia Minor.
examples.translation: 融合主義者、神秘主義者、信徒、清教徒，在小亞細亞這些地區都能找到合適的氛圍。

etymology.text: From devote + -ee. The narrowed meaning in sense 3 arises from the sound similarity with amputee.
etymology.native: 來自 devote + -ee。意義3的縮窄用法源自與 amputee 音近。

senses.definition: A person attached to a particular pursuit, study, science, or art (such as music or painting), especially one who cultivates any study, interest, taste, or attachment without engaging in it professionally.
Someone who is unqualified or insufficiently skillful.
A lover of something.

examples.text: Lord Carnarvon was an amateur Egyptologist.

examples.translation: 我的舅舅愛好打板球。

examples.text: I was still an amateur at that time.
examples.translation: 我那時還是個外行。

examples.text: Fermat was a great amateur mathematician.

etymology.text: Borrowed from French amateur, from Latin amātor (“lover”), from amāre (“to love”).

senses.definition: A person filled with or guided by enthusiasm.
A person exhibiting over-zealous religious fervour.

examples.text: Tom is a television enthusiast.
He is a big sumo enthusiast.
He is a music enthusiast.
Adriano loves discussing wine with other enthusiasts.

etymology.text: From Ancient Greek ἐνθουσιαστής (enthousiastḗs, “an enthusiast, a zealot”), from ἐνθουσιάζειν (enthousiázein, “(intransitive) be inspired or possessed by a god, be rapt, be in ecstasy, (transitive) inspire”): see enthusiasm.

senses.definition: An insane person, especially one who suffers from a mania.
A fanatic, a person with an obsession.
an insane person
a person who has an obsession with or excessive enthusiasm for something

examples.text: Homicidal maniacs are around every corner.

etymology.text: From mania + -ac. Borrowed from French maniaque, from Late Latin maniacus, from Ancient Greek μανιακός (maniakós), adjectival form of μανία (manía, “madness”). Compare manic.
etymology.native: 由「狂熱」加字尾組成。借自法語，來自後期拉丁語，源自古希臘語「瘋狂」的形容詞形式。可比較「狂躁的」。

senses.definition: One who follows, comes after another.
Something that comes after another thing.
One who is a part of master's physical group, such as a servant or retainer.
One who follows mentally, adherer to the opinions, ideas or teachings of another, a movement etc.
An imitator, who follows another's example.
A pursuer.
An account holder who subscribes to see content from another account on a social media platform.
A machine part receiving motion from another.
A tappet.
A man courting a maidservant; a suitor.
Young cattle.
A metal piece placed at the top of a candle to keep the wax melting evenly.
Any of the three players (the ruckman, ruck rover, and rover) who usually follow the ball around the ground rather than occupying a fixed position.
A tool used to remove the core from a pin-tumbler lock without causing the driver pins and springs to fall out.
A debt collector.

examples.text: Boris needs more followers on Instagram.

etymology.text: From Middle English folwer, folwere, folewer, from Old English folgere (“follower; attendant; disciple”), equivalent to follow + -er. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Foulger, West Frisian folger, Dutch volger, German Folger, Swedish följare.

senses.definition: Someone who is an expert in, or devoted to, some specific branch of study or research.

etymology.native: 源自法語 spécialiste，等同於 special 加上 -ist 詞尾。

examples.text: A beautiful valley lies behind the hill.

etymology.native: 源自中古英語，來自盎格魯諾曼語與古法語「山谷」（可比較法語同義字），來自拉丁語「谷」。與南非語「沼地」為同源異形詞。取代了本土字「谿」，並部分取代了「谷地」。

senses.definition: the vertical distance below a surface; the degree to which something is deep
the distance between the front and the back, as the depth of a drawer or closet
the intensity, complexity, strength, seriousness or importance of an emotion, situation, etc.
lowness
the total palette of available colors
the property of appearing three-dimensional
the deepest part (usually of a body of water)
a very remote part.
the most severe part
the number of simple elements which an abstract conception or notion includes; the comprehension or content
a pair of toothed wheels which work together

examples.text: Officers will henceforth wear ties at dinner.
examples.translation: 警官們從今以後用餐時須打領帶。

examples.text: Those like me and I won't repeat it henceforth.
examples.translation: 像我這樣的人，從今以後不再重複此舉。

examples.translation: 這隻松鼠從今以後將被稱為「可愛的一號」。

examples.translation: 從今以後，強大領袖格魯將藉此詛咒世界展現他驚人的風範。

senses.definition: Up to this or that time.

examples.text: Karl Marx says, "The history of all hitherto existing societies is the history of class struggles."

examples.text: The history of all hitherto existing societies is the history of class struggles.

senses.definition: Nevertheless; yet, still; in spite of that.

Regardless of how; regardless of the way in which.
In any way in which; how.
In any way that one likes or chooses; in a haphazard or spontaneous way.

In any case, at any rate, at all events.

examples.translation: 他們不思考，所以他們不存在。

examples.text: He is always sad, therefore, he never smiles.
examples.translation: 他總是悲傷，所以從不微笑。

examples.text: He came first. Therefore he got a good seat.
examples.translation: 他最先到，所以拿到了好位子。

examples.text: I am because you are, and therefore we are.
examples.translation: 因為有你才有我，所以才有我們。

etymology.text: From Middle English therfore, therfor, tharfore, thorfore; synchronically a univerbation of there (pronominal adverb) + for, literally “for that (reason)”. The spelling has been changed due to a reanalysis as there + fore (literally “forward from that; thence”). See also therefor, ultimately the same formation.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（therfore、tharfore），共時上是代副詞（there）加（for）合為一詞，字面意為「為了那個（理由）」。拼法因被重新分析為（there）加（fore）而改變。另見（therefor），本是同一構詞。

senses.definition: At any time.
When ever: emphatic form of when.

examples.text: Whenever you come, you are welcome.
examples.translation: 來的都是朋友。

examples.text: You may come whenever you like.
examples.translation: 你喜歡甚麼時候來就甚麼時候來吧。

examples.text: I'm happy whenever I see him.
examples.translation: 我看到他就高興

examples.text: Whenever I call, he is out.
examples.translation: 無論我甚麼時候打給他，他也不在家。

examples.translation: 每次聽到這首歌，都會讓我回憶起自己年輕的時候。

etymology.text: From Middle English whan evere, whanne ever, whanne evere, whener, when ever; equivalent to when + -ever.

senses.definition: Where ever; an emphatic form of where.
The place (no matter where) in, at or to which.
In, at or to any place that one likes or chooses.

examples.text: I don't care what you do with it; just put it wherever.
Where do you want to have lunch? — Wherever; I don't mind.

etymology.text: From where + -ever.

senses.definition: By it; by that; by that means, or as a consequence of that.

examples.text: Tom overslept, thereby missing the bus he usually catches.
The failure was detected in time, thereby preventing a disaster.
Over time, wave action undercuts sea cliffs and thereby causes them to fall into the ocean.
He is usually straightforward and sincere and thereby gains the confidence of those who meet him.
To raise one's name in later generations and thereby glorify one's parents, this is the greatest expression of filial piety.
Newly developed, IT-based, minimally invasive surgery techniques are currently gaining momentum, thereby revolutionizing healthcare in its entirety.

etymology.text: From Middle English therby, from Old English ðǣrbig, equivalent to there + by. Compare the parallel formation of German dabei.

senses.definition: At the present time.
Used to introduce a point, a qualification of what has previously been said, a remonstration or a rebuke.

senses.definition: At the time reached within a narration.
Used to indicate a context of urgency.
At the present point of a recurring cycle or event.
Used to address a switching side, or sharp change in attitude from before.
Sometimes; occasionally; used to list a series of often assumed states.
Very recently; not long ago; up to the present.

examples.text: Let's discuss the matter right now.
examples.translation: 讓我們馬上討論這個問題吧。

examples.text: I'm at Narita Airport right now.

examples.text: Thanks to his help, my work is going well now.
examples.translation: 得到他的幫助，我的工作現在很順利。

etymology.text: From Middle English nou, nu, from Old English nū, from Proto-West Germanic *nū, from Proto-Germanic *nu (“now”), from Proto-Indo-European *nū (“now”). Doublet of nu ("well?").

senses.definition: begin to be; turn into (often with permanent states).
To come about; happen; come into being; arise.
To be appropriate for.
Of an adornment, piece of clothing etc.: to look attractive on (someone).

To arrive, come (to a place).

senses.definition: Indispensable, supremely important.
Important, salient.

senses.definition: To attune to; to set at; to pitch.

senses.definition: To fasten or secure firmly; to fasten or tighten with keys or wedges.
senses.native: 牢固固定；以鍵或楔子加緊

senses.native: （口語）以鑰匙等刮花（汽車等）進行破壞

etymology.text: From Middle English henge (“hinge”), from Old English *henġ or *henġe (“hinge”), from Proto-West Germanic *hangiju or *hangī; compare Old English *henġe- in henġeclif (“overhanging cliff”), Old English henġen (“hanging; that upon which a thing is hung”). Akin to Scots heenge (“hinge”), Saterland Frisian Hänge (“hinge”), Low German henge (“hook, hinge, handle”), Dutch heng (“moving leaf of a hinge”), Dutch geheng (“hinge”), Middle Dutch henghe, hanghe (“hook, hinge, handle”), Scots hingel (“any a
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 henge（「活動軸」），來自古英語 *henġ 或 *henġe，再源自原始西日耳曼語 *hangiju 或 *hangī；可比較古英語 *henġe- 在 henġeclif（懸崖）中的用法、古英語 henġen（懸掛；用於懸掛之物）。與蘇格蘭話 heenge（活動軸）、薩特蘭德弗里斯蘭語 Hänge（活動軸）、低地德語 henge（鉤子、活動軸、手柄）、荷蘭語 heng（活動軸的葉片）、荷蘭語 geheng（活動軸）、中古荷蘭語 henghe、hanghe（鉤子、活動軸、手柄）相近；蘇格蘭話還有 hingel（任何...）。

examples.translation: 他們為敵人敗北而歡呼。

examples.text: They exulted in their unexpected success.
examples.translation: 他們為意外的成功而歡呼。

examples.text: He stood for a moment outside the walls of the prison, exulting in his miraculous escape.
examples.translation: 他站在監獄牆外片刻，為自己神蹟般的逃脫而歡呼。

etymology.text: From Middle French exulter, from Latin exsultō, frequentative of exsiliō (“jump up”), from ex- + saliō (“jump, leap”).
etymology.native: 來自中世紀法語 exulter，源自拉丁語 exsultō，是 exsiliō（「跳起」）的頻繁式，由 ex- + saliō（「跳、躍」）構成。

senses.definition: To use a crowbar, wedge, or other implement to attempt to open a surface by leveraging force on the opposite end of the tool to pry off the connection between the two surfaces.
To make the shrill sound characteristic of a rooster; to make a sound in this manner, either in gaiety, joy, pleasure, or defiance.
To shout in exultation or defiance; to brag.
senses.native: 歡呼、叫囂（以示勝利或挑釁）；誇耀

senses.definition: To test the reed of a double reed instrument by placing the reed alone in the mouth and blowing it.
senses.native: 以口含雙簧樂器的簧片並吹氣，以測試簧片

etymology.text: From Middle English crowe, from Old English crāwe, from Proto-West Germanic *krāā, from Proto-Germanic *krēǭ (compare West Frisian krie, Dutch kraai, German Krähe), from *krēaną (“to crow”). See below.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 crowe，再源自古英語 crāwe，後者來自日耳曼語族原初詞 *krēaną（意為「鳴叫」）。

senses.definition: To cause to rise; to lift or elevate.
To bring up; to grow.
To promote.
To mention (a question, issue) for discussion.
To create; to constitute (a use, or a beneficial interest in property).
To bring into being; to produce; to cause to arise, come forth, or appear.
To establish contact with (e.g., by telephone or radio).
To respond to a bet by increasing the amount required to continue in the hand.
To exponentiate, to involute.
To form by the accumulation of materials or constituent parts; to build up; to erect.
To cause something to come to the surface of water.
senses.native: 把（沉物）打撈起來、使浮出水面

senses.definition: To cause (the land or any other object) to seem higher by drawing nearer to it.
senses.native: （透過靠近）使（陸地或物體）看起來更高

senses.definition: To make (bread, etc.) light, as by yeast or leaven.
To cause (a dead person) to live again; to resurrect.
To remove or break up (a blockade), either by withdrawing the ships or forces employed in enforcing it, or by driving them away or dispersing them.
To relinquish (a siege), or cause this to be done.
To emboss (sheet metal), or to form it into cup-shaped or hollow articles, by hammering, stamping, or spinning.
senses.native: （金工）錘出、壓出（金屬板的凸紋或杯形器物）

senses.definition: To create, increase or develop.
To collect or amass.
To call up the forces of, to raise the troops from.

examples.text: Raise your hands.
examples.translation: 手舉起來。

examples.text: Raise your leg.
examples.translation: 把你的腿抬起來

examples.text: If you have a thought, please raise your hand.
examples.translation: 如果你有意見請舉手。

examples.text: Raise your hand when I call your name.
examples.translation: 我叫你的名字的時候，請你把手舉起來。

examples.text: Boston is a great place to raise kids.
examples.translation: 波士頓是養育孩子的好地方。

examples.text: If you have a question, please raise your right hand.
examples.translation: 如果有問題，請舉起你的右手。

etymology.text: From Middle English reysen, raisen, reisen, from Old Norse reisa (“to raise”), from Proto-Germanic *raisijaną, *raizijaną (“to raise”), causative form of Proto-Germanic *rīsaną (“to rise”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rey- (“to rise, arise”). According to Kroonen (2013), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃er- (“to stir, rise”).

senses.definition: To be larger, greater than (something).
To be better than (something).
To go beyond (some limit); to surpass; to be longer than.
To predominate.
To go too far; to be excessive.

examples.text: The new product's sales exceeded expectations.
The profits exceeded all our expectations.
This concert exceeded my expectations.
Imports exceeded exports last year.
examples.translation: 去年的進口商品額超過了出口商品額。

examples.text: Benefits of course should exceed the costs.
The temperature exceeds 30 degrees in the shade.

relations.native: 眼睛如牛眼般大而鼓出的

etymology.text: From Middle English exceden, from Old French exceder, from Latin excēdō (“to go beyond”), from ex- (“out, forth”) with cēdō (“to go”); see cede and compare accede etc. Partly displaced native Old English ofersteppan, whence Modern English overstep.

senses.definition: A lustrous, white, metallic element, atomic number 47, atomic weight 107.87, symbol Ag.
Coins made from silver or any similar white metal.
A shiny gray color.
Cutlery and other eating utensils, whether silver or made from some other white metal.
Any items made from silver or any other white metal.
A silver medal.
Anything resembling silver; something shiny and white.

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: The Silver Surfer is part of the Marvel Universe.
examples.translation: 銀色巡遊者是漫威宇宙的一部分。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English silver, selver, sulver, from Old English seolfor, from Proto-West Germanic *silubr, from Proto-Germanic *silubrą (“silver”), of uncertain origin.
etymology.native: 「銀」源自中世紀英文 silver、selver、sulver，來源為古英語 seolfor，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *silubr，源自古德語 *silubrą，其來源不明。

senses.definition: Made from silver.
Having a color like silver: a shiny gray.
Made from another white metal.
Denoting the twenty-fifth anniversary, especially of a wedding.
Premium, but inferior to gold.
senses.native: 高貴但次於金的（銀級的）

senses.definition: Pertaining or relating to elderly persons.
Having the clear, musical tone of silver; soft and clear in sound.
senses.native: 音色清脆悅耳的；聲音柔和清晰的

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: Every cloud has a silver lining.
examples.translation: 每朵雲都披著銀衣。

examples.text: I collect silver spoons.
examples.translation: 我收集銀湯匙。

examples.text: How do you buy silver?
examples.translation: 你在哪買的銀？

examples.text: I like silver cars.
examples.translation: 我喜歡銀色的車。

examples.text: Donna was born with a silver spoon in her mouth.
examples.translation: Donna是含著金鑰匙出生的。

examples.text: As the saying goes: Speech is silver, silence is gold.
examples.translation: 常言道：言語是銀，沉默是金。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English silver, selver, sulver, from Old English seolfor, from Proto-West Germanic *silubr, from Proto-Germanic *silubrą (“silver”), of uncertain origin.
etymology.native: 「銀」源自中世紀英文 silver、selver、sulver，來源為古英語 seolfor，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *silubr，源自古德語 *silubrą，其來源不明。

senses.definition: Effortless, fluent (of work, abilities etc.).
senses.native: 毫不費力、流暢（指工作、能力等）

senses.definition: Lazy, simplistic, superficial (especially of explanations, discussions etc.).
senses.native: 懶惰、簡單化、膚淺（特別指解釋、討論等）

senses.definition: Of a reaction or other process, taking place readily.
senses.native: 反應或其他過程發生得容易

senses.definition: Easy; contemptibly easy.
Amiable, flexible, easy to get along with.

examples.text: Her writing was facile and articulate.
examples.translation: 她的寫作毫不費力且生動。

examples.text: Decarboxylation of beta-keto acids is facile.
examples.translation: β-酮酸的脫羧反應毫不費力。

examples.text: Critics dismissed the proposal as facile, noting its superficial nature.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The poem is facile.
examples.translation: 這首詩毫不費力。

examples.text: The hunger for facile wisdom is the root of all false philosophy.
examples.translation: 對簡易智慧的渴望是所有虛偽哲學的根源。

examples.text: I don't like Tom Jackson's writing because of all the facile alliteration.
examples.translation: 我不喜歡湯姆·傑克森的寫作，因為其中充滿了膚淺的頭韻。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French facile, from Latin facilis (“easy to do, easy, doable”), from Latin facere (“to do, make”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to do, put”) Compare Spanish and Portuguese fácil (“easy”), Catalan fàcil, Romanian facil. First use appears c. 1484 in a translation by William Caxton.
etymology.native: 借自中古法語 facile，源於拉丁語 facilis（「容易做、容易、可行」），來自拉丁語 facere（「做、製造」），源自原始印歐語 *dʰeh₁-（「做、放置」）。西班牙語和葡萄牙語 fácil、加泰隆尼亞語 fàcil 及羅馬尼亞語 facil 皆同源。首次出現約於 1484 年，由威廉·卡克斯頓翻譯時使用。

senses.definition: An achromatic colour between black and white.
An animal or thing of grey colour, such as a horse, badger, or salmon.
A gray wolf
A gray whale, Eschrichtius robustus.
Synonym of grey alien.
A penny with a tail on both sides, used for cheating.
A gray dye or pigment.
A pen, pencil, crayon, etc., made of gray pigment.
In the International System of Units, the derived unit of absorbed dose of radiation (radiation absorbed by a patient); one joule of energy absorbed per kilogram of the patient's mass.

examples.text: I like the gray sweater more than the purple one.
examples.translation: 比起紫色的毛衣，我更喜歡灰色的毛衣。

etymology.text: From Middle English gray, from Old English grǣġ (West Saxon). The spelling gray reflects the West Saxon vowel development, whereas the variant grey stems from the Anglian form grēġ (through Middle English grey). Further derived from Proto-West Germanic *grāu, from Proto-Germanic *grēwaz (“grey”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰreh₁- (“to green, to grow”).
etymology.native: 「gray」源自中世紀英文，來源為古英文 grǣġ（西撒克遜語），拼寫反映西撒克遜語的元音演變；而「grey」則源自盎格魯語 grēġ（經中世紀英文 grey）。「gray」進一步源自古西日耳曼語 *grāu，再溯源自古德語 *grēwaz（意為「灰的」），最終源自印歐語系 *ǵʰreh₁-（意為「變綠、生長」）

senses.definition: An object, usually in the form of a statuette, cup, or shield, awarded for success in a competition or to mark a special achievement.
An object taken as a prize by a hunter, or a conqueror or belligerent, especially one that is displayed.
Any emblem of success; a status symbol.
An object taken by a serial killer or rapist as a memento of the crime.

A display of weaponry and other militaria, often captured from a defeated enemy, as an ornament designed for the purpose of triumphalist display by a victor or as a show of military prowess by a monarch.
An artifact or artwork that has been stolen by a criminal and traded on the black market.
An animal killed by a trophy hunter that usually has its parts sold on the black market.
A tropæum.

examples.text: She presented him with the trophy.
examples.translation: 她將獎盃送給他。

examples.text: Winning the trophy made me happy.
examples.translation: 贏得獎盃讓我感到開心。

examples.text: Winning a trophy made Tom happy.
examples.translation: 贏得獎盃讓湯姆感到開心。

examples.text: What a moment this is as she lifts the trophy.
examples.translation: 她舉起獎盃的這一刻真令人動容。

examples.text: Stefan took the creature’s head as a trophy.
examples.translation: 斯特凡把那生物的頭當作獎盃拿走。

examples.text: Gabor checked the trophies in the hallways.
examples.translation: 加博在走廊檢查了所有獎盃。

etymology.text: From Middle French trophée, from Latin trophaeum (“a sign of victory, a monument”), tropaeum, from Ancient Greek τρόπαιον (trópaion, “monument of an enemy's defeat”), from neuter of τροπαῖος (tropaîos, “of defeat”), from τροπή (tropḗ, “a rout, a turning of an enemy”). Doublet of tropæum.
etymology.native: 「trophée」源自拉丁語「trophaeum」，意為「勝利的象徵或紀念碑」，源自古希臘語「τρόπαιον」，意為「敵人敗亡的紀念物」，而該詞又來自「τροπαῖος」，意為「敗亡的」，再源自「τροπή」，意為「潰敗、敵軍轉向」。此詞亦為「tropæum」的同源詞。

senses.definition: Clear; effective.
senses.native: 清晰的、有效的、有關節的

senses.definition: Speaking in a clear and effective manner; having both good articulation and good elocution.
senses.native: 能說會道的、口齒伶俐的

senses.definition: Consisting of segments united by joints.
Distinctly marked off.
Expressed in articles or in separate items or particulars.
Related to human speech, as distinct from the vocalisation of animals.
Articulated (all senses).

examples.text: The robot arm was articulate in two directions.

etymology.text: The adjective is first attested in 1531, the verb in 1551; borrowed from Latin articulātus (“distinct, articulated, jointed”), perfect passive participle of articulō, see -ate (etymology 1, 2 and 3). Regular participial usage of the adjective up until Early Modern English.

senses.definition: To make or become clammy.
To become silent; to stop talking.

examples.text: Every time I think of asking her out, I clam up.
examples.translation: 每次想到要約她出去，我就吞吞吐吐。

examples.text: I must clam up if I don’t want trouble.
examples.translation: 我不想惹麻煩，只好吞吞吐吐。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The teacher asked us to clam up during the test.
examples.translation: 老師要求我們考試時要吞吞吐吐。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: By analogy with a clam closing itself. Compare clamshell (“mouth”), clam (“mouth”).
etymology.native: 由貝類閉合自身之形狀推演而得。參見 clamshell（嘴）、clam（嘴）。

senses.definition: In near proximity.

examples.text: All right, Mr. DeMille, I'm ready for my close-up.
examples.translation: 好的，德米勒先生，我準備好接受近距離拍攝了。

examples.text: The camera came in for a close-up.
examples.translation: 鏡頭慢慢拉近，呈現近距離特寫。

examples.text: This is an close-up shot of the strawberry tree fruit.
examples.translation: 這是草莓樹果實的近距離特寫。

examples.text: Seen close-up, things have a way of showing their defects, their innate ugliness.
examples.translation: 近距離觀察下，事物往往會顯現其缺點與本質的醜陋。

examples.text: I should redo the close-up in the fifth panel; that expression didn't convince me just now.
examples.translation: 我應該在第五格重新拍攝近距離特寫；剛剛那表情並未讓我信服。

examples.text: I constantly feel observed by aliens creatures, be it from a close-up disntance or from afar.
examples.translation: 我總覺得有外星生物在觀察我，無論是從近距離還是遠處。

senses.definition: A photographic (or other) image in which the subject is shown at a relatively large scale, and occupies most or all of the frame.

examples.text: She took a close-up.
examples.translation: 她拍了一張特寫。

senses.definition: A component that draws attention or interest.
A beneficial capability of a piece of software.
A long, prominent article or item in the media, or the department that creates them; frequently used technically to distinguish content from news.
Any of the physical constituents of the face (eyes, nose, etc.).
The cast or structure of anything, or of any part of a thing, as of a landscape, a picture, a treaty, or an essay; any marked peculiarity or characteristic.
Something discerned from physical evidence that helps define, identify, characterize, and interpret an archeological site.
Characteristic forms or shapes of parts. For example, a hole, boss, slot, cut, chamfer, or fillet.
An individual measurable property or characteristic of a phenomenon being observed; the input of a model.
The act of being featured in a piece of music, as a collaborator. See verb sense below; also feat.
The elements into which linguistic units can be broken down.
One's structure or make-up: form, shape, bodily proportions.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Aramaic features an Akkadian substrate.
examples.translation: 亞拉姆語有阿卡德語的底層。

examples.text: Tobias had that feature switched off.
examples.translation: 多比雅把那個功能關掉了。

examples.text: The bathroom features a rain shower.
examples.translation: 浴室配有雨淋式蓮蓬頭。

examples.text: It's not a bug, it's an undocumented feature.
examples.translation: 這不是一個漏洞，而是一個沒有寫進文件的特性。

examples.text: The CAR-aoke feature in WHAT THE CAR? had me singing along with my car!
examples.translation: 《（WHAT THE CAR）?》裡的「車拉（OK）」功能讓我跟著車子一起唱！

examples.text: This app attracts over 10,000 users each day who engage with its features.
examples.translation: 這個應用程式每日吸引超過一萬位使用者使用其功能。

etymology.text: From Middle English feture, from Anglo-Norman feture, from Old French faiture, from Latin factūra, from Latin factus, from Latin faciō (“do, make”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to do, put, place, set”). Doublet of facture.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（feture），來自英法語（feture）、古法語（faiture），再源自拉丁語（factūra），來自（factus），源自（faciō）「做」，最終可溯至原始印歐語（*dʰeh₁-）「做、放」。與（facture）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: Closeness; the state of being near in space, time, or relationship.

examples.text: The big change is the proximity to death.
examples.translation: 最大的改變是面對死亡的近在咫尺。

examples.text: Blind people sometimes develop a compensatory ability to sense the proximity of objects around them.
examples.translation: 某些失明者會產生一個彌補性的能力，這個能力讓他們察覺到他們與離他們很近的物體的距離。

examples.text: Proximity to work was essential for him.
examples.translation: 離工作地點很近對他很關鍵。

examples.text: They want to build a hotel in proximity to the beach.
examples.translation: 他們想在海灘附近蓋飯店。

examples.text: The space probe Lucy is expected to arrive in 2025 to the proximity of the asteroid Donaldjohanson.
examples.translation: 太空探測器露西預計將於 2025 年抵達小行星唐納德約翰遜附近。

examples.text: Basically, distance is not an obstacle (on the other hand, how often proximity is one) to reach.
examples.translation: 基本上，距離不是障礙（不過，有時鄰近卻會成為阻礙）。

relations.native: 緊鄰之物，特別是指直角三角形中既非斜邊也非對邊的側邊

etymology.text: From proxim(ate) + -ity, from Middle French proximité, from Latin proximitās, proximitāt-, from proximus.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 proximus，經中法語與古法語演變而成。

senses.definition: Happening right away, instantly, with no delay.
Very close; direct or adjacent.
Manifestly true; requiring no argument.
Embedded as part of the instruction itself, rather than stored elsewhere (such as a register or memory location).
Used to denote that a transmission is urgent.

An artillery fire mission modifier for two types of fire mission to denote an immediate need for fire: Immediate smoke, all guns involved must reload smoke and fire. Immediate suppression, all guns involved fire the rounds currently loaded and then switch to high explosive with impact fused (unless fuses are specified).

examples.text: Immediate action should be taken.
We have more immediate concerns.
My immediate family are Muslim.
We received an immediate answer to our letter.
Not every problem has an immediate solution.
I can't give you an immediate answer for that.

etymology.text: From Old French immediat (French immédiat), borrowed from Late Latin immediātus (“without in-between, moderation”), from Latin in + mediātus, perfect passive participle of mediō (“to halve, to be in the middle”) (see -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from medius (“middle”). By surface analysis, im- + mediate.

senses.definition: To stand or meet facing, especially in competition, hostility or defiance; to come face to face with.
To deal with.
To bring someone face to face with something.
To come up against; to encounter.
To engage in confrontation.
To set a thing side by side with; to compare.
To put a thing facing to; to set in contrast to.

examples.text: He is confronted by many difficulties.
examples.translation: 他面臨著許多困難。

examples.text: I didn't confront them.
examples.translation: 我沒跟他們發生衝突。

examples.text: Minorities are confronted with many hardships.
examples.translation: 少數民族面臨許多艱難處境。

examples.text: We are confronted with a difficult situation.
examples.translation: 我們正處於艱難的境地。

examples.text: Santiago confronted Walid for being a weirdo.
examples.translation: 桑地亞哥因瓦利德太怪異而跟他對峙。

examples.text: Japan is confronted with severe economic problems.
examples.translation: 日本正面臨著嚴重的經濟問題。

etymology.text: From Middle French confronter, borrowed from Medieval Latin cōnfrontāre, from con- + frontem (“front, forehead”).
etymology.native: 來自中世紀拉丁語 cōnfrontāre，由 con- 與 frontem（意為「前額」）組成，源自法語 confronter。

senses.definition: To invite (someone) to take part in a competition.
To dare (someone).
To dispute (something); to contest.
To call something into question or dispute.
To make a formal objection to a juror.
To be difficult or challenging for.
To question or demand the countersign from (one who attempts to pass the lines).
To object to the reception of the vote of, e.g. on the ground that the person is not qualified as a voter.
senses.native: 對（某人的）投票資格提出異議

senses.definition: To take (a final exam) in order to get credit for a course without taking it.
senses.native: 參加（期末考）以抵免課程

senses.definition: To claim as due; to demand as a right.
To censure; to blame.

examples.text: Maintaining friendships can be challenging.
examples.translation: 維持友誼可能很不容易。

examples.text: Tom likes challenging himself.
examples.translation: 湯姆喜歡挑戰自己。

examples.text: Being challenged in life is inevitable, being defeated is optional.
examples.translation: 生命中你無法選擇接踵而至的挑戰，但是你可以選擇不成為一個失敗者。

examples.text: This will challenge any preconception you may have of modern art.
examples.translation: 這將挑戰你對現代藝術的任何先入之見。

examples.text: Living on a state subsidy provides a safety net during challenging times, ensuring a basic level of stability.
examples.translation: 靠國家補助過活，在艱困時期提供了一張安全網，確保基本的穩定。

examples.text: We challenged the boys next door to a game of football.
examples.translation: 我們向隔壁的男孩們挑戰踢足球。

senses.definition: To force a person to the ground with the weight of one's own body, usually by jumping on top or slamming one's weight into them.

senses.definition: To equip something with armor or a protective coating or hardening.
