pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: That armored truck is carrying gold.
examples.translation: 那輛裝甲車正運送黃金。

examples.text: Algeria manufactures military armored cars.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞製造軍用裝甲車。

examples.text: Dmitri drove a perfectly armored vehicle.
examples.translation: 迪米特里駕駛了一輛完美裝甲的車輛。

etymology.text: From Middle English armure, armour, armor, armeure, borrowed from Anglo-Norman armure and Old French armeüre, from Latin armātūra. Doublet of armature and armure. By surface analysis, arm (“to cover or furnish”) + -or (suffix forming agent nouns or nouns of quality, state, or condition).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 armure，來自盎格魯-諾曼語 armure 與古法語 armeüre，再源自拉丁文 armātūra。為 armature 與 armure 的同源詞。由 arm（意為「覆蓋或裝備」）+ -or（構成表示工具、品質、狀態或條件的名詞後綴）組成。

senses.definition: To supply with something necessary in order to carry out a specific action or task; to provide with (e.g. weapons, provisions, munitions, rigging).
To dress up; to array; to clothe.
To prepare (someone) with a skill.
To equip oneself with (an item); to bring (equipment) into active use.

examples.text: We've equipped our office with computers.
Our car is equipped with airconditioning.
The soldiers were equipped with weapons.
Our car is equipped with air conditioning.
examples.translation: 我們的車配備了冷氣。

examples.text: Large ships are all equipped with a lifeboat.
Make sure you're well equipped for your trip.

etymology.text: From French équiper (“to supply, fit out”), originally said of a ship, Old French esquiper (“to embark”); of Germanic origin, most probably from Old Norse skipa (“to man (a ship)”), from Proto-Germanic *skipōną (“to ship, sail, embark”).

senses.definition: A knitted jacket or jersey, usually of thick wool, worn by athletes before or after exercise.
A similar garment worn for warmth.
One who sweats (produces sweat).
One who or that which causes to sweat.
A diaphoretic remedy.
An exploitative middleman who subcontracted piece work in the tailoring trade.
One who sweats coins, i.e. removes small portions by shaking them.
A London street ruffian in Queen Anne's time who prodded passers-by with his sword-point.

examples.text: Your sweater is inside out.
examples.translation: 你毛衣穿反了喲。

examples.text: This blue sweater is very pretty.
examples.translation: 這件藍色毛衣很漂亮。

examples.text: My mother made me a sweater.
examples.translation: 我媽媽為我做了一件毛衣。

examples.text: Lao Zhang bought a sweater.
examples.translation: 老張買了一件毛衣。

examples.text: You'd better wear a sweater under your jacket.
examples.translation: 您最好在外衣里穿一件套衫。

examples.text: This sweater is all stretched out of shape.
examples.translation: 這件毛衣整個撐變形了。

etymology.text: From Middle English swētere, equivalent to sweat + -er.

senses.definition: Engaged in warfare, warring.
Eager to go to war, warlike.
Of or pertaining to war.
Aggressively hostile, eager to fight.
Acting violently towards others.
Uncooperative.

examples.text: Netanyahu is very belligerent.
examples.translation: 內塔尼亞胡非常好戰。

examples.text: Tom is belligerent.
examples.translation: 湯姆很好戰。

examples.text: She flaunts a belligerent attitude.
examples.translation: 她展現出好戰的態度。

examples.text: That pot-bellied, belligerent green ogre is back for yet another animated adventure.
examples.translation: 那個肥肥胖胖、好戰的綠色怪物又回來了，準備再開始一次動畫冒險。

examples.text: A belligerent tone.
examples.translation: 好戰的語氣。

examples.text: Belligerent (or warring) nations.
examples.translation: 好戰（或交戰）的國家。

etymology.text: From Latin belligerans (“waging war”), present active participle of belligerō (“to wage war”), from belliger (“waging war, warlike”), from bellum (“war”) + -ger (from gerō (“to lead, wage, carry on”)).
etymology.native: 來自拉丁語 belligerans，是 belligerō 的現在分詞，源自 belliger（意為「戰爭中」），由 bellum（意為「戰爭」）與 -ger（源自 gerō，意為「帶領、戰鬥、持續」）組成。

senses.definition: A state or other armed participant in warfare

examples.text: The UN sent a treaty proposal to the belligerents.
examples.translation: 聯合國向雙方好戰者提出條約草案。

etymology.text: From Latin belligerans (“waging war”), present active participle of belligerō (“to wage war”), from belliger (“waging war, warlike”), from bellum (“war”) + -ger (from gerō (“to lead, wage, carry on”)).
etymology.native: 來自拉丁語 belligerans，是 belligerō 的現在分詞，源自 belliger（意為「戰爭中」），由 bellum（意為「戰爭」）與 -ger（源自 gerō，意為「帶領、戰鬥、持續」）組成。

senses.definition: A person who fights; a combatant.
A warrior; a fighting soldier.
A pugnacious, competitive person.
A class of fixed-wing aircraft whose primary purpose is to shoot down other aircraft, sometimes accompanied by a secondary purpose of attacking ground targets.
A starfighter
A participant in boxing or any martial art.
A game with a focus on physical combat.
A person with a strong determination to resist protracted or severe adversity, especially illness.
A firefighter.

examples.text: Our fighters averaged 430 missions a day.
Antonio is a successful karate fighter.
Algeria has Russian-made fighters.
One man's terrorist is another man's freedom fighter.
examples.translation: 一個人的恐怖分子為另人的自由戰士。

examples.text: The fire fighters put out the fire.
examples.translation: 消防隊員把火撲滅了。

examples.text: Archers were key fighters in ancient battles.

relations.native: 裁剪和試樣的服裝工人/裁縫

etymology.text: From Middle English fightere, feghtere, from Old English feohtere. Equivalent to fight + -er.

senses.definition: Fighting or disposed to fight; belligerent, warlike.
Aggressively supporting of an idea, group, political or social cause, etc.; adamant, combative.
senses.native: 積極支持某種理念、團體、政治或社會運動等；堅決好鬥的

examples.text: He was the head of the League of Militant Atheists.
examples.translation: 他是無神論者聯盟的好戰領袖。

examples.text: Militant in fighting for better wages for workers.
examples.translation: 為爭取工人較佳薪資而好戰地奮鬥。

examples.text: The man was said to be part of a rogue militant group.
examples.translation: 據說那個人屬於一個脫管的武裝團體。

examples.text: The militant group demanded immediate surrender from the government forces.
examples.translation: 該武裝團體要求政府部隊立即投降。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Her militant stance on social justice often alienates moderate political allies.
examples.translation: 她在社會正義問題上採取的好戰立場，常使溫和的政治盟友感到疏離。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Middle French militant, from Latin mīlitāns, present participle of mīlitāre (“to serve as a soldier”).
etymology.native: 源於中古法語 militant，來自拉丁語 mīlitāns，動詞 mīlitāre 之現在分詞（意為「服役」）。

senses.definition: Contending or acting against.
Relating to an antagonist.

examples.text: The two countries are antagonistic to each other.
examples.translation: 這兩個國家彼此敵對。

examples.text: Why is Tom being so antagonistic?
examples.translation: 為什麼湯姆這麼敵對？

examples.text: Buddhists seem less antagonistic towards science than are Christians.
examples.translation: 佛教徒對科學的態度似乎比基督徒更開放。

examples.text: The emotional qualities are antagonistic to clear reasoning.
examples.translation: 情感特質與清晰推理相悖。

examples.text: His antagonistic brusqueness.
examples.translation: 他那種敵對的粗魯態度。

examples.text: Europe was antagonistic to the United States.
examples.translation: 歐洲對美國持敵對態度。

etymology.text: From antagonist + -ic.
etymology.native: 來自 antagonist + -ic。

senses.definition: Not at war; not disturbed by strife or turmoil.
Inclined to peace.
Motionless and calm.

examples.text: Most people enjoy starry, peaceful nights.
Elephants are usually peaceful animals.
Adriano's street is peaceful at night.
Man should make peaceful use of technologies.
Is there a peaceful way to fight for freedom?
My neighbors are peaceful people of good will.

etymology.text: From Middle English peesful, pesful, paisful, pesefull. By surface analysis, peace + -ful. Displaced native Old English friþsum.

senses.definition: Warlike or combative in nature; aggressively hostile.

examples.text: Such a bellicose attitude won't win you any friends.
examples.translation: 這種好戰的態度無法讓你贏得任何朋友。

examples.text: "What's that supposed to mean?" he asked in a bellicose tone.
examples.translation: 「那代表什麼意思？」他帶著好戰的語氣問道。

examples.text: They would unquestionably diminish his bellicose outbursts.
examples.translation: 他們絕對會減少他的好戰爆發次數。

examples.text: You don't have to be so bellicose, and we can work out a peaceful solution.
examples.translation: 你不必如此好戰，我們可以找出和平的解決方案。

examples.text: Bellicose young officers.
examples.translation: 年輕的好戰軍官們。

examples.text: His bellicose nature often caused unnecessary conflicts in the office.
examples.translation: 他好戰的本性常在辦公室引發不必要的衝突。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

morphemes.native: 好戰的或具有攻擊性的、敵意強烈的

etymology.text: From Middle English bellicose, from Latin bellicosus.
etymology.native: 此詞源於中古英語，來自拉丁語。

senses.definition: Having the same pretensions or claims; standing in competition for superiority.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

etymology.text: Learned borrowing from Latin rīvālis (literally “person using the same stream as another”). By surface analysis, Latin rīvus + -al.
etymology.native: 此詞源自拉丁語 rivālis，字面意為「與他人共用同一條溪流的人」。若依表面分析，則由 rivus（溪流）加上 -al 構成。

senses.definition: Characteristic of members of the armed forces.
Relating to war.
Relating to armies or ground forces.
Relating to armed forces such as the army, marines, navy and air force (often as distinguished from civilians or police forces).

examples.text: What's Algeria's greatest military deterrence?
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞最大的軍事嚇阻力量是什麼？

examples.text: Algeria is increasing its military capacities.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞正在增強其軍事實力。

examples.text: Algeria manufactures military armored cars.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞製造軍用裝甲車。

examples.text: The military power of this country is very advanced.
examples.translation: 這個國家的軍事力量很先進。

examples.text: There is a military base near here.
examples.translation: 這附近有一個軍事基地。

examples.text: The Japanese military forces seemed too strong to stop.
examples.translation: 日本軍隊看來強大得不可阻擋。

relations.native: 固守某種特定理念之堅定支持者，現尤指特定意識形態派系之成員

etymology.text: From Middle English militari, from Old French militaire, from Latin mīlitāris, from mīles (“soldier”) + -āris (whence -ary). Doublet of militaire.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（militari），來自古法語（militaire），再源自拉丁語（mīlitāris），由（mīles）「士兵」加（-āris，即 -ary）組成。與（militaire）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: Alternative spelling of chain mail.

examples.text: I wear chainmail for protection.
examples.translation: 我穿鎖甲以作防護。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Chainmail is strong and durable.
examples.translation: 鎖甲堅固且耐久。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The knight wore chainmail to fight.
examples.translation: 騎士穿著鎖甲出戰。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Chainmail protects soldiers in battle.
examples.translation: 鎖甲在戰場上保護士兵。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Ancient warriors wore chainmail for safety.
examples.translation: 古代戰士穿著鎖甲以求安全。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Chainmail is a type of armor used in history.
examples.translation: 鎖甲是歷史中使用的一種盔甲。

senses.definition: That which remains; that which is left after loss or decay; a remaining portion.
A part of the body of a saint, or an ancient religious object, kept for veneration.
Something old and outdated, possibly kept for sentimental reasons.
A particle or entity that has existed since the Big Bang.

examples.text: Rome abounds with relics.
examples.translation: 羅馬遍佈古物。

examples.text: Here were some relics.
examples.translation: 這裡有些古物。

examples.text: Basque is a relic.
examples.translation: 巴斯克文化是一種古物。

examples.text: David will become a relic of the past.
examples.translation: 戴維將成為過去的古物。

examples.text: Antonio threw the relic from the boat.
examples.translation: 安東尼把古物從船上拋了出去。

examples.text: Cherish our cultural relics; it is all our duty.
examples.translation: 愛護文物, 人人有責。

etymology.text: From Middle English relik et al., from Old French relique, from Latin reliquiae (“remains, relics”), from relinquō (“to leave behind, abandon, relinquish”), from re- + linquō (“to leave, quit, forsake, depart from”). Doublet of relict, derelict, and relinquish.
etymology.native: 「relik」源自中世紀英文，來自古法文「relique」，再源自拉丁文「reliquiae」（意為「遺物、遺蹟」），而拉丁文則來自「relinquō」（意為「留下、放棄」），由「re-」與「linquō」（意為「離開、放棄」）組成。此詞與「relict」、「derelict」、「relinquish」同源。

senses.definition: A part or parts remaining after some has/have been removed or already occurred.

The amount left over after subtracting the divisor as many times as possible from the dividend without producing a negative result. If n (dividend) and d (divisor) are integers, then n can always be expressed in the form n = dq + r, where q (quotient) and r (remainder) are also integers and 0 ≤ r < d.
The number left over after a simple subtraction
Excess stock items left unsold and subject to reduction in price.
An estate in expectancy which only comes in its heir's possession after an estate created by the same instrument has been determined

examples.text: He was excused from the remainder of the work.
He will stay here for the remainder of his life.
The remainder of the evening was peaceful.
The remainder of his tirade included a number of swear words.
The remainder of his sentence was drowned out by the sudden noise.
Tom lived out the remainder of his days in peace and quiet reflection.

relations.native: 剩餘的、與殘渣有關的，或作為殘渣留存下來
剩餘的、與殘渣有關的，或作為殘渣留存下來

etymology.text: From Middle English remaindre, remeigner, from Anglo-Norman remaindre, with infinitive used as noun.

senses.definition: That which persists or remains following the removal or elimination of other elements.
A form of complex number, proportional to the contour integral of a meromorphic function along a path enclosing one of its singularities.
The substance that remains after evaporation, distillation, filtration or any similar process.
A molecule that is released from a polymer after bonds between neighbouring monomers are broken, such as an amino acid in a polypeptide chain.
Whatever property or effects are left in an estate after payment of all debts, other charges and deduction of what is specifically bequeathed by the testator.
A representative element of an equivalence class modulo some base, conventionally in the half-open interval from zero to the base; the nonnegative remainder after dividing a number by a base.

examples.text: Check the fridge's shelves and drawers for any food residue.
examples.translation: 檢查冰箱的架子和抽屜，查看是否有食物殘留。

examples.text: Check the ovenware for any stuck-on residue.
examples.translation: 檢查烤箱內的器具是否有黏附的殘留物。

examples.text: There's residue stuck to the bottom of the pot.
examples.translation: 鍋底黏著了一些殘留物。

examples.text: They found gunshot residue on the victim's hand.
examples.translation: 他們在受害者手上發現了槍擊殘留物。

examples.text: There was gunshot residue on Tom's jacket.
examples.translation: 湯姆的外套上有槍擊殘留物。

examples.text: They found gunshot residue on Tom's hands.
examples.translation: 他們在湯姆的手上發現了槍擊殘留物。

relations.native: 剩餘的、與殘渣有關的，或作為殘渣留存下來

etymology.text: From Middle English residue, from Old French residu, from Latin residuum, neuter of residuus (“remaining”), from resideō (“to remain behind”). Doublet of residuum.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 residue，來自舊法語 residu，拉丁語 residuum（剩餘物），residueō 之中性詞。與 residuum 同根。

senses.definition: A small portion remaining of a larger thing or group; part of a former whole.
The remaining fabric at the end of the bolt.
An unsold end of piece goods, as cloth, ribbons, carpets, etc.
senses.native: 未售出的整件貨物末端，如布料、絲帶、地毯等

senses.definition: The passionate, influential minority of radicals in a faction or party.
senses.native: 派系或政黨中熱情且有影響力的少數激進分子

examples.text: The statue stood as a remnant of a defunct civilization.
examples.translation: 那尊雕像作為一個廢棄文明遺留的殘蹟而矗立著。

examples.text: A remnant of the old army is supporting and perhaps leading the current chaos.
examples.translation: 舊軍隊的一小撮殘部正在支持並或許領導當前的混亂局面。

examples.text: The pursued remnant of soldiers decided it was high time for a show-down one way or another.
examples.translation: 被追趕的士兵殘部決定，無論如何都該是展開決戰的時候了。

examples.text: This usage isn't a sign of being uneducated but rather a remnant of an older form of the language.
examples.translation: 這種用法並非表示受教育程度不足，而是語言較古老形式的遺存。

examples.text: The remnants of the Neanderthal race mixed with members of Homo sapiens.
examples.translation: 尼安德特人的殘餘與智人成員混合在一起。

examples.text: Usually not enough to make an entire project by itself, remnants of several fabrics can be used to make quilts.
examples.translation: 通常單獨不足以完成整個專案，但幾種布料的殘片可縫製成被子。

relations.native: 屬於剩餘部分的性質或特徵
剩餘的一小部分，來自較大事物或群體；前一個整體的一部分
剩餘的一小部分，來自較大事物或群體；前一個整體的一部分
剩餘的一小部分，來自較大事物或群體；前一個整體的一部分

etymology.text: From Middle English, contraction of remenant, from Anglo-Norman remanant, present participle of remaindre, from Latin remaneō.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語，由 remenant 縮合而成，來自安格洛 - 諾曼語 remanant，即 remaindre 的現在分詞，源自拉丁語 remaneō。

senses.definition: Ancient times; faraway history; former ages.
The people of ancient times.
The historical period preceding the Middle Ages (c. 500-1500), primarily relating to European history.
A relic or monument of ancient times, such as a coin, a statue, etc.; an ancient institution.
The state of being ancient or of ancient lineage.
An old gentleman.

examples.text: Rivers are the roads of antiquity.
The museum exhibits sculptures from antiquity.
Since antiquity, man has always wanted to fly.
In antiquity, architecture was beautiful and refined.
He has an exclusive antiquities shop in Manhattan.
The origin of the universe has been studied by man since antiquity.

etymology.text: From Middle English antiquyte, antiquite, antiquytee, a borrowing from Old French antiquité, antiquitet, from Latin antiquitas, from antiquus. Equivalent to antique + -ity. See antique, antic. Compare with French antiquité.

senses.definition: The fact or act of surviving; continued existence or life.
Of, relating to or aiding survival.
The avoidance of relegation or demotion to a lower league or division.
A custom or belief that persists in folklore from earlier times, when the rationale behind it is forgotten.

examples.text: Tom's survival was considered miraculous.
Vladimir's survival instincts kicked in.
Has Tom learned new survival skills?
His own survival is more important now.
examples.translation: 他自己的生存現在更重要了。

examples.text: I gave up all hope of survival.
examples.translation: 我放棄了所有生存的希望。

examples.text: This medicine will increase the survival rate of the patients.
examples.translation: 這個藥品會提高病人的存活率。

etymology.text: From survive + -al.

senses.definition: The striking of one body against another; collision.
The force or energy of a collision of two objects.
A forced impinging.
A significant or strong influence or effect.

examples.text: How did colonization impact Algeria economically?
Astronomers are studying Mercury's impact craters.
They discussed the book's impact on society.
What about the environmental impact?
examples.translation: 那環境影響呢？

examples.text: The blizzard has already had a severe impact on the economy.
examples.translation: 這場暴風雪已經對經濟造成了嚴重的影響。

examples.text: Education can reduce the impact of fake news.

etymology.text: Attested since the 17th century, from Latin impāctus.

senses.definition: Related to a rite or repeated set of actions.

examples.text: The ritual was completed.
examples.translation: 儀式完成了。

examples.text: There's also the initiation ritual.
examples.translation: 也有入門儀式。

examples.text: The sky cleared up after the ritual was over.
examples.translation: 祭祀結束之後，天就晴了。

examples.text: A sacred ritual took place in the magnificent temple.
examples.translation: 一個神聖的儀式在莊嚴的廟宇中舉行。

examples.text: The Heavenly Timber Immolation is a kind of ancient ritual.
examples.translation: 燔柴祭天是一種古老的儀式。

examples.text: They're doing a pagan ritual in the backyard.
examples.translation: 他們在後院進行了原始宗教儀式。

etymology.text: From Latin rītuālis (adjective), from rītus (“rite”) + -ālis. Displaced native Old English ġewuna and wuna.
etymology.native: 此詞源自拉丁語 rītuālis，由 rītus（儀式）與 -ālis 組成，取代了古英語的 ġewuna 與 wuna。

senses.definition: A rite; a repeated set of actions, especially in religious contexts (that is, a service).

examples.text: The priests carried out the religious ritual carefully.
examples.translation: 神父們謹慎地執行宗教儀式。

etymology.text: From Latin rītuālis (adjective), from rītus (“rite”) + -ālis. Displaced native Old English ġewuna and wuna.
etymology.native: 此詞源自拉丁語 rītuālis，由 rītus（儀式）與 -ālis 組成，取代了古英語的 ġewuna 與 wuna。

senses.definition: A religious custom.
A prescribed behavior.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: It's a rite of passage.
examples.translation: 這是一種過渡儀式。

etymology.text: Via Middle English and Old French, from Latin ritus.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語與古法語，來自拉丁語 ritus。

senses.definition: An action performed on a regular basis.
An action performed repeatedly and automatically, usually without awareness.
An addiction.
A long piece of clothing worn by monks and nuns.

Outward appearance; attire; dress.

etymology.text: From Middle English habit, from Latin habitus (“condition, bearing, state, appearance, dress, attire”), from habeō (“to have, hold, keep”). Distantly related to gift. Replaced Middle English abit, from Old French abit, itself from the same Latin source. Displaced native Old English þēaw, wuna, ġewuna, and sidu.

senses.definition: The formal performance of a solemn rite, such as Christian sacrament.
The observance of a holiday or feast day, as by solemnities.

A social gathering for entertainment and fun; a party.

Customs include food, celebrations and dancing.

etymology.text: From Old French celebration, from Latin celebratio. Equivalent to celebrate + -ion.

senses.definition: Words or a formula supposed to have magical powers.
A magical effect or influence induced by an incantation or formula.
Speech, discourse.
A shift (of work); (rare) a set of workers responsible for a specific turn of labour.
A definite period (of work or other activity).
An indefinite period of time (usually with a qualifier); by extension, a relatively short distance.
A period of rest; time off.
A period of illness, or sudden interval of bad spirits, disease etc.
An uninterrupted series of alternate overs bowled by a single bowler.
A splinter, usually of wood; a spelk.
The wooden bat in the game of trap ball, or knurr and spell.

examples.text: How do you spell your name?

etymology.text: From Middle English spell, spel, from Old English spell (“news, story”), from Proto-Germanic *spellą (“speech, account, tale”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)pel- (“to tell”) or from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel- (“to speak, to sound”) with the s-mobile prefix. Cognate with dialectal German Spill, Icelandic spjall (“discussion, talk”), spjalla (“to discuss, to talk”), guðspjall (“gospel”) and Albanian fjalë (“word”).

senses.definition: The devotion accorded to a deity or to a sacred object.

senses.native: （宗教）崇拜，唯獨敬拜上帝，高於對聖母與聖人的尊崇

senses.definition: The religious ceremonies that express this devotion.
Voluntary, utter submission; voluntary, utter deference.

senses.definition: Ardent love.
An object of worship.
Used as a title or term of address for various officials, including magistrates.
senses.native: （英）閣下、大人，用於官員的敬稱

senses.definition: The fact of an artist's music heavily drawing influence from some other artist's work in a way that appears too obvious or unapologetic; a piece of music that does this.

etymology.native: 源自「儀式」加上表示狀態的後綴。

The glans penis.

The Old French is itself of Germanic origin (whence Old English helm). Used in English since the 15th century, it has largely displaced helm as the general word.

senses.definition: To cover with, or as if with, a helmet.

etymology.text: From Middle English helmet, helmett, a borrowing from Old French helmet, heaumet, a diminutive of helme (Modern French heaume), equivalent to helm + -et. The Old French is itself of Germanic origin (whence Old English helm). Used in English since the 15th century, it has largely displaced helm as the general word.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 helmet、helmett，來自古法文 helmet、heaumet，是 helme（現代法文 heaume）的縮小形式，等同於 helm + -et。古法文本身源自日耳曼語（ whence 古英語 helm）。自15世紀起在英文中使用，已 largely 取代 helm 成為通用詞。

senses.definition: The main bones of the head considered as a unit; including the cranium, facial bones, and mandible.

etymology.text: From Middle English sculle, scolle (also schulle, scholle), probably from a dialectal form of Old Norse skalli (“bald head, skull”), itself probably related to Old English sċealu (“husk”), to Proto-Norse *ᛋᚲᚨᛚᛟ (*skalo), from Proto-Germanic *skallô; compare Finnish kallo. Compare Scots scull, Danish skal (“skull”) and skalle (“bald head, skull”), Norwegian skalle, Swedish skalle and especially dialectal Swedish skulle.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 sculle 或 scolle，可能來自古諾斯語 skalli（「禿頭、頭骨」），與古英語 sċealu（「外皮」）有關，源自原始諾斯語 *skalo；對比芬蘭語 kallo。對比蘇格蘭語 scull、丹麥語 skal 和 skalle、挪威語 skalle、瑞典語 skalle 及方言瑞典語 skulle。

senses.definition: A junction or joining of ropes made by splicing them together.

examples.text: This sentence contains a comma splice. Replacing the comma with a period or a semicolon would fix the problem.
If the ball hits the splice, it is likely to dolly up for an easy catch.
The break was due to an imperfect splice.

etymology.text: Circa 1525, borrowed from Middle Dutch splissen (Modern Dutch splitsen); akin to Middle Dutch splitten (“to split”), German spleißen (“to split, splice”), Spliss (“split ends, hair breakage”), French épisser (also from Dutch). The Dutch word originally referred only to the fraying of the ropes' ends but was then also used for the entire process of fraying and retying; hence the peculiar semantic development from “split” to “join”. The same development occurred in German.

examples.text: This cold weather is really bad for rheumatoid arthritis.
examples.translation: 這寒冷天氣對類風濕性關節炎真的非常不利。

senses.definition: A person who is not susceptible to infection by a particular disease

examples.text: We will have lunch together at twelve-thirty.
examples.translation: 我們中午十二點半要一起吃午飯。

etymology.text: From Late Middle English together, from earlier togedere, togadere, from Old English tōgædere (“together”), from Proto-West Germanic *tōgadura, *tegadura, from Proto-Germanic *tō (“to”) + *gadar (“together”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰedʰ- (“to unite, keep”), equivalent to to-₂ + gather. Cognate with Scots thegither (“together”), Old Frisian togadera (whence West Frisian togearre (“together”)), Dutch tegader (“together”), Middle Low German tōgāder (“together”), Middle High German zegater (“tog
etymology.native: 源自晚期中古英語（together），更早為（togedere、togadere），來自古英語（tōgædere）「一起」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*tō）「到」加（*gadar）「一起」，最終來自原始印歐語（*gʰedʰ-）「結合」。相當於（to）加（gather）。與荷蘭語（tegader）同源。

senses.definition: A section.
In the schedule for an aircraft and its crew, the period starting with preparation of the plane before loading at one airport and ending with deplaning at the next.
An area designated by boundaries within which a unit operates, and for which it is responsible.
One of the subdivisions of a coastal frontier.
a fictional region of space designated for navigational or governance purposes.
A community or subculture within the wider intermicronational community.
Part of a circle, extending to the center; circular sector.
A portion of a sphere or ball defined by a conical boundary with apex at the center of the sphere.
A fixed-sized unit (traditionally 512 bytes) of sequential data stored on a track of a digital medium.
An instrument consisting of two rulers of equal length joined by a hinge.
A field of economic activity.
A toothed gear whose face is the arc of a circle.
A fixed, continuous section of the track, such that sectors do not overlap but all sectors make up the whole track.
An area of a crag, consisting of various routes

senses.definition: A piece of work done as part of one’s duties.
A state of diligence in work on a task.
Any piece of work done.
A single action undertaken by a given agent.
A difficult or tedious undertaking; a substantial project.
An objective or duty.
A process or execution of a program.
State of being subject to reprimands.
A tax or charge.

examples.text: What are my tasks?
examples.translation: 我的工作是什麼？

examples.text: This task can be completed effortlessly.
Have you already completed this task?
Tom's task is to teach the kid horse riding.
examples.translation: 湯姆的任務是教孩子騎馬。

examples.text: I must go through the task by tomorrow.

examples.text: Cleaning up the house is truly my most dreaded task.
examples.translation: 打掃屋子真的是我最害怕的工作。

etymology.text: From Middle English taske (“task, tax”), from Old Northern French tasque, (compare Old French variant tasche), from Medieval Latin tasca, alteration of taxa, from Latin taxō (“to censure; to charge”). Doublet of tax.

senses.definition: A cluster of heterogeneous things.
A corporation formed by the combination of several smaller corporations whose activities are unrelated to the corporation's primary activity.
A rock consisting of gravel or pebbles embedded in a matrix.

The conglomerate peoples of New England.

senses.definition: To display or show (something) for others to see, especially at an exhibition or contest.
To demonstrate.
To submit (a physical object) to a court as evidence.
To put on a public display.
To administer as a remedy.

examples.text: I'm going to exhibit my roses at the flower show.
examples.translation: 我要把我的玫瑰拿到花展上展示。

examples.text: The zoo's butterfly exhibit amazed Adriano.
examples.translation: 動物園的蝴蝶展區讓阿德里亞諾驚嘆

examples.text: He's exhibiting better mental health.
examples.translation: 他的心理狀態改善了

examples.text: The zoo's insect exhibit fascinated Adriano.

examples.translation: 博物館展出古代雕塑

examples.text: The zoo's nocturnal exhibit intrigued Adriano.

etymology.text: From Latin exhibitus, perfect passive participle of exhibeō (“to hold forth, present, show, display”), from ex (“out of, from”) + habeō (“to have, hold”); see habit.
etymology.native: 來自拉丁語 exhibitus，是 exhibeō 的完全動詞過去分詞（意為「展示、呈現」），由 ex（「出自、從」）+ habeō（「擁有、持有」）組成；見 habit。

senses.definition: To assemble for inspection, to receive orders, etc.

senses.definition: To assemble soldiers for inspection, to receive orders, etc.
senses.native: 集合士兵以接受檢閱或下達命令

senses.definition: Synonym of show off: to display or reveal prominently or ostentatiously, especially in a kind of procession.
senses.native: 炫耀；張揚地展示或陳列（常以遊行形式）

senses.definition: To furnish with a parade or parades.

examples.text: Boys and girls were parading along the street.
After the field show, it is customary to parade the stands before exiting the field.
They paraded dozens of fashions past the crowd.

etymology.text: From French parade (“an ostentatious display, a military display”), from parer (“to beautify, prepare, take pride in”) + -ade probably under influence from earlier Italian parata (“preparation, a military parade, an ostentatious display”) and Latin magnō parātū (“with great preparation”). Various senses similarly influenced by earlier French and Italian uses. Doublet of pare.

senses.definition: A large-scale public showing of objects or products.
An instance of exhibiting, or something exhibited.
A public display, intentional or otherwise, generally characterised as negative.
A demonstration of personal skill or feelings.
A financial award or prize given to a student (who becomes an exhibitioner) by a school or university, usually on the basis of academic merit.
A game which does not impact the standings for any major cup or competition.

examples.text: The exhibition is already open.
examples.translation: 展覽現在已經開放。

examples.text: The exhibition was very interesting.
examples.translation: 這次展覽非常有趣。

etymology.text: From Old French exhibicion. Equivalent to exhibit + -ion.
etymology.native: 源自古法語「展示」。相當於「展出」加名詞字尾。

To have the ability to use, or knowledge of (a language, a skill, etc.)
To inhabit or occupy (a place).
Chiefly followed by that: to convince or persuade (someone).

examples.translation: 我叔叔擁有很多的財富。

examples.text: I possess three kinds of video-game machines.
Possessing money does not equate with wisdom.

etymology.text: From Middle English possessen (“to have, own; to obtain possession of; to inhabit, occupy”) [and other forms], from Middle French possesser, possessier, Old French possesser, possessier (“to have, own, possess; to dominate”), from Latin possessus (“possessed; seized”), the perfect passive participle of possideō (“to have, hold, own, possess; to have possessions; to take control or possession of, occupy, seize; to abide, inhabit, occupy; to dominate”), from potis (“able, capable, possible”) (from

senses.definition: To forbid, disallow, or proscribe officially; to make illegal or illicit.

senses.definition: A smaller, self-contained part of a larger entity. Often refers to a manufactured object that is part of a larger device.

To become widespread.

examples.translation: 傳播知識並非該網站的使命。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin dissēminātus, the perfect passive participle of dissēminō (“to broadcast, disseminate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), further from dis- (“asunder, in all directions”) + sēminō (“to plant, sow”), from sēmen (“seed”) + -ō (verb-forming suffix). See also Middle English disseminat(e) (“disseminated”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 dissēminātus，為 dissēminō（「廣播、散佈」）之完成被動分詞。

senses.definition: To encourage or heavily exert force or influence.

senses.definition: The practice of manipulating or the state of being manipulated.

The usage of psychological influence over a person, event, or situation to gain a desired outcome.

Any influence which is compounded or used to gain an advantage.

The debt-to-equity ratio.

The distance of between an independent observation and other observations.

etymology.text: From lever + -age. The verb likely comes from martial arts/judo usage, where one would "use an opponent's leverage (i.e. their weight, height, centre of balance, etc.)" against them in order to defeat them.

senses.definition: Sly; crafty; clever in surreptitious behaviour.
Skillful, artful.
Wrought with, or exhibiting, skill or ingenuity; ingenious.
Cute, appealing.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Jayjay followed Jessica's cunning plan.

senses.definition: Practical knowledge or experience; aptitude in performance; skill, proficiency; dexterity.

The natural wit or instincts of an animal.
Knowledge; learning; special knowledge (sometimes implying occult or magical knowledge).

Smart, intelligent, or witty; mentally quick or sharp.

Possessing magical abilities.
Fit and healthy; free from fatigue or illness.

Good-natured; obliging.
Fit; suitable; having propriety.

senses.definition: Hard to deal with, complicated.
Adept at using deception.
Relating to or associated with a prostitution trick.

senses.definition: Of an action or movement: very delicate or slight, and thus barely noticeable; not obvious; inconspicuous, unintrusive.
Of a substance, especially a gas or liquid: of low density or thin consistency; rarefied, tenuous; hence, tending to spread everywhere due to this quality.

Of an argument or concept, words, etc.: requiring one to distinguish between fine points, especially if it is difficult to do so; nice; also (generally), difficult to grasp; not easily understood or obvious.
Giving only a slight impression; elusive, indistinct; also, skilfully restrained or understated.
Of an artist, a musician, etc.: having a light touch; sensitive.
Of a person: sensitive to the feelings of others; discreet, tactful.
Of a person, their intellect or mind, etc.: discerning, perceptive, shrewd, wise.
Acting (especially causing harm) in a stealthy, often gradual, manner; insidious.
Having a delicate or fine substance or texture; hence, exquisite, refined.
Slender, thin.
Of a substance: finely powdered; also, of particles of a substance: very fine or small.
Of weight: after the tare (“weight of an empty container”) has been subtracted; net.
Synonym of subtile (“of a ship: narrow, slender”).
Of a person or their fingers or hands, their ability, etc.: dexterous, skilful.
Of a person or animal, or of an action or words: clever or skilful in a crafty or devious way; cunning, sly, wily.
Of ground used for bowling: not smooth; uneven.
Of an object: cleverly contrived or made; also, of a plan, etc.: cleverly contrived or carried out.

examples.text: There wasn't anything subtle about it.
Jeffrey knows he's not subtle, right?

examples.translation: 這兩張圖片之間有細緻的差異。

examples.text: Being thirsty is a subtle sign of dehydration.

etymology.text: The adjective is derived from Middle English sotil, soubtil, subtil (“of a person, the mind, etc.: clever, ingenious, penetrating; cunning, sly; insidious; delicate, fine; not dense, light, thin; finely powdered; narrow, slender; etc.”), borrowed from Anglo-Norman sotel, subtil, sutil, Middle French soutil, subtil, sutil, and Old French sotil, soutil, subtil, sutil (“of an object: skilfully designed or made; delicate, fine; slender, thin; of an intangible thing: difficult to understand; of a per

senses.definition: Slender in an attractive way.
Designed to make the wearer appear slim.
Long and narrow.
Of a reduced size, with the intent of being more efficient.
Very small, tiny.
Bad, of questionable quality; not strongly built, flimsy.
Sly, crafty.

examples.text: I am getting slim!
examples.translation: 我正在變苗條！

examples.text: Tom reckoned his chances were slim.
My chances of winning are slim.

examples.translation: 她有著一頭金髮，瘦高的身材。

examples.text: The chance Tom will be executed is very slim.

etymology.text: Borrowing from Low German or Dutch slim (“bad, sly, clever”), from Middle Dutch slim (“bad, crooked”), from Old Dutch *slimb, from Proto-West Germanic *slimb, from Proto-Germanic *slimbaz (“oblique, crooked”). The sense development would have been "slanting, cunning" (Dutch) > "insignificant, slight" and then "thin, graceful" in English, a shift that Liberman calls an "incredible amelioration" of word meaning.

Lack of artificial ornament, pretentious style, or luxury; plainness

senses.definition: A capacity to do something well; a technique, an ability, usually acquired or learned, as opposed to abilities that are regarded as innate.

Discrimination; judgment; propriety; reason; cause.
Knowledge; understanding.
Display of art; exercise of ability; contrivance; address.

examples.translation: 你直覺到湯姆會這麼做，對吧？

examples.text: I had a hunch that something bad was going to happen.
examples.translation: 我有一種直覺，有壞事即將發生。

examples.text: Having boasted how sure his hunches were, he was forced to eat his hat when he guessed wrong.
examples.translation: 他自稱直覺很準，結果猜錯了，只好吃掉帽子。

etymology.text: Assibilated variant of hunk, of uncertain origin.
etymology.native: hunk 的一種送氣變體，起源不明。

senses.definition: To bend the top of one's body forward while raising one's shoulders.
To raise (one's shoulders) (while lowering one's head or bending the top of one's body forward); to curve (one's body) forward (sometimes followed by up).
To walk (somewhere) while hunching one's shoulders.
To thrust a hump or protuberance out of (something); to crook, as the back.
To push or jostle with the elbow; to push or thrust against (someone).
To have a hunch, or make an intuitive guess.

examples.text: Don't hunch over your computer if you want to avoid neck problems.
examples.translation: 若想避免頸部問題，請勿俯身盯著電腦。

examples.text:
1983, Jack Vance, Suldrun’s Garden, Spatterlight Press, 2012, Chapter 18,
[…] wheezing and grunting he hunched across the room.

etymology.text: Assibilated variant of hunk, of uncertain origin.
etymology.native: hunk 的一種送氣變體，起源不明。

senses.definition: The act of suspecting something or someone, especially of something wrong.
The condition of being suspected.
Uncertainty, doubt.
A trace, or slight indication.
The imagining of something without evidence.

examples.text: The news confirmed my suspicions.
examples.translation: 這一訊息證實了我的懷疑。

examples.text: My suspicions were unfounded.
examples.translation: 我的懷疑沒有根據。

examples.text: She was subject to groundless suspicions.
He was under suspicion of being a spy.
examples.translation: 人們懷疑他是間諜。

examples.text: I have a suspicion about his death.
examples.translation: 我覺得他的死有點可疑。

examples.text: Karl wanted to put himself above suspicions.

etymology.text: From Middle English suspecioun, borrowed from Latin suspīciō, suspīciōnem, from suspicere, from sub- (“up to”) with specere (“to look at”). Perhaps partly through the influence of Old French sospeçon (or rather the Anglo-Norman form suspecioun). Equivalent to suspect + -ion.

senses.definition: The indentation or depression made by the pressure of one object on or into another.
The overall effect of something, e.g., on a person.
A vague recalling of an event, a belief.
An impersonation, an imitation of the mannerisms of another person.
An outward appearance.
A performance metric representing an instance where a post or ad is shown once.
The first coat of colour, such as the priming in house-painting etc.
A print on paper from a wood block, metal plate, etc.
The vivid perception of something as it is experienced, in contrast to ideas or thoughts drawn from memory or the imagination.
set of copies of a publication printed at one time having the same content, layout, pagination, etc.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: China gives me many different impressions.
examples.translation: 中國給我許多不同的印象。

examples.text: What is your impression of America?
examples.translation: 你對美國的感覺是怎樣的？

examples.text: What's your impression of China?
examples.translation: 你對中國有什麼印象？

examples.text: First impressions matter.
examples.translation: 第一印象很重要。

examples.text: That left an impression.
examples.translation: 那留下了印象。

examples.text: What's your impression of that person like?
examples.translation: 你對他的印象怎麼樣？

etymology.text: From Old French impression, from Latin impressio. Equivalent to impress + -ion.

senses.definition: A light blow or jolting collision.
A swelling on the skin caused by illness or injury.
A small increase in an amount.
A small increase in excitement or interest.
A temporary, usually small, increase in a quantity, such as is shown in a graph.
The point, in a race in which boats are spaced apart at the start, at which a boat begins to overtake the boat ahead.
The act of using one's forearm to strike the ball in a volleyball match.
In skipping, a single jump over two consecutive turns of the rope.
The sound of such a collision.
Any light sound.
A fist bump.
A car accident, usually a small one.
senses.native: 汽車事故，通常是小規模的

senses.definition: A collision, especially a fall.
A dose of a drug, such as ketamine or cocaine, snorted; a small dose of a snorted drug.
senses.native: 藥物劑量，如可卡因或氯胺酮；鼻吸小劑量藥物

senses.definition: A conflict.
A protuberance on a flat surface or a straight line.
senses.native: 平坦表面或直線上凸起的突起物

senses.definition: A bouffant hairstyle; the puffy upper part of such a hairstyle.
senses.native: 蓬鬆的髮型（或其上部分）

senses.definition: The swollen abdomen of a pregnant woman.
A ripoff or bad deal; an unjustly high price.
A minor problem or difficulty.

examples.text: Tom has a large bump on the back of his head.
examples.translation: 湯姆後腦勺有一個大包。

examples.text: His car had a tiny bump with a moving bus.
examples.translation: 我的車子與一輛行駛中的巴士發生了輕微碰撞。

examples.text: She looks great with that bump Kelly gave her at the salon.
examples.translation: 凱莉在髮廊給她造成的那個凸起讓她看起來很帥氣。

examples.text: The addition of the fight scenes gave the story a little bump near the end, but overall, it bored me.
examples.translation: 加入戰鬥場景讓故事在結尾前增添了一些趣味，但整體來說讓我感到無聊。

examples.text: The ship encountered a severe bump in the Atlantic waves, resulting in significant structural damage and leaks.
examples.translation: 船隻遭遇大西洋波浪的嚴重撞擊，導致結構受損並發生洩漏。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: She wasn't hurt, but she got goose bumps when her car nearly crashed.
examples.translation: 她沒有受傷，但當車子差點撞車時，身上起了雞皮疙瘩。

etymology.text: From Early Modern English bump (“a shock, blow from a collision”), probably of North Germanic origin; compare Danish bump (“a thump”), Danish bumpe (“to thump”), Old Danish bumpe (“to strike with a clenched fist”), all probably of imitative origin.
etymology.native: 源於早期現代英語 bump（「衝擊、碰撞的打擊」），可能源自北日耳曼語系；比較丹麥語 bump（「重擊」）、bumpe（「重擊」）及古丹麥語 bumpe（「用握緊的拳頭擊打」），皆可能為擬聲詞。

senses.definition: The organisation, identification and interpretation of sensory information.
Conscious understanding of something.
Vision (ability)
Acuity

examples.text: Do you believe in extrasensory perception?
What was Adriano's perception about Islam?
Maybe it's a question of perception.
Our perception of beauty has changed over time.
The context influences the perception of truth.
Perception is reality.
examples.translation: 感知即現實。

etymology.text: From Middle English percepcioun, from Middle French percepcion, from Latin perceptiō (“a receiving or collecting, perception, comprehension”), from perceptus (“perceived, observed”), perfect passive participle of percipiō (“to perceive, observe”); see perceive.

senses.definition: A natural or inherent impulse or behaviour.
An intuitive reaction not based on rational conscious thought.

examples.text: Animals have instincts, we have taxes.
Tom and Mary followed their instincts.
You should've followed your instincts.
Animals act on instinct.
examples.translation: 動物依靠牠們的本能行動。

examples.text: I wish you'd trust your instincts more often.
In art, as in love, instinct is good enough.

etymology.text: From Latin īnstīnctus, past participle of īnstinguō (“to incite, to instigate”), from in (“in, on”) + stinguō (“to prick”).

senses.definition: The part of an object which is (designed to be) held in the hand when used or moved.
A reference to an object or structure that can be stored in a variable.
The smooth, irreducible subcurve of a comb which connects to each of the other components in exactly one point.
The amount wagered in the various pari-mutuel pools for a particular event or events.
An instrument for effecting a purpose (either literally or figuratively); a tool, or an opportunity or pretext.
The gross amount of wagering within a given period of time or for a given event at one of more establishments.
The tactile qualities of a fabric, e.g., softness, firmness, elasticity, fineness, resilience, and other qualities perceived by touch.
A name or nickname, especially as an identifier over the radio or Internet.
A title attached to one's name, such as Doctor or Colonel.
A traditional dimpled glass with a handle, for serving a pint of beer.
A 10 fluid ounce (285 mL) glass of beer.
A half-gallon (1.75-liter) bottle of alcohol.
A point, an extremity of land.
A topological space homeomorphic to a ball but viewed as a product of two lower-dimensional balls.
senses.native: 與球同胚、但可看作兩個低維球體乘積的拓撲空間（把手）

senses.definition: A person's nose.

examples.text: Small pots have long handles.
examples.translation: 小鍋柄長。

examples.text: We handle all type of books, both new and old.
examples.translation: 我們處理各種書籍，包括新的和舊的。

examples.text: The handle came away from the door when I grasped it.
examples.translation: 我握住門把，它就從門上掉了下來。

examples.text: It takes a skilled craftsman to carve a handle that ornate.
examples.translation: 要雕出如此精緻的把手，需有精湛技藝的工匠。

examples.text: The wardrobe is made from dark wood and has ornate gold handles.
examples.translation: 這組櫥櫃採用深色木材製成，配有精緻的金色把手。

examples.text: Two men are trying to get a handle on what's wrong with the car.
examples.translation: 兩個男人在檢查汽車出了什麼故障。

etymology.text: From Middle English handel, handle, from Old English handle (“handle”), from Proto-West Germanic *handulā (“handle”). See verb below. Cognate with German Hantel (“dumbbell, barbell”), Danish handel (“handle”). Related to hand.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 handel，意為「把手」，來自古英語 handle（「把手」），源自原始西日耳曼語 *handulā（「把手」）。見下文動詞。與德語 Hantel（「啞鈴、槓鈴」）、丹麥語 handel（「把手」）同源，與 hand（「手」）相關。

senses.definition: To touch; to feel or hold with the hand(s).
To manage, use, or wield with the hands.
To manage, control, or direct.
To treat, to deal with (in a specified way).
To deal with (a subject, argument, topic, or theme) in speaking, in writing, or in art.
senses.native: 在說話、寫作或藝術中處理（主題、論點等）

senses.definition: To receive and transfer; to have pass through one's hands; hence, to buy and sell.
To put up with; to endure (and continue to function).
To use the hands.
To illegally touch the ball with the hand or arm; to commit handball.
senses.native: 非法以手或手臂觸球（手球犯規）

senses.definition: To behave in a particular way when handled (managed, controlled, directed).
senses.native: 在被操作（管理、控制或指揮）時表現出某種行為

senses.definition: To accustom to the hand; to take care of with the hands.
senses.native: （罕用）使習慣於手的使用；以手照料

senses.definition: To be concerned with; to be an expert in.

examples.text: She's good at handling children.
examples.translation: 她對孩子很有一套。

examples.text: This machine is easy to handle.
examples.translation: 這台機器很容易操作。

examples.text: How do you want this handled?
examples.translation: 你想怎麼處理？

examples.text: This car is easy to handle.
examples.translation: 這輛車很容易操控。

examples.text: It is difficult for me to handle the case.
examples.translation: 我處理這事有困難。

examples.text: Tom should have handled the situation differently.
examples.translation: 湯姆應該用別的方式處理這狀況。

etymology.text: From Middle English handel, handle, from Old English handle (“handle”), from Proto-West Germanic *handulā (“handle”). See verb below. Cognate with German Hantel (“dumbbell, barbell”), Danish handel (“handle”). Related to hand.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 handel，意為「把手」，來自古英語 handle（「把手」），源自原始西日耳曼語 *handulā（「把手」）。見下文動詞。與德語 Hantel（「啞鈴、槓鈴」）、丹麥語 handel（「把手」）同源，與 hand（「手」）相關。

senses.definition: To direct or be in charge of.
To handle or control (a situation, job).
To handle with skill, wield (a tool, weapon etc.).
To succeed at an attempt in spite of difficulty.
To end up doing something that could or should have been avoided.
senses.native: 竟然（做了本可避免的事）

senses.definition: To achieve (something) without fuss, or without outside help.
To manage to say; to say while fighting back embarrassment, laughter, etc.
To train (a horse) in the manège; to exercise in graceful or artful action.
To treat with care; to husband.
To bring about; to contrive.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: She managed to drive a car.
examples.translation: 她成功地開車了。

examples.text: I can manage on my own.
examples.translation: 我能獨當一面。

examples.text: Did you manage it?
examples.translation: 你做到了嗎？

examples.text: Betty always managed to get what she wanted.
examples.translation: 貝蒂總是設法得到她想要的東西。

examples.text: We managed to get it back without her knowing.
examples.translation: 我們設法在她不知情的情況下把它拿回來了。

examples.text: That company is managed by my older brother.
examples.translation: 那家公司由我的哥哥經營。

etymology.text: From Early Modern English manage, menage, from Middle English *manage, *menage, from Old French manege (“the handling or training of a horse, horsemanship, riding, maneuvers, proceedings”), probably from Old Italian maneggiare (“to handle, manage, touch, treat”), from Vulgar Latin *manizāre (“handle”), from Latin manus (“hand”) + -izāre (verb-forming suffix). Doublet of manège.
etymology.native: 源自早期現代英語（manage、menage），來自中古英語（*manage），再源自古法語（manege）「馴馬、馬術、操練」，可能來自古義大利語（maneggiare）「處理、操作」，源自通俗拉丁語（*manizāre），由拉丁語（manus）「手」加動詞字尾（-izāre）組成。與（manège）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: Alternative spelling of plough.

examples.text: The farmers quickly plowed the fields.
Jaime's car plowed into a snowbank.
I am plowing my land.
examples.translation: 我在耕地。

examples.text: We started our spring plowing early this year.
Have you ever plowed a field with a horse?
The gigantic tornado plowed its way through the city.

senses.definition: To engage in communication and other shared activities (with someone).
To affect each other.

examples.text: They will interact.
examples.translation: 他們會互動。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

senses.definition: To move, arrange or operate something using the hands
To influence, manage, direct, control or tamper with something
To handle and move a body part, either as an examination or for a therapeutic purpose
To influence or control someone in order to achieve a specific purpose, especially one that is unknown to the one being manipulated and beneficial to the manipulator; to use
To use the hands, especially in scientific experiments.

They said that they felt manipulated.

A natural prolongation or projection from a part of any organism.
senses.native: 任何生物體的一部分的自然延伸或突出部分

senses.definition: A part that is joined to something larger.
senses.native: 與較大之物相連接的部分

examples.text: May you be touched by His Noodly Appendage.
examples.translation: 願您被祂那毛茸茸的附肢所觸動。

examples.translation: 安東尼擁有一個巨大的附肢。

examples.translation: 我呼出的水分凝結在鬍鬚上，直到那附肢感覺像鐵面具一樣。

examples.translation: 我的手臂是一條長長的附肢，幫助我拿取物品。

類似附肢的；具附肢狀的

etymology.text: From append + -age.
etymology.native: 由「附」與「部分」組合而成。

senses.definition: To manage, control, steer.
To aim (something) at (something else).
To point out to or show (somebody) the right course or way; to guide, as by pointing out the way; to refer.
To point out to with authority; to instruct as a superior; to order.
To address (a letter) to a particular person or place.

examples.text: Claudio typed "yo!" directed at Isabella.
examples.translation: 克勞迪歐打了「喲！」給伊莎貝拉。

examples.text: Tom ignored a superior's direct order.
examples.translation: 湯姆無視上級的直接命令。

examples.text: They directed their fire towards the men on the wall.
examples.translation: 他們把火力對準牆上的人。

examples.text: He directed his question to the room in general.
examples.translation: 他把問題拋給在場所有人。

examples.text: He directed me to the left-hand road.
examples.translation: 他指引我走左邊那條路。

examples.text: She directed them to leave immediately.
examples.translation: 她命令他們立刻離開。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin dīrēctus, perfect passive participle of dīrigō (“straighten, direct”), from dis- (“asunder, in pieces, apart, in two”) + regō (“make straight, rule”). Compare dress. Doublet of derecho.
etymology.native: 借自拉丁語（dīrēctus），是（dīrigō）「弄直、引導」的完成式被動分詞，由（dis-）「分開」加（regō）「弄直、統治」組成。比較（dress）。與（derecho）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: To make unauthorized or improper alterations, sometimes causing deliberate damage; to meddle (with something).
To try to influence someone, usually in an illegal or devious way; to try to deal (with someone).
To discuss future contracts with a player, against league rules.
To meddle (with something) in order to corrupt or pervert it.
To involve oneself (in a plot, scheme, etc.).
To attempt to practise or administer something (especially medicine) without sufficient knowledge or qualifications.

examples.text: The documents were tampered with.
Don't tamper with anything else.
His brakes were tampered with.
He crashed his car because someone tampered with the brakes.
examples.translation: 他撞車是因為有人在剎車上做了手腳。

examples.text: We can't tamper with the building's power.
This recording has been tampered with.

relations.native: 一把小提琴，一種四弦無品弦樂器，音高由低到高為 G-D-A-E，通常夾在下巴、肩膀、胸部或大腿上部演奏，使用弓拉奏（另見下方用法說明）

etymology.text: From tamp + -er.

senses.definition: Unsteady, random; prone to unexpected changes; not consistent.
Deviating from normal opinions or actions; eccentric; odd.

examples.text: He is erratic.
examples.translation: 他行為不穩定。

examples.text: Mary was troubled by Tom's erratic behavior.
examples.translation: 瑪麗對湯姆不穩定的行為感到困擾。

examples.text: Share prices have been erratic this last month.
examples.translation: 上個月股價波動不定。

examples.text: We had to lessen the impact of the erratic supplies.
examples.translation: 我們不得不減輕不穩定供應造成的影響。

examples.text: Fadil became so erratic that his wife decided to leave him.
examples.translation: 法迪爾變得如此不穩定，妻子決定離婚。

examples.text: Police are searching for an erratic driver believed to be involved in a fatal hit and run.
examples.translation: 警方正在搜尋一名被懷疑參與致命肇事逃逸的不穩定駕駛者。

etymology.text: From Middle English erratik, from Middle French erratique (from Old French erratique) and its etymon Classical Latin errāticus.
etymology.native: 來源為中世紀英文 erratik，源自中世紀法文 erratique（來自古法文 erratique），再溯至古典拉丁文 errāticus。

senses.definition: A rock moved from one location to another, usually by a glacier.
Anything that has erratic characteristics.

examples.text: That huge rock is an erratic.
examples.translation: 那塊巨石是冰河漂礫。

etymology.text: From Middle English erratik, from Middle French erratique (from Old French erratique) and its etymon Classical Latin errāticus.
etymology.native: 來源為中世紀英文 erratik，源自中世紀法文 erratique（來自古法文 erratique），再溯至古典拉丁文 errāticus。

senses.definition: Contrary to, forbidden, or not authorized by law, especially criminal law.
senses.native: 非法的、不合法的、不法的

senses.definition: Forbidden by established rules.
Totally fictitious, and often issued on behalf of a non-existent territory or country.
Being or doing something illegally.
Being an illegal immigrant; residing in a country illegally.

examples.text: Illegal logging is a transnational problem.
Cockfighting is illegal in many countries.
I've never done anything illegal in my life.
examples.translation: 我沒有做過非法的事。

examples.text: You know this is illegal, don't you?
examples.translation: 你知道這是違法的，對吧？

examples.text: It's illegal to park your car here.
examples.translation: 把車停在這裡是違法的。

examples.text: "Is it an illegal taxi?" I ask him.
examples.translation: 「是黑車嗎？」我問他。

etymology.text: Borrowed from French illégal, from Medieval Latin illegalis, from Latin legalis, by surface analysis, il- + legal. In senses relating to immigration, via clipping of illegal alien or illegal immigrant.

senses.definition: Not expected, anticipated or foreseen.
senses.native: 意外的、出乎意料的、始料不及的

examples.text: We've encountered some unexpected obstacles.
What happened here yesterday was unexpected.
Some unexpected difficulties have arisen.
Careful as he was, he made an unexpected mistake.
examples.translation: 雖然他很小心，但還是犯了個想不到的錯誤。

examples.text: That is rather unexpected.
examples.translation: 這真是很意外。

examples.text: Careful as he was he made unexpected mistakes.

etymology.text: From un- + expected.

senses.definition: An assembly or party of people wearing (usually elaborate or fanciful) masks and costumes, and amusing themselves with dancing, conversation, or other diversions.
The act of wearing a mask or dressing up in a costume for, or as if for, a masquerade ball.
An act of living under false pretenses; a concealment of something by a false or unreal show; a disguise, a pretence; also, a pretentious display.
An assembly of varied, often fanciful, things.
A cosplay event at which costumed attendees perform skits.
A dramatic performance by actors in masks; a mask or masque.
A Spanish entertainment or military exercise in which squadrons of horses charge at each other, the riders fighting with bucklers and canes.

examples.text: I've been invited to a masquerade party.
examples.translation: 我受邀參加了一場面具派對。

examples.text: What is the reason for this masquerade?
examples.translation: 這場面具派對的目的是什麼？

examples.text: I was invited to the masquerade at their home.
examples.translation: 我受邀到他們家參加面具派對。

etymology.text: The noun is borrowed from Middle French mascarade, masquarade, masquerade (modern French mascarade (“masquerade, masque; farce”)), and its etymon Italian mascherata (“masquerade”), from maschera (“mask”) + -ata. Maschera is derived from Medieval Latin masca (“mask”): see further there. The English word is cognate with Late Latin masquarata, Portuguese mascarada, Spanish mascarada.
etymology.native: 這個名詞來自中世紀法語 mascarade，masquarade，masquerade（現代法語 mascarade（「面具舞會」、「鬧劇」）），其源語為義大利語 mascherata（「面具舞會」），由 maschera（「面具」）+ -ata 組成。maschera 又源自中世紀拉丁語 masca（「面具」）。英文詞與晚期拉丁語 masquarata、葡萄牙語 mascarada、西班牙語 mascarada 同源。

senses.definition: To take part in a masquerade; to assemble in masks and costumes; (loosely) to wear a disguise.

To appear as something else.
To conceal (someone) with, or as if with, a mask; to disguise.

etymology.text: From Middle English false, fals, from Old English fals (“false; counterfeit; fraudulent; wrong; mistaken”), from Latin falsus (“counterfeit, false; falsehood”), perfect passive participle of fallō (“deceive”). Displaced native Middle English les, lese, from Old English lēas (“false”); See lease, lea

examples.translation: 雞湯是一種著名的解酒良方。

examples.text: Smiling is the best remedy for negative emotions.
examples.translation: 笑容是壞心情的最佳藥方。

examples.text: There is a remedy for everything except death.
examples.translation: 除了死亡之外，任何事情都有解法。

examples.text: I believe in non-violence as the only remedy.
examples.translation: 我認為非暴力是唯一的解法。

examples.translation: 絕望的疾病需要絕望的解法。

etymology.text: From Middle English remedie, from Old French *remedie, remede, from Latin remedium (“a remedy, cure”), from re- (“again”) + mederi (“to heal”). Doublet of remeid.
etymology.native: 「remedie」源自中世英文，來自古法文 *remedie、remede，源自拉丁文 remedium（意為「療法、治癒」），由 re-（意為「再次」）+ mederi（意為「治療」）組成。此詞與 remeid 為同源詞。

senses.definition: A substance that acts to increase physiological or nervous activity in the body.
Something that promotes activity, interest, or enthusiasm.

examples.text: Ecstasy is a stimulant type of drug.
examples.translation: 迷幻藥是一種興奮劑類型的藥物。

examples.text: Intoxication is what happens when the brain is affected by certain stimulants.
examples.translation: 中毒就是大腦受到某些興奮劑影響時發生的狀況。

examples.text: It turned out that some Russian athletes have used a new stimulant called "meldonium".
examples.translation: 結果發現，有些俄羅斯運動員使用過一種名為「梅爾尼翁」的新興奮劑。

examples.text: Coffee is a well-known stimulant.
examples.translation: 咖啡是一種眾所周知的興奮劑。

examples.text: Mary soon discovered that her husband grew more and more fond of his wine, and of even stronger stimulants.
examples.translation: 瑪麗很快發現，她的丈夫越來越喜歡他的葡萄酒，甚至更強的興奮劑。

examples.text: Caffeine is a stimulant because it makes you feel more awake.
examples.translation: 咖啡因是一種興奮劑，因為它能讓人感覺更清醒。

senses.definition: A substance administered to reduce the perception of pain or to induce numbness for surgery and may render the recipient unconscious.

examples.text: I'll give you the anesthetic.
examples.translation: 我會給你麻醉劑。

examples.text: I've given you a local anesthetic.
examples.translation: 我已經給你注射了局部麻醉劑。

examples.text: I'll give you a local anesthetic.
examples.translation: 我會給你局部麻醉劑。

examples.text: They administered the anesthetic a few minutes ago but Tom hasn't gone under yet.
examples.translation: 他們幾分鐘前給病人注射了麻醉劑，但病人尚未進入麻醉狀態。

examples.text: He lost consciousness under the influence of the anesthetic.
examples.translation: 他在麻醉劑的作用下，他失去了知覺。

examples.text: This new drug acts as a strong anesthetic for minor surgical procedures.
examples.translation: 這種新藥物可作為強效麻醉劑用於小型外科手術。

etymology.text: From an- + esthetic, or Latinized form of Ancient Greek ἀναίσθητος (anaísthētos, “insensible”) + -ic, from ἀν- (an-, “un-”) + αἰσθητικός (aisthētikós, “perceptible”).
etymology.native: 由前綴 an- 加上 esthetic，或源自古希臘語 ἀναίσθητος（無感）加上 -ic。

senses.definition: Any substance or drug that reduces pain, induces sleep and may alter mood or behaviour; in some contexts, especially in reference to the opiates-and-opioids class, especially in reference to illegal drugs, and often both.
Any type of numbing or soothing drug.
senses.native: 任何類型的麻醉或鎮靜藥物

examples.translation: 灰暗的天空令人昏昏欲睡。

examples.text: It's a narcotic.
examples.translation: 這是一種麻醉劑。

examples.text: The police seized a large shipment of illegal narcotics.
examples.translation: 警方扣押了大量非法麻醉劑。

examples.text: Illegal logging and trafficking in narcotics also play significant roles.
examples.translation: 非法伐木與麻醉劑走私也扮演重要角色。

examples.text: Prostitution, gambling, the use of narcotic substances, drunkenness, disorder, and all other illegal activities are STRICTLY FORBIDDEN.
examples.translation: 嚴禁賣淫嫖娼，賭博，吸毒，酗酒滋事等違法犯罪活動！

examples.text: This substance is a narcotic if inhaled.
examples.translation: 此物質若吸入則具麻醉性。

etymology.text: From Middle English narcotyk, from Middle French narcotique (from Old French narcotique, noun use of adjective) and directly from Medieval Latin narcōticum, from Ancient Greek ναρκωτῐκόν (narkōtĭkón), neuter of ναρκωτῐκός (narkōtĭkós), from Ancient Greek ναρκόω (narkóō, “to benumb”), from νάρκη (nárkē, “numbness, torpor”).
etymology.native: 此詞源於中古英語 narcotyk，來自中古法語 narcotique，直接源自中世紀拉丁語 narcōticum，再源自古希臘語 ναρκωτῐκόν。

senses.definition: Particularly with reference to waves, to reach a peak.
To reach the crest of (e.g. a hill or mountain).

senses.definition: To furnish with, or surmount as, a crest; to serve as a crest for.
senses.native: 為……加上冠飾；作為……的冠飾

senses.definition: To mark with lines or streaks like waving plumes.
senses.native: 以如飄動羽毛般的線條或條紋標示

examples.translation: 河川昨晚漲潮了。

examples.text: Hikers aim to reach the crest before sunset for the best photo.

etymology.text: From Middle English creste, from Old French creste (modern French crête) and perhaps continuing Old English cræsta (“crest, tuft, plume”); both ultimately from Vulgar Latin *cresta, from Latin crista. Doublet of crista.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 creste，來自古法文 creste（現代法文 crête），可能也源自古英語 cræsta（意為「冠羽、翎毛」）；最終源於通俗拉丁文 *cresta，來自拉丁文 crista。為 crista 的同源詞。

senses.definition: A royal, imperial or princely headdress; a diadem.
A wreath or band for the head, especially one given as reward of victory or a mark of honor.
Imperial or regal power, or those who wield it.
The topmost part of the head.
The raised centre of a road.
The highest part of an arch.
The upper range of facets in a rose diamond.
The dome of a furnace.
The upper part of certain fruits, as the pineapple or strawberry, that is removed before eating.
The top of a tree.
A kind of spire or lantern formed by converging flying buttresses.
Splendor; culmination; acme.

Any currency (originally) issued by the crown (regal power) and often bearing a crown (headdress); (translation) various currencies known by similar names in their native languages, such as the korona, koruna, krona, króna, krone.
Any reward of victory or mark of honor.
The sovereign (in a monarchy), as head of state.
The state, the government (headed by a monarch).
During childbirth, the appearance of the baby's head from the mother's vagina.
A round spot shaved clean on the top of the head, as a mark of the clerical state; the tonsure.
The highest part of a hill.
The top section of a hat, above the brim.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English coroune, from Anglo-Norman corone, from Latin corōna (“crown, wreath”), from Ancient Greek κορώνη (korṓnē). Doublet of corona, korona, koruna, krona, króna, and krone. Displaced Old English corenbēag (“crown”) and Middle English kinehelm, kynehelm, from Old English cynehelm (“crown”, literally “kinhelm” or “king's helm”).
etymology.native: 此詞源自中世英文 coroune，來源於盎格魯-諾曼語 corone，再源自拉丁文 corōna（意為「冠冕、花環」），而拉丁文則來自古希臘文 κορώνη（korṓnē）。與 corona、korona、koruna、krona、króna、krone 為同源詞。取代了古英語 corenbēag（意為「冠冕」）及中世英文 kinehelm、kynehelm，這些詞源自古英語 cynehelm（意為「王冠」，字面意為「君主之盔」）

senses.definition: A disposition or state of mind.
The position of the body or way of carrying oneself.
The orientation of a vehicle or other object relative to the horizon, direction of motion, other objects, etc.
A position similar to an arabesque, but with the raised leg bent at the knee.
Unpleasant behavior.

etymology.text: From French attitude, from Italian attitudine (“attitude, aptness”), from Medieval Latin aptitūdō (“aptitude”) and actitūdō (“acting, posture”), from Latin aptō and actitō. Doublet of aptitude.

senses.definition: The act of indoctrinating, or the condition of being indoctrinated.
Instruction in the rudiments and principles of any science or belief system; information.

examples.text: Providing lifesaving healthcare is not indoctrination.
examples.translation: 提供救命醫療並非灌輸思想。

examples.text: The indoctrination runs deep.
examples.translation: 這種灌輸思想已深植人心。

examples.translation: 被告訴可以做自己，恰恰與灌輸思想相反。

senses.definition: The act of initiating, or the process of being initiated or introduced.
The form or ceremony by which a person is introduced into any society; mode of entrance into an organized body; especially, the rite of admission into a secret society or order.
The first step of transcription or of transduction.

senses.definition: The state of being extremely friendly; intimacy.

Familiarity breeds contempt.

senses.definition: A belief or tenet, especially about philosophical or theological matters.
The body of teachings of an ideology, most often a religion, or of an ideological or religious leader, organization, group, or text.

etymology.native: 源於中古英語，來自古法語，再源自拉丁文 doctrina（教學、指導、學習、知識），來自 doctor（教師），來自 docere（教導）；參見 doctor。

Generation of an electric current by a varying magnetic field.
Derivation of general principles from specific instances.
A method of proof of a theorem by first proving it for a specific case (often an integer; usually 0 or 1) and showing that, if it is true for one case then it must be true for the next.

Given a group of cells that emits or displays a substance, the influence of this substance on the fate of a second group of cells.

senses.definition: The stock of a family; a race or generation of progenitors.
A branch of a family.
A branch, or group of branches, located outside a family or other cladistic group, but which is more closely related to that group than to any other taxon of the same rank.
An advanced or leading position; the lookout.
The above-ground stalk (technically axis) of a vascular plant, and certain anatomically similar, below-ground organs such as rhizomes, bulbs, tubers, and corms.

The vertical or nearly vertical forward extension of the keel, to which the forward ends of the planks or strakes are attached.

A part of an anatomic structure considered without its possible branches or ramifications.
A winder on a clock, watch, or similar mechanism.

A narrow part on certain man-made objects, such as a wine glass, a tobacco pipe, a spoon.
A person's leg.
The penis.
A vertical stroke of a letter.
A vertical stroke marking the length of a note in written music.

etymology.text: From an alteration (due to Dutch landschap) of earlier landskip, lantschip, from Middle English *landschippe, *landschapp, from Old English landsċipe, landsċeap (“region, district, tract of land”); in some senses from Dutch landschap (“region, district, province, landscape”), from Middle Dutch landscap, lantscap (“region”), from Old Dutch *landskepi, *landskapi (“region”). Cognate with Scots landskape, landskep, landskip (“landscape”), West Frisian lânskip (“landscape”), Low German landschop (“l
etymology.native: 此詞源自荷蘭語 landschap 的變體，而 landschap 又來自中世紀荷蘭語 landscap、lantscap，源自古荷蘭語 *landskepi、*landskapi，意為「地區、區域」；亦可追溯至古英語 landsċipe、landsċeap，意為「地區、區域」；在部分語義上亦與蘇格蘭語 landskape、landskep、landskip、弗里斯蘭語 lânskip、低德語 landschop 相關。

senses.definition: A view, vista or outlook.
The appearance of depth in objects, especially as perceived using binocular vision.
The technique of representing three-dimensional objects on a two-dimensional surface.
The choice of a single angle or point of view from which to sense, categorize, measure or codify experience.
The ability to consider things in such relative perspective.
A perspective glass.
A sound recording technique to adjust and integrate sound sources seemingly naturally.
An artwork that represents three-dimensional objects in this way.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Exploring other perspectives is encouraged.
We've accepted our different perspectives.
As time passes, your perspective widens.
I'd like to get a female perspective on this.
Mary helped me to put things in perspective.
Perspectives vary from one person to another.

etymology.text: From Middle English perspective, perspectif, attested since 1381, from Old French or Middle French, from the first word of the Medieval Latin perspectiva ars (“science of optics”), the feminine of Latin perspectivus (“of sight, optical”), from perspectus, the past participle of perspicere (“to inspect, look through”), itself from per- (“through”) + specere (“to look at”); the noun sense was influenced or mediated by Italian prospettiva, from prospetto (“prospect”).

senses.definition: A place from which something can be viewed.
The view from such a place.
An attitude or point of view.
Expectation for the future.
look; appearance

examples.text: The outlook is bleak.
Let go of your negative outlook on life.
examples.translation: 請拋開你那些負面的人生觀。

examples.text: They hoped to change their outlook and plans.
The weather outlook for tomorrow is not good.
It completely transformed my outlook on life.
I take pride in my positive outlook on life.

etymology.text: From out- + look.

senses.definition: An illustration or artwork done with the use of paint.
The action of applying paint to a surface.
The same activity as an art form.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: These paintings are different sizes.
examples.translation: 這些畫的尺寸不一樣。

examples.text: The boy enjoyed painting a picture.
examples.translation: 這個男孩喜歡繪畫。

examples.text: Ann finished painting the picture.
examples.translation: 安畫完了這幅畫。

examples.text: Jack is interested in painting.
examples.translation: 傑克對畫畫感興趣。

examples.text: These paintings are beautiful.
examples.translation: 這些畫很美。

examples.text: His hobby is painting pictures of flowers.
examples.translation: 他的愛好是畫有花的圖。

etymology.text: By surface analysis, paint + -ing.
etymology.native: 從表面分析，油漆 + -ing。

senses.definition: A kind; a stylistic category or sort, especially of literature or other artworks.

examples.text: She collected books from different genres.
Makina is Adriano's favorite music genre.
What's your favourite video game genre?
What genres of music are you into?
examples.translation: 你喜歡哪種型別的音樂？

examples.text: You actually listen to this genre of music?
Rock is the most self-obsessed music genre.

etymology.text: Unadapted borrowing from French genre, from Old French gen(d)re, borrowed from Latin genere. Doublet of gender and genus.

senses.definition: View, natural features, landscape.
Stage backdrops, property and other items on a stage that give the impression of the location of the scene.
senses.native: 舞台佈景、道具及其他營造場景地點印象的項目

examples.text: This mountain scenery is very beautiful.
examples.translation: 這座山的景色非常美。

examples.text: Japan is rich in beautiful scenery.
examples.translation: 日本有很多美麗的景色。

examples.text: We gazed at the beautiful scenery.
examples.translation: 我們望著這美麗的風景。

examples.text: They admired the lovely scenery.
examples.translation: 他們欣賞了美麗的風景。

examples.text: Tom needs a change of scenery.
examples.translation: 湯姆需要換換風景。

examples.text: The scenery was beautiful beyond description.
examples.translation: 這風景美得無法形容。

relations.native: 遠景或景色，特別是指透過開口、大道或通道所見的景色
生動的畫面或場景；一幅圖畫

etymology.text: Earlier scenary, from scene + -ary, but now remodelled as scene + -ery.
etymology.native: 早期的 scenary 源自 scene 加上 -ary，但現在已改為 scene 加上 -ery。

senses.definition: A distant view or prospect, especially one seen through some opening, avenue or passage.
A site offering such a view.
A vision; a view presented to the mind in prospect or in retrospect by the imagination.
senses.native: 想像中呈現於腦海中的景象；回顧或展望時所見之景

examples.text: I hated Windows Vista.
examples.translation: 我討厭 Windows Vista。

examples.text: Hasta la vista, baby.
examples.translation: 直到最後一瞥，寶貝。

examples.text: The street, lined with trees, provided a vista of the sea.
examples.translation: 那條街道兩旁種滿樹木，呈現出大海的遠景。

examples.text: The Buena Vista Social Club is no longer an active band of musicians.
examples.translation: Buena Vista 社交俱樂部已不再是一支活躍的音樂團體。

examples.text: Which one is better: Windows XP, Windows Vista, Windows 8 or Windows 10?
examples.translation: 哪一個更好：Windows XP、Windows Vista、Windows 8 還是 Windows 10？

examples.text: Once at the summit enjoy the vista, then on the descent reap the benefits of your hard work.
examples.translation: 登上頂峰後享受遠景，然後在下山時收穫辛勤工作的成果。

morphemes.native: 遠景或景色、特別是指透過開口

etymology.text: Borrowed from Italian vista (“view, sight”), from visto, past participle of vedere (“to see”), from Latin vidēre (“to see”). Compare vision, video, visa.
etymology.native: 借自義大利語 vista（「視界、景象」），源於 visto，見 vedere 之過去分詞，來自拉丁語 vidēre（「看」）。比較 vision、video、visa。

senses.definition: The visible horizontal line (in all directions) where the sky appears to meet the earth in the distance.
The range or limit of one's knowledge, experience or interest; a boundary or threshold.
The range or limit of any dimension in which one exists.
A specific layer of soil, or stratum
A cultural sub-period or level within a more encompassing time period.
Any level line or surface.
The point at which a computer chess algorithm stops searching for further moves.

examples.text: The sun appeared on the horizon.
examples.translation: 太陽從地平線上升起。

examples.text: The moon was above the horizon.
examples.translation: 月亮已從地平線升起了。

examples.text: The sun went below the horizon.
examples.translation: 太陽落到地平線下了。

examples.text: The sun rose over the horizon.
examples.translation: 太陽升出了地平線。

examples.text: The sun has just sunk below the horizon.
examples.translation: 太陽剛下山。

examples.text: We watched the sun sinking below the horizon.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English orisonte, orisoun, from Middle French horizon, horizonte, from Old French orisonte, orison, via Latin horizōn, from Ancient Greek ὁρίζων (horízōn), from ὅρος (hóros, “boundary”).

senses.definition: Synonym of quadrilateral (“a polygon with four sides”).
A courtyard which is quadrangular.
senses.native: （建築）四方庭院，四邊形的院子

senses.definition: The buildings forming the border of such a courtyard.

examples.translation: 四邊形與四角形有何不同？

examples.translation: 湯姆畫了一個不規則的四邊形。

examples.translation: 我的房間是四邊形，有四面牆。

examples.text: The garden is a quadrangle, four sides, no corners.
examples.translation: 這座花園是四邊形，四條邊，沒有角。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.translation: 這張桌子是四邊形——四條邊，像正方形。
