etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English quadrangle, borrowed from Old French quadrangle, from Late Latin quadrangulum.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 quadrangle，借自古法文 quadrangle，來源為拉丁文 quadrangulum。

senses.definition: A plane figure bounded by edges that are all straight lines.
The boundary of such a figure.
A figure comprising vertices and (not necessarily straight) edges, alternatingly.
senses.native: 由頂點與（未必是直線）的邊交替組成的圖形

senses.definition: Such a figure and its interior, taken as a whole.
senses.native: 此圖形及其內部，視為整體

examples.text: Each face of a polyhedron is a polygon.
examples.translation: 多面體的每個面都是多邊形。

examples.text: Calculate the area of this polygon.
examples.translation: 計算此多邊形的面積。

examples.text: A nonagon, sometimes called an enneagon, is a polygon with nine sides.
examples.translation: 九邊形，有時稱為正九邊形，是一個有九條邊的圖形。

examples.text: A seven-sided polygon is typically called a heptagon, but is occasionally referred to as a septagon.
examples.translation: 七邊形通常稱為七邊形，但偶爾也被稱為七角形。

examples.text: Mathematicians have finally discovered an aperiodic monotile, that is, a polygon that can only tile the plane in aperiodic tessellations.
examples.translation: 數學家終於發現了一種非週期性單磚，即一種只能以非週期性密鋪方式平鋪平面的多邊形。

examples.text: This shape has four straight sides and is called a polygon.
examples.translation: 此形狀有四條直線邊，稱為多邊形。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Ancient Greek πολύγωνον (polúgōnon), from πολύς (polús, “many”) + γωνία (gōnía, “angle”), equivalent to poly- + -gon.
etymology.native: 源自古希臘語 πολύγωνον，由表示「許多」的 πολύς 與表示「角度」的 γωνία 組成，相當於 poly- 加上 -gon。

senses.definition: An image, symbol, picture, portrait, or other representation, usually as an object of religious devotion.
A type of religious painting portraying a saint or scene from Scripture, often done on wooden panels.
A person or thing that is the best example of a certain profession or some doing.
A small picture that represents something.
A word, character, or sign whose form reflects and is determined by the referent; onomatopoeic words are necessarily all icons.
An image used to represent a user; an avatar or profile picture.

examples.text: Koalas are an Australian icon.
The icons are beautiful.
Gandhi is a peace icon.
Click twice on the browser's icon to open it.
To change the flag, click on the flag icon.
This bridge has become our national icon.

etymology.text: From Latin īcōn, from Ancient Greek εἰκών (eikṓn, “likeness, image, portrait”). Eastern Orthodox Church sense is attested from 1833. Computing sense first recorded in 1982.

senses.definition: A clear or translucent liquid coating composed of resin dissolved in a solvent, which dries by evaporation to form a hard, protective, and typically glossy finish.
Anything resembling such a coating; a glossy appearance.
senses.native: 類似此種塗層的東西；光澤的外觀

senses.definition: A deceptively showy appearance.

senses.definition: A passenger train, probably derived from the varnished passenger cars used at one time.
senses.native: 一列乘客列車，可能源自過去使用的塗漆乘客車廂

examples.text: We must give it a good coat of varnish.

examples.text: Which nail varnish goes with the yellow dress?
examples.translation: 哪種指甲油搭配黃色禮服？

examples.text: Mum doesn't let me wear nail varnish.
examples.translation: 媽媽不讓我戴指甲油。

examples.text: What colour nail varnish goes with this yellow dress?
examples.translation: 哪種顏色的指甲油配這件黃色禮服？

examples.text: Turpentine is widely used as a solvent in paints, varnishes and lacquers.
examples.translation: 松節油廣泛用作油漆、清漆和光油的溶劑。

examples.text: If Earth were the size of a desktop globe, its atmosphere would be the size of the varnish.
examples.translation: 如果地球的大小是桌面地球儀，其大氣層的大小就是那層清漆。

etymology.text: From Middle English vernisch, vernish, from Old French vernis, from Medieval Latin vernix, veronix, from Byzantine Greek Βερενίκη (Bereníkē, “Berenice”), a town in Cyrenaica, now called Benghazi.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 vernisch，來自舊法式 vernis，再源自中世紀拉丁語 vernix。

senses.definition: A substance that is applied as a liquid or paste, and dries into a solid coating that protects or adds colour to an object or surface to which it has been applied.
A set of containers or blocks of paint of different colors/colours, used for painting pictures.
senses.native: 一套顏料，多個盛裝顏料的容器或色塊

senses.definition: The free-throw lane, construed with the.
senses.native: （籃球）禁區，罰球線與底線之間的區域

senses.definition: Paintballs.
Synonym of face card (king, queen, or jack).
Graphics drawn using an input device, not scanned or generated.
senses.native: （電腦）繪圖，用輸入裝置繪製的圖像，非掃描或生成的

senses.definition: Makeup.
Tattoo work.
The appearance of an object on a radar screen.
senses.native: （雷達）回波，物體在雷達螢幕上的影像

senses.definition: A paint horse.
Any substance fixed with latex to harden it.
senses.native: （俗）乳膠硬化物，以乳膠固化的任何物質

examples.text: I made him paint the house.
examples.translation: 我讓他刷房子。

examples.translation: 你是何時創作這幅畫的?

examples.text: I've bought a new palette and a few paint brushes.
examples.translation: 我買了一個新的調色盤和幾支水彩筆。

examples.text: Paint our house. Use the orange paint.
examples.translation: 油漆我們的房子。使用橙色的油漆。

examples.translation: 我要粉刷我的房子。

etymology.text: From Middle English peynten, from Old French peintier, paincter, itself from paint, the past participle of paindre, from Latin pingō (“to paint”) (perfect passive participle pictus). Displaced native Old English tēafor (“paint”), *tīefran (“to paint”); and Old English mētan (“to paint”) and mǣlan (“to paint, mark with colour”).

senses.definition: A land area free of woodland, cities, and towns; an area of open country.
A wide, open space that is used to grow crops or to hold farm animals, usually enclosed by a fence, hedge or other barrier.
A region containing a particular mineral.
A place where a battle is fought; a battlefield.
The open country near or belonging to a town or city.
When coupled with a number (e.g. two-field) used to define types of crop rotation, denoting the number of different crop types (and possibly fallow) that are used.
An airfield, airport or air base; especially, one with unpaved runways.
An area reserved for playing a game or race with one’s physical force.
The outfield.
A place where competitive matches are carried out with figures, or playing area in a board game or a computer game.
A competitive situation, circumstance in which one faces conflicting moves of rivals.
senses.native: 競爭情境或局面，面對對手相衝突的行動

senses.definition: All of the competitors in any outdoor contest or trial, or all except the favourites in the betting.

A physical phenomenon (such as force, potential or fluid velocity) that pervades a region; a mathematical model of such a phenomenon that associates each point and time with a scalar, vector or tensor quantity.
The extent of a given perception.
A realm of practical, direct or natural operation, contrasted with an office, classroom, or laboratory.
A domain of study, knowledge or practice.
An unrestricted or favourable opportunity for action, operation, or achievement.
A non-zero commutative ring in which all non-zero elements are invertible; a simple commutative ring.
The background of the shield.
The team in a match that throws the ball and tries to catch it when it is hit by the other team (the bat).

examples.text: Linguistics is a very interesting field.
examples.translation: 語言學是門很有意思的學科。

examples.text: The field measures more than 300 acres.
examples.translation: 這片田地面積超過300公頃。

examples.text: Computers have invaded every field.
examples.translation: 電腦已侵入每一領域。

examples.text: The hunter chases the rabbit in the fields.
examples.translation: 獵人在田野追兔子

examples.text: Japan has caught up with America in some fields.
examples.translation: 日本在某些領域趕上了美國。

examples.text: Field hockey is not very popular in China.
examples.translation: 曲棍球在中國不是很流行。

etymology.text: From Middle English feld, feeld (“field”), from Old English feld (“field”), from Proto-West Germanic *felþu (“field”), from Proto-Germanic *felþuz (“field”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“field, plain”) or *pleth₂- (“flat”) (with schwebeablaut).
etymology.native: 「field」源自中世紀英文 feld，來源為古英語 feld，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *felþu，更上溯至古德語 *felþuz，最終源自印歐語系 *pleh₂- 或 *pleth₂-（意為「平原」或「平坦之地」）

senses.definition: To intercept or catch (a ball) and play it.
To be the team catching and throwing the ball, as opposed to hitting it.
senses.native: （棒球）擔任守備方（接球與傳球，而非擊球）

senses.definition: To place (a team, its players, etc.) in a game.
senses.native: （比賽中）派出（球隊或球員）上場

senses.definition: To answer; to address.
To execute research (in the field).
To deploy in the field.

examples.text: After a brief speech the mayor fielded questions from reporters.

etymology.text: From Middle English feld, feeld (“field”), from Old English feld (“field”), from Proto-West Germanic *felþu (“field”), from Proto-Germanic *felþuz (“field”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“field, plain”) or *pleth₂- (“flat”) (with schwebeablaut).
etymology.native: 「field」源自中世紀英文 feld，來源為古英語 feld，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *felþu，更上溯至古德語 *felþuz，最終源自印歐語系 *pleh₂- 或 *pleth₂-（意為「平原」或「平坦之地」）

senses.definition: A controlled behaviour; self-control.
An enforced compliance or control.
A systematic method of obtaining obedience.
A state of order based on submission to authority.
A set of rules regulating behaviour.
A punishment to train or maintain control.
A whip used for self-flagellation.
A flagellation as a means of obtaining sexual gratification.
A specific branch of knowledge, learning, or practice.
A category in which a certain art, sport or other activity belongs.

examples.text: Each discipline develops its own conventions.
Improving yourself requires discipline.
Take a belt and discipline your son right now.
The child was completely lacking in discipline.
He is too young to benefit from firm discipline.
Discipline is rather mild at this school.

etymology.text: From Middle English [Term?], from Anglo-Norman, from Old French descipline, from Latin disciplina (“instruction”), from discipulus (“pupil”), influenced by disco (“to learn”), from Proto-Indo-European *dek- (“(cause to) accept”).

senses.definition: A particular discipline or branch of knowledge that is natural, measurable or consisting of systematic principles rather than intuition or technical skill.
Specifically the natural sciences.
The fact of knowing something; knowledge or understanding of a truth.
The collective discipline of study or learning acquired through the scientific method; the sum of knowledge gained from such methods and discipline.
Knowledge derived from scientific disciplines, scientific method, or any systematic effort.
The scientific community.
Synonym of sweet science (“the sport of boxing”).
Knowledge gained through study or practice; mastery of a particular discipline or area.

examples.text: I'm studying computer science.
examples.translation: 我在學習電腦科學。

examples.text: I like both science and math.
examples.translation: 科學和數學我都喜歡。

examples.text: Science has changed our life.
examples.translation: 科學改變了我們的生活。

examples.text: Science doesn't have an answer to everything.
examples.translation: 科學並不能解答所有問題。

examples.text: Science begins when you ask why and how.
examples.translation: 為何如何？你疑問的當下就是科學的開端。

examples.text: He likes reading science fiction novels.
examples.translation: 他喜歡看科幻小說。

etymology.text: From Middle English science, scyence, borrowed from Old French science, escience, from Latin scientia (“knowledge”), from sciēns, the present participle stem of scire (“to know”).

senses.definition: Motivated by an inappropriate, excessive, or unjustified desire to impress others.
Marked by an unwarranted claim to importance or distinction.
Marked by pretense (not necessarily false pretense); intent upon success; ambitious.

examples.text: He's just a pretentious douchebag.
examples.translation: 他只是個自命不凡的混蛋。

examples.text: Tom was very pretentious.
examples.translation: 湯姆非常自命不凡。

examples.text: What a pretentious woman!
examples.translation: 這女人太自命不凡了！

examples.text: You're pretentious, you don't care about anyone.
examples.translation: 你自命不凡，根本不在乎別人。

examples.text: She began speaking in a pretentious tone.
examples.translation: 她開始用自命不凡的語氣說話。

examples.text: You pride yourself on being pretentious, don't you?
examples.translation: 你自以為什麼樣的自命不凡都很了不起，是嗎？

etymology.text: From French prétentieux, from prétention, from Latin praetēnsus (“false or hypocritical profession”), past participle of praetendō.
etymology.native: 來自法語 prétentieux，源自 prétention，源自拉丁語 praetēnsus（意為「虛偽或偽裝的自稱」），是 praetendō 的過去分詞。

senses.definition: Making a show of being morally better than others, especially hypocritically pious.
Holy, devout.

examples.text: I've had enough of this sanctimonious talk.
examples.translation: 我已經受夠這種偽善的談話了。

examples.text: Stop being so sanctimonious.
examples.translation: 別這麼偽善了。

examples.text: Some critics loved the film, while others did not, one calling it sanctimonious drivel.
examples.translation: 有些評論家喜歡這部電影，有些人則不，其中一人稱其為偽善的廢話。

examples.text: They pretend to be sanctimonious but, in fact, they are hypocrite and despicable.
examples.translation: 他們假裝聖潔，實際上卻是偽善且卑鄙的。

examples.text: He was the strongest candidate for the position.
examples.translation: 他是那個職位最有希望的候選人。

examples.text: I have a good opinion of the young candidate.
He is one of the candidates running for mayor.
examples.translation: 他是市長的候選人之一。

etymology.text: From Latin candidātus (“a person who is standing for public office”, noun), from candidus (“dazzling white, shining, clear”) + -ātus, -āta, -ātum (participial adjective-forming suffix), in reference to Roman candidates wearing bleached white togas as a symbol of purity at a public forum. By surface analysis, candid + -ate (noun-forming suffix).

senses.definition: To cast out; to banish.

examples.text: They said they felt like outcasts.
examples.translation: 他們說自己像被排斥在外的人。

examples.text: Tom felt like an outcast.
examples.translation: 湯姆覺得自己像被排斥在外的人。

examples.text: I felt like an outcast.
examples.translation: 我覺得自己像被排斥在外的人。

examples.text: Tom and Mary said they felt like outcasts.
examples.translation: 湯姆和瑪麗說他們覺得自己像被排斥在外的人。

examples.text: Boldi became an outcast and a laughing stock for everyone.
examples.translation: 博爾迪成了被所有人排斥且笑柄的人。

etymology.text: From Middle English outcasten, equivalent to out- + cast.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 outcasten，由 out- 與 cast 組成。

senses.definition: That has been cast out; banished, ostracized.

examples.text: I feel outcast.

etymology.text: From Middle English outcasten, equivalent to out- + cast.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 outcasten，由 out- 與 cast 組成。

senses.definition: A person, animal, plant, or other thing which is from outside the family, group, organization, or territory under consideration.
A citizen or national of another sovereign state.
Any life form of extraterrestrial or extradimensional origin.
One excluded from certain privileges; one alienated or estranged.
A mischievous or suspicious foreigner.

examples.text: Do you think there are aliens?
examples.translation: 你覺著有外星人存在嗎？

examples.text: I was abducted by aliens.
examples.translation: 我被外星人綁架了。

examples.text: Mary senses the aliens are watching her.
examples.translation: 瑪麗發現外星人正在看她。

examples.text: Let's pretend we're aliens.
examples.translation: 讓我們假裝是外星人。

examples.text: I swear, I saw an alien!
examples.translation: 我發誓我看到了外星人。

examples.text: Aliens controlled Earth's progress in secret.

etymology.text: From Middle English alien, a borrowing from Old French alien, aliene, from Latin aliēnus (“belonging to someone else”, later “exotic, foreign”), from Latin alius (“other”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂élyos. Related to English else.

senses.definition: A person whom one does not know; a person who is neither a friend nor an acquaintance.
An outsider or foreigner.
One not admitted to communion or fellowship.
A newcomer.
One not privy or party to an act, contract, or title; a mere intruder or intermeddler; one who interferes without right.
A moth, Lacanobia blenna
Used ironically to refer to a person who the speaker knows.
One not belonging to the family or household; a guest; a visitor.
A superstitious premonition of the coming of a visitor by a bit of stalk in a cup of tea, the guttering of a candle, etc.

examples.text: A stranger is just a friend you haven't met yet.
examples.translation: 所謂陌生人，只是還未相見的友人而已。

examples.text: "How long does it take to get to Vienna on foot?" "Sorry, I'm a stranger here."
examples.translation: 「到維也納步行要多久？」　「對不起，我是外地人。」

examples.text: That gentleman is a stranger to me.
Children are taught not to talk to strangers.

etymology.text: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

senses.definition: The middle layer of the wall of a blood vessel or lymph vessel which is composed of connective and muscular tissue.
One of the major veins of the insect wing, between the radius and the cubitus.
An ant specialized as a forager in a leaf-cutter ant colony.
Synonym of cuarto: a half-fanega, a traditional Spanish unit of dry measure equivalent to about 27.8 L
The means and institutions for publishing and broadcasting information.
The totality of content items (television shows, films, books, photographs, etc.) which are broadcast or published.
The journalists and other professionals who comprise the mass communication industry.
Files and data comprising material viewable by humans, but usually not plain text; audiovisual material.
A voiced stop consonant.

examples.text: Yuri was monitoring Martha's social media.
Social media have enabled the protests.
In Hungary, Orban controls the media.
I had otitis media last year.
examples.translation: 我去年得了中耳炎。

examples.text: The Arabs are being dehumanized by some media.
I also have my own media company in Kabylie.

etymology.text: Learned borrowing from Latin media, the feminine nominative of medius (“middle”, adjective), from Proto-Italic *meðjos, from Proto-Indo-European *médʰyos (“between”). In the sense of a unit of dry measure, via Spanish media. Doublet of medium, medio, and mediate.

senses.definition: See other (determiner) below.
Second.
Alien.
Different.
Left, as opposed to right.

examples.text: Where is your other younger brother?
examples.translation: 你另一個弟弟在哪裡？

examples.text: Did Tom give any other suggestions?
examples.translation: 湯姆提出其他建議了嗎？

examples.text: Tom was always different from other children.
examples.translation: 湯姆總是跟別的小孩不一樣。

examples.text: He is the boy of whom we spoke the other day.
examples.translation: 他是前幾天我們談到的那個男孩。

examples.text: He is as smart as any other boy in the class.
examples.translation: 他和班上其他男生一樣聰明。

examples.text: I hope we'll see each other again sometime.
examples.translation: 我希望我們有時間還可以見面。

etymology.text: From Middle English other, from Old English ōþer (“other, second”), from Proto-West Germanic *ą̄þar, *anþar, from Proto-Germanic *anþeraz (“other, second”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énteros (“other”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（other），來自古英語（ōþer）「其他、第二」，經原始日耳曼語（*anþeraz），上溯至原始印歐語（*h₂énteros）「其他」。

senses.definition: A sudden departure of a large number of people.

examples.text: There was a mass exodus of Malian Tuaregs to Algeria.
examples.translation: 馬利圖阿雷格人曾大規模遷往阿爾及利亞。

examples.text: As Michael Jackson said in the Book of Exodus, "Anachronisms are fun."
examples.translation: 正如麥可·傑克森在《出埃及記》中所說：「時代錯誤的事物很有趣。」

examples.text: Maybe unbanning Nazis isn't the right way to replace the massive exodus from your site.
examples.translation: 也許解除納粹禁令並非取代您網站上大批人員離去的正確方法。

examples.text: The rural exodus depopulated entire villages in this region of Germany.
examples.translation: 農村遷出導致德國該地區許多村莊人口枯竭。

examples.text: In the 1990s, the civil war in Algeria triggered a severe rural exodus.
examples.translation: 一九九零年代，阿爾及利亞內戰引發了嚴重的農村遷出。

examples.text: I understand that this sounds far-fetched, but in order to understand Exodus you have to see the bigger picture.
examples.translation: 我理解這聽起來不太可能，但要了解《出埃及記》，必須看清大局。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin Exodus, borrowed from Ancient Greek Ἔξοδος (Éxodos), from ἔξοδος (éxodos, “departure”), from ἐξ- (ex-, “out”) + ὁδός (hodós, “path, road”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 Exodus，該詞又來自古希臘語 Ἔξοδος，由前綴 ἐξ-（「出」）加上ὁδός（「道路」）組成。

senses.definition: Green foliage or verdure.
Foliage used as decoration.
Marijuana.

examples.text: The spring greenery has appeared.
examples.translation: 春天的綠意已現

examples.text: You like greenery.
examples.translation: 你喜歡綠意

examples.text: He loves greenery.
examples.translation: 他愛綠意

examples.text: What is the size of this district's greenery area?
examples.translation: 這片小區的綠地面積有多少？

examples.text: There's a lot of greenery in Tokyo Midtown!
examples.translation: 東京中心區綠意盎然！

examples.text: There is less crime in apartment buildings surrounded by trees and greenery.
examples.translation: 環繞樹木與綠意的公寓大樓犯罪率較低

etymology.text: From green + -ery.
etymology.native: 由 green + -ery 組成。

senses.definition: A person who is severely impaired or deficient in some non-physical way.
A shortened wooden stud or brace used to construct the portion of a wall above a door or above and below a window.
A rocky shallow in a stream.
Scrapple.
A person who has severely impaired physical abilities because of deformation, injury, or amputation of parts of the body.

examples.text: He returned from war a cripple.
examples.translation: 他從戰爭中歸來，受傷

etymology.text: From Middle English cripel, crepel, crüpel, from Old English crypel (“crippled; a cripple”), from Proto-Germanic *krupilaz (“tending to crawl; a cripple”), from Proto-Indo-European *grewb- (“to bend, crouch, crawl”), from Proto-Indo-European *ger- (“to bend, twist”), equivalent to creep + -le. Cognate with Dutch kreupel, Low German Kröpel, German Krüppel, Old Norse kryppill.
etymology.native: 「cripel」源自中古英語，來源為古英語「crypel」，再溯自原始日耳曼語「*krupilaz」，意為「行動困難者」，源自原始印歐語「*grewb-」，意為「彎曲、爬行」，而「*ger-」則意為「彎曲、扭曲」，與「creep」相關。與荷蘭語「kreupel」、下德語「Kröpel」、德語「Krüppel」、古諾斯語「kryppill」同源。

senses.definition: To scatter in different directions.
To break up and disappear; to dissipate.
To disseminate.
To separate rays of light, etc., according to wavelength; to refract.
senses.native: 將光線等按波長分開；折射

senses.definition: To distribute throughout.

examples.text: How do trees disperse their seeds?
examples.translation: 樹木如何傳播種子？

examples.text: We dispersed from each other.
examples.translation: 我們彼此分散開來。

examples.text: Fungi disperse spores.
examples.translation: 真菌散佈孢子。

examples.text: The bank robbers dispersed in all directions.
examples.translation: 銀行強盜四處逃竄。

examples.text: The police used tear gas to disperse the crowd.
examples.translation: 警方使用催淚瓦斯驅散人群。

examples.text: The first men lived dispersed, and cities did not exist yet.
examples.translation: 最初的人們分散而居，城市尚未存在。

etymology.text: From Middle French disperser, from Latin dispersus, past participle of dispergō (“to scatter abroad, disperse”), from dis- (“apart”) + spargō (“to scatter”); see sparse.
etymology.native: 源自中法語的 disperser，來自拉丁語 dispergō（「四處散佈」），由 dis-（「分開」）與 spargō（「撒灑」）組成。

senses.definition: To destroy completely; to reduce to nothing radically; to put an end to.
To pull up by the roots.
eradicated

examples.text: Algeria has eradicated many diseases.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞已根除許多疾病。

examples.text: They tried to eradicate my culture.
examples.translation: 他們試圖根除我的文化。

examples.text: The savage in man is never quite eradicated.
examples.translation: 人性中的野性從未完全被根除。

examples.text: The US attempted to eradicate Native Americans.
examples.translation: 美國曾試圖根除美洲原住民。

examples.text: Algeria should eradicate illegal dumps.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞應根除非法垃圾場。

examples.text: It is urgent to eradicate poverty in Africa.
examples.translation: 必須緊急根除非洲的貧困。

etymology.text: From Middle English eradicaten (“to eradicate”), from eradicat(e) (“eradicated”, past participle of eradicaten) + -en (verb-forming suffix), borrowed from Latin ērādīcātus, the perfect passive participle of ērādīcō (“to uproot, root out; to anihilate, eradicate”), from ē- (“out”) + rādīx (“root”) + -ō (verb-forming suffix). See also radish.
etymology.native: 此詞源於中世紀英語，由拉丁語組成，意為拔除根部。

senses.definition: To deprive of inhabitants.
To devastate or lay waste somewhere.
To abandon or forsake something.
To make someone sad, forlorn and hopeless.
senses.native: 使某人悲傷、絕望且無希望

examples.text: Mary's explanations enchanted me and desolated me all at once.

relations.native: 摧毀大片區域內眾多或所有事物

etymology.text: From Middle English desolat(e). See Etymology 2 and -ate (adjective-forming suffix) for more.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 desolat(e)。請參閱詞源 2 和 -ate（形容詞構成後綴）以獲取更多資訊。

senses.definition: To make weaker or less strong.
To become weaker or less strong.

examples.text: Yanni's body was weakened.
Damiano started to weaken.
Are you weakening?
The storm has not weakened for several hours.
examples.translation: 風暴幾個小時沒有減弱了。

examples.text: Time, which strengthens friendship, weakens love.
examples.translation: 時間能夠加深友誼，但是卻會沖淡愛情。

examples.text: The storm has weakened.
examples.translation: 風暴減弱了。

etymology.text: From weak + -en.

senses.definition: To get in the way of; to hinder.

examples.text: He was impeded in his work.
examples.translation: 他在工作中受到阻礙。

examples.text: A stalled car impedes traffic in the left lane.
examples.translation: 一輛故障的汽車阻擋了左側車道的交通。

examples.text: I hope it doesn't impede my online classes.
examples.translation: 我希望它不會干擾我的線上課程。

examples.text: Obstructions near doors can impede people in an emergency.
examples.translation: 門附近的障礙物可能會在緊急情況下阻礙人們通行。

examples.text: He has tried to impede an official investigation.
examples.translation: 他試圖阻擋官方調查。

examples.text: Storms at sea impeded our progress.
examples.translation: 海上的風暴阻礙了我們的進度。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin impediō (“to shackle”), from pēs (“foot”) (compare pedestrian). First attested use as a verb was in William Shakespeare's Macbeth, see quotations.
etymology.native: 此詞源自拉丁語 impediō，由 pēs（腳）組成。該動詞最早於莎士比亞的《麥克白》中出現。

senses.definition: To cause to fail; to frustrate, to prevent.
To place (something) across (another thing); to position crosswise.
To hinder or obstruct by placing (something) in the way of; to block, to impede, to oppose.
To move (something) across or counter to; to cross.

examples.text: He's always thwarting my nefarious plans.
Tom tried to thwart Mary's plans.
Tom thwarted everything he could.
You've thwarted my plans for the last time!
Once again, my plans have been thwarted.
A moat was dug around the castle to thwart attackers.

etymology.text: From Middle English thwerte, from the adjective thwert (“obstinate, perverse”), from Old Norse þvert, neuter of þverr (“transverse”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語，來自形容詞「頑固的、乖張的」，來自古諾斯語「橫向的」的中性形式。

senses.definition: To hold in or hold back; to keep in check; restrain.
To recuse.

examples.text: I should act, yet fear inhibits me from doing so.
Fear can inhibit success.
It won't do to be so inhibited when you go up on stage.
He noticed that this drug seemed to inhibit bacterial growth.
The passive-aggressive behavior of the English teacher inhibits effective communication.
Some claim that taxing the rich inhibits job creation.

etymology.text: From Latin inhibitus, perfect passive participle of inhibeō (“to hold in, check, restrain”), from in (“in, at, on”), + habeō (“to have, hold, keep”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語「抑制」的完成被動分詞，由「在內」加「持有、保持」組成。

senses.definition: Offspring resulting from cross-breeding different entities, e.g. two different species or two purebred parent strains.
Something of mixed origin or composition; often, a tool or technology that combines the benefits of formerly separate tools or technologies.
A hybrid vehicle, especially a car; a vehicle that runs on both fuel (gasoline or diesel) and electricity (battery or energy from the sun).
A computer that is part analog computer and part digital computer.
A bicycle that is a compromise between a road bike and a mountain bike.
An electronic circuit constructed of individual devices bonded to a substrate or PCB.
A golf club that combines the characteristics of an iron and a wood.
A word that is internally macaronic, its elements being derived from different languages.

examples.text: What should we call this hybrid?
"Automobile" is a hybrid word.
My neighbor's car is a hybrid.
"Is it an indica or a sativa?" "It's a hybrid."
The car Tom bought yesterday is a hybrid.
The orange is a hybrid between a pomelo and a mandarin.

etymology.text: From Latin hybrida, a variant of hibrida (“a mongrel; specifically, an offspring of a tame sow and a wild boar”). Attested since 1601, but rare before c. 1850.

senses.definition: A male child.
A male servant, slave, assistant, or employee, particularly
A young man.
A son of any age.
A male human younger than the speaker.
A male human of any age, as opposed to a "girl" (female human of any age).
A younger such worker.
A male friend.
A male submissive.
A male non-human animal, especially, in affectionate address, a male pet, especially a dog.
Heroin.
A male (tree, gene, etc).
Any tangible object close to one's person; often used in emphatic forms such as bad boy.
A male of low station, (especially as pejorative) a worthless male, a wretch; a mean and dishonest male, a knave.
A male camp follower.
A former low rank of various armed services; a holder of this rank.
A non-white male servant regardless of age, particularly as a form of address.
Any non-white male, regardless of age.

examples.text: The boy denied stealing the bicycle.
examples.translation: 那個男孩否認偷了腳踏車。

examples.text: That class has 15 boys and 28 girls.
examples.translation: 那個班有15名男孩和28名女孩子。

examples.text: The boy enjoyed painting a picture.
examples.translation: 這個男孩喜歡繪畫。

examples.text: They rescued the boy from drowning.
examples.translation: 他們救了這個男孩，使他免於淹死。

examples.text: That boy put on his sneakers and ran outside.
examples.translation: 那個男孩穿上了他的運動鞋，跑向外面。

examples.text: The boy reached out for another piece of cake.
examples.translation: 男孩伸手又拿了一塊蛋糕。

etymology.text: From Middle English boy /boye (“servant, commoner, knave, boy”), from Old English *bōia (“boy”), from Proto-West Germanic *bōjō, from Proto-Germanic *bōjô (“younger brother, young male relation”), from Proto-Germanic *bō- (“brother, close male relation”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰā-, *bʰāt- (“father, elder brother, brother”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語「僕人、平民、小子、男孩」，來自古英語，上溯至原始日耳曼語「弟弟、年輕男性親屬」，再追溯至原始印歐語「父親、兄長」的字根。

senses.definition: To speak (words) with a spasmodic repetition of vocal sounds.
To expel a gas with difficulty.

examples.text: Why are you stuttering?
examples.translation: 你為什麼在結巴。

examples.text: Tom is stuttering.
examples.translation: Tom在結巴。

examples.text: I am stuttering.
examples.translation: 我在結巴。

examples.text: How is it you speak with such a stutter?
examples.translation: 你怎麼說這樣的口吃？

examples.text: When she began to stutter, her classmates couldn't help laughing.
examples.translation: 她一開始結巴，她的同學們就忍不住笑了。

examples.text: Talk slowly and you won't stutter that much.
examples.translation: 慢慢說，就不會那麼結巴了。

etymology.text: From Middle English stutten, stoten (“stutter”); cognate with Dutch stotteren (“stutter”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 stutten、stoten（意為「結巴」）；與荷蘭語 stotteren 同源。

senses.definition: A speech disorder characterized by stuttering.
One who stutters.

examples.text: I have a stutter.

etymology.text: From Middle English stutten, stoten (“stutter”); cognate with Dutch stotteren (“stutter”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 stutten、stoten（意為「結巴」）；與荷蘭語 stotteren 同源。

senses.definition: To waver or be unsteady; to weaken or trail off.
senses.native: 搖擺或站不穩；變弱或漸行漸遠

senses.definition: To stammer; to utter with hesitation, or in a weak and trembling manner.
senses.native: 口吃；以猶豫、微弱且顫抖的方式說話

senses.definition: To fail in distinctness or regularity of exercise; said of the mind or of thought.
senses.native: 失去清晰度或規律性；用於形容心智或思想

senses.definition: To stumble.
To lose faith or vigor; to doubt or abandon (a cause).
senses.native: 失去信心或活力；懷疑或放棄（某種信念）

senses.definition: To hesitate in purpose or action.
senses.native: 在目的或行動上猶豫不決

senses.definition: To cleanse or sift, as barley.

examples.text: The stars never falter.
examples.translation: 星星從未搖擺不定。

examples.text: You must not falter.
examples.translation: 你絕不能搖擺不定。

examples.text: He faltered at the last second, costing them the game.
examples.translation: 他在最後時刻猶豫了一下，導致他們輸掉了比賽。

examples.text: We can't allow ourselves to falter.
examples.translation: 我們不允許自己搖擺不定。

examples.text: Her voice always falters when she mentions her late father.
examples.translation: 她一提到已故的父親，聲音就會顫抖。

examples.text: We never saw him hesitate or falter.
examples.translation: 我們從沒見過他猶豫或搖擺不定。

etymology.text: From Middle English falteren (“to stagger; be unsteady, tremble, quiver; to stammer; be entangled, get caught”), further origin unknown. Probably from a North Germanic source such as Old Norse faltrask (“to hesitate, be puzzled, be encumbered”). May also be a frequentative of fold, although the change from d to t is unusual.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 falteren（「踉蹌；站不穩、顫抖、發抖；口吃；糾結」），起源不明。可能來自北日耳曼語源，如古諾斯語 faltrask（「猶豫、困惑、受困」）。也可能源自 fold 的頻繁化形式，但從 d 變為 t 的情況並不常見。

senses.definition: A short, high-pitched sound, as of two objects rubbing together, or the sounds made by mice and other small animals.
senses.native: 短促的高音，如兩物摩擦或鼠類等小動物發出的聲音

senses.definition: A card game similar to group solitaire.
senses.native: 類似群組獨贏的紙牌遊戲

senses.definition: A narrow squeak.

examples.text: Don't talk to your mom like that, pip squeak!
examples.translation: 別對你媽媽那樣說話，Pip Squeak！

examples.text: The door to the kitchen squeaks too loudly.
examples.translation: 廚房那扇門吱嘎聲太響了。

examples.text: The squeak of shoes on powdery snow.
examples.translation: 鞋子在粉雪上發出吱嘎聲。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English rocke, rokke (“rock formation”), from Old English *rocc (“rock”), as in Old English stānrocc (“high stone rock, peak, obelisk”), and also later from Anglo-Norman roque, (compare Modern French roc, roche, rocher), from Medieval Latin rocca (attested 767), of uncertain origin, sometimes said to be of Celtic (in particular, perhaps Gaulish) origin (compare Breton roc'h). Related also to Middle Low German rocke (“rock ledge”). One suggestion is that it derives from Vulg
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 rocke, rokke（岩層），來自古英語 *rocc（岩石），如古英語 stānrocc（高聳石岩、峰頂、方尖碑），亦源自盎格魯-諾曼語 roque（比較現代法語 roc, roche, rocher），來自中世紀拉丁語 rocca（767年有記載），起源不明，有說源自凱爾特語（特別是高盧語）（比較布列塔尼語 roc'h）。亦與中古低德語 rocke（岩縫）相關。有一說認為源自 Vulg

etymology.text: From Middle English tilte, from Old English *tyltan, *tieltan (“to be unsteady”), related to the adjective tealt (“unsteady”), from Proto-West Germanic *talt, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *del-, *dul- (“to shake, hesitate”), see also Dutch touteren (“to tremble”), North Frisian talt, tolt (“unstable, shaky”). etymology.text: From Middle English understanden, from Old English understandan (“to understand”), from Proto-West Germanic *understandan (“to stand between, understand”), from Proto-Germanic *understandaną (“to stand between, understand”), equivalent to Old English under- (“between, inter-”) + standan (“to stand”) (Modern English under- + stand). Cognate with Old Frisian understonda (“to understand, experience, learn”), Old High German understantan (“to understand”), Middle Danish understande (“to understand”)
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（understanden），來自古英語（understandan）「理解」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*understandaną）「站在中間、理解」，相當於古英語（under-）「在……之間」加（standan）「站」，即現代英語（under）- 加（stand）。與古弗里斯語（understonda）、古高地德語（understantan）同源。

examples.text: Igor placed sleeping pills on the nightstand.

etymology.text: From night (“the conventional time for a person to be in bed”) + stand (“an object which supports things”).
etymology.native: 由「夜」（一般人睡覺的傳統時間）與「立」（支撐物）組成。

senses.definition: Autism spectrum disorder, a condition characterized by impairment in social communication and interaction, as well as a need or strong preference for predictability and routine, sensory processing differences, focused interests, or repetitive behaviours. This includes classic autism as well as other, previously distinct disorders such as Asperger's syndrome, childhood disintegrative disorder, and pervasive developmental disorder not otherwise specified.

Classic autism, a pervasive neurological condition that is observable in early childhood and persists throughout the lifespan, characterised by atypical communication patterns (e.g., differences in body language or eye contact), delayed language development, and sensory processing sensitivities.
A diagnosis involving a pathological tendency to engage in self-centered fantasy thinking, historically considered a symptom of insanity or schizophrenia.
Abnormal and unhealthy focus or persistence, stereotypically coupled with low self-awareness and unhealthy hatred of opposition or criticism.

examples.text: Autism continues to be underdiagnosed.
examples.translation: 自閉症仍被低估診斷。

examples.text: Most drivers don't have autism.
examples.translation: 大多數駕駛員並非自閉症患者。

examples.text: Tom was diagnosed with autism.
examples.translation: 湯姆被診斷出有自閉症。

examples.text: Vaccines don't cause autism.
examples.translation: 疫苗不會導致自閉症。

examples.text: Tom was diagnosed as having autism at age four.
examples.translation: 湯姆四歲時被診斷出有自閉症。

examples.text: I was diagnosed with autism at the age of five.
examples.translation: 我五歲時被診斷出有自閉症。

etymology.text: Borrowed from German Autismus, coined by Swiss psychiatrist Eugen Bleuler, first usage dated to 1907 attributed by Carl Jung as an alternative of his for "auto-erotism", although Bleuler himself differentiates the terms in his book Dementia Praecox, first published 1911. From Ancient Greek αὐτός (autós, “self”) + -ισμός (-ismós, “-ism”).
etymology.native: 此詞源自德文Autismus，由瑞士精神科醫師Eugen Bleuler創製，最早使用可追溯至1907年，由Carl Jung稱為「自體性快感」的替代詞，但Bleuler本人在其著作《Dementia Praecox》（1911年出版）中已將兩者區分。詞源來自古希臘語αὐτός（autós，意為「自我」）＋-ισμός（-ismós，意為「-ism」）。

senses.definition: A recognizable pattern of signs, symptoms and/or behaviours, especially of a disease or medical or psychological condition.
Any set of characteristics regarded as identifying a certain type, condition, etc., usually adverse.

examples.text: Tom was diagnosed with Asperger's syndrome.
Antonio suffered from Down's syndrome.
Tom was diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome.
All of her children were born with Down syndrome.
Asperger syndrome is a form of autism.
I suffer from restless leg syndrome.

etymology.text: Learned borrowing from New Latin syndrome, from Ancient Greek συνδρομή (sundromḗ, “concurrence of symptoms, concourse”), from σύνδρομος (súndromos, “running together”), from συν- (sun-, “with”) + δρόμος (drómos, “running, course”).

senses.definition: Something that prevents, hampers, or hinders.

An allowance of a certain amount of time or distance in starting, granted in a race (or other contest of skill) to the competitor possessing disadvantages; or an additional weight or other hindrance imposed upon the one possessing advantages, in order to equalize, as much as possible, the chances of success.
senses.native: 在競賽中給予處於劣勢的參賽者一定時間或距離的寬限，或對處於優勢者施加額外重量或其他障礙，以盡量平衡成功機會

senses.definition: An individual's physical or mental disadvantage or disability.
senses.native: 個人的身體或精神缺陷或殘疾

senses.definition: A race or similar contest in which there is an allowance of time, distance, weight, or other advantage, to equalize the chances of the competitors.
senses.native: 一種允許給予時間、距離、重量或其他優勢以平衡競爭對手機會的競賽

senses.definition: An old card game, similar to lanterloo.
senses.native: 類似蘭特魯的老式紙牌遊戲

senses.definition: Synonym of hand-in-cap (“old English trading game”).
senses.native: 「手入帽」的同義詞（舊英語交易遊戲）

examples.text: Having no will is the worst handicap.
examples.translation: 沒有願望是最大的障礙。

examples.text: The blind young man has got over his handicap.
examples.translation: 那位失明年輕人已克服了他的 handicap。

examples.text: Poor eyesight is a handicap to a sportsman.
examples.translation: 視力不佳對運動員而言是一種 handicap。

examples.text: Age is often a handicap.
examples.translation: 年齡常是一種 handicap。

examples.text: His lack of experience proved to be a major handicap in securing the job.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: He's good. His handicap is in the single digits.
examples.translation: 他表現很好，他的 handicap 僅在個位數範圍。

relations.native: 主管 handicap 的裁判人員
手動障礙（非殘疾相關詞，語境不符）
handicap 資本主義（非殘疾相關詞，語境不符）
對 handicap 的恐懼（非殘疾相關詞，語境不符）
無 handicap 狀態（非殘疾相關詞，語境不符）
過度 handicap（非殘疾相關詞，語境不符）
手控攝影機（非殘疾相關詞，語境不符）
手動障礙（非殘疾相關詞，語境不符）

etymology.text: From hand-in-cap, in reference to holding the game stakes in a cap.
etymology.native: 源自「手入帽」，指將賭注持於帽中。

senses.definition: The act or instance of being defeated, of being overcome or vanquished; a loss.
The act or instance of defeating, of overcoming, vanquishing.
Frustration (by prevention of success), stymieing; (law) nullification.
Destruction, ruin.

examples.text: Licking their wounds after a temporary defeat, they planned their next move.
The inscription records her defeat of the country's enemies in a costly war.

etymology.text: From Middle English defeten, from Middle English defet (“disfigured”, past participle) and defet (“defect”, noun), see Etymology 2 below.

senses.definition: Oneness: the state or fact of being one undivided entity.
Agreement; harmony.
A single undivided thing, seen as complete in itself.

Any of the three classical rules of drama: unity of action (nothing should be admitted not directly relevant to the development of the plot), unity of place (the scenes should be set in the same place), and unity of time (all the events should be such as might happen within a single day).
The number 1 or any element of a set or field that behaves under a given operation as the number 1 behaves under multiplication.
The peculiar characteristics of an estate held by several in joint tenancy.

The form of consensus in a Quaker meeting for business which signals that a decision has been reached. In order to achieve unity, everyone who does not agree with the decision must explicitly stand aside, possibly being recorded in the minutes as doing so.

examples.text: Algeria's unity can never be questioned.
Humanity's future depends on unity.
The EU's unity is gradually becoming shakier.
Spirituality reveals the unity of all things.
The enemies of Berber unity are our enemies.
It is necessary to protect the national unity.

etymology.text: From Middle English unite, from Anglo-Norman, Old French unité, from Latin ūnitās, from ūnus (“one”) + noun of state suffix -itās, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *óynos (“one, single”), hence distantly related to one and an. By surface analysis, unite + -y. Displaced native Old English ānnes (literally “oneness”).

senses.definition: A grasp or grip.
An act or instance of holding.
senses.native: 持有、握住的行為或例子

senses.definition: A place where animals are held for safety
senses.native: 為了安全而收容動物的地方（收容所）

senses.definition: An order that something is to be reserved or delayed, limiting or preventing how it can be dealt with.
senses.native: 保留或延遲處理某事的指令，限制或阻止其被處理（暫停、留置）

senses.definition: Something reserved or kept.
Power over someone or something.
senses.native: 對某人或某物的支配力

senses.definition: The ability to persist.
The property of maintaining the shape of styled hair.
A position or grip used to control the opponent.
senses.native: 用於控制對手的姿勢或握法（抱法）

senses.definition: An exercise involving holding a position for a set time
senses.native: 在特定時間內保持某姿勢的運動（靜止停留）

senses.definition: The percentage the house wins on a gamble, the house or bookmaker's hold.
senses.native: 莊家在賭博中的抽頭比例（莊家抽水）

senses.definition: The wager amount, the total hold.
senses.native: 賭注的總金額（總下注額）

senses.definition: An instance of holding one's service game, as opposed to being broken.
The part of an object one is intended to grasp, or anything one can use for grasping with hands or feet.
A fruit machine feature allowing one or more of the reels to remain fixed while the others spin.
The queueing system on telephones and similar communication systems which maintains a connection when all lines are busy.
A statistic awarded to a relief pitcher who is not still pitching at the end of the game and who records at least one out and maintains a lead for his team.
A region of airspace reserved for aircraft being kept in a holding pattern.
A pause facility.
The cargo area of a ship or aircraft (often holds or cargo hold).

examples.text: Please hold the line a moment.
examples.translation: 請在綫稍候。

examples.text: This minibus holds 25 persons.
examples.translation: 這輛迷你巴士能容納25個人。

examples.text: Do you know how to correctly hold chopsticks?
examples.translation: 你知道要怎麼拿筷子才是正確的嗎？

examples.text: Unconsciously my mom took hold of the chair.
examples.translation: 母親無意中握住了椅子。

examples.text: He holds an important position in the company.
examples.translation: 他在公司裡身兼要職。

examples.text: He holds an extreme opinion on education.
examples.translation: 關於教育，他持極端意見。

etymology.text: Derived from Middle English holden, derived from Old English healdan, derived from Proto-West Germanic *haldan, derived from Proto-Germanic *haldaną (“to tend, herd”), maybe derived from Proto-Indo-European *kel- (“to drive”). Doublet of halt.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 holden，來自古英語 healdan，源自古西日耳曼語 *haldan，源自古德語 *haldaną（意為「放牧、照料」），可能源自印歐語系 *kel-（意為「驅馭」）。為 halt 的同源詞。

senses.definition: To control or keep in check.
To deprive of liberty.
To restrict or limit.
To strain again.

examples.text: You should learn to restrain yourself.
examples.translation: 你應該學習控制自己的情緒。

examples.text: We ate with chopsticks in restrained silence.
examples.translation: 我們用筷子在沉靜中用餐。

examples.text: You're in violation of the restraining order.
examples.translation: 你違反了保護令。

examples.text: Jonas got a restraining order against Amelia.
examples.translation: Jonas 對 Amelia 獲得了保護令。

examples.text: He laboured to restrain his desire to speak.
examples.translation: 他努力抑制說話的慾望。

examples.text: I barely restrained myself from vomiting.
examples.translation: 我幾乎無法忍住不嘔吐。

etymology.text: From Middle English restreinen, from Old French restreindre, from Latin rēstringere (“fasten, tighten”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 restreinen，來自舊法式 restreindre，再來自拉丁語 rēstringere（綁住、拉緊）。

senses.definition: To force physically, by strong persuasion or pressuring; to compel; to oblige.
To keep within close bounds; to confine.
To reduce a result in response to limited resources.

examples.text: I felt constrained to help her.
We are constrained to and restrained from an action.
What human trespass would constrain thy power, O Zeus?
I am constrained by lack of time.
The government finances are severely constrained because of falling tax revenues.
Changes in water availability, both episodic and long-lasting, will constrain different forms of energy production.

etymology.text: From Middle English constreinen, from Old French constreindre, from Latin cōnstringō, from cōn- (“with, together”) + stringō (“to draw, bind or tie tight”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *streyg- (“to stroke, to shear, stiff”).

senses.definition: To bind, compel, constrain, or oblige by a social, legal, or moral tie.
To cause to be grateful or indebted; to oblige.
To commit (money, for example) in order to fulfill an obligation.

examples.text: I felt obligated.
examples.translation: 我覺得有義務。

examples.text: Many methanogenic Archaea are obligate anaerobes.
Tom felt obligated to say something.
You're not obligated to answer that question.
Tom and Mary say they feel obligated to help.
Tom and Mary said they felt obligated to help.

etymology.text: First attested in 1533; borrowed from Latin obligātus, perfect passive participle of obligō, see -ate (verb-forming suffix). Doublet of oblige, taken through French.

senses.definition: To have rightful possession of (property, goods or capital); to have legal title to; to acquire a property or asset.
To have recognized political sovereignty over a place, territory, as distinct from the ordinary connotation of property ownership.
To virtually or figuratively enslave.
To admit, concede, grant, allow; not to deny.
To acknowledge.
To proudly acknowledge; to not be ashamed or embarrassed of.
To take responsibility for.
To recognise.
To claim as one's own.
To confess.
To defeat or embarrass; to overwhelm.
To defeat, dominate, or be above.
To illicitly obtain administrative access to a computer system, thereby having full access to all the files thereon (including executables).
To be very good.

examples.text: The company is wholly owned by the local government.
examples.translation: 這家公司由地方政府百分之百持有。

examples.text: She makes all her own clothes.
examples.translation: 她的衣服全部都是她自己做的。

etymology.text: From Middle English oun, owen, from Old English āgen (“own, proper, peculiar”), originally the past participle of āgan; from Proto-West Germanic *aigan (“own”), from Proto-Germanic *aiganaz (“own”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eyḱ- (“to have, possess”). Doublet of eigen-.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（oun、owen），來自古英語（āgen）「自己的、特有的」，原為（āgan）的過去分詞，經原始日耳曼語（*aiganaz），上溯至原始印歐語（*h₂eyḱ-）「擁有」。

senses.definition: To ward off attacks against (something or someone).
To ward off attacks from (something or someone).
To support by words or writing; to vindicate, talk in favour of.
To make legal defence of; to represent (the accused).
To focus one's energies and talents on preventing opponents from scoring, as opposed to focusing on scoring.
Mostly in tests. The action of not putting force into hitting a shot, but to conserve energy and wear down bowlers so they can attack later.
To attempt to retain a title, or attempt to reach the same stage in a competition as one did in the previous instance of that competition.
To call a raise from the big blind.
To ward off, repel (an attack or attacker).
To prevent, to keep (from doing something).
To prohibit, forbid.

examples.text: He tried to defend her.
examples.translation: 他試圖保護她。

examples.text: He who defends everything defends nothing.
I can't believe you're defending them.
To defend ourselves, we had to tell a lie.
examples.translation: 為了保護自己，我們只好說謊。

examples.text: They defended their country against the invaders.
examples.translation: 他們抵禦入侵者，保衛了國家。

examples.text: You are not in a position to defend yourself.

relations.native: 看守，以防逃脫或制止暴力行為
看守，以防逃脫或制止暴力行為

etymology.text: From Middle English defenden, from Old French defendre, deffendre (Modern French défendre), from Latin dēfendō (“to ward off”), from Proto-Italic *fendō, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰen-. Displaced native Old English bewerian.

senses.definition: To hold in belief or estimation; to adjudge as a conclusion; to regard as being; to evaluate according to one's beliefs; to account.
To think, judge, or have or hold as an opinion; to decide or believe on consideration; to suppose.
To judge, to pass judgment on; to doom, to sentence.
To adjudge, to decree.
To dispense (justice); to administer (law).

examples.text: The doctor deemed Damiano a psychopath.
My sister deems your efforts futile.
The study was deemed unscientific.
Interest rates are deemed by Islam as usury.
He deemed any action futile and threw in the towel.
Vladimir deemed Anna old enough to stay home alone.

etymology.text: From Middle English dēmen (“to judge; to criticize, condemn; to impose a penalty on, sentence; to direct, order; to believe, think, deem”), from Old English dēman (“to decide, decree, deem”), from Proto-West Germanic *dōmijan, from Proto-Germanic *dōmijaną (“to judge, think”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to set, put”).

senses.definition: All the persons who live in a given house or other home; a family including attendants, servants etc.; a domestic or family establishment.
Legal or culturally determined unit of people living together.
Entirety of work and management required to sustain the household.
senses.native: 維持家庭所需的全部工作與管理

senses.definition: A line of ancestry; a race or house.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: At least 20 households caught fire.
examples.translation: 至少20戶人家著火了。

examples.text: The idea of getting ammonia-powered household appliance inside my house doesn't attract me a lot.
examples.translation: 我對將氨氣動力家電裝在家裡沒什麼興趣。

examples.text: A coupon industry publication estimates that 89 percent of American households redeem coupons as a way to economize.
examples.translation: 一份優惠券產業刊物估計，美國有 89% 的家戶會使用優惠券來節省開支。

examples.text: A large household often requires significant resources for maintaining a domestic establishment.
examples.translation: 大家庭通常需要大量資源來維持家庭運作。

examples.text: Her household consisted of her parents and three elderly servants who cared for them.
examples.translation: 她的家戶由父母與三位照顧他們的年長僕役組成。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: She was busy with household work.
examples.translation: 她忙於家務。

etymology.text: From Middle English houshold. By surface analysis, house + hold.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 houshold，字面分析為 house 加上 hold。

senses.definition: The path an object takes as it moves.
The path of a body as it travels through space.
The ordered set of intermediate states assumed by a dynamical system as a result of time evolution.
senses.native: 動態系統時間演變之狀態序列

senses.definition: A course of development, such as that of a war or career.

examples.text: Damiano changed the ship’s trajectory.
examples.translation: 達米亞諾調整了船的航跡。

examples.text: Mary's life trajectory has changed greatly since then.
examples.translation: 自那以來，瑪麗的人生軌跡已大幅改變。

examples.text: Does Algeria need to reshape its geopolitical trajectory?
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞需要重新規劃其地緣政治軌跡嗎？

examples.text: Karl tried his best to maintain his trajectory.
examples.translation: 卡爾盡力維持自己的發展軌跡。

examples.text: Algeria needs to change its economic trajectory.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞需要改變其經濟軌跡。

examples.text: Mary's life trajectory has changed radically since then.
examples.translation: 自那以來，瑪麗的人生軌跡已劇烈改變。

etymology.text: From New Latin trāiectōria f (“trajectory”) (used by Newton), the feminine of trāiectōrius (“of or pertaining to throwing across”), from Latin trāiectus (“thrown over or across”), past participle of trāiciō, from trans- (“across, beyond”) (see trans-) + iaciō (“to throw”) (from Proto-Indo-European *(H)yeh₁- (“to throw, impel”)). Middle French and Middle English had trajectorie (“end of a funnel”), from Latin trāiectōrium.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁文 trāiectōria f（牛頓所用），為 trāiectōrius 的陰性形，源自拉丁文 trāiectus（「拋過或跨越」），為 trāiciō 的過去分詞，而 trāiciō 又源自 trans-（「跨越、超越」）+ iaciō（「拋」），源自印歐語系原始詞 *(H)yeh₁-（「拋、推」）。法文與英文曾有 trajectorie（「漏斗末端」），源自拉丁文 trāiectōrium。

senses.definition: The act of flying; the ability to fly.
An instance of flying.
The trajectory or passage through air or space of a projectile, ship, etc.
A swift movement, especially as to escape; an escape.
A trip made by an aircraft, particularly one between two cities or countries, which is often planned or reserved in advance.
The aircraft used in a journey through air or space.
The movement of a spinning ball through the air from the bowler to where it bounces on the pitch.
An episode of imaginative thinking or dreaming.
The feathers on an arrow or dart used to help it follow an even path.
An aerodynamic surface designed to guide a projectile's trajectory.
The shaped material forming the thread of a screw.
An air force unit, ranked below a squadron, comprising several planes and their crews.
A group of angels or types of angels, e.g., seraphim, cherubim.
A paper airplane.
A series of stairs between landings.
A floor which is reached by stairs or escalators.
A level of a terrace; a series of such levels making up a terrace.
A group of canal locks with a short distance between them
A numbered subclass of a given class of warship, denoting incremental modernizations to the original design.
A group of birds, especially doves (pigeons), goshawks or swallows.

examples.text: Sorry, the flight is already full.
examples.translation: 對不起，航班已經客滿了。

examples.text: Tom is a flight attendant.
examples.translation: 湯姆是空少。

examples.text: The flight was cancelled.
examples.translation: 航班取消了

examples.text: Our flight was canceled.
examples.translation: 我們的航班被取消了。

examples.text: Tom's flight was delayed and then cancelled.
examples.translation: 湯姆的航班延誤了，然後被取消了。

examples.text: All the flights on March 30th were fully booked.
examples.translation: 3月30號的班機全部滿座。

relations.native: 平坦地區（有時覆蓋淺水或潮汐水）
用於在水中或其他液體中承載物體的浮力裝置

etymology.text: From Middle English flight, from Old English flyht (“flight”), from Proto-West Germanic *fluhti (“flight”), derived from *fleuganą (“to fly”), from Proto-Indo-European *plewk- (“to fly”), enlargement of *plew- (“flow”). Analyzable as fly + -t (variant of -th).

senses.definition: A manoeuvre of troops or ships.
A turning movement, especially of the body.
The opening out of a curve; now more generally, the gradual transformation of a curve by a change of the conditions generating it.
The extraction of a root from a given power.
The act or an instance of giving off gas; emission.
Development; the act or result of developing what was implicit in an idea, argument etc.
A process of gradual change in a given system, subject, product etc., especially from simpler to more complex forms.
The transformation of animals, plants and other living things into different forms (now understood as a change in genetic composition) by the accumulation of changes over successive generations.
A turned or twisted shape; an involution, a complex or intricate shape.
The act or process of unfolding or opening out; the progression of events in regular succession.

examples.text: Evolution is cleverer than you are.
Welcome to the world of evolution.
He does not believe in evolution.
Evolution is a tinkerer and not an engineer.
Language evolves with the evolution of culture.
The evolution of dinosaurs interests me greatly.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin ēvolūtiō, ēvolūtiōnis (“the act of unrolling, unfolding or opening (of a book)”), from ēvolūtus, perfect passive participle of ēvolvō (“unroll, unfold”), from ex + volvō (“roll”).

senses.definition: The determination of the relative position of something or someone.
The relative physical position or direction of something.
The construction of a Christian church to have its aisle in an east-west direction with the altar at the east end.
An inclination, tendency or direction.
The ability to orient, or the process of so doing.
An adjustment to a new environment.
An introduction to a (new) environment.
Events to orient new students at a school; events to help new students become familiar with a school.
The direction of print across the page; landscape or portrait.
The choice of which ordered bases are "positively" oriented and which are "negatively" oriented on a real vector space.
The designation of a parametrised curve as "positively" or "negatively" oriented; the analogous description of a surface or hypersurface.

examples.text: This room's orientation is great.
examples.translation: 這間房間朝向很好。

examples.text: How was orientation?
We will have a period of orientation for freshmen.
Now I'll give you an orientation course.
Sensitized consumers seek orientation.
Children are quick to gain orientation to new circumstances.

senses.definition: Free from burden or impediment; unencumbered.

senses.definition: Lightly built; typically designed for speed or small loads.
senses.native: 結構輕巧的；通常為速度或小負載而設計的（輕型）

examples.text: There was a light rain yesterday.

examples.text: I usually have a light breakfast.

examples.text: All plants need water and light.
examples.translation: 所有的植物都需要陽光和水。

examples.text: It is getting lighter outside.
examples.translation: 外面天色越來越亮了。

examples.text: At dusk, the sky was dyed with purple light.
examples.translation: 黃昏時分，天空染上了紫色的光。

examples.text: Please turn off the light before you go to bed.
examples.translation: 上床睡覺之前請關燈。

etymology.text: From Middle English light, liht, leoht, from Old English lēoht, from Proto-West Germanic *leuht, from Proto-Germanic *leuhtą, from Proto-Indo-European *lewktom, from the root *lewk- (“to shine”).

senses.definition: Not being used appropriately; not occupied; (of time) with no, no important, or not much activity.
Not engaged in any occupation or employment; unemployed; inactive; doing nothing in particular.
Averse to work, labor or employment; lazy; slothful.
Of no importance; useless; worthless; vain; trifling; thoughtless; silly.
Empty, vacant.
Light-headed; foolish.

examples.text: No matter how rich a man may be, he ought not to be idle.
examples.translation: 無論一個男人多有錢，都不應無所事事。

examples.text: My computer hibernates after it has been idle for 30 minutes.
Light idle chatter.

etymology.text: From Middle English idel, ydel, from Old English īdel, from Proto-West Germanic *īdl, from Proto-Germanic *īdlaz. Cognate with Dutch ijdel (“vain, meaningless”), ijl (“rareified, skinny”), iel (“thin, slender”); German Low German iedel (“vain, idle”); German eitel (“vain, conceited”); and possibly Old Norse illr ("bad"; > English ill).

senses.definition: To set fire to (something), to light (something)
To spark off (something), to trigger
To commence burning.
To subject to the action of intense heat; to heat strongly; often said of incombustible or infusible substances.
senses.native: 使受強烈熱的作用；強熱；常用於形容不易燃燒或不易熔化的物質

examples.text: Damiano ignited the bom manually.
examples.translation: 達米安用手動方式點燃了炸彈。

examples.text: He tried to ignite it.
examples.translation: 他試圖點燃它。

examples.text: I ignited the fire.
examples.translation: 我點燃了火。

examples.text: Tinder is a material that is easily ignited.
examples.translation: 引火物是一種容易點燃的材料。

examples.text: The spirit of jihad was ignited once again.
examples.translation: 聖戰的精神再次被點燃。

examples.text: After he turned the key, the car engine ignited.
examples.translation: 他轉動鑰匙後，汽車引擎點燃了。

relations.native: 點燃（某物，通常是建築物）

etymology.text: From Latin ignītus, past participle of igniō, ignire (“to set on fire, ignite”), from Latin ignis (“fire”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁n̥gʷnis, and thus related to Sanskrit अग्नि (agní), Lithuanian ugnis, and Russian ого́нь (ogónʹ).
etymology.native: 源於拉丁語 ignītus，為 igniō 或 ignire（「點火」）的分詞形式，該詞來自拉丁語 ignis（「火」），並與梵語 अग्नि、立陶宛語 ugnis 及俄語 ого́нь 同源。

senses.definition: A person, typically someone other than a family member, spouse or lover, whose company one enjoys and towards whom one feels affection.
Brand name of a spring-loaded camming device, now used to refer to any such device, often uncapitalized, as friend.
An associate who provides assistance; patron, mentor.
A person with whom one is vaguely or indirectly acquainted.
A person who backs or supports something.
An object or idea that can be used for good.
Used as a form of address when warning someone.
A function or class granted special access to the private and protected members of another class.
A spring-loaded camming device.
A lover; a boyfriend or girlfriend.
A relative, a relation by blood or marriage.
Used to refer collectively to a group of associated individuals, especially those comprising a cast, company, or crew
A Quaker; a member of the Society of Friends. (See also Friends.)

examples.text: They became friends in elementary school.

examples.text: His coolness has alienated his friends.
examples.translation: 他冷酷的性格使朋友們一個一個地疏遠了他。

examples.text: I visited American friends in Oakland.
examples.translation: 我拜訪了奧克蘭的美國朋友們。

examples.text: They talked together like old friends.

examples.text: You must be careful in choosing your friends.
examples.translation: 交友須謹慎。

etymology.text: From Middle English freend, frend, frende, freynde, friend, frind, frond, frund, vrend, vryend, from Old English frēond, frīond (“friend”, literally “loving [one], lover”), from Proto-West Germanic *friund, from Proto-Germanic *frijōndz (“friend, loved one”), from Proto-Indo-European *preyH- (“to please; to love”), roughly equivalent to free + -nd. See also Friday.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（freend、frend），來自古英語（frēond）「朋友」，字面意思是「愛人者」，經原始日耳曼語（*frijōndz），上溯至原始印歐語（*preyH-）「取悅、愛」。另見（free、Friday）。

senses.definition: Lacking in earnestness, ability, or profundity.
Having less than average weight.
Lacking in strength.
Having a small footprint or performance impact.

examples.text: It's a small and lightweight audio player with extensive format support.

etymology.text: From light (“not heavy”, adjective) + weight (noun).

senses.definition: Not sufficient; of a type or kind that does not suffice, that does not satisfy requirements or needs.
Not sufficient; lacking competent power or ability; unqualified, unequal, unfit.

examples.text: There is insufficient light for reading.
Housing is insufficient in Algeria.
The money is insufficient.
There is insufficient light to take pictures.
examples.translation: 拍照片光線不夠亮。

examples.text: Due to insufficient sales, many shops are closed.
My knowledge of German is insufficient.

etymology.text: From Middle French insufficient, from Latin insufficiens. See also in- + sufficient.

senses.definition: Irradiated by light, lit.
Decorated and illustrated.

examples.text: The full moon illuminated the garden.
examples.translation: 滿月照亮了花園。

examples.text: The candles illuminated the room.
The square was illuminated by bright lights.
examples.translation: 廣場被鮮明的燈火照亮。

examples.translation: 這個房間被紅色的燈照亮了。

examples.text: The street is illuminated by many lights.
examples.translation: 許多燈照亮了街道。

examples.text: The room was illuminated by a candle.

senses.definition: To increase, to rise
To reach or come to by way of increase; to arise or spring up because of growth or result, especially as the produce of money lent.
To be incurred as a result of the passage of time.
To accumulate.
To become an enforceable and permanent right.

examples.text: Interest will begin to accrue after the first year.
Many advantages accrue to society from the freedom of speech.
Accrued interest will be paid into your account.
She accrued her wealth slowly but surely.
Interest accrued from the money left in my savings account.
She had to adjust her schedule to accommodate the compensatory time off she had accrued.

etymology.text: First attested in mid 15th century. From Middle English acrewen, borrowed from Old French acreüe, past participle of accreistre (“to increase”), from Latin accrēsco (“increase”), from ad (“in addition”) + crēscō (“to grow”). Compare accrete.

senses.definition: To give a sermon.
To proclaim by public discourse; to utter in a sermon or a formal religious harangue.
To advise or recommend earnestly.
To teach or instruct by preaching; to inform by preaching.
To give advice in an offensive or obtrusive manner.

examples.text: Yidir doesn't practice what he preaches.
examples.translation: 義德不實踐他所講的

examples.text: Tom doesn't practice what he preaches.
examples.translation: 湯姆不實踐他所講的

examples.text: You should practice what you preach.
examples.translation: 你應該實踐你所講的

examples.text: I'm fed up with him always preaching to me.
examples.translation: 我厭煩了他對我說教。

examples.text: My sister doesn't practice what she preaches.
examples.translation: 我姊不實踐她所講的

examples.text: You're preaching to the choir.
examples.translation: 你是在對同調的人講話

etymology.text: From Middle English prechen, from Old French prëechier, precchier (Modern French prêcher), from Latin praedicō (“to proclaim, announce”, literally “to fore-assign, pre-dedicate”). Doublet of predicate.
etymology.native: 「prechen」源自中世紀英文，來源為古法文 prëechier、precchier（現代法文 prêcher），再源自拉丁文 praedicō（意為「宣告、宣傳」，字面意為「預先指定」）。此詞與「predicate」為同源詞。

senses.definition: To bring (something such as a vehicle) to a halt or store in a specified place.
To defer (a matter) until a later date.

To enclose in a park, or as in a park.
senses.native: 把……圈入公園（或類似的圍場）中

senses.definition: To hit a home run; to hit the ball out of the park.
senses.native: （棒球）擊出全壘打（把球打出球場外）

senses.definition: To register a domain name, but make no use of it (See domain parking)
senses.native: 註冊網域名稱但不加以使用（域名停放）

examples.text: You can park behind the hotel.
examples.translation: 你們可以把車停到旅館背後。

examples.text: Sir, you are not allowed to park your car here.

examples.text: I've paid parking fines a number of times myself.
examples.translation: 我自己也因違例泊車而被罰了許多次款。

etymology.text: From Middle English park, from Old French parc (“livestock pen”), from Medieval Latin parcus, parricus, from Frankish *parrik (“enclosure, pen, fence”). Cognate with Dutch perk (“enclosure; flowerbed”), Old High German pfarrih, pferrih (“enclosure, pen”), Old English pearroc (“enclosure”) (whence modern English paddock), Old Norse parrak, parak (“enclosure, pen; distress, anxiety”), Icelandic parraka (“to keep pent in under restraint and coercion”). More at parrock, paddock.
etymology.native: 「park」源自中世紀英語，來源為古法語「parc」，再源自中世紀拉丁語「parcus」或「parricus」，而這些詞又來自古弗蘭克語「*parrik」（意為圍欄或籠子）。與荷蘭語「perk」（意為圍欄或花壇）、古高地德語「pfarrih」或「pferrih」（意為圍欄或籠子）、古英語「pearroc」（意為圍欄，後演變為現代英語「paddock」）、古諾斯語「parrak」或「parak」（意為圍欄或籠子，亦可指困擾或焦慮）、冰島語「parraka」（意為拘束或壓制）同源。另見「parrock」與「paddock」。

senses.definition: One who explores something
A person who by means of travel (notably an expedition) searches out new information.
Any of various hand tools, with sharp points, used in dentistry.
A visual representation of a file system etc. through which the user can navigate.
A participant in the Exploring program, which focuses on career exploration.
A participant in the Fire Service Exploring program.

examples.text: The explorers ventured inside the caverns.
James Cook was a British explorer.
The explorers cut their way through the forest.
The first explorers navigated by the stars.
The explorer bartered with the natives for food.
The explorers discovered a skeleton in the cave.
examples.translation: 探險家們在洞穴裡發現了骸骨。

etymology.text: From explore + -er.

senses.definition: Someone who scavenges, especially one who searches through rubbish for food or useful things.
An animal that feeds on decaying matter such as carrion.
A substance used to remove impurities from the air or from a solution.
A child employed to pick up loose cotton from the floor in a cotton mill.
A street sweeper.

examples.text: Jackals are scavengers.
examples.translation: 鬣狗是食腐動物。

examples.text: There are lots of garbage scavengers in Algiers.

examples.text: Lions are scavengers, among other things.
examples.translation: 獅子也是食腐動物，除此之外還有其他行為。

examples.text: Tom and Mary organized a scavenger hunt.
examples.translation: 湯姆和瑪麗組織了一場尋寶遊戲。

examples.text: Carlos's friends had a scavenger hunt at the party.
examples.translation: 卡洛斯的朋友在派對上舉辦了尋寶遊戲。

examples.translation: 我正在參加一場尋寶遊戲。

relations.native: 什麼東西都不肯扔的人
什麼東西都不肯扔的人

etymology.text: Originally from Middle English scavager, from Anglo-Norman scawageour (“one who had to do with scavage, inspector, tax collector”), from Old Northern French *scawage, escauwage (“scavage”), Old French *scavage, escavage, alteration of escauvinghe (compare Medieval Latin scewinga, sceawinga), from Old Dutch scauwōn (“to inspect, to examinate, to look at”). Usually reinterpreted/re-analysed today as scavenge (which was originally a backformation from this word) + -er. Compare Old English sċēawung
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 scavager，來自安熱諾曼語 scawageour（指與 scavage 有關者、檢查員或稅收官），源自舊北法語 *scawage。

senses.definition: An enclosure within which workers, prisoners, or soldiers are confined.
A group of buildings where members of the same extended family live together.
An enclosure for secure storage.
A group of buildings situated close together, e.g. for a school or block of offices.
senses.native: 緊密相連的建築群，例如學校或辦公大樓

senses.definition: Anything made by combining several things.

senses.definition: A substance formed by chemical bonding of two or more elements in definite proportions by weight.

senses.native: 刑事或違規者向當局支付罰金以換取法院免予起訴的法律程序

senses.definition: A lexeme that consists of more than one stem.
senses.native: 由一個以上詞根組成的詞彙（複合詞）

senses.definition: A lexeme that consists of more than one stem or affix, e.g. "bookshop", "high school" or "non-standard".
senses.native: 複合詞：由一個以上詞根或詞綴組成的詞彙（如 bookshop、high school、non-standard）

senses.definition: A compound locomotive, a steam locomotive with both high-pressure and low-pressure cylinders.
senses.native: 複式機車（具高壓與低壓汽缸的蒸汽機車）

senses.native: 由任何組合的原料製成的物質

兩種或兩種以上物質混合後的結果；混合物

etymology.text: Possibly from Malay kampong, kampung (“group of buildings, village”), via Dutch or Portuguese, altered under the influence of Etymology 2. Doublet of kampung.

senses.definition: Quickness of perception or discernment; penetration of mind; the faculty of nice discrimination; acuity of mind.
A sharp, tapering point extending from a plant.
A bony, often sharp, protuberance, especially that of the ischium.

examples.text: You have business acumen.
examples.translation: 你有商業直覺。

examples.text: She is a lady of business acumen.
examples.translation: 她是一位具備商業直覺的女士。

examples.text: I trust her acumen.
examples.translation: 我信任她的直覺。

examples.text: It is obvious to me that he has no political acumen at all.
examples.translation: 我明確覺得他完全沒有政治直覺。

examples.text: His wealth was inherited, not a consequence of his own business acumen.
examples.translation: 他的財富是繼承而來，而非源自自身商業直覺。

examples.text: We had the mental acumen, the efficacy of the bow and arrow, opposite the clumsy musket.
examples.translation: 我們擁有足夠的智慧，弓箭的效力，對抗笨拙的火槍。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin acūmen (“sharp point”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 acūmen（意為「尖端」）

senses.definition: The capacity of mind, especially to understand principles, truths, facts or meanings, acquire knowledge, and apply it to practice; the ability to comprehend and learn; the ability to process sentient experience to generate true beliefs with a justified degree of confidence.
An individual's expected relative performance in a cognitive test.
The quality of making use or having made use of such capacities: depth of understanding, mental quickness.
An entity that has such capacities.
Information, often secret, about an enemy or about hostile activities.
A political or military department, agency or unit designed to gather information, usually secret, about the enemy or about hostile activities.
Acquaintance; intercourse; familiarity.

examples.text: He complimented her on her intelligence.
Her intelligence often surprises me.
Intelligence is better than science.
AI stands for artificial intelligence.
examples.translation: AI 代表人工智慧。

senses.definition: A sight or view of the interior of anything; a deep inspection or view; introspection; frequently used with into.

Knowledge (usually derived from consumer understanding) that a company applies in order to make a product or brand perform better and be more appealing to customers
Intuitive apprehension of the inner nature of a thing or things; intuition.
An extended understanding of a subject resulting from identification of relationships and behaviors within a model, context, or scenario.
An individual's awareness of the nature and severity of one's mental illness.

examples.text: Any insight would be appreciated.
I need that kind of insight.
Thanks for all your insight.
She has a feminine insight into human behavior.
Your insights have opened my mind to new ideas.
He often shares insights about English culture.

Perhaps continuing Old English insiht (“narrative, argument, account”), from Proto-Germanic *insahtiz (“account, narrative, argument”). Compare West Frisian ynsjoch (“insight”), Dutch inzicht (“insight, awareness, view, opinion”), German Low German Insicht (“insight”), German Einsicht (“insight, knowledge, perception, understanding”), Danish indsigt (“insight”), Swedish insikt

senses.definition: Great skill or knowledge in a particular field or hobby.
Advice, or opinion, of an expert.

The sense that detects odours.
A conclusion or intuition that a situation is wrong, more complex than it seems, or otherwise inappropriate.

examples.translation: 因為你真的很臭，這就是為什麼。

The noun is from Middle English smel, smil, smul (“smell, odour”). Related to Saterland Frisian smeele (“to smoulder”), Middle Dutch smōlen (“to burn, smoulder”) (whence Dutch smeulen (“to smoulder”)), Middle Low German smölen (“to be hazy, b

senses.definition: The quality of being sexual; that which is characterized or distinguished by sex.
Sexual activity; concern with, or interest in, sexual activity.
Sexual potency.
Sexual orientation.
Sexual identity, gender.

etymology.native: 「flake」源自中世英文 flake（雪片），來自古英語 flacca 和／或古諾斯語 flak（鬆散或撕裂的碎片），又源自原始日耳曼語 *flaką（扁平之物），再溯源自原始印歐語 *pleh₂-（平坦、寬廣）。與挪威語 flak（切片、薄片，字面為「撕下的碎片」）、瑞典語 flak（薄片）、丹麥語 flage（碎屑）、德語 Flocke（碎屑）、荷蘭語 vlak（平滑表面）及 vlok（碎屑）同源，亦與拉丁語相關。

etymology.text: From Middle English trotten, from Old French trotter, troter (“to go, trot”), from Medieval Latin *trottō, *trotō (“to go”), from Frankish *trottōn (“to go, run”), from Proto-Germanic *trudōną, *trudaną, *tradjaną (“to go, step, tread”), from Proto-Indo-European *dreh₂- (“to run, escape”). Cognate with Old High German trottōn (“to run”), Modern German trotten (“to trot, plod”), Gothic 𐍄𐍂𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌽 (trudan, “to tread”), Old Norse troða (“to walk, tread”), Old English tredan (“to step, tread”). Doublet
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 trotten，來自舊法語 trotter, troter（「行走、奔跑」），來自中世紀拉丁語 *trottō, *trotō（「行走」），來自弗蘭克語 *trottōn（「行走、奔跑」），來自原始日耳曼語 *trudōną, *trudaną, *tradjaną（「行走、步伐、踩踏」），來自原始印歐語 *dreh₂-（「奔跑、逃離」）。與舊高地德語 trottōn（「奔跑」）、現代德語 trotten（「小跑、蹣跚」）同源，古哥特語 𐍄𐍂𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌽 (trudan, 「踩踏」），舊諾斯語 troða（「行走、踩踏」），舊英語 tredan（「步伐、踩踏」）。雙胞胎詞根。

A fee charged by an agent or broker for carrying out a transaction.
The thing to be done as agent for another.
A body or group of people, officially tasked with carrying out a particular function.
A bonus in pay awarded to a salesperson for selling a particular, secretly sponsored product, for which the sponsor will reimburse the employer.
A payment by a fan to an artist, after which the artist will produce a work of art requested by the fan.
The act of committing (e.g. a crime or error).
A shirt or chemise.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: How much is the commission?

examples.translation: 我賣任何東西都可獲取三％佣金。

etymology.text: From Middle English commissioun, from Old French commission, from Latin commissiō (“sending together; commission”), from committō + -tiō (suffix forming nouns of action), from com- (“with”) + mittō (“to send”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 commissioun，來自古法文 commission，源自拉丁文 commissiō（意為「一起委派；委託」），由 committō + -tiō（構成動作名詞的後綴）組成，而 committō 來自 com-（意為「與」）+ mittō（意為「送」）。

senses.definition: To send or officially charge someone or some group to do something.
To place an order for (often a piece of art).
To put (a ship or boat, etc.) into active service.

examples.text: James Bond was commissioned with recovering the secret documents.

etymology.text: From Middle English commissioun, from Old French commission, from Latin commissiō (“sending together; commission”), from committō + -tiō (suffix forming nouns of action), from com- (“with”) + mittō (“to send”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 commissioun，來自古法文 commission，源自拉丁文 commissiō（意為「一起委派；委託」），由 committō + -tiō（構成動作名詞的後綴）組成，而 committō 來自 com-（意為「與」）+ mittō（意為「送」）。

The condition of being delegated.
A group of delegates.
A method-dispatching technique describing the lookup and inheritance rules for self-referential calls.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin dēlēgātiō, dēlēgātiōnis, from dēlēgō: compare French délégation.

A share of the sales, profits, gross margin or similar.

senses.definition: Benefit or advantage.
