examples.text: Where's the newsroom of this newspaper?
examples.translation: 這家報社的新聞編輯室在哪裡？

examples.text: He reads the newspaper every morning.
examples.translation: 他每天早晨讀報。

examples.text: My grandfather often nods over his newspaper.
examples.translation: 祖父常常邊看報紙邊點頭。

examples.text: I traded old newspapers for toilet paper.
examples.translation: 我用舊報紙換衛生紙。

etymology.text: From news + paper.
etymology.native: 由「新聞」加「紙」組成。

senses.definition: A piece of nonfiction writing such as a story, report, opinion piece, or entry in a newspaper, magazine, journal, encyclopedia, etc.

A part of speech that indicates, specifies and limits a noun (a, an, or the in English). In some languages the article may appear as an ending (e.g. definite article in Swedish) or there may be none (e.g. Russian, Pashto).
A section of a legal document, bylaws, etc. or, in the plural, the entire document seen as a collection of these.
An object, a member of a group or class.
A part or segment of something joined to other parts, or, in combination, forming a structured set.
senses.native: （與其他部分相連的）部分；條款

senses.definition: A person; an individual.
A wench.
Subject matter; concern.
A distinct part.
A precise point in time; a moment.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Sammy is reading an article.
examples.translation: 薩米正在閱讀文章。

examples.text: Have you read this article?
examples.translation: 你有沒有看過這篇文章？

examples.text: I want to write an article.
examples.translation: 我想寫篇文章。

examples.text: This article is very good.
examples.translation: 這篇文章很好。

examples.text: Did you read the article?
examples.translation: 你看文章了沒？

examples.text: In any case, I've finished writing the article.
examples.translation: 不管怎麼說，我都把文章寫完了。

etymology.text: From Middle English article, from Old French article, from Latin articulus (“a joint, limb, member, part, division, the article in grammar, a point of time”), from Latin artus, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂értus (“that which is fit together; juncture, ordering”), from the root *h₂er- (“to join, fit (together)”). Doublet of articulus.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（article），來自古法語（article），再源自拉丁語（articulus）「關節、肢體、部分、文法上的冠詞、時間點」，來自（artus），最終來自原始印歐語（*h₂er-）「連接」。與（articulus）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: A film, TV program, publication etc. which presents a social, political, scientific or historical subject in a factual or informative manner.
Such works collectively, as a genre.

examples.text: A documentary has been made about Tom Jackson.

senses.definition: Writing materials, envelopes, office materials.

examples.text: All of this stationery is his.
examples.translation: 這些都是他的文具。

examples.text: He bought some stationery at the school store.
Where is the stationery cupboard, please?
I bought new notebooks and stationery to use at school.
What stationery isn't worth buying?
examples.translation: 哪些文具不值得買？

examples.text: The department store also has a stationery department.

etymology.text: From stationer + -y.

senses.definition: Routine work involving written documents.
senses.native: 文書工作、公文處理、文書處理

senses.definition: Written documents.
Excessive paperwork, busy work, red tape.
A work in paper.

Court documents or pre-sentencing investigation reports detailing the prisoner's criminal history (usually in the context of discerning whether an inmate has been charged for sex-related offenses or is likely to be an informant).

examples.text: The bureaucrats are militants of paperwork.
They're at their desks doing paperwork.
Boldi flipped through the paperwork.
I knew that Tom was in his office doing paperwork.
examples.translation: 我知道湯姆正在辦公室處理文件。

examples.text: We were bogged down in a morass of paperwork.
Tom got flustered when filling out the paperwork.

etymology.text: From paper + work.

senses.definition: A precious stone, usually of substantial monetary value or prized for its beauty or shine.
Any precious or highly valued thing or person.
Anything of small size, or expressed within brief limits, which is regarded as a gem on account of its beauty or value, such as a small picture, a verse of poetry, or an epigram.
Internet content of good quality.
A geometrid moth of the species Orthonama obstipata.
A package containing programs or libraries for the Ruby programming language.
A strong, dominating pitching performance.
A native or resident of the American state of Idaho.
A gemma or leaf bud.
A size of type between brilliant (4-point) and diamond (4½-point), running 222 lines to the foot.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: That guy is a gem.
examples.translation: 那個傢伙真是個寶貝。

examples.text: This is a gem.
examples.translation: 這真是個寶貝。

examples.text: The gem I bought from the shop is authentic.
examples.translation: 我在店裡買的那顆寶石是真正的。

examples.text: The thief does not want to sell the gems.
examples.translation: 那夥計不想賣掉這些寶石。

examples.text: These gems are priced at over a million yen each.
examples.translation: 這些寶石每顆售價超過一百萬日圓。

examples.text: She stumbled upon a hidden gem of a book.
examples.translation: 她意外發現了一本隱藏的珍貴書籍。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English gemme, gimme, yimme, ȝimme, from Old English ġimm, from Proto-West Germanic *gimmu (“gem”) and Old French gemme (“gem”), both from Latin gemma (“a swelling bud; jewel, gem”). Doublet of gemma and Gemma.
etymology.native: 此詞源於中古英語的 gemme、gimme 等，再追溯至古英語 ġimm 及舊法語 gemme。

senses.definition: To adorn with, or as if with, gems.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: They will gem the crown with rubies.
examples.translation: 他們會在王冠上鑲滿紅寶石。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English gemme, gimme, yimme, ȝimme, from Old English ġimm, from Proto-West Germanic *gimmu (“gem”) and Old French gemme (“gem”), both from Latin gemma (“a swelling bud; jewel, gem”). Doublet of gemma and Gemma.
etymology.native: 此詞源於中古英語的 gemme、gimme 等，再追溯至古英語 ġimm 及舊法語 gemme。

senses.definition: Nacre; mother-of-pearl.
A white color inspired by the shade of pearls.
senses.native: 珍珠白，如珍珠般的白色

senses.definition: Something precious.
A capsule of gelatin or similar substance containing liquid for, e.g., medicinal application.
A whitish speck or film on the eye.
senses.native: （眼）白翳，眼球上白色的斑點或薄膜

senses.definition: A fish allied to the turbot; the brill.
A light-colored tern.
One of the circle of tubercles which form the bur on a deer's antler.
senses.native: （鹿角）珠粒，鹿角基部圍成一圈的小突起

senses.definition: A fringe or border.
A valuable little nugget of information; especially, an aphorism or tip that is operationally useful for decision-making.
senses.native: 珍貴的小知識，尤指對決策有用的箴言或建議

senses.definition: Argent, in blazoning by precious stones.
The size of type between diamond and agate, standardized as 5-point.
A jewel or gem.
The clitoris.

examples.text: His teeth are white like a pearl.
examples.translation: 他的牙齒白得像珍珠一樣。

senses.definition: To hunt fish or other aquatic animals in a body of water, or to collect coral or pearls from the bottom of the sea.
To search (a body of water) for something other than fish.
senses.native: （在水域中）搜尋魚以外的東西（如打撈）

senses.definition: To use as bait when fishing.
To (attempt to) find or get hold of an object by searching among other objects.
senses.native: 在其他物件中搜尋或取得某物（摸找）

senses.definition: To talk to people in an attempt to get them to say something, or seek to obtain something by artifice.
senses.native: 與人交談以套話，或以手段騙取某物

senses.definition: Of a batsman, to attempt to hit a ball outside off stump and miss it.
senses.native: （板球）擊球員試圖擊打外角球卻揮空

senses.definition: To repair (a spar or mast) by fastening a beam or other long object (often called a fish) over the damaged part (see Noun above).
senses.native: 以梁（俗稱 fish）覆於受損處，修補桅桿或圓材

senses.definition: To hoist the flukes of.
senses.native: （鯨魚）將（尾鰭）吊起（潛水前動作）

senses.definition: To draw or guide (a wire or cable) by means of fish tape.
senses.native: 以穿線帶（fish tape）牽引或引導電線、纜線

examples.text: I've never gone fishing at night.
examples.translation: 我從沒在晚上釣過魚。

examples.text: You may go swimming or fishing.
examples.translation: 你可以去游泳或者釣魚。

examples.text: My father and I go fishing from time to time.
examples.translation: 我父親和我時不時地去釣魚。

examples.text: I would rather stay at home than go fishing.
examples.translation: 比起出去釣魚，我更想待在家裡。

examples.text: When he was a child, he would go fishing on Sundays.
examples.translation: 他小時候，星期天會去釣魚。

examples.text: She devoted all her spare time to fishing.
examples.translation: 她把所有的業餘時間都用在釣魚上了。

etymology.text: From Middle English fisch, from Old English fisċ (“fish”), from Proto-West Germanic *fisk, from Proto-Germanic *fiskaz (“fish”), from Proto-Indo-European *piskós (“fish”).

senses.definition: Someone with a Pisces astrological sign.

examples.text: Tom isn't a Pisces.
Tom is a Pisces.
She was born under the sign of Pisces.
Pisces men will always have my heart.
Do you think a male Gemini would get on well with a female Pisces?
I'm a Pisces, which means I believe in astrology.

etymology.text: From Latin piscēs, the nominative plural of piscis (“fish”), calque of Ancient Greek ἰχθύες (ikhthúes, “fish (pl); name of constellation”). Compare Akkadian 𒁺𒉺𒉺 (DU.NU.NU, “fish-cord”); the constellation is often depicted as two fish tied by a ribbon.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語「魚」的主格複數，仿譯自古希臘語「魚（複數）；星座名」。可比較阿卡德語「魚繩」；此星座常被描繪成以緞帶相繫的兩條魚。

senses.definition: A portable or wearable timepiece.
A particular time period when guarding is kept.
The act of guarding and observing someone or something.
senses.native: 監視或觀察某人或某物之行為

senses.definition: A period of wakefulness between the two sleeps of a biphasic sleep pattern (the dead sleep or first sleep and morning sleep or second sleep): the first waking.
senses.native: 雙相睡眠模式中兩次睡眠之間醒來的時段（即第一次醒來）

senses.definition: A person or group of people who guard.
senses.native: 負責看守的人或一群人

senses.definition: The post or office of a watchman; also, the place where a watchman is posted, or where a guard is kept.
senses.native: 巡邏員的職位；亦指巡邏員被派駐之處或守衛人員駐紮之地

senses.definition: A group of sailors and officers aboard a ship or shore station with a common period of duty: starboard watch, port watch.
senses.native: 船隻或岸上基地上一群具有共同勤務時期的水手與官員：右舷值班、左舷值班

senses.definition: A period of time on duty, usually four hours in length; the officers and crew who tend the working of a vessel during the same watch. (FM 55–501).
senses.native: 通常長達四小時的勤務時段；在同一班次中照料船隻運作的官員與船員。（FM 55–501）

senses.definition: The act of seeing, or viewing, for a period of time.
senses.native: 觀看或檢視一段時間的行為

senses.definition: A group of nightingales.

examples.text: I'll do my homework after I watch television.
examples.translation: 我看完電視才去做功課。

examples.text: "Did you watch TV last week?" "No, I didn't."
examples.translation: 「上週你看電視了嗎？」「沒有，我沒看。」

examples.text: Watch out for cars when you cross the street.
examples.translation: 當你過馬路的時候要當心汽車。

examples.text: It cost me 50 dollars to have my watch fixed.
examples.translation: 我花了五十美元修好了手表。

examples.text: Adam was furious with me when I broke his watch.
examples.translation: 我把亞當的手錶弄壞了，氣得他七竅生煙。

examples.text: They seldom watch television these days.
examples.translation: 這些天他們很少看電視。

etymology.text: As a noun, from Middle English wacche, from Old English wæċċe. See below for verb form.

senses.definition: A person sent out to gather and bring back information; especially, one employed in war to gain information about the enemy and ground.
A member of any number of youth organizations belonging to the international scout movement, such as the Boy Scouts of America or Girl Scouts of the United States.
A person who assesses or recruits others; especially, one who identifies promising talent on behalf of a sports team.
A member of any of various scouting organizations.
A member of one of several army units, such as the Selous Scouts or the Arunachal Scouts.
An act of scouting or reconnoitering.
A person employed to monitor rivals' activities in the petroleum industry.
senses.native: 石油業中受僱監視競爭對手活動的人員

senses.definition: A housekeeper or domestic cleaner, generally female, employed by one of the constituent colleges of Oxford University to clean rooms; generally equivalent to a modern bedder at Cambridge University.
senses.native: 牛津大學各組成學院聘請的女清潔工，負責整理房間；相當於劍橋大學現代床底人（bedder）

senses.definition: A domestic servant, generally male, who would attend (usually several) students in a variety of ways, including cleaning; generally equivalent to a gyp at Cambridge University or a skip at Trinity College, Dublin.
senses.native: 受僱服務學生（通常數名）的男家庭傭人，包括清潔等各種工作；相當於劍橋大學的吉普（gyp）或都柏林三一學院的斯基普（skip）

senses.definition: A fielder in a game for practice.
A fighter aircraft.
A preliminary image that allows the technician to make adjustments before the actual diagnostic images.
senses.native: 讓技術人員在進行實際診斷影像前可作調整的初步影像

senses.definition: A term of address for a man or boy.
A swift sailing boat.
The guillemot.

examples.text: He joined the Algerian Muslim Scouts.
examples.translation: 他加入了阿爾及利亞穆斯林童子軍。

examples.text: She's selling Girl Scout cookies.
examples.translation: 她正在銷售女童子軍餅乾。

examples.text: Have you ever bought cookies from a Girl Scout?
examples.translation: 你曾從女童子軍那裡買過餅乾嗎？

examples.text: Boy Scouts need to do one good deed every day.
examples.translation: 童子軍每天都要完成一件好事。

examples.text: Mary sold Girl Scout cookies in her neighborhood.
examples.translation: 瑪麗在社區內銷售女童子軍餅乾。

examples.text: Scouts can start a fire using only flint and steel.
examples.translation: 童子軍僅使用打火石和鋼刀即可生火。

etymology.text: From Middle English scout, scoult, from Old French escoute (“action of listening”), verbal noun from escouter (“to listen, heed”), from Latin auscultō (“to listen”). The verb comes from the noun.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 scout、scoult，來自舊法式 escoute（聽覺動作），是 escouter（傾聽、heed）的動名詞，而 escouter 又來自拉丁語 auscultō（傾聽）。動詞由名詞演化而來。

senses.definition: Deep mud; moist, spongy earth.
A bog or fen; (in wetland science, specifically) a peatland which is actively forming peat, such as an active bog or fen.
senses.native: 泥沼；（在濕地科學中，特指正在形成泥炭的泥炭地，如活躍的泥沼或沼澤。)

senses.definition: An undesirable situation; a predicament.
An ant.

examples.text: This is what the vox populi reports: he who stirs up the mire brings the mud to the surface.
examples.translation: 這就是民意報導的內容：煽動泥沼者，將泥濘帶至表面。

examples.text: The country is still trying to climb out of the mire left by its previous president.
examples.translation: 該國仍試圖爬出前任總統留下的泥沼。

examples.text: Caught in the mire of poverty.
examples.translation: 陷入貧困的泥沼之中。

examples.text: The dog walked slowly through the deep mire.
examples.translation: 那隻狗緩慢地穿過深處的泥沼。

examples.text: It is very hard to walk on this mire.
examples.translation: 在這片泥沼上行走非常困難。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The farmer drove his tractor carefully through the mire.
examples.translation: 那農民小心地駕駛拖拉機穿過泥沼。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Middle English mire, a borrowing from Old Norse mýrr, from Proto-Germanic *miuzijō, whence also Swedish myr, Norwegian myr, Icelandic mýri, Dutch *mier (in placenames, for example Mierlo). Related to Proto-Germanic *meusą, whence Old English mēos, and Proto-Germanic *musą, whence Old English mos (English moss).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 mire，借自古諾斯語 mýrr，來自原始日耳曼語 *miuzijō，由此也衍生出瑞典語 myr、挪威語 myr、冰島語 mýri 及荷蘭語 *mier（用於地名，例如 Mierlo）。與原始日耳曼語 *meusą 相關，由此產生古英語 mēos；亦與原始日耳曼語 *musą 相關，由此產生古英語 mos（英語中的地衣）。

senses.definition: The ocean, the sea.

examples.text: The briny of the bay was cold.
examples.translation: 海灣的海水很冷。

etymology.text: The adjective is from brine (noun) + -y (suffix forming adjectives with the sense ‘having the quality of’).
etymology.native: 此形容詞源自「brine（海鹽水）」加上表示「具有……性質」的副詞後綴 -y。

senses.definition: An area of or portion of sea away from the shore.
An island, outcrop, or other land away from shore.
Something or someone in, from, or associated with another country.

examples.text: Tom invested in an offshore drilling company.
I spotted a fishing boat about a mile offshore.
An offshore island.

etymology.text: From off- + shore.

senses.definition: Of, causing, or involving unity or union.

examples.text: The unitive force brings all friends together happily.
examples.translation: 統一的力道讓所有朋友快樂地聚在一起。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: This unitive act makes the whole group feel one.
examples.translation: 這個統一的行動讓整個團體感覺像一個人。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: We need a unitive moment to fix our broken team.
examples.translation: 我們需要一個統一的時刻來修復破碎的團隊。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The unitive ceremony united the two families officially.
examples.translation: 這個統一的儀式正式將兩個家庭團結在一起。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Her unitive speech made everyone feel connected and safe.
examples.translation: 她那統一的演說讓每個人感覺連結且安全。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: This unitive project aims to join all schools together.
examples.translation: 這個統一的專案旨在將所有學校結合在一起。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Late Latin unitīvus.
etymology.native: 此詞源於晚拉丁語 unitīvus。

senses.definition: To a great extent or degree.
Conforming to fact, reality or rule; true.
Used to firmly establish that nothing else surpasses in some respect.

examples.text: Nicole can speak Japanese very well.
examples.translation: 尼可日語說得很好。

examples.text: Russian is very difficult to learn.
examples.translation: 俄語非常難學。

examples.text: Toshio can speak English very well.
examples.translation: 敏男能說流利的英語。

examples.text: Seen from space, the earth is very beautiful.
examples.translation: 從太空裡看，地球是個十分美麗的星球。

examples.text: He may be clever, but he is not very helpful.
examples.translation: 他很聰明，但卻不太幫得上忙。

examples.text: I look forward to seeing you again very soon.
examples.translation: 希望早日再見到你。

relations.native: 真空輔助樹脂注射模塑

etymology.text: From Middle English verray, from Old French verai (“true”), from Early Medieval Latin vērāgus, from Classical Latin vērāx, derived from vērus, from Proto-Italic *wēros, from Proto-Indo-European *weh₁ros.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（verray），來自古法語（verai）「真的」，來自早期中世紀拉丁語（vērāgus），再來自古典拉丁語（vērāx），衍生自（vērus）「真實的」，上溯至原始印歐語（*weh₁ros）。

senses.definition: Having the same relationship, each to each other.
Collective, done or held in common.
Reciprocal.
Possessed in common.
Owned by the members.

examples.text: Our love is mutual.
examples.translation: 我們的愛是相互的。

examples.text: We met through a mutual friend.
They discussed mutual benefits.
True friendship is based on mutual trust.
examples.translation: 真正的友誼建立在彼此信任的基礎上。

examples.text: I'm in love, but I don't know if it's mutual.
Tom loves Mary, but the feeling isn't mutual.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French mutuel, from Latin mūtuus. Displaced native Old English ġemǣne.

senses.definition: Bearing full likeness by having precisely the same set of characteristics; indistinguishable.
Not different or other; not another or others; not different as regards self; selfsame; numerically identical.
Of twins, sharing the same genetic code.
Exactly equivalent.
Approximating or approaching exact equivalence.

examples.text: Identical twins have different fingerprints.
Amanda's and Skura's faces were identical.
They're identical other than in colour.
No two words are identical in meaning.
examples.translation: 每一個字的意思都是獨特的。

examples.text: He is identical to his older brother.
examples.translation: 他跟哥哥一模一樣。

examples.text: Your personal computer is identical with mine.

etymology.text: From identic + -al.

senses.definition: simple past and past participle of align
senses.native: 對齊的過去式與過去分詞

examples.text: They aligned themselves with the Liberals.
examples.translation: 他們與自由黨站在一起。

To deflect or turn (something) away from a true, proper or moral course; to pervert; to bias.
senses.native: 使（某事物）偏離正途或正當、道德的路線；扭曲、使偏頗

senses.definition: To go astray or be deflected from a true, proper or moral course; to deviate.
senses.native: 偏離正途或正當、道德的路線；走偏

senses.definition: To arrange strands of thread lengthwise on a loom.
senses.native: 在織機上將經紗排列好（上經）

senses.definition: To move a vessel by hauling on a line or cable that is fastened to an anchor or pier; (especially) to move a sailing ship through a restricted place such as a harbour.
senses.native: 以拉動錨鍊或纜繩將船隻移動，尤指帆船在狹窄水域（如港口）移位（拖船移位）

senses.definition: To move or be moved by this method.
senses.native: 以此方式移動或被移動

senses.definition: To travel or transport across a medium without passing through it normally, as by using a teleporter or time warp.
senses.native: 不經由正常途徑而跨越介質移動或被傳送，如使用傳送器或時間扭曲（瞬移）

senses.definition: To run (yarn) off the reel into hauls to be tarred.
senses.native: （過時）將紗線從線軸抽出，成束準備焦油處理

senses.definition: To plot; to fabricate or weave (a plot or scheme).
senses.native: （比喻，罕用，過時）策劃、編造（陰謀）

senses.definition: To change or fix (make fixed, for example by freezing).
senses.native: （罕用，古，詩）改變或使固定（如凍結）

senses.definition: To fly with a bending or waving motion, like a flock of birds or insects.
senses.native: （如鳥群或昆蟲群）以彎曲或波動的方式飛行（過時）

senses.definition: To bring forth (young) prematurely.
To throw.

examples.text: I think videogames are warping our kids' minds.
examples.translation: 我認為電子遊戲正在扭曲我們孩子的思維。

examples.text: Gift warping might become a thing in the future.
examples.translation: 未來或許會出現「扭曲」成為一種潮流的情況。

examples.text: Store the CDs in a cool, dry place to prevent warping.
examples.translation: 請將光碟存放在陰涼乾燥處，以免變形。

examples.text: Boards will warp unless kept dry.
examples.translation: 若未保持乾燥，板材會發生變形。

examples.text: The tree roots are warping the pavement.
examples.translation: 樹根正在撐裂路面。

examples.text: The wood has warped because of the constant humidity.
examples.translation: 木材因持續的濕氣而變形。

etymology.text: From Middle English warp, werp, from Old English wearp, warp (“a warp, threads stretched lengthwise in a loom, twig, osier”), from Proto-Germanic *warpą (“a warp”).
etymology.native: 此詞源於中古英語的 warp、werp，再追溯至古英語 wearp（指織機上縱向拉伸的經線或柳條），最終來自原始日耳曼語 *warpą。

senses.definition: To fasten (something) using a buckle (noun etymology 1, noun sense 1); hence (obsolete), to fasten (something) in any way.
senses.native: 使用鉤扣將某物緊固；因此（已棄用），以任何方式緊固某物

senses.definition: To apply (oneself) to, or prepare (oneself) for, a task or work; also (obsolete), to equip (oneself) for a battle, expedition, etc.
senses.native: 投入或準備從事任務或工作；也（已棄用），為戰鬥或遠征等裝備自己

senses.definition: To unite (people) in marriage; to marry.
To apply oneself to or prepare for a task or work.
senses.native: 投入或準備從事任務或工作

senses.definition: To unite with someone in marriage; to marry.
To participate in some contest or labour; to join in close fight; to contend.
senses.native: 參與某些競賽或勞動；加入近戰；爭辯

senses.definition: To cause (something) to bend, or to become distorted.
Of a thing (especially a slender structure under compression): to collapse or distort under physical pressure.
Of a person: to (suddenly) cease resisting pressure or stress; to give in or give way, to yield.
To curl (hair).

examples.text: Smoked herring is called buckling.
examples.translation: 煙燻鯖魚稱為 buckling。

examples.text: I forgot to buckle my seatbelt.
examples.translation: 我忘記繫好安全帶了。

examples.text: The roof of the house suddenly buckled.
examples.translation: 屋頂突然崩塌了。

examples.text: The paper buckles if wet media is used on it.
examples.translation: 若使用濕潤的媒體，紙張會皺縮。

examples.text: His knees buckled.
examples.translation: 他的膝蓋軟了。

examples.text: The highway buckled during the heat wave.
examples.translation: 高速公路在熱浪中彎曲變形。

etymology.text: The noun is derived from Middle English bokel (“spiked metal ring for fastening; ornamental clasp; boss of a shield; a shield, buckler; (figurative) means of defence”) [and other forms], from Old French boucle, bocle (“spiked metal ring for fastening; boss of a shield; a shield”) [and other forms], from Latin buccula (“cheek strap of a helmet; boss of a shield”) (from bucca (“soft part of the cheek”)).
etymology.native: 此名詞源於中古英語 bokel，意為「帶尖的金屬環用於緊固；裝飾性鉤扣；盾牌上的凸起；盾牌；（比喻）防禦手段」，來自舊法式 boucle 與 bocle，再源自拉丁語 buccula。

senses.definition: Something that is slightly different from a type or norm.
A different sequence of a gene (locus).
A variable that can hold any of various unrelated data types.
One of a set of words or other linguistic forms that conveys the same meaning or serves the same function.

examples.text: It's an old-fashioned variant.
What features do the different variants have in common?
Ga-ga is a variant of dodgeball.
Paul created a deadlier variant of the virus.
Many of the most concerning variants share the same mutations.
"Does the variant that Tom suggested fit better here?" "I could imagine either one being used."

etymology.text: From Old French variant, from Latin variāns, the present active participle of variō (“to change”). First attested in c. 1380.

senses.definition: Software which has been designed to operate in a malicious, undesirable manner.

examples.text: The site was taken down because it contained malware.
examples.translation: 該網站因含有惡意軟體而被關閉。

examples.text: Don't download files from unknown sources; it could be malware.
examples.translation: 請勿從不明來源下載檔案；它可能是惡意軟體。

examples.text: The Iranian nuclear program has just been attacked by malware.
examples.translation: 伊朗核計劃剛遭惡意軟體攻擊。

examples.text: The files that you are downloading from this website may contain malware.
examples.translation: 您從本網站下載的檔案可能含有惡意軟體。

examples.text: Cyber experts say hundreds of thousands of viruses and malware bombard personal computers every day.
examples.translation: 網路專家表示，每天數百萬種病毒與惡意軟體會襲擊個人電腦。

examples.text: Malware is software designed to disrupt, alter, or destroy logical elements essential to the proper functioning of a computer system.
examples.translation: 惡意軟體是設計用於干擾、修改或破壞電腦系統正常運作所需邏輯元件的軟體。

etymology.text: From mal- + -ware.
etymology.native: 源自 mal- 與 -ware。

senses.definition: Encoded computer instructions, usually modifiable (unless stored in some form of unalterable memory such as ROM).
The human beings involved in warfare, as opposed to hardware such as weapons and vehicles.
Recorded music content, as opposed to the hardware necessary for reproducing it.
Soft goods, such as textiles.

examples.text: You really shouldn't use pirated software.
examples.translation: 你真的不該用盜版軟體。

examples.text: Ubuntu includes lots of software.
Tom is now a software engineer.
examples.translation: 湯姆現在是軟體工程師。

examples.text: I use all kinds of software to study Chinese.
examples.translation: 我用各種各樣的軟體學習中文。

examples.text: I'm having some problems compiling this software.
examples.translation: 我編譯這個程式有些困難。

examples.text: Pierre has a lot of pirated software on his computer.

etymology.text: Computing sense from soft + -ware, by contrast with hardware (“the computer itself”). Coined by John Tukey in 1958. The earlier sense of software to mean tangible products with a soft texture may have fallen out of common usage before the computing sense was created.

senses.definition: A newly sprouted leaf or blossom that has not yet unfolded.
Something that has begun to develop.
A small rounded body in the process of splitting from an organism, which may grow into a genetically identical new organism.
senses.native: 正在從生物體分裂開來的小型圓潤體，可能成長為基因相同的新的生物體

senses.definition: Cannabis that has been taken from the flowering part of the plant intended to be smoked.
senses.native: 從預備抽菸的植物花部摘取的大麻

senses.definition: Marijuana.
A weaned calf in its first year, so called because the horns are then beginning to bud.
senses.native: 斷奶後的第一年小牛，因角開始長芽而得名

senses.definition: Buddy, friend.
Synonym of guy, term of address for a man or person.
A pretty young girl.
Brother.

examples.text: The buds became beautiful red roses.
The buds are just showing.
A rose is sweeter in the bud than full blown.
Algeria needs to nip this problem in the bud.
Taste buds are very useful.
examples.translation: 味蕾很有用。

examples.text: Adriano's steak is a treat for the taste buds.

etymology.text: From Middle English budde, bodde (“bud, seed pod”), from Old English *budde, from Proto-West Germanic *buʀdā, from Proto-Germanic *buzdǭ (compare archaic German Butte (“rosehip”), Swedish dialect bodd (“head”)), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *bʰew-, *bu- (“to swell”). Compare also German Low German Butte, Butt (“bud”), Dutch bot (“bud”), regional German Butz, Butzen (“seed pod; apple core”), German Low German Haagbutt ("rosehip"; Haagbudden (“rosehips”, plural)).

senses.definition: To form buds.
To reproduce by splitting off buds.
To begin to grow, or to issue from a stock in the manner of a bud, as a horn.
senses.native: 開始生長，或像芽一樣從母體發出，如角

senses.definition: To be like a bud in respect to youth and freshness, or growth and promise.
senses.native: 在青春、新鮮度、成長與希望方面像芽一樣

senses.definition: To put forth as a bud.
To graft by inserting a bud under the bark of another tree.

examples.text: Trees put forth new leaves and buds in spring.
The trees are finally starting to bud.
Yeast reproduces by budding.

etymology.text: From Middle English budde, bodde (“bud, seed pod”), from Old English *budde, from Proto-West Germanic *buʀdā, from Proto-Germanic *buzdǭ (compare archaic German Butte (“rosehip”), Swedish dialect bodd (“head”)), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *bʰew-, *bu- (“to swell”). Compare also German Low German Butte, Butt (“bud”), Dutch bot (“bud”), regional German Butz, Butzen (“seed pod; apple core”), German Low German Haagbutt ("rosehip"; Haagbudden (“rosehips”, plural)).

senses.definition: To start, to initiate or take the first step into something.
To come into existence.

examples.text: Class doesn't begin until eight-thirty.
examples.translation: 八點半開始上課。

examples.text: You should begin with easier questions.
examples.translation: 你應該先從最簡單的問題開始。

examples.text: When did you begin studying English?
examples.translation: 你什麼時候開始學英語的？

examples.text: Life begins when we realize who we really are.
examples.translation: 當我們明白真正的自己時，生活開始了。

examples.text: 2001 is the year when the 21st century begins.
examples.translation: 2001年是21世紀的開始。

examples.text: In Japan, the new school year begins in April.
examples.translation: 日本的新學年在四月開始。

etymology.text: From Middle English beginnen, from Old English beginnan (“to begin”), from Proto-West Germanic *biginnan, from Proto-Germanic *biginnaną (“to begin”), from be- + base verb *ginnaną also found in Old English onginnan.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（beginnen），來自古英語（beginnan）「開始」，經原始日耳曼語（*biginnaną），由字首（be-）加基礎動詞（*ginnaną）組成，後者也見於古英語（onginnan）。

senses.definition: An inflamed (raised and colored) spot on the surface of the skin that is usually painful and fills with pus.
An annoying person.
Scotch (whisky)

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: I have a pimple from eating too much chocolate.

senses.definition: A regularly-shaped slab of clay or other material, affixed to cover or decorate a surface, as in a roof-tile, glazed tile, stove tile, carpet tile, etc.
A rectangular graphic.
Any of various flat cuboid playing pieces used in certain games, such as dominoes, Scrabble, or mahjong.
A Lego piece that is 1/3 the height of a brick, and is smooth without studs on top.
A stiff hat.

examples.text: How many tiles do you need?
examples.translation: 你需要多少塊兒磁磚？

examples.text: How many tiles should we buy?
examples.translation: 我們應該買多少塊磚？

examples.text: You cannot cover a house with a single tile.
examples.translation: 單靠一塊磚無法蓋起一棟房子。

examples.text: Nobody can roof a house with a single tile.
examples.translation: 沒有人能只用一塊磚來蓋房頂。

examples.text: The tile that fell from the roof broke into pieces.
examples.translation: 從屋頂掉落的磚塊碎裂成多片。

examples.text: The kitchen was lined with pale yellow tiles.
examples.translation: 廚房裡鋪著淡黃色的磁磚。

etymology.text: From Middle English tile, tyl, tigel, tiȝel, teȝele, from Old English tiġele, tieġle, tiġle (“tile, brick”), from Proto-West Germanic *tigulā (“tile, brick”), from Proto-Germanic *tigulǭ (“tile, brick”), from Latin tēgula, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)teg- (“to cover”). Doublet of tegula.
etymology.native: 「磚」一詞源於中古英語，最終可追溯至拉丁語 tēgula。

senses.definition: To cover with tiles.
To arrange in a regular pattern, with adjoining edges (applied to tile-like objects, graphics, windows in a computer interface).
To optimize (a loop in program code) by means of the tiling technique.
To seal a lodge against intrusions from unauthorised people.
To protect from the intrusion of the uninitiated.

examples.text: The handyman tiled the kitchen.
White marble tiled the bathroom.

etymology.text: From Middle English tile, tyl, tigel, tiȝel, teȝele, from Old English tiġele, tieġle, tiġle (“tile, brick”), from Proto-West Germanic *tigulā (“tile, brick”), from Proto-Germanic *tigulǭ (“tile, brick”), from Latin tēgula, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)teg- (“to cover”). Doublet of tegula.
etymology.native: 「磚」一詞源於中古英語，最終可追溯至拉丁語 tēgula。

senses.definition: The regions beneath the surface of the earth, both natural (eg. caves) and man-made (eg. mines).
Synonym of subway: a railway that is under the ground.
A movement or organization of people who resist political convention.
A movement or organization of people who resist artistic convention.

examples.text: Get on the underground here.
examples.translation: 在這裡搭捷運。

examples.text: The subway runs underground.
examples.translation: 捷運在地下通行。

examples.text: Let's take the underground.
examples.translation: 我們坐捷運去吧。

examples.text: In Britain they call the subway the underground.
Which is quicker, a taxi or the underground?
His house is close to the underground railway.

etymology.text: From Middle English undergrounde (adverb), equivalent to under + ground or under- + ground. Compare Dutch ondergrond, ondergronds, German Untergrund, Danish undergrunds.

senses.definition: To ask questions of; to interrogate; to ask for information.
To raise doubts about; have doubts about.
To ask a question or questions; inquire or seek to know; examine.
To argue; to converse; to dispute.

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: Such questioning is routine police business.
examples.translation: 這樣訊問只是警察例行公事。

etymology.text: From Middle English questioun, from Anglo-Norman questiun, from Old French question, from Latin quaestiōnem, accusative of quaestiō (“a seeking, investigation, inquiry, question”), from quaerere (“to seek, ask, inquire”), of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-Italic *kʷaizeō, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷeh₂- (“to acquire”). Doublet of quest.

senses.definition: Disbelief or uncertainty (about something); (countable) a particular instance of such disbelief or uncertainty.
A point of uncertainty, especially a yes/no or a multiple-choice question
a question (that one has)

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: I cannot forbear expressing my doubts.
examples.translation: 我忍不住要說出我的疑惑。

examples.text: There's no doubt Tom poisoned Mary.
examples.translation: 毋庸置疑，湯姆毒害了瑪麗。

examples.text: I doubt if that would happen.
examples.translation: 我懷疑這是否會發生。

examples.text: There's no doubt about it.
examples.translation: 關於此事毫無疑問。

examples.text: There's no doubt that he likes taking walks.
examples.translation: 他顯然喜歡散步。

examples.text: In a way you're right, but I still have doubts.
examples.translation: 在某種程度上你是對的，但我還是有疑問。

etymology.text: The verb is derived from Middle English douten (“to doubt, fear, worry”) [and other forms], from Old French douter, doter, duter (compare Middle French doubter), from Latin dubitāre (“to be uncertain, doubt; to hesitate, waver in coming to an opinion; to consider, ponder”); the further etymology is uncertain, but one theory is that dubitō may be derived from dubius (“fluctuating, wavering; doubtful, dubious, uncertain”), from duhibius (“held as two”), from duo (“two”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo

senses.definition: A scheme or design.
The terms or conditions proposed.
The document on which such a thing is written.
The act of asking someone to be one's spouse; an offer of marriage.
The offer by a party of what they have in view as to an intended business transaction, which, with acceptance, constitutes a contract.

examples.text: He wouldn't look at my proposal.
examples.translation: 他不會考慮我的建議。

examples.text: Anne accepted Henry's proposal.
examples.translation: 安妮接受了亨利的求婚。

examples.text: He didn't agree to my proposal.
examples.translation: 他不同意我的建議。

examples.text: She turned down every proposal.
examples.translation: 她拒絕了每一項提議。

examples.text: You should've rejected such an unfair proposal.
examples.translation: 你本該拒絕一個那麼不公平的提議。

examples.text: That sounds like a fairly good proposal.
examples.translation: 這方案聽起來不錯。

etymology.text: From propose + -al.

senses.definition: A form containing a list of questions; a means of gathering information for a survey.

examples.text: The questionnaires were distributed randomly.
examples.translation: 問卷表是隨機分發的。

examples.text: Please fill out the following questionnaire.
examples.translation: 請填寫以下問卷表。

examples.text: Let me know when you complete the questionnaire.
examples.translation: 請告知您完成問卷表時。

examples.text: I'll mail this questionnaire as soon as I finish.
examples.translation: 我會在完成後盡快寄出這份問卷表。

examples.text: There are too many questions on this questionnaire.
examples.translation: 這份問卷表的問題太多了。

examples.text: The questionnaire form was distributed properly.
examples.translation: 問卷表表格是正確分發的。

etymology.text: Borrowed from French questionnaire, from Late Latin quaestionarius, from quaestio (English question) + -arius, from quaerō (“to question”) (English query).
etymology.native: 源自法文 questionnaire，來自晚拉丁文 quaestionarius，由 quaestio（英文 question）加上 -arius 構成，源於 quaerō（英文 query）。

senses.definition: To record in documents.
To furnish with documents or papers necessary to establish facts or give information.
senses.native: 提供證明文件，以證實事實或提供資訊

examples.text: We're trying to document all the giraffes of this area.
examples.translation: 我們正在記錄該地區所有的長頸鹿。

examples.text: This research paper is meticulously well documented.
examples.translation: 這篇研究論文記錄得非常詳盡。

examples.text: He documented each step of the process as he did it, which was good when the investigation occurred.
examples.translation: 他在進行時將每個步驟都記錄下來，這在調查發生時很有幫助。

examples.text: A ship should be documented according to the directions of law.
examples.translation: 船隻應依照法律規定進行登記。

examples.text: The parents documented every step of their child's development.
examples.translation: 父母記錄了孩子成長的每一個步驟。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French document, from Latin documentum.

senses.definition: To strengthen; to make firm or resolute.
To administer the sacrament of confirmation on (someone).
To assure the accuracy of previous statements.
To approve a proposal or nomination.

examples.text: The news confirmed my suspicions.
examples.translation: 這一訊息證實了我的懷疑。

examples.text: Confirm the order.
examples.translation: 確認訂單。

examples.text: The teacher confirmed that nothing happened.
Can you confirm that it is a correctable error?
examples.translation: 你確認那是可糾正的錯誤嗎？

examples.text: I want to quickly confirm my flight again.
examples.translation: 我想要再確認一下我的航班。

examples.text: We will confirm your order as follows.
examples.translation: 您的訂單確認如下。

etymology.text: From Middle English confirmen, confermen, from Old French confermer, from Latin cōnfirmāre (“to make firm, strengthen, establish”), from con- (“together”) + firmāre (“to make firm”), from firmus (“firm”).

senses.definition: A firm decision or an official decision.
A strong will; the state of being resolute.
A statement of intent, a vow.
The act of discerning detail.
The degree of fineness with which an image can be recorded or produced, often expressed as the number of pixels per unit of length (typically an inch).
The number of pixels in an image being stored or displayed.
The process of determining the meaning of a symbol or address; the process of executing a link to it.
The act or process of resolving: solving.
An exact sequence of modules (or, objects in the same category as M) either terminating in M or such that M is the homology at degree zero. See Resolution (algebra).
A formal statement adopted by an assembly, or during any other formal meeting.
The separation of the constituent parts (of a spectrum etc).
The degree of fineness of such a separation.
Progression from dissonance to consonance; a chord to which such progression is made.
The moment in which the conflict ends and the outcome of the action is clear.
In a pathological process, the phase during which pathogens and damaged tissues are removed by macrophages.

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: Congress approved the resolution in October.
The UN resolution was never implemented.
Many people make New Year's resolutions.
My resolution dissolved at the last moment.
examples.translation: 到了最後的一刻，我的決心突然動搖了。

examples.text: Did you make any New Year's resolutions?
examples.translation: 你有沒有許下什麼新年願望？

examples.text: I have made a resolution to keep a diary this year.
examples.translation: 這一年我下了決心寫日記。

etymology.text: Recorded since 1412, as Middle English resolucioun (“dissolution”), either from Anglo-Norman resolucion or directly from Latin resolūtiō (“a loosening, solution”), from resolvō (“to loosen”), itself from the intensive prefix re- + solvō (“to loosen”). By surface analysis, recognizably related to resolve and -tion.

senses.definition: A physician; a member of the medical profession; one who is trained and licensed to heal the sick or injured. The final examination and qualification may award a doctor degree in which case the post-nominal letters are DO, DPM, MD, DMD, or DDS in the US, or MBBS or BDS in the UK.

etymology.text: From Middle English whittel (“large knife”), an alteration of thwitel, itself from thwiten (“to whittle”), from Old English þwītan (“to strike down, whittle”), from Proto-Germanic *þwītaną, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *twey- (“to shake, hurl, toss”). Compare Old Norse þveita (“to hurl”), Ancient Greek σείω (seíō, “I shake”). Related to thwite and thwaite.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 whittel（「大刀」），是 thwitel 的變體，來自 thwiten（「削刻」），再源自古英語 þwītan（「擊倒、削刻」），來自原始日耳曼語 *þwītaną，可能來自原始印歐語 *twey-（「搖動、投擲、拋棄」）。比較古諾斯語 þveita（「投擲」）和古希臘語 σείω（seíō，「我搖動」）。與 thwite 和 thwaite 相關。

senses.definition: Covered in frost; frosty.
Translucent, appearing to be covered in frost.
senses.native: 半透明的，看起來像覆蓋著霜

senses.definition: Damaged by frost.
Extremely intoxicated.

examples.text: Frosted tips are making a comeback.
examples.translation: 霜尖正在回歸潮流。

examples.text: A cake was frosted.
examples.translation: 蛋糕被塗上了霜。

examples.text: The sight of frosted trees is simply beautiful.
examples.translation: 看見結霜的樹木簡直美不勝收。

examples.text: Anne peeped out from her frosted gable window with delighted eyes.
examples.translation: 安妮從結霜的山牆窗戶探出頭來，眼中充滿喜悅。

examples.text: They trudged up the frosted hill, every step a testament of their will to live.
examples.translation: 他們艱難地爬上結霜的山坡，每一步都是他們求生意志的見證。

examples.text: Eiswein is made from frosted grapes.

etymology.native: 由霜加上「ed」構成。

senses.definition: Fine, dry particles of matter found in the air and covering the surface of objects, typically consisting of soil lifted up by the wind, pollen, hair, fiber debris, dead skin cells, etc.

senses.definition: Disintegration of a solid, like silica.

senses.definition: The act of cleaning by dusting.

senses.definition: Earth, ground, soil, sediment.

senses.definition: The substance of the human body or mortal frame.

senses.definition: Something worthless.

Rubbish, garbage, refuse.
A cloud of dust.
A tumult, disturbance, commotion, uproar.
A fight or row.
A totally disconnected set of points with a fractal structure.

senses.definition: cash; money (in reference to gold dust).

senses.definition: To remove dust from.
To remove dust; to clean by removing dust.
Of a bird, to cover itself in sand or dry, dusty earth.
To spray or cover (something) with fine powder or liquid, to sprinkle.

senses.definition: Any of various large insects of the order Mantodea that catch insects or other small animals with their powerful forelegs.
A green colour, like that of many mantises.

examples.text: There's a praying mantis in the garden.
examples.translation: 花園裡有隻禿鷹狀螳螂。

examples.text: The female mantis devours the male after copulation.
examples.translation: 雌螳螂交配後會吃掉雄螳螂。

senses.definition: Of or situated on the inside.
Within the body.
Concerned with the domestic affairs of a nation, state or other political community.
Concerned with the non-public affairs of a company or other organisation.
Present or arising within an organism or one of its parts.
Applied or intended for application through the stomach by being swallowed.
Experienced in one's mind; inner rather than expressed.

senses.definition: Being or occurring (farther) inside, situated farther in, located (situated) or happening on the inside of something, situated within or farther within contained within something.

Inside or closer to the inside of the body.

Not obvious, private, not expressed, not apparent, hidden, less apparent, deeper, obscure; innermost or essential; needing to be examined closely or thought about in order to be seen or understood.

Privileged, more or most privileged, more or most influential, intimate, exclusive, more important, more intimate, private, secret, confined to an exclusive group, exclusive to a center; especially a center of influence being near a center especially of influence.

senses.definition: Of or relating to the home.

etymology.text: From Late Middle English fragment, from Latin fragmentum (“a fragment, remnant”), from frangō (“to break”) + -mentum.

senses.definition: A part of a whole, especially a comparatively small part.

A ratio of two numbers (numerator and denominator), usually written one above the other and separated by a horizontal bar called the vinculum or, alternatively, in sequence on the same line and separated by a solidus (diagonal bar).
A component of a mixture, separated by fractionation.
In a eucharistic service, the breaking of the host.
A small amount.
The act of breaking, or state of being broken, especially by violence.
senses.native: 破碎的行為或狀態，尤指暴力所致

examples.text: One half, 1/3, and 1/4 are fractions.

examples.text: Tom earns only a fraction of what Mary earns.

examples.text: Tom did that in only a fraction of a second.

etymology.text: From Middle English fraccioun (“a breaking”), from Anglo-Norman, Old French fraccion, from Medieval Latin fractio (“a fragment, portion”), from earlier Latin fractio (“a breaking, a breaking into pieces”), from fractus, past participle of frangere (“to break”) (whence English frangible), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰreg- (English break). Doublet of frazione.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 fraccioun（「破碎」），來自安格洛 - 諾曼語、古法語 fraccion，再源自中世紀拉丁語 fractio（「碎片、部分」），後來自更早的拉丁語 fractio（「破碎、碎裂成塊」），來自 fractus，frangere 的過去分詞（即英語可碎之 frangible），源於原始印歐語 *bʰreg-（英語 break）。與 frazione 為雙胞胎詞。

senses.definition: Consisting of fragments; disconnected; scattered.

etymology.native: 由 fragment 加上 -ary 組成。

senses.definition: A pause of a specified length in a piece of music.

etymology.text: Partial calque of Dutch ijsberg (compound of ijs (“ice”) + berg (“mountain”)), from Middle Dutch ijsberch. First used to describe a glacier as seen at a distance from a ship then used as a term to describe the floating chunks of ice broken off from such glaciers. Cognate to German Eisberg, Danish isbjerg, Norwegian isberg and Swedish isberg. Figurative senses in reference to the fact that only one-tenth of an iceberg is usually visible above water.
etymology.native: 源自荷蘭語 ijsberg（由 ijs「冰」與 berg「山」組成），初用於描述遠處看到的冰川，後指從冰川斷裂的浮冰塊；與德語 Eisberg、丹麥語 isbjerg 等詞同源。

My conversion to Islam was a wise decision.
His conversion to Islam was a very short process.

etymology.text: From Middle English conversion, conversioun, borrowed from Anglo-Norman conversion, from Latin conversiō, from convertō.

senses.definition: A strip of gauze or similar material used to protect or support a wound or injury.
A strip of cloth bound round the head and eyes as a blindfold.
senses.native: 眼罩布條，綁於頭上遮住雙眼的布

senses.definition: A provisional or makeshift solution that provides insufficient coverage or relief.
senses.native: 權宜之計，臨時拼湊、只能暫時緩解的辦法

examples.text: He cleansed the wound before putting on a bandage.
examples.translation: 他先清洗了傷口，再綁上繃帶。

senses.definition: Items of clothing; apparel.
The covering of a bed; bedclothes.
Laundry (hung on a clothesline).

examples.text: Your classmate's clothes are very pretty.
examples.translation: 你同學的衣服很漂亮。

examples.text: Teenagers often wear strange clothes.
examples.translation: 年輕人常穿怪衣服。

examples.text: Mary started taking her clothes off.
examples.translation: 瑪麗開始脫衣服了。

examples.text: My mother washes clothes every day.
examples.translation: 我媽媽每天洗衣服。

examples.text: I have already changed my clothes.
examples.translation: 我已經換了我的衣服。

examples.text: You are always digging at me about my clothes.
examples.translation: 你總是挖苦我的著裝。

relations.native: 曬衣繩上夾衣服之夾子

etymology.text: From Middle English clothes, cloþes (plural of cloth, cloþ (“cloth, garment”)), from Old English clāþas (“clothes”, plural of clāþ (“cloth”)), equivalent to cloth + -es. Cognate with Scots clathes, claes (“clothes”), Dutch klederen, kleren (“clothes”), German Kleider (“clothes”), Danish klæder (“clothes”), Swedish kläder (“clothes”), Norwegian Bokmål klær (“clothes”), Norwegian Nynorsk klede (“clothes”), Faroese klæði, klæðir (“clothes”).

senses.definition: Frightful, evil, cruel, or monstrous.
Offensive or heinous.
Very bad; abominable, disgusting.

examples.text: This is atrocious weather.
examples.translation: 惡劣的天氣。

examples.text: Yesterday's weather was atrocious.
examples.translation: 昨天的天氣非常糟糕。

examples.text: Lucy's cute, but she's got an atrocious character.
examples.translation: 露西很可愛，但她的性格很差。

examples.text: That's just low and atrocious.
examples.translation: 這簡直又低又差勁。

examples.text: His fake accent is atrocious, even if he can roll his r's.
examples.translation: 他的假口音非常糟糕，即使他能捲舌頭發音。

examples.text: Tom is a wonderful storyteller, but his spelling is atrocious.
examples.translation: 湯姆是個絕佳的說故事者，但他的拼寫很差。

etymology.text: From Latin atrōx (“cruel, fierce, frightful”) + -ious.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 atrōx（殘忍、兇猛、可怕的）加上 -ious 詞尾。

senses.definition: Causing pain or distress, either physical or mental.
Afflicted or suffering with pain (of a body part or, formerly, of a person).
Requiring effort or labor; difficult, laborious.
Very bad, poor.
Painstaking; careful; industrious.

examples.text: Some people live under painful conditions.
Many painful memories inhabited her mind.
The truth can be more painful than a lie.
examples.translation: 真相可能比謊言更令人痛苦。

examples.text: Getting kicked in the groin is painful.
examples.translation: 被踢襠是很痛的。

examples.text: There's nothing more painful than losing one's child.
examples.translation: 沒有比失去孩子更傷心的事。

examples.text: Any task may become painful.
examples.translation: 任何任務都可能變得費力。

etymology.text: From Middle English paynful, peinful, peynful, paynefull, peynefull, equivalent to pain + -ful. Compare Danish pinefuld (“painful”).

senses.definition: Genuinely horrific, awful, or alarming; dangerous, risky.
Unpleasant, awful, very bad (also used as an intensifier).
senses.native: 令人厭惡、糟糕、非常壞（也可用作強調詞）

senses.definition: Awesome, awe-inspiring, causing feelings of reverence.
senses.native: 令人驚嘆、令人敬畏、引發崇敬之情

senses.definition: Scared, afraid, frightened.
Timid, easily frightened.
Reverential, full of pious awe.
senses.native: 虔敬的、充滿聖潔的敬畏

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: I've never heard anything more dreadful.
examples.translation: 我從未聽過如此可怕的事物。

examples.text: This morning the weather is dreadful.
examples.translation: 今天早上天氣非常糟糕。

examples.text: This place is so dreadful.
examples.translation: 這裡太可怕了。

examples.text: The consequences of Sendai's earthquake were dreadful!
examples.translation: 仙台地震的結果很恐怖。

examples.text: A dreadful accident happened on the corner.
examples.translation: 街角發生了一起可怕的意外。

examples.text: Dreadful apparition, why do you trouble me?
examples.translation: 可怕的幻象，為什麼要困擾我？

relations.native: 可怕、令人恐懼的事物或狀態

etymology.text: From Middle English dredful, dredfull, dredeful (also dreful). By surface analysis, dread + -ful.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 dredful 或 dredeful，字面分析為 dread 加上 -ful 詞綴。

senses.definition: Having excelled, having surpassed.
Of higher or the highest quality; splendid.
Exceptionally good of its kind.
Superior in kind or degree, irrespective of moral quality.

examples.text: Sammy Davis was an excellent singer.
examples.translation: 山米戴維斯是一個優秀的歌手。

examples.text: Her father is an excellent pianist.
examples.translation: 她的父親是一位優秀的鋼琴家。

examples.text: Her husband is an excellent cook.
examples.translation: 她丈夫是個優秀的廚師。

examples.text: He's an excellent tennis player.
examples.translation: 他是個很棒的網球選手。

examples.text: Martha is an excellent pianist.
examples.translation: 瑪莎是一位優秀的鋼琴家。

examples.text: I have a good-paying job with excellent hours.
examples.translation: 我有一份工資很高工作時間理想的工作.

etymology.text: From Middle English excellent, from Old French excellent, from Latin excellēns (“elevated, exalted”), present participle of excellō (“elevate, exult”), equivalent to excel + -ent.

senses.definition: The quality of being assertive.

examples.text: Her assertiveness opens doors.
examples.translation: 她的果斷讓她打開了大門。

examples.text: Assertiveness isn't one of Tebboune's strong suits.
examples.translation: 果斷不是 Tebboune 的強項之一。

examples.text: The assertiveness of the man made him win the argument.
examples.translation: 那個人的果斷讓他贏得了辯論。

examples.text: There's a fine line between assertiveness and aggression.
examples.translation: 果斷與侵略性之間有一條細微的界線。

examples.text: Algeria needs to increase its assertiveness in the region.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞需要在該地區加強其果斷性。

examples.text: Algeria needs to increase its assertiveness in foreign politics.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞需要在外交政治上加強其果斷性。

etymology.text: From assertive + -ness.
etymology.native: 源自 assertive 加上後綴 -ness。

senses.definition: A declaration or remark.
A document that summarizes financial activity.
An instruction in a computer program, especially one that returns no value, as opposed to a function call.
A presentation of opinion or position.

examples.text: The statement must introduce new information.
examples.translation: 陳述必須提出新資訊。

examples.text: Statements will be mailed every quarter.
examples.translation: 對帳單每季郵寄一次。

examples.text: Do you believe the witness's statement?
examples.translation: 你相信證人的證詞嗎？

examples.text: She acknowledged that my statement was true.
examples.translation: 她承認我的聲明是真實的。

examples.text: The chairman shall make a statement tomorrow.
examples.translation: 主席明天將發表聲明。

examples.text: I would like to retract my previous statement.
examples.translation: 我想撤回我之前的陳述。

etymology.text: From state + -ment.
etymology.native: 由（state）加（-ment）組成。

senses.definition: A sense of one's own worth; reasonable self-esteem and satisfaction (in oneself, in one's work, one's family, etc).

An unreasonable overestimation of one's own superiority in terms of talents, or looks, wealth, importance, etc., which comes across as being haughty, lofty, and often showing contempt of others; exaggerated self-worth.
Proud or disdainful behavior or treatment that reflects such an attitude (of haughtiness); arrogance.
Something or someone of which one is proud; that which is the source of self-congratulation and self-esteem (whether reasonable or arrogant), for example
Show; ostentation; glory.
Highest level or rank; (figurative) elevation reached; loftiness or glory.
Consciousness of power; fullness of animal spirits; mettle; wantonness.
A group of lions or other large felines or similar animals.

A festival or other event, usually involving a march or parade and organized annually within a city, to celebrate the experiences and identities of LGBTQ people and to promote their interests and rights.
A movement encouraging a positive approach to personal identity amongst LGBTQ people.
The small European lamprey species Petromyzon branchialis.
Lust or heat; sexual desire (especially in a female animal)

examples.text: Humility often achieves more than pride.
examples.translation: 滿招損, 謙受益。

examples.text: What I said hurt his pride.
examples.translation: 我的話傷了他的自尊心。

examples.text: Too much humility is pride.
examples.translation: 過度的謙遜就是驕傲。

examples.text: He takes pride in his work.
examples.translation: 他以他的工作為傲。

examples.text: He is free from pride.
examples.translation: 他絕不高傲。

examples.text: She takes great pride in her appearance.
examples.translation: 她因為自己的美貌而十分高傲。

etymology.text: From Middle English pryde, pride, from Old English prȳde, prȳte (“pride”) (compare Old Norse prýði (“bravery, pomp”)), derivative of Old English prūd (“proud”). More at proud. The verb derives from the noun, at least since the 12th century.

senses.definition: The act, process, or result of any accurate measurement, as of length, volume, weight, intensity, etc.
The act of defining a concept or notion by giving its essential constituents.
The addition of a distinguishing feature to a concept or notion, thus limiting its extent.
The act of determining the relations of an object, such as genus and species; the referring of minerals, plants, or animals, to the species to which they belong; classification
Direction or tendency to a certain end; impulsion.
The quality of mind which reaches definite conclusions; decisive character; resoluteness; fortitude.
The state of decision; a judicial decision, or ending of controversy.
That which is determined upon; result of deliberation; purpose; conclusion formed; fixed resolution.
A flow, rush, or tendency to a particular part
Bringing to an end; termination; limit.

examples.text: We've got to have determination.
examples.translation: 我們要下決心了。

examples.text: He navigates life with quiet determination.
Donald's words filled Jessica with determination.
She works with single-minded determination.
examples.translation: 她一心一意地工作。

examples.text: He made a determination to be a doctor.
examples.translation: 他下定了決心要做醫生。

examples.text: The soul is made up of reason, determination, and passion.
examples.translation: 靈魂是由理性、意志和情慾構成的。

etymology.text: From Middle English determinacion, determynacioun, from Old French determinacion, from Latin dēterminātiō. Morphologically determine + -ation.

senses.definition: A firmly held belief.
A judgement of guilt in a court of law.
The state of being wholly convinced.
The state of being found or proved guilty.

examples.text: Tom appealed his conviction and won.
His words carry little conviction.
Nothing could sway his conviction.
She said all this with complete conviction.
It is hard to live up to your convictions.
There was great conviction in Tom's voice.

etymology.text: From late Middle English conviction, from Anglo-Norman conviction, from Latin convictiō, from convictus, the past participle of convincō (“to convict”). Equivalent to convict + -ion.

senses.definition: The act of asserting; positive declaration or averment.
Something which is asserted; a declaration; a statement asserted.
A statement or declaration which lacks support or evidence.
Maintenance; vindication.
A statement in a program asserting a condition expected to be true at a particular point, used in debugging.
The set of information that the statement preparer is providing in a financial statement audit.

examples.text: This assertion is false.
Tom refuted that assertion with a counterexample.
examples.translation: 湯姆用一個反例反駁了那個說法。

examples.text: It's not a question, but rather an assertion.
That's not a question, that's an assertion.
Can you prove the validity of your assertion?
Nobody will believe his assertion that he is innocent.

etymology.text: From Middle English assercioun, from Latin assertiō. By surface analysis, assert + -ion.

senses.definition: To stock with people or inhabitants; to fill as with people; to populate.
To become populous or populated.
senses.native: 變得人口稠密或被居住

senses.definition: To inhabit; to occupy; to populate.
To interact with people; to socialize.

examples.text: Who hears music feels his solitude peopled at once.

etymology.text: From Middle English puple, peple, peeple, from Anglo-Norman people, from Old French pueple, peuple, pople, from Latin populus (“a people, nation”), from Old Latin populus, from earlier poplus, from even earlier poplos, from Proto-Italic *poplos (“army”) of unknown origin. Doublet of pueblo. Gradually ousted native English lede and, partially, folk.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 puple、peple 或 peeple，來自盎格魯 - 諾曼人的 people，再源自舊法語的 pueple、peuple 等，最終來自拉丁語 populus（「人民、民族」），其詞源可追溯至更早的拉丁語 poplus 及原始義大利語 *poplos（意為「軍隊」），具體起源不明。它與 pueblo 同源，逐漸取代了本土英語中的 lede 和 folk。

senses.definition: A great amount or number, often of people; abundance, myriad, profusion.
The mass of ordinary people; the masses, the populace.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Riches cover a multitude of woes.
examples.translation: 財富能掩蓋許多災禍。

examples.text: They are faced with a multitude of stresses.
examples.translation: 他們面臨著眾多壓力。

examples.text: It is the love that covers a multitude of sins.
examples.translation: 愛能寬恕眾多的罪過。

examples.text: There's a multitude of hotels in tourist areas.
examples.translation: 旅遊區有大量的飯店。

examples.text: Charity creates a multitude of sins.
examples.translation: 慈善會製造出許多罪惡。

examples.text: So lightly do the multitude take the search for truth.
examples.translation: 大眾對追求真理輕視之極。

etymology.text: From Middle English multitude, multitud, multytude (“(great) amount or number of people or things; multitudinous”), borrowed from Old French multitude (“crowd of people; diversity, wide range”), or directly from its etymon Latin multitūdō (“great amount or number of people or things”), from multus (“many; much”) + -tūdō (suffix forming abstract nouns indicating a state or condition). The English word is analysable as multi- + -itude.
etymology.native: 此詞源於中世紀英語，借自古法語或拉丁語，由「多」與表示狀態的後綴組成。

senses.definition: A farm owned by a collection of people.
One of more farms managed and owned, through the state, by the community.
A collective noun or name.
A group dedicated to a particular cause or interest.
The flight control used to control a helicopter's ascent or descent.

examples.text: Algeria had collective farms.
In the 1970s, Algeria had collective farms.
There are many pigs on our collective farm.
We're starting a collective to resist landlords.
Are you part of an artist collective?
He is making use of the collective's name for his own profit.
examples.translation: 他在利用集體的名義，為自己謀利。

etymology.text: From Middle French collectif, from Latin collēctīvus, from collēctus, past participle of colligō (“to collect”), from com- (“together”) + legō (“to gather”). Compare French collectif. Doublet of colectivo.

senses.definition: People, persons.
One’s relatives, especially one’s parents.
A people; a tribe or nation; the inhabitants of a region, especially the native inhabitants.

examples.text: What's your favorite Australian folk song?
Good morning, folks. How's everyone doing?
We have to sing at an old folks home today.
examples.translation: 我們今天得去養老院唱歌。

examples.text: My folks used to tell me stories about that.
Those folks are insane!
examples.translation: 那些人瘋了！

examples.text: I listened to it from the old folks in the past.

etymology.text: From Middle English folk, from Old English folc, from Proto-West Germanic *folk, from Proto-Germanic *fulką, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₁-gós, from *pleh₁- (“to fill”).

senses.definition: To supply with inhabitants; to people.
To live in; to inhabit.
To increase in number; to breed.
To fill initially empty items in a collection.
To fill initially empty slots or sockets on a circuit board or similar.

examples.text: Algiers is Algeria's most populated city.
examples.translation: 阿爾及爾是阿爾及利亞人口最多的城市。

examples.text: Algiers is a very populated city.
examples.translation: 阿爾及爾是一座人口稠密的城市。

examples.text: When were the Americas populated?
examples.translation: 美洲何時有人類居住？

examples.text: The Algerian south is very sparsely populated.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞南部人口非常稀疏。

examples.text: The most populated city of Europe is Istanbul.
examples.translation: 歐洲人口最多的城市是伊斯坦堡。

examples.text: Are you from a planet solely populated by women?
examples.translation: 你是來自僅由女性居住的星球嗎？

etymology.text: Borrowed from Medieval Latin populātus, past participle of populor (“populate”), from Latin populus (“people”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀拉丁語 populātus，為 populus（人民）的分詞。

senses.definition: A person who is popular, especially at a school.
An inexpensive newspaper with wide circulation.
A member of the Populares
A member of any political party with "Popular" in the title, such as the Partido Popular in Spain or Popolari di Italia Domani in Italy
senses.native: （名稱中有「人民」的政黨，如西班牙人民黨）黨員

examples.text: Soccer is the most popular of all sports.
examples.translation: 足球是所有體育運動中最受歡迎的。

examples.text: He is by nature a kind person and is popular with the children in his neighborhood.
examples.translation: 他天生就是一個和藹可親的人，所以很受住在附近的孩子歡迎。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English populer, borrowed from Old French populaire, or borrowed from Latin populāris.
etymology.native: 承襲自中古英語（populer），借自古法語（populaire）或拉丁語（populāris）。

senses.definition: The people living within a political or geographical boundary.
A count of the number of residents within a political or geographical boundary such as a town, a nation or the world.
A collection of organisms of a particular species, sharing a particular characteristic of interest, most often that of living in a given area.
A group of units (persons, objects, or other items) enumerated in a census or from which a sample is drawn.
The people with a given characteristic.
The number of living cells in a pattern.
The act of filling initially empty items in a collection.
General population.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: We debated on the question of world population.
examples.translation: 我們在世界人口問題上爭辯了一番。

examples.text: The world's population tends to increase.
examples.translation: 世界人口有上升的趨勢。

examples.text: World population has rapidly increased.
examples.translation: 世界人口急劇增長。

examples.text: More than a third of the world population lives near a coast.
examples.translation: 全世界有超過三分之一的人在沿岸地區居住。

examples.text: We must not ignore populations suffering under misgovernment.
examples.translation: 我們不能忽視暴政之下飽受苦難的人民。

examples.text: All oil-rich countries should be invaded and annihilated by US forces to protect their civilian populations and teach them democracy.
examples.translation: 所有石油資源豐富的國家都應該被美國軍隊入侵並摧毀，以保護那裡的平民並向他們傳授民主。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Late Latin populatio (“a people, multitude”), as if a noun of action from Classical Latin populus, equivalent to populate + -ion. Doublet of poblacion.
etymology.native: 借自晚期拉丁語（populatio）「人民、群眾」，彷彿是古典拉丁語（populus）的動作名詞，相當於（populate）加（-ion）。與（poblacion）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: A demographic criterion: a characteristic used to classify people for statistical purposes, such as age, race, or gender.
A demographic group: a collection of people sharing a value for a certain demographic criterion.
An individual person's characteristic, encoded for the purposes of statistical analysis.

examples.text: The country's demographics are changing.
Does Algeria have the same demographics as Turkey?
I'm not a big fan of this show, but I know I'm not the target demographic.

etymology.text: From demography + -ic.

senses.definition: To survey using questionnaires.

examples.text: Please fill out this 7-question questionnaire.

etymology.text: Borrowed from French questionnaire, from Late Latin quaestionarius, from quaestio (English question) + -arius, from quaerō (“to question”) (English query).
etymology.native: 源自法文 questionnaire，來自晚拉丁文 quaestionarius，由 quaestio（英文 question）加上 -arius 構成，源於 quaerō（英文 query）。

senses.definition: Critical assessment of a process or activity or of their results.
The part of an output signal that is looped back into the input to control or modify a system.
The high-pitched howling noise heard when there is a loop between a microphone and a speaker.

examples.text: Give constructive feedback to your colleagues.
Please give me constructive feedback.
Give feedback on this Facebook post.
The company welcomes feedback from consumers who use their products.
examples.translation: 公司歡迎消費者對他們產品的反饋

examples.text: What kind of feedback have you gotten so far?
Thank you for your feedback on the situation.

etymology.text: From feed + back.

senses.definition: A sheet of paper or computerized document on which problems are worked out or solved and the answers are recorded.
A sheet of paper listing work that is completed, to be completed or in progress.

examples.text: He handed out worksheets to the students.
The reward for finishing your worksheet early is another worksheet.
You can format and customize a worksheet, and insert and use tables, charts, formulas and functions.
Sami and Layla did their worksheets.
Yanni referred to those worksheets.
Sami was doing some worksheets.

etymology.text: From work + sheet. First use appears c. 1823 in the publications of Isaac D'Israeli.

senses.definition: The act or process of developing an opinion of value.
A judgment or assessment of the value of something, especially a formal one.

examples.text: Our quarterly results will serve as the best appraisal of our approach.
The World Bank has begun appraisal of Laos’ controversial Nam Theun II hydroelectric project.
Tom generally makes good decisions based on a realistic appraisal of the situation he's faced with.

etymology.text: From appraise + -al.

senses.definition: To make (an animal or person) unconscious or cause (an animal or person) to die by preventing breathing; to smother, to suffocate.
senses.native: 使（動物或人）失去意識，或因阻止呼吸而致其死亡；悶死、窒息

senses.definition: To cause (someone) difficulty in breathing, or a choking or gagging feeling.
senses.native: 使人呼吸困難，或感到噎住、乾嘔的感覺

senses.definition: To prevent (a breath, cough, or cry, or the voice, etc.) from being released from the throat.
senses.native: 阻止（呼吸、咳嗽、哭聲，或聲音等）從喉嚨發出

senses.definition: To make (something) unable to be heard by blocking it with some medium.
senses.native: 用某種媒介阻擋，使（某物）無法被聽見

senses.definition: To keep in, hold back, or repress (something).
To prevent (something) from being revealed; to conceal, to hide, to suppress.
senses.native: 阻止（某事）被揭露；隱藏、掩蓋、壓制

senses.definition: To treat (a silkworm cocoon) with steam as part of the process of silk production.
senses.native: 將（蠶繭）蒸氣處理，作為製絲過程之一環

senses.definition: To die of suffocation.
To smother; to make breathing difficult.
To cause (a dog, horse, or other four-legged mammal) to dislocate or sprain its stifle joint.

examples.text: Tom stifled a laugh.
It's stifling hot today. There's no wind at all.
Wokeism is making the world too stifling.

The French term derives ultimately from Latin Latin habēre (“to have, hold”).

etymology.text: Figurative use of Moghul, which originally meant Mongol, or person of Mongolian descent. In this context, it refers to the Mughal Empire (Mughal being Persian or Arabic for "Mongol") of the Indian subcontinent that existed between 1526 and 1857: the early Mughal emperors claimed a heritage dating back to the Mongol ruler Genghis Khan. The modern meaning of the word is supposedly derived from the storied riches of the Mughal emperors, which, for example, produced the Taj Mahal.
etymology.native: Moghul 的比喻用法，原指蒙古人或蒙古裔人士；在此語境中，它指的是印度次大陸上存在的莫臥兒帝國（莫臥兒為波斯或阿拉伯語中的「蒙古」），該帝國存在於 1526 年至 1857 年間：早期莫臥兒皇帝聲稱其血統可追溯至蒙古統治者成吉思汗。現代詞義據說源自莫臥兒皇帝的傳奇財富，例如他們建造了泰姬瑪哈陵。

senses.definition: Fraught with danger.

senses.definition: Of doubtful or uncertain efficacy, provenance, etc.; dodgy.

examples.text: It got pretty dicey weaving in and out of traffic.

senses.definition: A cone-shaped marker, generally made out of plastic or rubber, that is placed on roads or footpaths to temporarily redirect traffic in a safe manner.

examples.translation: 他努力用功，並在人生道路上取得了進展。

senses.definition: To exert for the sake of training or improvement; to practice in order to develop.

To occupy the attention and effort of; to task; to tax, especially in a painful or vexatious manner; harass; to vex; to worry or make anxious.

senses.definition: To perform a work or labour; to exert power or strength, physical or mechanical; to act.

senses.native: 產生適當的物理效果；發出自然設計的結果；特別是在醫學上，對人體系統產生適當的效果

senses.definition: To act or produce an effect on the mind; to exert moral power or influence.

senses.definition: To put into, or to continue in, operation or activity; to work.

senses.definition: To engross or hold the attention of; to keep busy or occupied.

To enter into conflict with (an enemy).
To enter into battle.
To arrange to employ or use (a worker, a space, etc.).
To guarantee or promise (to do something).

etymology.text: From Middle English engagen, from Old French engagier (“to pledge, engage”), from Old French en- (“in, under”) + gage (“pledge”), from Frankish *wadi (“pledge”), from Proto-Germanic *wadją (“pledge, guarantee”), from Proto-Indo-European *wedʰ- (“to pledge, redeem a pledge; guarantee, bail”), equivalent to en- + gage. Cognate with Old English weddian (“to engage, covenant, undertake”), German wetten (“to bet, wager”), Icelandic veðja (“to wager”). More at wed.

senses.definition: To apply, enforce, or establish (something, often regarded as burdensome as a restriction or tax: see verb sense 1.2.2) with authority.

To place or put (something chiefly immaterial, especially something regarded as burdensome as a duty, an encumbrance, a penalty, etc.) on another thing or on someone; to inflict, to repose; also, to place or put (on someone a chiefly immaterial thing, especially something regarded as burdensome).
To force or put (a thing) on someone or something by deceit or stealth; to foist, to obtrude.

To affect authoritatively or forcefully; to influence strongly.

To practise deceit or stealth; to cheat, to deceive, to trick.
To physically lay or place (something) on another thing; to deposit, to put, to set.

To lay (columns or pages of type, or printing plates) arranged in a proper order on the bed of a press or an imposing stone and secure them in a chase in preparation for printing.
To appoint (someone) to be in authority or command over other people.
To accuse someone of (a crime, or a sin or other wrongdoing); to charge, to impute.
To put (a conclusion or end) to something definitively.
To subject to an impost, levy, tax, etc.
