examples.text: New York bristles with towering buildings.
examples.translation: 紐約充滿著高樓大廈。

examples.text: You can't equate nationalism with fascism.
examples.translation: 你不能將民族主義與法西斯混為一談。

examples.text: We furnished the refugees with blankets.
examples.translation: 我們提供了難民們毛毯。

examples.text: Ming wasn't dancing with Masao then.
examples.translation: 那時明沒有在和正雄跳舞。

examples.text: Did you fall in love with her at first sight?
examples.translation: 你對她是不是一見鍾情？

etymology.text: From Middle English with, from Old English wiþ (“against, opposite, toward, with”), from Proto-West Germanic *wiþi, a shortened form of Proto-Germanic *wiþrą (“against”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（with），來自古英語（wiþ）「對抗、相對、朝向、和」，是原始日耳曼語（*wiþrą）「對抗」的縮短形式。

senses.definition: Side by side with.
Together with or at the same time.

examples.text: Daniel worked out alongside Amanda.
The boat was alongside the quay.
The son is alongside the father.
The two houses stand alongside of each other.
The star of the band played alongside Adriano.
Houses were lined up alongside the highway.

etymology.text: From along + side; compare alongsides.

senses.definition: Of a person or thing: in the midst of and surrounded by (other people or things).
Associated with or living alongside (other people or things).
senses.native: 與（其他人或物）在一起；生活在……之中

senses.definition: Belonging to (a group comprising similar people or things).
Distinct in some way from (other members of a group); specifically, superior or pre-eminent compared to (other members of a group).
senses.native: 在（群體中）與眾不同；出類拔萃

senses.definition: Originally, in the course of; during; now, in the circumstances or context of.
Distributed or divided between (members of a group).
Done jointly by (two or more people).
senses.native: 由（兩人或多人）共同完成

senses.definition: In the general custom or opinion of (members of a group).
senses.native: 在（某群體）的普遍習俗或看法中

senses.definition: Occurring between (members of a group) or within (a group).
senses.native: 在（群體成員）之間；在（群體）內部

examples.text: Bees are flying among the flowers.
examples.translation: 蜜蜂在花叢中飛行。

examples.text: Choose any one from among these.
examples.translation: 從這些裡選一個。

examples.text: He is included among my friends.
examples.translation: 他是我的朋友之一。

examples.text: It's among the highest mountains in the Alps.
examples.translation: 這是阿爾卑斯山脈最高的山峰之一。

examples.text: This movie is very popular among young people.
examples.translation: 這部電影在年輕人之間很流行。

examples.text: London is among the world's largest cities.
examples.translation: 倫敦是全世界最大的城市之一。

etymology.text: The preposition is derived from Middle English among, amang, amange, amonge (“in the presence of, amid, among; in, within; between; during”), from Old English amang, onġemang (preposition), from on (“on, among, in”) (probably ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂en- (“on, onto”)) + ġemang (“crowd; mixture”, noun) (from ġe- (prefix forming nouns denoting association or similarity) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱóm (“beside, by; near; with”)) + mang- (from mængan, mengan (“to mingle, mix
etymology.native: 介系詞源自中古英語（among、amang）「在……之中；在……期間」，來自古英語（amang、onġemang），由（on）「在……上、在……之中」加（ġemang）「人群；混合」組成。

senses.definition: Denotes a mingling or intermixing with distinct or separable objects. See usage note at amidst.

examples.text: He's the tallest amongst the boys.
examples.translation: 他算是男孩子中最高的了。

examples.text: Mary was chosen amongst 500 applicants.
Beautiful things grow amongst thorns.
He is the youngest amongst us four.
examples.translation: 他是我們四人中間最年輕的。

examples.text: Who amongst them do you think is the coolest?
Truth springs from argument amongst friends.

etymology.text: From amongs + -t (excrescent), from among + -s (genitive). By surface analysis, among + -st (excrescent). Root among from Old English ongemang, from on (“in”) + gemang (“assemblage, mingling”).

senses.definition: The (thing) here (used in indicating something or someone nearby).
The known (thing) (used in indicating something or someone just mentioned).
Referring to oneself.
The known (thing) (used in indicating something or someone about to be mentioned).
A known (thing) (used in first mentioning a person or thing that the speaker does not think is known to the audience). Compare with “a certain ...”.
Designates the current or next instance.
senses.native: 指現在或下一個：這個；本

examples.text: "This looks pretty interesting," Hiroshi says.
examples.translation: 「這看起來挺有趣的。」浩說。

examples.text: Brian studied English for this trip.
examples.translation: 布萊恩為了這次旅行學英語。

examples.text: Mrs. Hughes, this is Peter Brown.
examples.translation: 休斯女士，我是彼得布朗。

examples.text: Nancy cannot have read this book.
examples.translation: 南西不可能讀過這本書。

examples.text: It was yesterday that Jake broke this window.
The boat is to leave for England this evening.
examples.translation: 這艘船會在傍晚出發去英國。

etymology.text: From Middle English þis, this, from Old English þis (neuter demonstrative), from the North Sea Germanic base *þa- (“that”), from Proto-Germanic *þat, from Proto-Indo-European *tód, extended form of demonstrative base *to-; + North-West Germanic definitive suffix *-s, from Proto-Indo-European *só (“this, that”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（þis、this），來自古英語中性指示詞（þis），由指示詞基（*þa-）「那」加限定後綴構成，上溯至原始印歐語（*tód）。

senses.definition: The thing, item, etc. being indicated.

examples.text: This is strange.
examples.translation: 奇怪。

etymology.text: From Middle English þis, this, from Old English þis (neuter demonstrative), from the North Sea Germanic base *þa- (“that”), from Proto-Germanic *þat, from Proto-Indo-European *tód, extended form of demonstrative base *to-; + North-West Germanic definitive suffix *-s, from Proto-Indo-European *só (“this, that”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（þis、this），來自古英語中性指示詞（þis），由指示詞基（*þa-）「那」加限定後綴構成，上溯至原始印歐語（*tód）。

senses.definition: The female (typically) person or animal previously mentioned or implied.
A ship or boat.
The Catholic Church.
A country, or sometimes a city, province, planet, etc.
A thing, especially a machine or other object, such as a car, a computer, or (poetically) a season.
A person whose gender is unknown or irrelevant (used in a work, along with or in place of he, as an indefinite pronoun).
senses.native: （性別不明或無關的人）她；他或她

examples.text: To all appearances, she is healthy.
examples.translation: 無論從哪方面看，她很健康。

examples.text: Jane didn't play tennis, did she?
examples.translation: 珍沒打網球，是嗎？

examples.text: She's selling drugs at concerts.
examples.translation: 她在演唱會的場地販賣毒品。

examples.text: More often than not, she had to go in person.
examples.translation: 很多時候她要親自去。

examples.text: She lives a block away and her name is Susan.
examples.translation: 她住在一個街區之外，名叫蘇珊。

examples.text: After she had lunch, she got ready to go out.
examples.translation: 吃過午飯後，她準備好要出門了。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English sche, scho, hyo, ȝho (“she”), whence also Yorkshire dialectal shoo (“she”), Scots she, sho (“she”).
etymology.native: 承襲自中古英語（sche、scho）「她」；約克郡方言與蘇格蘭語的「她」也源自此。

senses.definition: Though, however.
Merely, only, just, no more than.
Used to repeat an adverb for emphasis; simply; just; absolutely.
senses.native: 用於重複副詞以加強語氣；簡直；完全

examples.text: I want a car, but I have no money to buy one.
examples.translation: 我想要一輛車，但我沒錢買。

examples.text: Labor is not merely a necessity but a pleasure.
examples.translation: 勞動不僅是一種需要，而還是一種愉快。

examples.text: We need not only adequate water but clean water.
examples.translation: 我們不僅需要充足的水，還需要乾淨的水。

examples.text: I accept, but only under one condition.
Benedito laughed as his billy goat playfully butted its head against his leg.
examples.translation: Benedito 笑著看著他的比利山羊玩耍時用頭撞他的腿。

examples.text: He butted his head against the wall yesterday.
examples.translation: 他昨天把頭撞在牆上。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Middle English but, buten, boute, bouten, from Old English būtan (“without, outside of, except, only”), from Proto-West Germanic *biūtan, *biūtini, equivalent to be- + out. Cognate with Scots but, bot (“outside, without, but”), Saterland Frisian buute (“without”), West Frisian bûten (“outside of, apart from, other than, except, but”), Dutch buiten (“outside”), Dutch Low Saxon buten (“outside”), German Low German buuten, buute (“outside”), obsolete German baußen (“outside”), Luxembourgish ba
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（buten），來自古英語（būtan）「沒有、在外面、除了、只」，由「在旁」加「外面」構成。與荷蘭語（buiten）「外面」同源。

senses.definition: However, although, nevertheless, on the other hand (introducing a clause contrary to prior belief or in contrast with the preceding clause or sentence).
On the contrary, rather (as a regular adversative conjunction, introducing a word or clause in contrast or contradiction with the preceding negative clause or sentence).

Except that (introducing a subordinate clause which qualifies a negative statement); also, (archaic) with omission of the subject of the subordinate clause, acting as a negative relative, "except one that", "except such that".
Used at the beginning of a sentence to express opposition to a remark.
Used to link an interjection to the following remark as an intensifier.
Without it also being the case that; unless that (introducing a necessary concomitant).
Except with; unless with; without.
Only; solely; merely.
Until.
That.

examples.text: He lives for nothing but pleasure.
examples.translation: 他生活除了享樂之外沒別的了。

examples.text: They are not enemies, but friends.
examples.translation: 她們不是敵人，而是朋友。

examples.text: Sure, but let's eat dinner first.
examples.translation: 好的，但我們先吃晚飯吧。

examples.text: I'll give you anything but this.
examples.translation: 除了這個之外我會給你任何東西。

examples.text: He does nothing but read comics.
examples.translation: 他什麼都不做只是看漫畫。

examples.text: Lisa speaks not only English but also French.
examples.translation: 麗薩不但會說英文，而且會說法文。

etymology.text: From Middle English but, buten, boute, bouten, from Old English būtan (“without, outside of, except, only”), from Proto-West Germanic *biūtan, *biūtini, equivalent to be- + out. Cognate with Scots but, bot (“outside, without, but”), Saterland Frisian buute (“without”), West Frisian bûten (“outside of, apart from, other than, except, but”), Dutch buiten (“outside”), Dutch Low Saxon buten (“outside”), German Low German buuten, buute (“outside”), obsolete German baußen (“outside”), Luxembourgish ba
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（buten），來自古英語（būtan）「沒有、在外面、除了、只」，由「在旁」加「外面」構成。與荷蘭語（buiten）「外面」同源。

senses.definition: Without any other reason etc.; only, just, and nothing more.
Wholly, entirely.

examples.text: Igor and Anna were merely kissing.
You're merely Arabized Berbers.
I was merely stating the facts.
Don't look down on him merely because he is poor.
examples.translation: 不要因為他窮就看不起他。

examples.text: He said it merely as a joke.
examples.translation: 他這麼說就是為了開玩笑。

examples.text: We are merely creatures of our master's will.

etymology.text: From Middle English mereli, equivalent to mere + -ly.

senses.definition: During the time that something is happening, often specifically in a different place.
During an intervening time; from now until a future time.
In contrast to aspects previously mentioned.

examples.text: Meanwhile, conditions have drastically altered.
examples.translation: 在這期間，情況發生了巨大變化。

examples.text: Meanwhile, Mary is laying the table.
Meanwhile, Jiang Qin distracted Jiang Feng's older brother Yan Daxia.
examples.translation: 與此同時江琴分散了江楓的哥哥燕大俠的注意力。

examples.text: Meanwhile you are out and about with her!
Meanwhile, you should get a little sleep.
Meanwhile, the foolish uncle was sitting in the living room.

etymology.text: From Middle English menewhile, equivalent to mean (“intermediate”) + while. Adverb is by ellipsis from in the mean while, noun being conventionally written as one word after the adjective.

senses.definition: To such an extent or degree; to the same extent or degree.
Considered to be, in relation to something else; in the relation (specified).
Used to intensify an adjective; very much; extremely.
to the same degree (often followed by ‘as’)
For example; for instance. (Compare such as.)

examples.text: Few things give us as much pleasure as music.
examples.translation: 很少有東西像音樂一樣帶給我們這麼多的快樂。

etymology.text: From Middle English as, als(a), alswa, from Old English eallswā (“just so; as”), thus representing a reduced form of also. Compare German Low German a(l)s, German als, Dutch als.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（as、alswa），來自古英語（eallswā）「正是如此、如同」，是（also）的弱化形式。比較德語（als）、荷蘭語（als）。

senses.definition: In the (same) way or manner that; to the (same) degree that.
Used after so or as to introduce a comparison.
senses.native: 用在「如此」（so、as）之後引出比較：像……一樣

senses.definition: Used to introduce a result: with the result that it is; as to.
Expressing concession: though.
At the same instant or moment that: when.
At the same time that, during the same time when: while.
Varying through time in the same proportion that.
Being that, considering that, because, since.
used before a preposition to clarify that the prepositional phrase restricts the meaning of the sentence; specifically.
senses.native: 用在介系詞前，限定句子的意思：具體來說

senses.definition: Functioning as a relative conjunction, and sometimes like a relative pronoun: that, which, who. (See usage notes.)
senses.native: 作關係連接詞或關係代名詞用（方言）

senses.definition: Introducing a comparison with a hypothetical state (+ subjunctive, or with the verb elided): as though, as if.
Than.

examples.text: My real address is as follows.
examples.translation: 我的真實地址如下。

examples.text: He can speak Russian as well.
examples.translation: 他還會說俄語。

examples.text: Is Germany as cold as Canada?
examples.translation: 德國有加拿大冷嗎？

examples.text: Are you from Kashgar as well?
examples.translation: 您也是喀什人嗎？

examples.text: Tom can speak French as well.
examples.translation: 湯姆也說法文。

examples.text: They regarded him as the best doctor in town.
examples.translation: 他們把他視為城裡最好的醫生。

etymology.text: From Middle English as, als(a), alswa, from Old English eallswā (“just so; as”), thus representing a reduced form of also. Compare German Low German a(l)s, German als, Dutch als.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（as、alswa），來自古英語（eallswā）「正是如此、如同」，是（also）的弱化形式。比較德語（als）、荷蘭語（als）。

senses.definition: Introducing a basis of comparison, with an object in the objective case.
In the role of.
In the form of.

examples.text: Stop seeing me as a "normal" person!
examples.translation: 不要再把我當成「正常」人！

etymology.text: From Middle English as, als(a), alswa, from Old English eallswā (“just so; as”), thus representing a reduced form of also. Compare German Low German a(l)s, German als, Dutch als.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（as、alswa），來自古英語（eallswā）「正是如此、如同」，是（also）的弱化形式。比較德語（als）、荷蘭語（als）。

senses.definition: In an equal manner; in equal shares or proportion; with equal and impartial justice; evenly
In equal degree or extent; just as.
Used to link two or more coordinate elements

examples.text: Men and women are equally important.
Men and women drive equally poorly.
Tom and Mary looked equally happy.
Are both English versions equally acceptable?
The two groups share equally in the company.
Mirabelles are equally delicious in a compote.

etymology.text: From equal + -ly.

senses.definition: Although, despite (it) being.

examples.text: Igor looked like his normal self, albeit traumatized a bit.
She is reasonable, albeit strict.
Shemini Atzeret is also observed by Samaritans and Karaites, albeit on different days.
Tom hopes to make a profit this year, albeit a small one.
Have you ever eaten javelina? It's quite good, albeit somewhat gamey.
She says her organization, albeit a non-profit, has an economic impact that should be acknowledged.

morphemes.native: 非他也非她者；生物；被非人化的存在

etymology.text: From the Middle English expression al be it (that), itself shortened from althagh it be that (“although it be that”), and thus composed from al (“completely, entirely”, literally “all”) + be (3rd person singular present subjunctive of been (“to be”)) + it.

senses.definition: In, near, or in the general vicinity of (a particular place).
Indicating distance or direction relative to the speaker.
Attending (an educational institution).
Working for (a company) or in (a place or situation).
senses.native: 在（某公司）工作；在（某處或情況）

senses.definition: Present or taking place during (an event).
Indicating time of occurrence, especially an instant of time, or a period of time relatively short in context or from the speaker’s perspective.
senses.native: 表示發生的時間（尤指某一時刻）：在

senses.definition: (also as at; before dates) On (a particular date).
In the direction of; towards; (often implied to be in a hostile or careless manner).
senses.native: 朝向；對著（常帶敵意或漫不經心）

senses.definition: Indicating action bearing upon something, especially continued or repeated action.
senses.native: 表示對某事持續或反覆的動作

senses.definition: In response or reaction to.
Occupied in (activity).
In a state of.
Subject to.
Denotes a price.
Indicates a position on a scale or in a series.
senses.native: 表示位置或順序中的某一點

senses.definition: In certain phrases, used to indicate the manner in which something happens or is done.
senses.native: 用於表示事情發生的方式或做法

senses.definition: Indicates a specific speed or rate that is maintained by something.
senses.native: 表示維持的特定速度或速率

senses.definition: Indicates a means or method.
On the subject of; regarding.
Bothering, irritating, causing discomfort to.
senses.native: 令人困擾、煩躁或造成不適

examples.text: The airplane landed at Narita Airport.
examples.translation: 飛機在成田機場著陸。

examples.text: Please enjoy yourself at the dance.
examples.translation: 請盡情地跳舞。

examples.text: The fire was extinguished at once.
examples.translation: 火馬上就被撲熄了。

examples.text: I'm staying at the Sheraton Hotel.
examples.translation: 我住在喜來登飯店。

examples.text: There is the train at 10 o'clock.
examples.translation: 十點鐘有一班火車。

examples.text: Did you fall in love with her at first sight?
examples.translation: 你對她是不是一見鍾情？

etymology.text: From Middle English at, from Old English æt (“at, near, by, toward”), from Proto-West Germanic *at, from Proto-Germanic *at (“at, near, to”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éd (“near, at”). Cognate with Scots at (“at”), North Frisian äät, äit, et, it (“at”), Danish at (“to”), Swedish åt (“for, toward”), Norwegian åt (“to”), Faroese at (“at, to, toward”), Icelandic að (“to, towards”), Gothic 𐌰𐍄 (at, “at”), Latin ad (“to, near”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（at），來自古英語（æt）「在、靠近、朝向」，經原始日耳曼語（*at），上溯至原始印歐語（*h₂éd）「靠近」。與拉丁語（ad）「到」同源。

senses.definition: Used to express the future tense, sometimes with an implication of volition or determination when used in the first person. Compare shall.
To be able to, to have the capacity to.
Expressing a present tense or perfect tense with some conditional or subjective weakening: "will turn out to", "must by inference".
To habitually do (a given action).
To choose or agree to (do something); used to express intention but without any temporal connotations, often in questions and negation.
To wish, desire (something).
To instruct (that something be done) in one's will.
To bequeath (something) to someone in one's will (legal document).
To exert one's force of will (intention) in order to compel, or attempt to compel, something to happen or someone to do something.
To wish or desire (that something happen); to intend (that).
Implying will go.

examples.text: How soon will the meeting begin?
examples.translation: 會議什麼時候開始？

examples.text: What time will the game start?
examples.translation: 比賽甚麼時候開始？

examples.text: I will say something about it.
examples.translation: 我會談談它。

examples.text: I will come, time permitting.
examples.translation: 有時間我就來。

examples.text: People who will lie for you, will lie to you.
examples.translation: 會為你說謊的人，就會對你說謊。

examples.text: You will soon get used to speaking in public.
examples.translation: 你很快就會習慣在公開場合講話了。

etymology.text: From Middle English willen, wullen, wollen, from Old English willan (“to want”), from Proto-West Germanic *willjan, from Proto-Germanic *wiljaną, from Proto-Indo-European *welh₁- (“to choose, wish”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（willen），來自古英語（willan）「想要」，經原始日耳曼語（*wiljaną），上溯至原始印歐語（*welh₁-）「選擇、希望」。

senses.definition: One's independent faculty of choice; the ability to be able to exercise one's choice or intention.
The act of choosing to do something; a person’s conscious intent or volition.
One's intention or decision; someone's orders or commands.
Firmness of purpose, fixity of intent
A formal declaration of one's intent concerning the disposal of one's property and holdings after death; the legal document stating such wishes.
A weak-side linebacker.
That which is desired; one's wish.
Desire, longing. (Now generally merged with later senses.)

examples.text: The meeting will be held tomorrow.
examples.translation: 會議將於明天舉行。

examples.text: Such a plan will give rise to many problems.
examples.translation: 這樣的計劃會引發很多問題。

etymology.text: From Middle English willen, wullen, wollen, from Old English willan (“to want”), from Proto-West Germanic *willjan, from Proto-Germanic *wiljaną, from Proto-Indo-European *welh₁- (“to choose, wish”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（willen），來自古英語（willan）「想要」，經原始日耳曼語（*wiljaną），上溯至原始印歐語（*welh₁-）「選擇、希望」。

senses.definition: Connects at least two alternative words, phrases, clauses, sentences, etc., each of which could make a passage true.
An operator denoting the disjunction of two propositions or truth values. There are two forms: the inclusive or and the exclusive or.
senses.native: 表示兩個命題或真值析取的運算子，有包容性的「或」與排他性的「或」兩種

senses.definition: Counts the elements before and after as two possibilities.
senses.native: 把前後的元素視為兩種可能：或者

etymology.text: From Middle English from (“from”), from Old English from, fram (“forward, from”), from Proto-West Germanic *fram, from Proto-Germanic *fram (“forward, from, away”). senses.definition: To make (someone) aware of something.

examples.text: I became aware of someone looking at me.
examples.translation: 我感覺到有人在看著我。

examples.text: Tom was aware that someone was standing behind him.
Mary was aware that someone was standing behind her.
Tom and Mary were aware that someone was standing behind them.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English aware, iwar, iware, ywar, from Old English ġewær (“aware”), from Proto-West Germanic *gawar, from Proto-Germanic *waraz (“aware, cautious”), from Proto-Indo-European *worós (“attentive”), from *wer- (“to heed; watch out”). Cognate with Dutch gewaar, German gewahr, Danish var, Swedish var, Icelandic varr.

senses.definition: In an honest manner.
Frankly, to be honest.
Expresses mild surprise or hesitation about one's own conclusion.

examples.text: Honestly, I really like you.
examples.translation: 說實在的，我真的喜歡你。

examples.text: Honestly, his speeches are always boring.
I honestly don't think Tom and Mary care.
examples.translation: 我真的認為湯姆和瑪麗不在乎。

examples.text: Honestly, I also want to learn Japanese.
examples.translation: 其實我也想學日語。

examples.text: I may look strong, but I'm honestly not.
examples.translation: 我看上去像是很有力氣的人，可實際上並非如此。

examples.text: It is a matter of principle with him to answer your questions honestly.
examples.translation: 誠實地回答你的問題對他來說是個原則問題。

etymology.text: From Middle English honestly, honestlyche, honestliche, equivalent to honest + -ly.

senses.definition: What, of those mentioned or implied.
The/Any ... that; whichever.
Designates the one(s) previously mentioned.

examples.text: In which folder did you save the file?
examples.translation: 你把檔案存到哪個資料夾了?

etymology.text: From Middle English which, hwic, wilche, hwilch, whilk, hwilc, from Old English hwelċ (“which”), from Proto-Germanic *hwilīkaz (“what kind”, literally “like what”), derived from *hwaz.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（which、hwilch），來自古英語（hwelċ）「哪個」，來自原始日耳曼語（*hwilīkaz）「哪一種」，字面意思是「像什麼」。

senses.definition: What one or ones (of those mentioned or implied).
The/Any ones that; whichever.
Referring to a preceding noun.
Referring to a preceding statement.
In a restrictive relative clause, referring to a noun previously mentioned.
senses.native: （限定關係子句）指前面提到的名詞

senses.definition: Used of people (now generally who, whom, that; which remains possible with words also referred to by it such as baby, child).
Used of people.

examples.text: Which is larger, Japan or England?
examples.translation: 日本和英格蘭哪個大？

examples.text: Which countries have you visited?
examples.translation: 你去過哪些國家？

examples.text: Which game are you talking about?
examples.translation: 你在說哪個遊戲？

examples.text: Which of these rackets is yours?
examples.translation: 這些球拍中哪一支是你的？

examples.text: Which station are you going to?
examples.translation: 你去哪站？

examples.text: He broke his word, which made his wife angry.
examples.translation: 他失信了，這讓他妻子生氣。

etymology.text: From Middle English which, hwic, wilche, hwilch, whilk, hwilc, from Old English hwelċ (“which”), from Proto-Germanic *hwilīkaz (“what kind”, literally “like what”), derived from *hwaz.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（which、hwilch），來自古英語（hwelċ）「哪個」，來自原始日耳曼語（*hwilīkaz）「哪一種」，字面意思是「像什麼」。

senses.definition: In or at a place or location (stated, implied or otherwise indicated) that is perceived to be away from, or at a relative distance from, the speaker (compare here).
To or into a place or location; thither.
Into an undesirable topic or subject matter; see also go there.
At that point, stage, etc., visualised as a distinct place.
In a notional place where one will provide support or care; see also be there.
senses.native: 在身邊支持（見 be there）

senses.definition: In existence in some place.
In its correct position, so as to be fully and properly fitted or inserted.
After the name of a person perceived as located ‘away’ from the speaker, used familiarly to indicate that person.
In a notional place or situation of mental soundness and competence; see also all there.
In that matter, relation, etc..
In this world: used to say that someone or something exists; see also pronoun section below.
senses.native: 在這個世界上：用於表示某人或某物存在；另見下方代詞章節

senses.definition: After certain determiners, especially ‘them’, ‘that’ and ‘those’, used to emphasise demonstrative sense; see also them there.
senses.native: 用在指示詞（them、that、those）之後加強指示意味

senses.definition: Where, there where, in which place.

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: How many sandwiches are there left?
examples.translation: 還剩多少個三明治？

examples.text: There are exceptions to every rule.
examples.translation: 每條規則都有例外。

examples.text: There's nothing good on television.
examples.translation: 電視上沒有什麼好事。

examples.text: There wasn't anybody in the house.
examples.translation: 沒有人在家。

examples.text: Look out! There's a truck coming!
examples.translation: 小心！有卡車！

examples.text: There is a small garden in front of my house.
examples.translation: 我家前面有個小庭院。

relations.native: 他們是（they are 的縮寫）
他們是（they are 的縮寫）

etymology.text: From Middle English there, ther, thare, thar, thore, from Old English þēr, þǣr, þār (“there; at that place”), from Proto-West Germanic *þār, from Proto-Germanic *þar (“at that place; there”), from Proto-Indo-European *tó-r (“there”), from demonstrative pronominal base *to- (“the, that”) + adverbial suffix *-r.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（there、thar），來自古英語（þǣr）「在那裡」，經原始日耳曼語（*þar），上溯至原始印歐語（*tó-r），由指示詞基加副詞後綴構成。

senses.definition: At this moment, at present, now.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: This store is currently selling vegetables.
examples.translation: 這家店在賣蔬菜。

examples.text: The students are currently on holiday.
examples.translation: 現在學生在放假。

examples.text: I'm not doing anything currently.
examples.translation: 目前我沒在做什麼事情。

examples.text: Tom currently resides in Boston.
examples.translation: 湯姆現在住在波士頓。

examples.text: He currently works in the UK.
examples.translation: 他現在在英國工作.

examples.text: The suspect's gender is currently unknown.
examples.translation: 嫌疑犯目前性別不明。

etymology.text: From current + -ly.

senses.definition: A person who is in attendance or in the audience of an event.
A person who is attended.

examples.text: The meeting had 12 attendees.
The seminarclass is full of pigheaded attendees.
Tom closed the meeting by thanking all the attendees.
The attendees were met with silence instead of music.
Her petulant humor upset the attendees.
The concert drew attendees from the surrounding towns.

etymology.text: From attend + -ee.

senses.definition: At what time? At which time? Upon which occasion or circumstance? Used to introduce direct or indirect questions about time.
Used after a noun or noun phrase in isolation to express impatience with an anticipated future event.
At an earlier time and under different, usually less favorable, circumstances.
senses.native: 在從前（情況通常較差的時候）

senses.definition: At which, on which, during which: often omitted or replaced with that.
The time at, on or during which.
A circumstance or situation in which.

examples.text: Investing money in your home has some merit; when it is time to sell it you can get more money.
examples.translation: 多花點錢在房子上，也有一些好處 ﹣ 例如，賣的時候可以賣個比較好的價錢。

etymology.text: From Middle English when(ne), whan(ne), from Old English hwonne, from Proto-West Germanic *hwannē, from Proto-West Germanic *hwan, from Proto-Germanic *hwan (“at what time, when”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷís (interrogative base).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（whanne），來自古英語（hwonne），經原始日耳曼語（*hwan）「何時」，上溯至原始印歐語（*kʷís）疑問詞基。

senses.definition: At (or as soon as) that time that; at the (or any and every) time that; if.
During the time that; at the time of the action of the following clause or participle phrase.
At what time; at which time.
Since; given the fact that; considering that.
Whereas; although; at the same time as; in spite of the fact that.

examples.text: I take a walk every day except when it rains.
examples.translation: 除了雨天我每天都散步。

examples.text: When you send a telegram, brevity is essential because you will be charged for every word.
examples.translation: 當我們發電報的時候，簡明扼要是關鍵，因為是以字計費的。

etymology.text: From Middle English when(ne), whan(ne), from Old English hwonne, from Proto-West Germanic *hwannē, from Proto-West Germanic *hwan, from Proto-Germanic *hwan (“at what time, when”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷís (interrogative base).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（whanne），來自古英語（hwonne），經原始日耳曼語（*hwan）「何時」，上溯至原始印歐語（*kʷís）疑問詞基。

senses.definition: What person or people; which person or people; asks for the identity of someone; used in a direct or indirect question.
With antecedent as subject.
With antecedent as object: whom.
Whoever, he who, they who.
Also used with names of collective nouns that are groups of people, especially singularly-named musical groups or sports teams.

examples.text: People who will lie for you, will lie to you.
examples.translation: 會為你說謊的人，就會對你說謊。

examples.text: She doesn't like people who aren't punctual.
examples.translation: 她不喜歡不守時的人。

examples.text: I'm trying to find the person who owns this guitar.
examples.translation: 我在找這把吉他的主人。

examples.text: Those who forget everything are happy.
examples.translation: 健忘的人最幸福。

examples.text: Everything comes to those who wait.
examples.translation: 成功屬於耐心等待的人。

examples.text: "Who is that girl?" "That's Keiko."
examples.translation: 「那個女孩是誰？」 「那是惠子。」

etymology.text: From Middle English who, hwo, huo, wha, hwoa, hwa, from Old English hwā (dative hwām, genitive hwæs), from Proto-West Germanic *hwaʀ, from Proto-Germanic *hwaz, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷos, *kʷís.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（who、hwa），來自古英語（hwā），經原始日耳曼語（*hwaz），上溯至原始印歐語（*kʷos）疑問詞。

senses.definition: A person under discussion; a question of which person.
senses.native: 討論中的人；是誰的問題

examples.text: There are always some people who are unreasonable.
examples.translation: 總有一些人不講理。

etymology.text: From Middle English who, hwo, huo, wha, hwoa, hwa, from Old English hwā (dative hwām, genitive hwæs), from Proto-West Germanic *hwaʀ, from Proto-Germanic *hwaz, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷos, *kʷís.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（who、hwa），來自古英語（hwā），經原始日耳曼語（*hwaz），上溯至原始印歐語（*kʷos）疑問詞。

senses.definition: To enjoy, be pleased by; favor; be in favor of.
To find attractive; to prefer the company of; to have mild romantic feelings for.
To show support for, or approval of, something posted on the Internet by marking it with a vote.
To prefer and maintain (an action) as a regular habit or activity.
To want, desire. See also would like.
To be prone to.
Of a computer or other system: to tolerate as an input; to accept.
To please (same meaning as above but with subject and object reversed).
To derive pleasure [with of or by or with ‘from someone or something’].
To come near; to avoid with difficulty; to escape narrowly.
To have an appearance or expression; to look; to seem to be (in a specified condition).
To liken; to compare.
To be likely.

examples.text: Almost all the students like English.
examples.translation: 幾乎所有的學生喜歡英語。

examples.text: Peter isn't anything like his father.
examples.translation: 彼得一點也不像他父親。

examples.text: Help yourself to anything you like.
examples.translation: 喜歡什麼就隨便吃吧。

examples.text: I feel like eating something sweet.
examples.translation: 我想吃點甜的東西。

examples.text: Would you like something to drink?
examples.translation: 你想喝點什麼嗎？

examples.text: I don't feel like taking a walk this morning.
examples.translation: 我今天早上不想散步。

etymology.text: Verb from Middle English liken, from Old English līcian (“to like, to please”), from Proto-West Germanic *līkēn, from Proto-Germanic *līkāną, from Proto-Indo-European *leyg- (“image; likeness; similarity”).
etymology.native: 動詞源自中古英語（liken），來自古英語（līcian）「喜歡、使高興」，經原始日耳曼語（*līkāną），上溯至原始印歐語（*leyg-）「形象、相似」。

senses.definition: Something that a person likes (prefers).
An individual vote showing support for, approval of, or enjoyment of, something posted on the Internet.
Someone similar to a given person, or something similar to a given object; a comparative; a type; a sort.
The stroke that equalizes the number of strokes played by the opposing player or side.

examples.text: I never expected to meet her in a place like that.
examples.translation: 我想也沒有想過會在這樣的地方踫到她。

etymology.text: Verb from Middle English liken, from Old English līcian (“to like, to please”), from Proto-West Germanic *līkēn, from Proto-Germanic *līkāną, from Proto-Indo-European *leyg- (“image; likeness; similarity”).
etymology.native: 動詞源自中古英語（liken），來自古英語（līcian）「喜歡、使高興」，經原始日耳曼語（*līkāną），上溯至原始印歐語（*leyg-）「形象、相似」。

senses.definition: Similar to, reminiscent of.
Typical of.
Approximating.
In the manner of, similarly to.
Such as; including.
As if there would be.
Used to ask for a description or opinion of someone or something.

examples.text: Why would you marry a woman if you like men?
examples.translation: 喜歡男人，為什麼還要和女人結婚？

examples.text: Be it ever so humble, there's no place like home.
examples.translation: 金窩銀窩不如自己的狗窩。

examples.text: His upper body looks like it has the shape of an inverted triangle; standing there, he seems extremely handsome!
examples.translation: 他上身長得呈倒三角形，站在那裡看上去特帥！

etymology.text: Verb from Middle English liken, from Old English līcian (“to like, to please”), from Proto-West Germanic *līkēn, from Proto-Germanic *līkāną, from Proto-Indo-European *leyg- (“image; likeness; similarity”).
etymology.native: 動詞源自中古英語（liken），來自古英語（līcian）「喜歡、使高興」，經原始日耳曼語（*līkāną），上溯至原始印歐語（*leyg-）「形象、相似」。

senses.definition: Having resemblance or similitude; similar; without difference.

examples.text: She loved her children alike.
examples.translation: 她的孩子她都一樣愛。

examples.text: I hate women who say that all men are alike.
examples.translation: 我討厭那些說男人都是一個樣的女人。

examples.text: Bill and his younger brother are nothing alike.
Not even our fingers look alike.
examples.translation: 甚至我們的手指都不相像。

examples.text: Those two are exactly alike.
examples.translation: 那兩個是一模一樣的。

examples.text: It is, even now, a book loved by men and women alike.
examples.translation: 這仍是一本男女皆愛的書。

etymology.text: The adjective comes from a conflation of several different terms:

senses.definition: Not like; dissimilar (to); having no resemblance; unalike.
Unequal.
Not likely; improbable; unlikely.

examples.text: Unlike profanity, transphobia affects real people.
Unlike my brother, I cannot swim.
The two brothers are quite unlike in their appearance.
examples.translation: 哥哥和弟弟的樣子一點也不像。

examples.text: The crane, unlike the dog, has never dreamed of flying.
examples.translation: 不像狗, 這隻鶴從來沒有夢想過飛翔。

examples.text: It's unlike him to get so angry.
examples.translation: 這麼生氣不像他。

examples.text: Unlike you, I'm not enthusiastic about that.

etymology.text: From Middle English unlic, unlich, from Old English unlīċ, unġelīċ (“unlike, different, dissimilar, diverse”), from Proto-Germanic *ungalīkaz. By surface analysis, un- + like. Cognate with Dutch ongelijk, German ungleich, Old Norse úlíkr (see there for North Germanic descendants).

senses.definition: To perceive or detect someone or something with the eyes, or as if by sight.
To reference or to study for further details.
To witness or observe by personal experience.
To watch (a movie) at a cinema, or a show on television etc.
To form a mental picture of, to perceive in a certain way.
To understand.
To come to a realization of having been mistaken or misled.
To foresee, predict, or prophesy.
Used to emphasise a proposition.
To have an interview with; especially, to make a call upon; to visit.
To date frequently.
To visit for an appointment, especially a medical appointment.
To be attended to during an appointment, especially a medical appointment.
To be the setting or time of.
Chiefly followed by that: to ensure that something happens, especially by personally witnessing it.
To wait upon; attend, escort.
To respond to another player's bet with a bet of equal value.
To determine by trial or experiment; to find out (if or whether).
To examine something closely, or to utilize something, often as a temporary alternative.
To include as one of something's experiences.

examples.text: Yesterday morning I saw many birds.
examples.translation: 我昨天早上看到了很多鳥。

examples.text: I'll see you again this afternoon.
examples.translation: 今天下午我會再見到你。

examples.text: I saw Christine here yesterday.
examples.translation: 我昨天在這裡看到克莉絲汀。

examples.text: I'm sure I've seen him before.
examples.translation: 我確定我以前見過他。

examples.text: Kyoto has many places to see.
examples.translation: 在京都，有很多的景點值得一看。

examples.text: If you see a mistake, then please correct it.
examples.translation: 如果你發現有錯的話請幫忙改正。

etymology.text: From Middle English seen, from Old English sēon (“to see, look, behold, perceive, observe, discern, understand, know”), from Proto-West Germanic *sehwan, from Proto-Germanic *sehwaną (“to see”), from Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ- (“to see, notice”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（seen），來自古英語（sēon）「看、注視、察覺、理解」，經原始日耳曼語（*sehwaną）「看」，上溯至原始印歐語（*sekʷ-）「看見、注意」。

senses.definition: Brand; marque; manufacturer; maker.
Manner or style of construction (style of how a thing is made).
Origin (of a manufactured article); manufacture; production.
A person's character or disposition.
Quantity produced, especially of materials.
A software utility for automatically building large applications, or an implementation of this utility.
Identification: recognition (of identity), especially from police records or evidence.
A promotion.
A homemade project, particularly one demonstrated on television.
Turn to declare the trump for a hand (in bridge), or to shuffle the cards.
A made basket.
The closing of an electrical circuit.
Past, present, or future target of seduction (usually female).
The act or process of making something, especially in industrial manufacturing.
Mate; a spouse or companion; a match.
A halfpenny.
An agricultural tool resembling a scythe, used to cut (harvest) certain plants such as peas, reeds, or tares.

examples.text: The curtains make this room beautiful.
examples.translation: 窗簾使房間變漂亮了。

examples.text: Make this sentence a little shorter.
examples.translation: 把這句話弄短點。

examples.text: To make an excuse for having stayed out late.
examples.translation: 為晚歸找個藉口。

examples.text: The mere thought of a snake makes me shiver.
examples.translation: 一想到蛇就發顫。

examples.text: Jessie is boiling water to make coffee.
examples.translation: 傑西正在燒開水來沖咖啡。

examples.text: Oxygen and hydrogen make water.
examples.translation: 氧和氫組成了水。

etymology.text: From Middle English macen, machiæ, macian, macke, mak, make, maken, makiȝe, from Old English macian (“to build, make, work”), from Proto-West Germanic *makōn (“to build, make, work”), from *mak (“agreeable, comfortable, fit, suitable”), from Proto-Germanic *makaz (“agreeable, comfortable, fit, suitable”), from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂ǵ-, *meh₂ḱ- (“to knead”) or *meg- (“to be comfortable, pleasant”). Related to match.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（maken），來自古英語（macian）「建造、做、工作」，經原始西日耳曼語（*makōn），來自（*mak）「合適的」，可能上溯至原始印歐語（*meh₂ǵ-）「揉捏」。與（match）相關。

senses.definition: The inevitable progression into the future with the passing of present and past events.
A quantity of availability of duration.
A measurement of a quantity of time; a numerical or general indication of a length of progression.
The duration of time of a given day that has passed; the moment, as indicated by a clock or similar device.
A particular moment or hour; the appropriate moment or hour for something (especially with prepositional phrase or imperfect subjunctive).
A numerical indication of a particular moment.
An instance or occurrence.
The feeling of the passage of events and their relative duration, as experienced by an individual.
A dimension of spacetime with the opposite metric signature to space dimensions; the fourth dimension.
Change associated with the second law of thermodynamics; the physical and psychological result of increasing entropy.
The property of a system which allows it to have more than one distinct configuration.
The serving of a prison sentence.
An experience.
An era; (articulated, sometimes in the plural) the current era, the current state of affairs.
A person's youth or young adulthood, as opposed to the present day.
Time out; temporary, limited suspension of play.
Closing time.
The hour of childbirth.
The end of someone’s life, conceived by the speaker as having been predestined.
senses.native: 生命終結，由說話者視為命中注定

senses.definition: The measurement under some system of region of day or moment.
senses.native: 某種區域或瞬間的測量

examples.text: Take your time. There's no hurry.
examples.translation: 慢慢來，沒那麼急。

examples.text: What time did you arrive there?
examples.translation: 你是在甚麼時候到達的？

examples.text: What time does boarding begin?
examples.translation: 什麼時候開始登機？

examples.text: It's high time you left for school, isn't it?
examples.translation: 你現在該上學去了吧？

examples.text: Finish your homework by the time they return.
examples.translation: 你要在他們回來之前把功課做完。

examples.text: Would you mind my staying here for some time?
examples.translation: 你介意我在這兒待一會兒嗎？

examples.text: How are your parents getting along?

examples.text: We got all the materials together.
examples.translation: 我們把所有的材料放在一起。

examples.text: This coat hasn't got any pockets.
examples.translation: 這件外套沒有口袋。

examples.text: What did you get for Christmas?
examples.translation: 你耶誕節得到了什麼?

examples.text: The clouds are getting darker.
examples.translation: 雲越來越黑。

examples.text: You will soon get used to speaking in public.
examples.translation: 你很快就會習慣在公開場合講話了。

etymology.text: From Middle English geten, from Old Norse geta, from Proto-Germanic *getaną (“to find; to acquire, attain, get, hold, receive”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰed- (“to find; to hold; to seize; to take”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（geten），來自古諾斯語（geta），經原始日耳曼語（*getaną）「找到、得到」，上溯至原始印歐語（*gʰed-）「找到、抓住」。

senses.definition: An act of taking.
Money that is taken in, (legal or illegal) proceeds, income; (in particular) profits; takings.
The or a quantity of fish, game animals or pelts, etc which have been taken at one time; catch.
An interpretation or view, opinion or assessment; perspective; a statement expressing such a position.
An approach, a (distinct) treatment.
A scene recorded (filmed) at one time, without an interruption or break; a recording of such a scene.
A recording of a musical performance made during an uninterrupted single recording period.
A visible (facial) response to something, especially something unexpected; a facial gesture in response to an event.
An instance of successful inoculation/vaccination.
A catch of the ball (in cricket, especially one by the wicket-keeper).
The quantity of copy given to a compositor at one time.

examples.text: Take this medicine every six hours.
examples.translation: 每六個小時吃一次這個藥。

examples.text: Please take good care of yourself.
examples.translation: 請好好照顧你自己。

examples.text: Take your time. There's no hurry.
examples.translation: 慢慢來，沒那麼急。

examples.text: Let's have lunch downtown and take in a show.
examples.translation: 我們去市區吃飯，然後再看場電影吧。

examples.text: How long does it take to walk to the station?
examples.translation: 走到車站要花多少時間？

examples.text: Our eyes take time to adjust to the darkness.
examples.translation: 我們的眼睛需要時間來適應黑暗。

etymology.text: From Middle English taken (“to take, lay hold of, grasp, strike”), from Old English tacan (“to grasp, touch”), probably of North Germanic origin, from Old Norse taka (“to touch, take”). Alternatively, inherited from Proto-West Germanic *takan (“to take; grasp, touch”). Both from Proto-Germanic *tēkaną (“to touch”), from pre-Germanic *deh₁g- (“to touch”), possibly a phonetically altered form of Proto-Indo-European *te-th₂g- (“to touch, take”) (see there for details).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（taken）「拿、抓住、打」，來自古英語（tacan）「抓住、觸摸」，可能來自古諾斯語（taka）「觸摸、拿」。都源自原始日耳曼語（*tēkaną）「觸摸」。

senses.definition: Factually right, correct; factual.
Morally right; upright, righteous, equitable; fair.
Rationally right, correct.
Proper, adequate.

etymology.text: From Middle English juste, from Old French juste, from Latin iūstus (“just, lawful, rightful, true, due, proper, moderate”), from Proto-Italic *jowestos, related to Latin iūs (“law, right”); ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂yew-. Compare Scots juist (“just”), Saterland Frisian juust (“just”), West Frisian just (“just”), Dutch juist (“just”), German Low German jüst (“jüst”), German just (“just”), Danish just (“just”), Swedish just (“just”). Doublet of giusto.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（juste），來自古法語（juste），來自拉丁語（iūstus）「公正的、合法的、正確的」，與（iūs）「法律、權利」相關，上溯至原始印歐語（*h₂yew-）。與義大利語（giusto）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: Only, simply, merely.
Moments ago, only very recently.
Exactly, precisely, perfectly.
Introduces a disappointing or surprising outcome that renders futile something previously mentioned.
senses.native: （引出令人失望或意外的結果）偏偏；結果卻

senses.definition: Used to reduce the force of an imperative; simply.
Used to increase the force of an imperative; simply, without questioning.
Used to convey a less serious or formal tone.
Absolutely, positively.
By a narrow margin; closely; narrowly; almost not.

examples.text: Tom has just finished washing dishes.
examples.translation: 湯姆剛洗完了碗。

examples.text: I have just returned from Britain.
examples.translation: 我剛從英國回來。

examples.text: I have just finished eating lunch.
examples.translation: 我剛剛吃完了午飯。

examples.text: I have just finished my homework.
examples.translation: 我剛剛完成我的作業。

examples.text: If it rains tomorrow, I'll just stay at home.
examples.translation: 如果明天下雨，我就待在家。

examples.text: Mary isn't really sick. She's just faking it.
examples.translation: 瑪麗不是真病。她只是裝病。

etymology.text: From Middle English juste, from Old French juste, from Latin iūstus (“just, lawful, rightful, true, due, proper, moderate”), from Proto-Italic *jowestos, related to Latin iūs (“law, right”); ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂yew-. Compare Scots juist (“just”), Saterland Frisian juust (“just”), West Frisian just (“just”), Dutch juist (“just”), German Low German jüst (“jüst”), German just (“just”), Danish just (“just”), Swedish just (“just”). Doublet of giusto.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（juste），來自古法語（juste），來自拉丁語（iūstus）「公正的、合法的、正確的」，與（iūs）「法律、權利」相關，上溯至原始印歐語（*h₂yew-）。與義大利語（giusto）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: In a proper manner, appropriately, suitably; correctly, justifiably
Entirely; extremely; thoroughly.
individually; in one's own manner.

examples.text: The toilet doesn't flush properly.
examples.translation: 廁所沖水不正常。

examples.text: The door is not closed properly.
examples.translation: 門沒有關好。

examples.text: Flammable substances should be stored properly.
Can you please properly study a foreign language?
examples.translation: 你能不能好好讀外語？

examples.text: If you understand, then do it properly.
examples.translation: 懂了就正確做。

examples.text: My boy can't do addition properly yet.
examples.translation: 我的兒子還不懂加法。

etymology.text: From proper + -ly.

senses.definition: In a precise manner; exactly.
Used to provide emphasis.

examples.text: Use words that precisely describe something.
Precisely what happened here yesterday evening?
I can't remember precisely what happened.
I arrive precisely when I mean to.
examples.translation: 我想準時到，就會準時到。

examples.text: Tom doesn't know precisely where he was born.
What befell him was precisely what he feared.

etymology.text: From precise + -ly.

senses.definition: By or for the cause that; on this account that; for the reason that.
As is known, inferred, or determined from the fact that.
senses.native: 因為；由於（從已知事實推斷）

senses.definition: So that, in order that.

examples.text: Because there's pollution in the cities.
examples.translation: 因為有城市公害。

examples.text: Because they're watching television.
examples.translation: 因為他們正在看電視。

examples.text: Because he's sick, he can't come.
examples.translation: 因為他生病了，所以他不能來。

examples.text: Their trip was postponed because of the rain.
examples.translation: 他們的旅行因為下雨延期了。

examples.text: The picnic was cancelled because of the rain.
examples.translation: 由於下雨，野餐泡湯了。

examples.text: He was absent from school because of illness.
examples.translation: 他病了，所以沒有上學。

etymology.text: From Middle English bi cause, from bi (“by”) + cause, modelled on Old French par cause.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（bi cause），由「由於」（bi）加「原因」（cause）組成，仿照古法語（par cause）。

senses.definition: Used alone to refuse to provide a full answer to a question begun with "why", usually taken as an anapodoton of the elided full phrase "Because I said so".

examples.text: I'm eating fruits because I'm hungry.
examples.translation: 我在吃水果，因為我餓。

examples.text: Because you smell bad, that's why.
examples.translation: 因為你真的很臭，這就是為什麼。

examples.text: I couldn't enter because the door was closed.
examples.translation: 我因為門關著進不去。

examples.text: Because of the snow, I couldn't see anything.
examples.translation: 因為下雪了，我什麼也沒能看見。

examples.text: I was able to succeed because of your advice.
examples.translation: 我因為有你的建議才能成功。

examples.text: I always have to wear a tie because of my job.
examples.translation: 因為這份工作的關係，我總是要打領帶。

etymology.text: From Middle English bi cause, from bi (“by”) + cause, modelled on Old French par cause.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（bi cause），由「由於」（bi）加「原因」（cause）組成，仿照古法語（par cause）。

senses.definition: True, real, actual.
The same; identical.
With limiting effect: mere.

examples.text: Everyone was listening very carefully.
examples.translation: 大家都在聚精會神地聽著。

examples.text: Arabic is a very important language.
examples.translation: 阿拉伯語是一種很重要的語言。

examples.text: I have a feeling you'll be a very good lawyer.
examples.translation: 我感覺你將來會成為一名優秀的律師。

examples.text: It was very kind of you to lend me an umbrella.
examples.translation: 你借給我傘真好。

examples.text: I found the new magazine very interesting.
examples.translation: 我發現這本新雜誌非常有趣。

examples.text: In real combat, you must not forget that hesitation is a very dangerous thing.
examples.translation: 在實戰中，你要知道三心二意是很危險的。

etymology.text: From Middle English verray, from Old French verai (“true”), from Early Medieval Latin vērāgus, from Classical Latin vērāx, derived from vērus, from Proto-Italic *wēros, from Proto-Indo-European *weh₁ros.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（verray），來自古法語（verai）「真的」，來自早期中世紀拉丁語（vērāgus），再來自古典拉丁語（vērāx），衍生自（vērus）「真實的」，上溯至原始印歐語（*weh₁ros）。

senses.definition: Very close to, but not quite.
Up to, except for a negligible set (where negligible is not universally but contextually defined).
senses.native: 除了可忽略的部分之外；幾乎全部（數學用語）

senses.definition: Up to a null set; except for a set of measure 0.
senses.native: 除了測度為零的集合以外；幾乎處處（數學用語）

examples.text: Almost everybody here can speak French.
examples.translation: 這裡幾乎所有人都會講法語。

examples.text: I'm almost finished reading this book.
examples.translation: 我就要讀完這本書了。

examples.text: Almost all the students like English.
examples.translation: 幾乎所有的學生喜歡英語。

examples.text: Tom comes home almost every weekend.
examples.translation: 湯姆幾乎每個週末都回家。

examples.text: Mike eats out almost every night.
examples.translation: 麥克幾乎每天晚上出去吃飯。

examples.text: The beer glass is almost bigger than you are.
examples.translation: 啤酒杯差一點比你還大。

etymology.text: From Middle English almost, from Old English eallmǣst (“nearly all, almost, for the most part”), equivalent to al- (“all”) + most.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（almost），來自古英語（eallmǣst）「幾乎全部；大部分」，相當於（al）-「全部」加（most）。

senses.definition: Mainly or chiefly; for the most part; usually, generally, on the whole.
Synonym of probably, likely.
To the greatest extent; most.

examples.text: I mostly have fruit for breakfast.
examples.translation: 我早飯主要吃水果。

examples.text: The Algerian Sahara is mostly uninhabited.
Sappho's surviving works are mostly fragmentary.
Tom mostly kept to himself.
examples.translation: 湯姆大多一個人獨處。

examples.text: The passengers on board were mostly Japanese.
Tom and Mary mostly talked about their trips.

etymology.text: From most + -ly.

senses.definition: Used in comparisons, to introduce the basis of comparison.
Because; for.

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: I'm much better today than yesterday.
examples.translation: 我今天覺得比昨天好多了。

examples.text: Generally speaking, women live longer than men.
examples.translation: 一般來說，女人活得比男人久。

examples.text: No sooner had I gone out than it began to rain.
examples.translation: 我一出門就開始下雨了。

examples.text: Generally speaking, men are stronger than women.
examples.translation: 男人一般都比女人強壯。

examples.text: I should have known better than to call him.
examples.translation: 早知道我不應該打電話給他。

examples.text: Bob was somewhat chubbier than his brother.
examples.translation: 鮑勃比他兄弟稍胖點。

etymology.text: From Middle English than, thanne (“than; then”), from Old English þanne, a variant of þonne (“then; when; than”), from Proto-West Germanic *þannē, an alteration of *þan (“then; than”), from Proto-Germanic *þan (“then; than”), from earlier *þam, from Proto-Indo-European *tóm, accusative masculine of *só (“that”, demonstrative pronoun).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（than、thanne）「比、然後」，來自古英語（þanne），是（þonne）「然後、當、比」的變體，經原始日耳曼語（*þan），上溯至原始印歐語（*tóm），是指示代名詞（*só）「那」的陽性受格。

senses.definition: Introduces a comparison, and is associated with comparatives, and with words such as more, less, and fewer. Typically, it seeks to measure the force of an adjective or similar description between two predicates.

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: This library has more than 50,000 volumes.
examples.translation: 這個圖書館有超過50000冊書。

examples.text: Is English more difficult than Japanese?
examples.translation: 英文比日文更難嗎？

examples.text: There's more cloud today than yesterday.
examples.translation: 今天的雲比昨天多。

examples.text: Onions cook more quickly than potatoes.
examples.translation: 洋蔥比馬鈴薯煮得更快些。

examples.text: More often than not, she had to go in person.
examples.translation: 很多時候她要親自去。

examples.text: It is no less than two hours' walk from here.
examples.translation: 從這開始走用不了兩小時。

etymology.text: From Middle English than, thanne (“than; then”), from Old English þanne, a variant of þonne (“then; when; than”), from Proto-West Germanic *þannē, an alteration of *þan (“then; than”), from Proto-Germanic *þan (“then; than”), from earlier *þam, from Proto-Indo-European *tóm, accusative masculine of *só (“that”, demonstrative pronoun).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（than、thanne）「比、然後」，來自古英語（þanne），是（þonne）「然後、當、比」的變體，經原始日耳曼語（*þan），上溯至原始印歐語（*tóm），是指示代名詞（*só）「那」的陽性受格。

senses.definition: Farther along or away.
In addition; more.
extremely, more than

examples.text: The village is just beyond.
examples.translation: 村莊就在前面不遠處。

etymology.text: From Middle English biyonde, from Old English beġeondan, from be- + ġeond; related to yonder.

senses.definition: Used as a past subjunctive (contrary to fact).
senses.native: （假設語氣，與事實相反）能；可以

senses.definition: Used to politely ask for permission to do something.
Used to politely ask for someone else to do something.
Used to show the possibility that something might happen.
Used to suggest something.

examples.text: Could you please autograph this book?
examples.translation: 請你在這本書上簽名好嗎？

examples.text: Could you call again later, please?
examples.translation: 你可以晚點再打電話來嗎？

examples.text: Could you call me tonight, please?
examples.translation: 今晚你能打電話給我嗎？

examples.text: He could not answer that question.
examples.translation: 他無法回答這個問題。

examples.text: I could answer all the questions.
examples.translation: 我能回答所有的問題。

examples.text: I caught him by the arm before he could fall.
examples.translation: 在他倒下前我抓住了他的手臂。

etymology.text: From Middle English coude, couthe, cuthe, from Old English cūþe, past indicative and past subjunctive form of cunnan (“to be able”) (compare related cūþ, whence English couth). Cognate with German konnte, Swedish kunde.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（coude、couthe），來自古英語（cūþe），是（cunnan）「能夠」的過去直述與過去假設形式（比較相關的 cūþ，英語 couth 由此而來）。與德語（konnte）、瑞典語（kunde）同源。

senses.definition: Which, especially which of an open-ended set of possibilities.
Which.
Any ... that; all ... that; whatever.
Emphasises that something is noteworthy or remarkable in quality or degree, in either a good or bad way; may be used in combination with certain other determiners, especially 'a', less often 'some'.
Used to form exclamations indicating that something is remarkable, in either a good or bad way.

examples.text: What prevented her from coming yesterday?
examples.translation: 她昨天為甚麼不來？

examples.text: What prevented you from coming earlier?
examples.translation: 為什麼你不能早點來?

examples.text: What happened? The car's slowing down.
examples.translation: 發生了什麼事？車子慢下來了。

examples.text: What language is spoken in America?
examples.translation: 在美國的人說什麼語言?

examples.text: It's not what you wear, it's how you wear it.
examples.translation: 關鍵不在穿什麼，而是怎麼穿。

examples.text: No matter what happens, you must not give up.
examples.translation: 無論發生甚麼事情，你也絕對不能放棄。

etymology.text: From Middle English what, from Old English hwæt (“what”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwat, from Proto-Germanic *hwat (“what”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷód (“what”), neuter form of *kʷós (“who”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（what），來自古英語（hwæt）「什麼」，經原始日耳曼語（*hwat），上溯至原始印歐語（*kʷód）「什麼」，是（*kʷós）「誰」的中性形式。

senses.definition: Which thing, event, circumstance, etc.: used in asking for the specification of an identity, quantity, quality, etc.
That which; those that; the thing(s) that.
Anything that; all that; whatever.
That; which; who.

examples.text: What can go wrong?
examples.translation: 什麼可以出岔子？

etymology.text: From Middle English what, from Old English hwæt (“what”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwat, from Proto-Germanic *hwat (“what”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷód (“what”), neuter form of *kʷós (“who”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（what），來自古英語（hwæt）「什麼」，經原始日耳曼語（*hwat），上溯至原始印歐語（*kʷód）「什麼」，是（*kʷós）「誰」的中性形式。

senses.definition: An expression of surprise or disbelief.
What do you want? An abrupt, usually unfriendly enquiry as to what a person desires.
What did you say? I beg your pardon? This usage is often considered impolite, with the more polite "Pardon?" or "Excuse me?" preferred.
Indicating a guess or approximation, or a pause to try to recall information.

examples.text: I'll always love you, no matter what happens.
examples.translation: 不論發生了什麼事，我會永遠愛你。

examples.text: What is your greatest source of inspiration?
examples.translation: 什麼是您最大的靈感來源？

examples.text: Not knowing what to say, he remained silent.
examples.translation: 因為不知道該說什麼, 他保持沉默。

examples.text: Do you know what it is like to be really hungry?
examples.translation: 你嘗過真正飢餓的滋味嗎？

examples.text: I still haven't found what I'm looking for.
examples.translation: 我還是沒有找到我要找的。

examples.text: What the hell are you going to do with it?
examples.translation: 你到底要對它怎麼樣？

etymology.text: From Middle English what, from Old English hwæt (“what”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwat, from Proto-Germanic *hwat (“what”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷód (“what”), neuter form of *kʷós (“who”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（what），來自古英語（hwæt）「什麼」，經原始日耳曼語（*hwat），上溯至原始印歐語（*kʷód）「什麼」，是（*kʷós）「誰」的中性形式。

senses.definition: The identity of a thing, as an answer to a question of what.
Something that is addressed by what, as opposed to a person, addressed by who.
Something; thing; stuff.

etymology.text: From Middle English what, from Old English hwæt (“what”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwat, from Proto-Germanic *hwat (“what”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷód (“what”), neuter form of *kʷós (“who”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（what），來自古英語（hwæt）「什麼」，經原始日耳曼語（*hwat），上溯至原始印歐語（*kʷód）「什麼」，是（*kʷós）「誰」的中性形式。

senses.definition: The act of using.
The act of consuming alcohol or narcotics.
Usefulness, utility, benefit; purpose, point.
A function; a purpose for which something may be employed.
Occasion or need to employ; necessity.
A special form of a rite adopted for use in a particular context, often a diocese.
A slab of iron welded to the side of a forging, such as a shaft, near the end, and afterward drawn down, by hammering, so as to lengthen the forging.
Interest for lent money; premium paid for the use of something; usury.
Continued or repeated practice; usage; habit.
Common occurrence; ordinary experience.

examples.text: You may always use my dictionary.
examples.translation: 你可以隨時用我的詞典。

examples.text: "May I use your telephone?" "By all means."
examples.translation: 「請問能借一下你的電話嗎？」 「可以。」

examples.text: I often use SSH to access my computers remotely.
examples.translation: 我常用（SSH）遠端連線到我的電腦。

examples.text: I often use SSH to remotely connect to my computer.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English use, from Old French us, from Latin ūsus (“use, custom, skill, habit”), from past participle stem of ūtor (“use”). Displaced native Middle English note (“use”) (see note) from Old English notu; Middle English nutte (“use”) from Old English nytt; as well as Old English fricu and Old English sidu.
