senses.native: 從事某項活動時，特別是在進食時

senses.definition: Concerning or regarding.
Above, implying superiority after a contest; in spite of; notwithstanding.
senses.native: 在競賽中表示勝出；儘管如此；不顧

senses.definition: Expressing causation: due to, as the result of.
senses.native: 表示因果關係：由於；作為結果

examples.text: My father traveled all over the world by air.
examples.translation: 我的父親坐飛機環遊了世界。

examples.text: Refugees poured in from all over the country.
examples.translation: 難民從整個國家湧來。

examples.text: His death was broadcast all over the world.
examples.translation: 他去世的消息在世界各地播出。

examples.text: Grr! I'm itchy all over, and it's driving me crazy.
examples.translation: 哎呦好難受啊，全身發癢！

etymology.text: From Middle English over, from Old English ofer, ofor, ouer, from Proto-West Germanic *obar, from Proto-Germanic *uber (“over”), from Proto-Indo-European *upér (“above; over”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（over），來自古英語（ofer），經原始日耳曼語（*uber），上溯至原始印歐語（*upér）「在上方」。

senses.definition: A radio procedure word meaning that the station is finished with its transmission and is expecting a response.
Instructs the reader to turn the page and continue reading the other side.

examples.text: The two scholars wrangled over the meaning of an obscure Tibetan phrase.
examples.translation: 兩位學者為一句意思含糊的藏文句子爭論了一番。

etymology.text: From Middle English over, from Old English ofer, ofor, ouer, from Proto-West Germanic *obar, from Proto-Germanic *uber (“over”), from Proto-Indo-European *upér (“above; over”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（over），來自古英語（ofer），經原始日耳曼語（*uber），上溯至原始印歐語（*upér）「在上方」。

senses.definition: all things that are of importance to a person

examples.text: As soon as our manager got off our backs, everything started to go off without a hitch.
examples.translation: 經理一不再盯著我們，一切就開始順利進行了。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English every thing; univerbation of every + thing.
etymology.native: 承襲自中古英語（every thing），由（every）加（thing）合為一詞。

senses.definition: The day after the present day.
A future period or time.

examples.text: What will you be doing at this time tomorrow?
examples.translation: 你明天這個時候會是在做什麼？

examples.text: Tomorrow is the first time I will accompany the Chinese delegation, and I'm extremely nervous.
examples.translation: 明天第一次陪中國代表團， 我緊張得不得了。

etymology.text: From Middle English tomorwe, tomorwen, from Old English tō morgne (“tomorrow”, adverb), from tō (“at, on”) + morgne (dative of morgen (“morning”)), from Proto-Germanic *murganaz (“morning”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *mergʰ- (“to blink, to twinkle”), equivalent to to- + morrow.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（tomorwe、tomorwen），來自古英語副詞（tō morgne）「明天」，由（tō）「在」加（morgne，morgen「早晨」的與格）組成，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*murganaz）「早晨」，可能來自原始印歐語（*mergʰ-）「眨眼、閃爍」。相當於（to-）加（morrow）。

senses.definition: The day immediately before today; one day ago.
The past, often in terms of being outdated.

examples.text: That ship crossed the equator yesterday.
examples.translation: 那條船昨天穿過了赤道。

examples.text: It was a bag that I lost in the room yesterday.
examples.translation: 那是我昨天落在房間裡的包。

examples.text: I built an amplifier yesterday.
examples.translation: 昨天我組裝了一個揚聲器。

examples.text: Notification of the smoking ban was posted outside the restaurant yesterday.
examples.translation: 禁菸通知昨天貼在餐廳外面。

examples.text: Today is the child of yesterday and the parent of tomorrow.
examples.translation: 今天是昨天的孩子，也是明天的父母。

etymology.text: From Middle English yesterday, yisterday, ȝesterdai, ȝisterdai, from Old English ġiestrandæġ, ġister dæġ, ġestor dæġ, ġeostran dæġ (“yesterday”), by surface analysis, yester- + day. Cognate with Scots yisterday, yesterday (“yesterday”), Saterland Frisian jässendeeg, järsendeges (“yesterday”, adverb), West Frisian justerdei (“yesterday”), Dutch gisterdag (“yesterday”), dialectal German gestertag (“yesterday”), Swedish gårdag (“yesterday”), Gothic 𐌲𐌹𐍃𐍄𐍂𐌰𐌳𐌰𐌲𐌹𐍃 (gistradagis, “tomorrow”, adverb). Com
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（yesterday、ȝesterdai），來自古英語（ġiestrandæġ、ġister dæġ）「昨天」，表面分析為（yester-）加（day）。與蘇格蘭語（yisterday）、西弗里斯語（justerdei）、荷蘭語（gisterdag）、瑞典語（gårdag）、哥德語（gistradagis）「明天」同源。

senses.definition: A day on which a religious event or secular celebration is traditionally observed.
A day declared free from work by the state or government.
A period of one or more days taken off work for leisure and often travel; often plural.
A period during which pupils do not attend their school; often plural; rarely used for students at university (usually: vacation).
A period during which, by agreement, the usual payments are not made.
A gap in coverage, e.g. of paint on a surface, or sonar imagery.
senses.native: （油漆等的）漏塗處；（聲納影像的）空白

examples.text: Did you enjoy your winter holidays?
examples.translation: 你寒假過得愉快嗎？

examples.text: Christmas is a special holiday.
examples.translation: 聖誕節是一個特別的節日。

examples.text: At present, he is on holiday.
examples.translation: 目前,他正在度假。

examples.text: Did you enjoy your holiday?
examples.translation: 假期過得開心嗎？

examples.text: I am on holiday this week.
examples.translation: 我這個星期放假了。

examples.text: In common with many people he likes holidays.
examples.translation: 跟很多人一樣, 他喜歡假期。

etymology.text: From Middle English halyday, holyday, halidei, haliȝdei, from Old English hāliġdæġ (“holy day, Sabbath”), equivalent to holy + day. Compare West Frisian hjeldei (“holiday”), Danish helligdag (“holiday”), Norwegian helligdag (“holiday”), Swedish helgdag (“holiday, feast”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（halyday、holyday），來自古英語（hāliġdæġ）「聖日、安息日」，相當於（holy）加（day）。比較西弗里斯語（hjeldei）、丹麥語（helligdag）、挪威語（helligdag）、瑞典語（helgdag）。

senses.definition: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday, but not Saturday or Sunday.
Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, but not Friday.
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, or Saturday, but not Sunday. (e.g. in Vietnam)
Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday, but not Saturday.
Any day of the week (Monday through Sunday).

examples.text: I wear white shirts on weekdays.
She is always busy on weekdays.
The weekdays are: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday.
examples.translation: 工作日包括：星期一、二、三、四、五。

examples.text: Luckily, not all weekdays are this difficult.
The shop always closed at five pm on weekdays.
The doctor is only available on weekdays.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English wykeday, from Old English wicdæġ (“weekday”), from Proto-West Germanic *wikadag, from Proto-Germanic *wikadagaz (“weekday”). By surface analysis, compound of week + day. Compare West Frisian wikedei (“weekday”), Dutch weekdag (“weekday”), German Low German Wekendag (“weekday”), German Wochentag (“weekday”), Danish ugedag (“weekday”), Swedish veckodag (“weekday”), Norwegian ukedag (“weekday”), Faroese vikudagur (“weekday”), Icelandic vikudagur (“weekday”).

senses.definition: Since, because, in light of the fact.

examples.text: It's good now; neither too heavy nor too light.
examples.translation: 現在正好，不重也不輕。

etymology.text: From Middle English nou, nu, from Old English nū, from Proto-West Germanic *nū, from Proto-Germanic *nu (“now”), from Proto-Indo-European *nū (“now”). Doublet of nu ("well?").
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（nou、nu），來自古英語（nū），經原始日耳曼語（*nu）「現在」，上溯至原始印歐語（*nū）「現在」。

senses.definition: The present time.
The state of not paying attention to the future or the past.
senses.native: 當下（不在意過去或未來的狀態）

senses.definition: A particular instant in time, as perceived at that instant.

examples.text: You should do your homework now.
examples.translation: 你應該現在做功課。

examples.text: He's busy with his homework now.
examples.translation: 他現在正忙著做他的家庭作業。

examples.text: It is no use blaming him for the accident now.
examples.translation: 事情已經發生了，現在怪他也沒有用。

examples.text: It's still too early to talk about this now.
examples.translation: 現在談這件事還為時過早。

examples.text: Every now and then they clash over their differences.
examples.translation: 他們有時候有矛盾衝突

etymology.text: From Middle English nou, nu, from Old English nū, from Proto-West Germanic *nū, from Proto-Germanic *nu (“now”), from Proto-Indo-European *nū (“now”). Doublet of nu ("well?").
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（nou、nu），來自古英語（nū），經原始日耳曼語（*nu）「現在」，上溯至原始印歐語（*nū）「現在」。

senses.definition: While on the contrary; although; whereas.
That.

examples.text: Where there's a will, there's a way.
examples.translation: 有志者事竟成。

etymology.text: From Middle English wher, from Old English hwǣr (“where”, literally “at what place”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwār, from Proto-Germanic *hwar (“where”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷ- (interrogative pronoun).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（wher），來自古英語（hwǣr）「哪裡」，字面意思是「在什麼地方」，經原始日耳曼語（*hwar），上溯至原始印歐語的疑問代名詞（*kʷ-）。

senses.definition: What place.

examples.text: Where is your twenty? I'll give you five bucks for it.
examples.translation: 你的二十塊在哪裡? 我給你五塊錢找到它。

etymology.text: From Middle English wher, from Old English hwǣr (“where”, literally “at what place”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwār, from Proto-Germanic *hwar (“where”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷ- (interrogative pronoun).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（wher），來自古英語（hwǣr）「哪裡」，字面意思是「在什麼地方」，經原始日耳曼語（*hwar），上溯至原始印歐語的疑問代名詞（*kʷ-）。

senses.definition: A large amount of.
Used to indicate, demonstrate or compare the quantity of something.
senses.native: 用來表示或比較數量：多少；這麼多

senses.definition: many ( + plural countable noun).
A great number of; many (people).

examples.text: It would take me too much time to explain to you why it's not going to work.
examples.translation: 給你解釋這為什麼行不通要花很多時間。

relations.native: 壁龕：一般位於牆體厚度內，用於放置雕像、半身像或其他豎立裝飾品的凹室
壁龕：一般位於牆體厚度內，用於放置雕像、半身像或其他豎立裝飾品的凹室

etymology.text: From Middle English muche (“much, great”), apocopated variant of muchel (“much, great”), from Old English myċel, miċel (“big, much”), from Proto-West Germanic *mikil, from Proto-Germanic *mikilaz (“great, many, much”), from Proto-Indo-European *meǵh₂- (“big, stour, great”). See also mickle, muckle.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（muche）「多、大」，是（muchel）的詞尾脫落形式，來自古英語（miċel）「大、多」，經原始日耳曼語（*mikilaz），上溯至原始印歐語（*meǵh₂-）「大」。另見（mickle、muckle）。

senses.definition: To a great extent.
for emphasis or to indicate a great difference
senses.native: 非常；（用於強調差別）……得多

senses.definition: Often; frequently.
Used to indicate or compare extent.
Combining with an adjective or (occasionally) a noun, used in a rhetorical question to mock someone for having the specified quality.
to a great degree or extent
incredibly
(degree adverb used before a noun phrase) for all practical purposes but not completely
senses.native: 實際上全部，但非完全如此

senses.definition: frequently or in great quantities
Almost.

examples.text: I'm much better today than yesterday.
examples.translation: 我今天覺得比昨天好多了。

examples.text: Thank you very much for everything.
examples.translation: 非常感謝你所做的一切。

examples.text: Asia is much larger than Australia.
examples.translation: 亞洲比澳洲大很多。

examples.text: He studies much harder than before.
examples.translation: 他比以前學得更努力了。

examples.text: I don't know much about computers.
examples.translation: 我對電腦知道的不多。

examples.text: Few things give us as much pleasure as music.
examples.translation: 很少有東西像音樂一樣帶給我們這麼多的快樂。

etymology.text: From Middle English muche (“much, great”), apocopated variant of muchel (“much, great”), from Old English myċel, miċel (“big, much”), from Proto-West Germanic *mikil, from Proto-Germanic *mikilaz (“great, many, much”), from Proto-Indo-European *meǵh₂- (“big, stour, great”). See also mickle, muckle.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（muche）「多、大」，是（muchel）的詞尾脫落形式，來自古英語（miċel）「大、多」，經原始日耳曼語（*mikilaz），上溯至原始印歐語（*meǵh₂-）「大」。另見（mickle、muckle）。

senses.definition: A large amount or great extent; a lot.

examples.text: I didn't know he drank so much.
examples.translation: 我不知道他喝那麼多酒。

etymology.text: From Middle English muche (“much, great”), apocopated variant of muchel (“much, great”), from Old English myċel, miċel (“big, much”), from Proto-West Germanic *mikil, from Proto-Germanic *mikilaz (“great, many, much”), from Proto-Indo-European *meǵh₂- (“big, stour, great”). See also mickle, muckle.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（muche）「多、大」，是（muchel）的詞尾脫落形式，來自古英語（miċel）「大、多」，經原始日耳曼語（*mikilaz），上溯至原始印歐語（*meǵh₂-）「大」。另見（mickle、muckle）。

senses.definition: Frequently; many times on different occasions.

examples.text: Alexandre often goes to the supermarket.
examples.translation: 亞歷山大常去超市。

examples.text: Teenagers often wear strange clothes.
examples.translation: 年輕人常穿怪衣服。

examples.text: Ann often plays tennis after school.
examples.translation: 安常常在放學後打網球。

examples.text: Tom often doesn't keep his promises.
examples.translation: 湯姆經常不守約。

examples.text: I often play football after school.
examples.translation: 我常常在放學後踢足球。

examples.text: More often than not, she had to go in person.
examples.translation: 很多時候她要親自去。

etymology.text: From Middle English often, alteration (with final -n added due to analogy with Middle English selden (“seldom”)) of Middle English ofte, oft, from Old English oft (“often”), from Proto-Germanic *ufta, *uftō (“often”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（often），是中古英語（ofte、oft）的變體（因類比 selden「很少」而加上字尾 -n），來自古英語（oft）「經常」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*ufta）。

senses.definition: To a great extent or degree.
Nobly; magnanimously.

examples.text: Japan is greatly famous for earthquakes.
Welcoming new ideas matters greatly.
Your help is greatly appreciated.
The north differs greatly from the south.
examples.translation: 南方和北方的差異很大。

examples.text: We were all greatly amused by his jokes.
examples.translation: 我們都被他的笑話逗得很開心。

examples.text: The number of tourists has increased greatly in recent years.
examples.translation: 近年的遊客數量大幅增加。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English gretly. By surface analysis, great + -ly.

senses.definition: Used to issue an instruction (traditionally seen as carrying less force of authority than alternatives such as 'shall' or 'must').
Used to give advice or opinion that an action is, or would have been, beneficial or desirable.
In questions, asks what is correct, proper, desirable, etc.
Indicates that something is expected to have happened or to be the case now.
To suggest (that someone ought to do something, or that something ought to be the case) by, or as if by, using the word should.
With verbs such as 'see' or 'hear', usually in the second person, used to point out something remarkable in either a good or bad way.
Will be likely to (become or do something); indicates a degree of possibility or probability that the stated thing will happen or be true in the future.
Used to form a variant of the present subjunctive, expressing a state or action that is hypothetical, potential, mandated, etc.
Used to express a conditional outcome.
Used to impart a tentative, conjectural or polite nuance.
Used to express what the speaker would do in another person's situation, as a means of giving a suggestion or recommendation.

examples.text: Beginners should learn spoken English first.
examples.translation: 初學者應先學習口說英語。

examples.text: You should learn to restrain yourself.
examples.translation: 你應該學習控制自己的情緒。

examples.text: You should have attended the meeting.
examples.translation: 你應該參加這個會議的。

examples.text: Children should drink milk every day.
examples.translation: 孩子們應該每天喝牛奶。

examples.text: You should have introduced yourself.
examples.translation: 你本來應該介紹自己的。

examples.text: You should make better use of your free time.
examples.translation: 你要更好地利用閒暇時間。

etymology.text: From Middle English scholde, from Old English sċolde, first and third person preterite form of sċulan (“should,” “have to,” “to owe”), the ancestor of English shall. By surface analysis, shall + -ed. Cognate with German sollte, Gothic 𐍃𐌺𐌿𐌻𐌳𐌰 (skulda), Swedish skulle. Related to Middle English shild and shildy.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（scholde），來自古英語（sċolde），是（sċulan）「應該、必須、欠」的第一及第三人稱過去式，即英語（shall）的前身。與德語（sollte）、瑞典語（skulle）同源。

senses.definition: Something that ought to be the case as opposed to already being the case.

examples.text: Food should be chewed before being swallowed.
examples.translation: 食物在吞嚥前要經過咀嚼。

examples.text: According to custom, the bride should be compliant.
examples.translation: 根據習俗，新娘應該循規蹈矩。

etymology.text: From Middle English scholde, from Old English sċolde, first and third person preterite form of sċulan (“should,” “have to,” “to owe”), the ancestor of English shall. By surface analysis, shall + -ed. Cognate with German sollte, Gothic 𐍃𐌺𐌿𐌻𐌳𐌰 (skulda), Swedish skulle. Related to Middle English shild and shildy.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（scholde），來自古英語（sċolde），是（sċulan）「應該、必須、欠」的第一及第三人稱過去式，即英語（shall）的前身。與德語（sollte）、瑞典語（skulle）同源。

senses.definition: To wish for or desire (something); to feel a need or desire for; to crave, hanker, or demand.
To make it easy or tempting to do something undesirable, or to make it hard or challenging to refrain from doing it.
To wish, desire, or demand to see, have the presence of or do business with.
To desire (to experience desire); to wish.
To be advised to do or aim for something (compare should, ought).
To lack and be in need of or require (something, such as a noun or verbal noun).
To desire a romantic or (especially) sexual relationship with someone; to lust for.
To have occasion for (something requisite or useful); to require or need.
To be lacking or deficient or absent.
To be in a state of destitution; to be needy; to lack.
To lack and be without, to not have (something).
To lack and perhaps be able or willing to do without.

examples.text: I've always wanted to meet you.
examples.translation: 我一直想見你。

examples.text: Thousands of people wanted to know the answer.
examples.translation: 成千上萬的人想要知道答案。

examples.text: I don't want there to be any misunderstanding.
examples.translation: 我不想有任何誤會。

examples.text: I don't want to participate in the ceremony.
examples.translation: 我不想參加典禮。

examples.text: I have a ball-point pen, but I want another.
examples.translation: 我有一支圓珠筆，可是我還想再要一支。

examples.text: He did everything to be able to survive, hence he never wants to talk about it.
examples.translation: 他為了活下去竭盡全力，所以他從來不想談起這件事。

etymology.text: From Middle English wanten (“to lack, to need”), from Old Norse vanta (“to lack”), from Proto-Germanic *wanatōną (“to be wanting, lack”), from *wanô (“lack, deficiency”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁weh₂- (“empty”). Cognate with Middle High German wan (“not full, empty”), Middle Dutch wan (“empty, poor”), Old English wana (“want, lack, absence, deficiency”), Latin vanus (“empty”). See wan, wan-.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（wanten）「缺乏、需要」，來自古諾斯語（vanta）「缺乏」，經原始日耳曼語（*wanatōną），來自（*wanô）「缺乏」，上溯至原始印歐語（*h₁weh₂-）「空的」。與拉丁語（vanus）「空的」同源。

senses.definition: A desire, wish, longing.
Lack, absence, deficiency.
Poverty.
Something needed or desired; a thing of which the loss is felt.
A depression in coal strata, hollowed out before the subsequent deposition took place.
A mole (Talpa europea).

examples.text: Everybody wants to sit beside her.
examples.translation: 大家都想坐在她旁邊。

examples.text: Amy wants something new to wear.
examples.translation: 艾美想穿戴新的衣物。

examples.text: I want something cold to drink.
examples.translation: 我想喝冷飲。

examples.text: I don't think any more students want to come.
examples.translation: 我覺得不會有更多學生想來了。

examples.text: I want a compact car with an air conditioner.
examples.translation: 我想要一輛有冷氣的小型車。

examples.text: Most people only want to hear their own truth.

etymology.text: From Middle English how, hou, hu, hwu, from Old English hū, from Proto-West Germanic *hwō, from Proto-Germanic *hwō (“through what, how”), from the same root as hwæt (“who, what”). /hw/ > /h/ due to wh-cluster reduction in Old English; compare who, which underwent this change later, and thus is spelt wh (Middle English spelling of /hw/) but pronounced /h/ (it previously had a different vowel, hence avoided the spelling and sound change in Old English). Vowel change per Great Vowel Shift.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（how、hou），來自古英語（hū），經原始日耳曼語（*hwō）「如何」，與（hwæt）「什麼」同一詞根。古英語時期字首音簡化，後經母音大推移改變讀音。

senses.definition: In, on, or at this place (a place perceived to be close to the speaker); compare there.

In this matter.
Notionally at the speaker's location by virtue of happening now.
In this context.

To go or come down; to descend.

etymology.text: From Middle English betwene, from Old English betwēonum (“between, among”, dative plural, literally “by the two, near both”), from Proto-Germanic *bi- (“be-”) + *twīhnaz (“two each”), corresponding to be- + twain. examples.translation: 你這些想法是與現實脫節的。

etymology.text: From French réalité (“quality of being real”), from Middle French realité (“property, possession”), from Medieval Latin reālitās, from Late Latin reālis (“real”), equivalent to real + -ity. Recorded since 1550 as a legal term in the sense of “fixed property” (compare real estate, realty); the sense “real existence” is attested from 1647. First attested in c. 1540.

senses.definition: To engage the attention of; to awaken interest in; to excite emotion or passion in, in behalf of a person or thing.
To be concerned with or engaged in; to affect; to concern; to excite.
To cause or permit to share.

examples.text: She is a particularily interesting person.
examples.translation: 她是一個非常有意思的人.

examples.text: Are you interested in foreign languages?
examples.translation: 你們對外語感興趣嗎？

examples.text: Yoko is interested in collecting stamps.
examples.translation: 洋子有收集郵票的興趣。

examples.text: What subject do you think he is interested in?
examples.translation: 你覺得他會對什麼主題感興趣？

examples.text: To what degree are you interested in baseball?
examples.translation: 你喜歡棒球到什麼程度？

examples.text: I'm not the least bit interested in physics.
examples.translation: 我對物理學完全沒有興趣。

etymology.text: From Middle English interest, from Old French interesse and interest (French intérêt), from Medieval Latin interesse, from Latin interesse.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（interest），來自古法語（interesse、interest），來自中世紀拉丁語（interesse），再來自拉丁語（interesse）「在中間、有關係」。

senses.definition: To return to its owner.

examples.text: The moment Pip saw its owner come home, it excitedly wagged its tail.
examples.translation: 皮皮一看到主人回家，就興奮地搖尾巴。

etymology.text: From Middle English hōm, from Old English hām, from Proto-West Germanic *haim, from Proto-Germanic *haimaz (“home, village”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱóymos (“village, home”), from the root *tḱey-. Doublet of heyem.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（hōm），來自古英語（hām），經原始日耳曼語（*haimaz）「家、村莊」，上溯至原始印歐語（*ḱóymos）「村莊、家」。

senses.definition: Of, from, or pertaining to one’s dwelling or country; domestic; not foreign.
Relating to the home team (the team at whose venue a game is played).
That strikes home; direct, pointed.
Personal, intimate.

examples.text: I am not looking forward to going to university abroad - I will feel intense nostalgia for my home town.
examples.translation: 我不太期待出國念大學，我會非常想念家鄉。

examples.text: If our last batter had not hit a home run, team would have lost the game.
examples.translation: 要不是最後一棒打出全壘打，球隊就輸了。

etymology.text: From Middle English hōm, from Old English hām, from Proto-West Germanic *haim, from Proto-Germanic *haimaz (“home, village”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱóymos (“village, home”), from the root *tḱey-. Doublet of heyem.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（hōm），來自古英語（hām），經原始日耳曼語（*haimaz）「家、村莊」，上溯至原始印歐語（*ḱóymos）「村莊、家」。

senses.definition: To one's place of residence or one's customary or official location.
To one's place of birth.
To the place where it belongs; to the end of a course; to the full length.
To the home page.
At or in one's place of residence or one's customary or official location; at home.
To a full and intimate degree; to the heart of the matter; fully, directly.
into the goal
into the right, proper or stowed position

examples.text: Jim's father always comes home late.
examples.translation: 吉姆的父親總是很晚才回家。

examples.text: She doesn't speak Japanese at home.
examples.translation: 她在家不說日語。

examples.text: Were your mother and father home?
examples.translation: 你父母親在家嗎？

examples.text: Kate made her family leave home.
examples.translation: 凱特使她的家人離家出走。

examples.text: Does your father get home early?
examples.translation: 你爸爸很早回家嗎？

examples.text: The fire broke out after the staff went home.
examples.translation: 在全體職員回家後，火事爆發了。

etymology.text: From Middle English hōm, from Old English hām, from Proto-West Germanic *haim, from Proto-Germanic *haimaz (“home, village”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱóymos (“village, home”), from the root *tḱey-. Doublet of heyem.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（hōm），來自古英語（hām），經原始日耳曼語（*haimaz）「家、村莊」，上溯至原始印歐語（*ḱóymos）「村莊、家」。

senses.definition: To relate details of (an event or incident); to recount, describe (something).
To repeat (something one has heard), to retell; to pass on, convey (a message, information etc.).
To notify someone of (particular intelligence, suspicions, illegality, misconduct etc.); to make notification to relevant authorities; to submit a formal report of.
Of a ship, to return to a port.
To take oneself (to someone or something) for guidance or support; to appeal.
To make a formal statement, especially of complaint, about (someone).
To show up or appear at an appointed time; to present oneself.
To write news reports (for); to cover as a journalist or reporter.
To be accountable to or subordinate to (someone) in a hierarchy; to receive orders from (someone); to give official updates to (someone who is above oneself in a hierarchy).
To return or present as the result of an examination or consideration of any matter officially referred.
To take minutes of (a speech, the doings of a public body, etc.); to write down from the lips of a speaker.
To refer.
To return or repeat, as sound; to echo.

examples.text: He felt compelled to report the incident.
examples.translation: 他覺得必須報道這件事。

examples.text: They reported seeing the incident.
examples.translation: 他們報告目擊了事故。

examples.text: Tom wasted our time reporting a lot of irrelevant details.
examples.translation: 湯姆報告了一堆無關的細節，浪費我們的時間。

examples.text: How long did it take you to write this report?
examples.translation: 你寫這份報告花了多長時間？

examples.text: Pei-rong, can I take a look at your report for reference?
examples.translation: 佩蓉，你那份報告可以借我參考一下嗎？

relations.native: 度假勝地、度假村、渡假村
度假勝地、度假村、渡假村

etymology.text: From Middle English reporten, from Anglo-Norman reporter, from Latin reportāre (“to carry back, return, remit, refer”), from re- + portāre.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（reporten），來自英法語（reporter），來自拉丁語（reportāre）「帶回、送回、提及」，由「回」（re-）加「搬運」（portāre）組成。

senses.definition: In a direction away from the speaker or other reference point.
Into a state of non-operation or non-existence.
So as to remove or separate, or be removed or separated.
Specifying the number of some item in bills, parts lists, etc.
Offstage.
Used in various other ways specific to individual idiomatic phrases, e.g. bring off, show off, put off, tell off, etc. See the entry for the individual phrase.
senses.native: （用於各種片語，如 show off、put off）

examples.text: Everyone paired off and began dancing.
examples.translation: 眾人紛紛結伴跳起了舞來。

examples.text: The baseball game was called off due to rain.
examples.translation: 棒球比賽因為天雨取消了。

examples.text: We have to put off the game till next Sunday.
examples.translation: 我們不得不把遊戲擱到下週日了。

etymology.text: From Middle English of, from Old English of, af, æf (“from, off, away”), from Proto-West Germanic *ab, from Proto-Germanic *ab (“from”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epo (“from, off, back”). Doublet of of.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（of），來自古英語（of、af）「從、離開」，經原始日耳曼語（*ab），上溯至原始印歐語（*h₂epo）「從、離開」。與（of）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: Inoperative, disabled.
Cancelled; not happening.
Not fitted; not being worn.
Not correct; not properly formed; not logical, harmonious, etc.
Inappropriate; untoward.
Less than normal, in temperament or in result.
Designating a time when one is not performing to the best of one's abilities.
Rancid, rotten, gone bad.
Disgusting, repulsive, abhorrent.
Circumstanced.
Started on the way.
Far; off to the side.
Temporarily not attending a usual place, such as work or school, especially owing to illness or holiday.
Designating a time when one is not strictly attentive to business or affairs, or is absent from a post, and, hence, a time when affairs are not urgent.
Presently unavailable. (of a dish on a menu)
On the side furthest from the kerb (the right-hand side if one drives on the left).
In, or towards the half of the field away from the batsman's legs; the right side for a right-handed batsman.
senses.native: 離打者腳部較遠的那半場

senses.definition: Offsuit.

examples.translation: 把電視關掉。我無法專心。

examples.translation: 這個氣體散發出強烈難聞的氣味。

examples.text: He lost his balance and fell off his bicycle.
examples.translation: 他失去了平衡，從腳踏車上摔了下來。

examples.text: Excuse me, I have to get off at the next stop.
examples.translation: 對不起，我要在下一站下。

examples.text: He lost his balance and fell off the ladder.
examples.translation: 他失去了平衡，從梯子上摔了下來。

examples.text: The unclaimed items were sold off at auction.
examples.translation: 無人領取的物品被拍賣了。

etymology.text: From Middle English of, from Old English of, af, æf (“from, off, away”), from Proto-West Germanic *ab, from Proto-Germanic *ab (“from”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epo (“from, off, back”). Doublet of of.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（of），來自古英語（of、af）「從、離開」，經原始日耳曼語（*ab），上溯至原始印歐語（*h₂epo）「從、離開」。與（of）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: Not positioned upon; away from a position upon.
Detached, separated, excluded or disconnected from; away from a position of attachment or connection to.
Outside the area or region of.
Temporarily not attending (a usual place), especially owing to illness or holiday.
senses.native: （因病或休假）沒去（平常的地方）

senses.definition: Used to indicate the location or direction of one thing relative to another, implying adjacency or accessibility via.
Used to express location at sea relative to land or mainland.
Used to indicate separation from a natural home or origin.
Removed or subtracted from.
No longer wanting or taking.
Out of the possession of.
Placed after a number (of products or parts, as if a unit), in commerce or engineering.
Under the influence of.
As a result of; resulting from the actions of.

examples.text: I am taking tomorrow afternoon off.

examples.text: We've been off the grid for three days now.

etymology.text: From Middle English of, from Old English of, af, æf (“from, off, away”), from Proto-West Germanic *ab, from Proto-Germanic *ab (“from”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epo (“from, off, back”). Doublet of of.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（of），來自古英語（of、af）「從、離開」，經原始日耳曼語（*ab），上溯至原始印歐語（*h₂epo）「從、離開」。與（of）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: Beginning; starting point.

examples.text: Mary started taking her clothes off.
examples.translation: 瑪麗開始脫衣服了。

examples.translation: 牆上的紙漸漸脫落了。

etymology.text: From Middle English of, from Old English of, af, æf (“from, off, away”), from Proto-West Germanic *ab, from Proto-Germanic *ab (“from”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epo (“from, off, back”). Doublet of of.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（of），來自古英語（of、af）「從、離開」，經原始日耳曼語（*ab），上溯至原始印歐語（*h₂epo）「從、離開」。與（of）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: To appear; to look outwardly; to be perceived as.
To befit; to beseem.

examples.text: Picasso's paintings seem strange to me.
examples.translation: 畢加索的畫對我來說似乎很奇怪。

examples.text: This clock seems to be malfunctioning.
examples.translation: 這個時鐘似乎壞了。

examples.text: It seems that something has happened.
examples.translation: 似乎發生了什麼事。

examples.text: It seems that he knows everything.
examples.translation: 他似乎什麼都知道。

examples.text: Tom didn't seem to be intimidated.
examples.translation: 湯姆似乎沒有被嚇到。

examples.text: My brother seems to enjoy himself at college.
examples.translation: 我弟弟似乎在大學過得很愉快。

etymology.text: From Middle English semen (“to seem, befit, be becoming”), from Old Norse sœma (“to conform to, beseem, befit”), from Proto-Germanic *sōmijaną (“to unite, fit”), from Proto-Indo-European *sem- (“one; whole”). Cognate with Scots seme (“to be fitting; beseem”), Danish sømme (“to beseem”), Old Swedish søma, Faroese søma (“to be proper”). Related also to Old Norse sómi (“honour”) ( > archaic Danish somme (“decent comportment”)), Old Norse sœmr (“fitting, seemly”), Old English sēman (“to reconcile, b
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（semen）「似乎、適合」，來自古諾斯語（sœma）「符合、適合」，經原始日耳曼語（*sōmijaną）「結合、適合」，上溯至原始印歐語（*sem-）「一、整體」。

senses.definition: As it appears; apparently.
In a seemly manner; decorously; with propriety.

examples.text: Lorenzo was seemingly following Melissa.
Lajos was seemingly expecting candy.
There was nothing seemingly there.
Seemingly, I have not clearly explained myself.
People will seemingly believe anything nowadays.
Seemingly impossible things sometimes happen.

etymology.text: From Middle English semyngly, equivalent to seeming + -ly.

senses.definition: Introducing a complete question.
With a negative, used rhetorically to make a suggestion.
senses.native: （與否定詞連用，提出建議）何不

senses.definition: Introducing a verb phrase (bare infinitive clause).
Introducing a noun or other phrase.
For which cause, reason, or purpose.
The cause, reason, or purpose for which.

examples.text: Why couldn't you come on Saturday?
examples.translation: 為什麼你星期六來不了？

examples.text: Why don't we have lunch together?
examples.translation: 為什麼我們不一起吃午飯呢？

examples.text: Why didn't you read the magazine?
examples.translation: 你為什麼不讀這雜誌呢？

examples.text: Why are you feigning innocence?!
examples.translation: 為什麼你假裝無辜！

examples.text: Why were you late this morning?
examples.translation: 今天早上你為什麼遲到了呢?

examples.text: Why did you get such a costly dictionary?
examples.translation: 為什麼你買了一本那麼貴的詞典？

etymology.text: From Middle English why, from Old English hwȳ (“why”), from Proto-Germanic *hwī (“by what, how”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷey, instrumental case of *kʷís (“who”), *kʷid (“what”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（why），來自古英語（hwȳ）「為什麼」，經原始日耳曼語（*hwī）「藉由什麼、如何」，上溯至原始印歐語（*kʷey），是（*kʷís）「誰」的工具格。

senses.definition: By which.
Where, wherein, in which.
By what, in which direction; how.

examples.text: Castling is a special move in chess whereby a rook is transferred to the square crossed by the king.
Scientists say a new geologic epoch has begun whereby humans are causing major damage to global water systems.

Whereby goest thou?

etymology.text: From where + by.

senses.definition: A reason, explanation, or excuse which someone believes provides convincing, morally acceptable support for behavior or for a belief or occurrence.
The forgiveness of sin.
The alignment of text to the left margin (left justification), the right margin (right justification), or both margins (full justification).

examples.text: He was punished with justification.
That's a very flimsy justification.
I can't find any justification for your actions.
There's no justification for his behavior.
The justification is worse than the act.
The justifications for some wars are sheer absurdity.

etymology.text: From Middle English justificacioun, justification, from Middle French justification, from Late Latin iustificationem, justificationem < iustificatio, from iustifico, from Latin iustus.

senses.definition: To continue in (a course or mode of action); to not intermit or fall from; to uphold or maintain.
To maintain possession of.
To maintain the condition of; to preserve in a certain state.
To raise; to care for.
To remain faithful to a given promise or word.
To record transactions, accounts, or events in.
To enter (accounts, records, etc.) in a book.
To restrain.
To watch over, look after, guard, protect.
To supply with necessities and financially support (a person).
To refrain from freely disclosing (a secret).
To maintain (an establishment or institution); to conduct; to manage.
To have habitually in stock for sale.
To continue.
To remain edible or otherwise usable.
To remain in a state.
To remain in; to be confined to.
To reside for a time; to lodge; to dwell.
To have rooms at college, at the University of Cambridge.
To wait for, keep watch for.

examples.text: Keep this information under your hat.
examples.translation: 不要把這些資料洩露出去。

examples.text: Yumi keeps getting better at Korean.
examples.translation: 由美的韓語越來越好了。

examples.text: She kept me waiting for 30 minutes.
examples.translation: 她讓我等了30分鐘。

examples.text: Helen always keeps her room clean.
examples.translation: 海倫的房間一直很乾淨。

examples.text: If you want to keep meat for long, freeze it.
examples.translation: 如果你想把肉類保存久一點，就要把它們放進冰箱裡冷藏。

examples.text: He fell into the habit of keeping late hours.
examples.translation: 他養成了熬夜的習慣。

etymology.text: From Middle English kepen (“to keep, guard, look after, watch”), from Old English cēpan (“to seize, hold, observe”), from Proto-West Germanic *kōpijan, from Proto-Germanic *kōpijaną (“to look, heed, watch, observe”) (compare West Frisian kypje (“to look”)), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵab-, *ǵāb- (“to look after”) (compare Lithuanian žẽbti (“to eat reluctantly”), Russian забо́та (zabóta, “care, worry”)).

The state of being kept; hence, the resulting condition; case.
A cap for holding something, such as a journal box, in place.
The main tower of a castle or fortress, located within the castle walls.
The act or office of keeping; custody; guard; care; heed; charge; notice.
That which is kept in charge; a charge.
A mistress (the other woman in an extramarital relationship, generally including sexual relations).

etymology.text: From Middle English kepen (“to keep, guard, look after, watch”), from Old English cēpan (“to seize, hold, observe”), from Proto-West Germanic *kōpijan, from Proto-Germanic *kōpijaną (“to look, heed, watch, observe”) (compare West Frisian kypje (“to look”)), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵab-, *ǵāb- (“to look after”) (compare Lithuanian žẽbti (“to eat reluctantly”), Russian забо́та (zabóta, “care, worry”)).

senses.definition: Used to indicate a desired past action that was not done.

senses.definition: Used to indicate conditional or possible actions; would perhaps/maybe.
Used concessively to admit something before making a more accurate or important statement; although
Used to express certainty.
Used in polite requests for permission.

examples.text: Something might have happened to her.
examples.translation: 她可能出什麼事了。

examples.text: Tom might be studying French now.
examples.translation: 湯姆現在可能在學習法文。

examples.text: We might have misunderstood her.
examples.translation: 我們可能誤解她了。

examples.text: I might have forgotten my keys.

etymology.native: 源自中古英語（might、myght），來自古英語（miht）「能力、力量、美德」，經原始日耳曼語（*mahtiz），上溯至原始印歐語（*megʰ-）「能夠」，相當於（may + -th）。

senses.definition: A type, race or category; a group of entities that have common characteristics such that they may be grouped together.

Goods or services used as payment, as e.g. in barter.
Equivalent means used as response to an action.
Each of the two elements of the communion service, bread and wine.
The type of a type constructor or a higher-order type operator.
Food in a particular category.
One's inherent nature; character, natural disposition.
Family, lineage.
Manner.

examples.text: You know I would never do that kind of thing.
examples.translation: 你知道我絕不會做那種事。

examples.text: Forgiving others is a kind deed to yourself.

etymology.text: From Middle English kynde, kinde, from Old English cynd, ġecynd (“inherent nature, disposition, kind, gender, generation, race”), from Proto-West Germanic *kundi, from Proto-Germanic *kinþiz, related to Proto-Germanic *kunją (“race, kin”) and Old English cennan (“to bear, give birth”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（kynde），來自古英語（ġecynd）「本性、種類、性別、世代、種族」，經原始日耳曼語（*kinþiz），與（*kunją）「種族、親屬」及古英語（cennan）「生育」相關。

senses.definition: Having a benevolent, courteous, friendly, generous, gentle, liberal, sympathetic, or warm-hearted nature or disposition, marked by consideration for – and service to – others.
Affectionate.
Favorable.
Mild, gentle, forgiving
Gentle; tractable; easily governed.
Characteristic of the species; belonging to one's nature; natural; native.

examples.text: This month was kind of difficult.
examples.translation: 這個月我過得有點艱難。

examples.text: She was feeling kind of tired.
examples.translation: 她覺得有點累了。

examples.text: She was very kind to everyone.
examples.translation: 她對大家都很親切。

examples.text: He was kind enough to take me to the hospital.
examples.translation: 他好心地把我送到醫院。

examples.text: He was bathed in the warmth of the kind light.
examples.translation: 親切的燈光讓他的身上充滿了溫暖的感覺。

examples.text: It was very kind of you to lend me an umbrella.
examples.translation: 你借給我傘真好。

etymology.text: From Middle English kynde, kinde, from Old English cynd, ġecynd (“inherent nature, disposition, kind, gender, generation, race”), from Proto-West Germanic *kundi, from Proto-Germanic *kinþiz, related to Proto-Germanic *kunją (“race, kin”) and Old English cennan (“to bear, give birth”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（kynde），來自古英語（ġecynd）「本性、種類、性別、世代、種族」，經原始日耳曼語（*kinþiz），與（*kunją）「種族、親屬」及古英語（cennan）「生育」相關。

senses.definition: For all of a given time interval; throughout; in; pending.
At any time or period within a given time interval or while a given event is ongoing.

examples.text: I did nothing during the holidays.
examples.translation: 在假期中我無所事事。

examples.text: There is no school during August.
examples.translation: 8月份沒課。

examples.text: Talking during a concert is rude.
examples.translation: 在音樂會中說話是不禮貌的。

examples.text: Tom dozed off during the meeting.
examples.translation: 湯姆在會議期間打瞌睡。

examples.text: You can't chatter during class.
examples.translation: 上課時不能閒聊。

examples.text: Many people go abroad during summer vacation.
examples.translation: 許多年輕人在暑假時出國。

etymology.text: From Middle English during, durynge, durinde, durand, durende, present participle of duren (“to last”), equivalent to dure + -ing. Compare Dutch gedurende (“during”). More at dure.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（during），是（duren）「持續」的現在分詞，相當於（dure + -ing）。比較荷蘭語（gedurende）「在……期間」。

senses.definition: To bring into a group, class, set, or total as a (new) part or member.
To consider as part of something; to comprehend.
To use a directive that allows the use of source code from another file.
senses.native: （程式）引入（其他檔案的原始碼）

senses.definition: To enclose, confine.
To conclude; to terminate.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Is breakfast included?
examples.translation: 包括早飯嗎？

examples.text: Futurology includes notions of probabilities.
examples.translation: 未來學包含機率的概念。

examples.text: Tom speaks five languages, including Russian.
examples.translation: 湯姆會說五種語言，包括俄語。

examples.text: The class of forty includes eighteen girls.
examples.translation: 四十人的班級當中有十八位女生。

examples.text: The woodwind section includes both pipes and reeds.
examples.translation: 木管樂器組中包含無簧片管樂器與簧片管樂器。

examples.text: The price does not include the box.
examples.translation: 這個價格不包含這個箱子。

etymology.text: From Middle English includen, borrowed from Latin inclūdere (“to shut in, enclose, insert”), from in- (“in”) + claudere (“to shut”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂w- (“key, hook, nail”). Doublet of enclose. Displaced native Old English belūcan (“to include,” also “to shut in”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（includen），借自拉丁語（inclūdere）「關在裡面、圍住」，由「在內」（in-）加「關閉」（claudere）組成，上溯至原始印歐語（*kleh₂w-）「鑰匙、鉤」。與（enclose）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: To review materials already learned in order to make sure one does not forget them, usually in preparation for an examination.
To take a course or courses on a subject.
To acquire knowledge on a subject with the intention of applying it in practice.
To look at carefully and minutely.
To fix the mind closely upon a subject; to dwell upon anything in thought; to muse; to ponder.
To endeavor diligently; to be zealous.

examples.text: He studied hard in order to get into college.
examples.translation: 他努力學習，為的是能夠考上大學。

examples.text: Biologists study living things.
examples.translation: 生物學家研究生物。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English studien, from Old French estudier (Modern French étudier), from estudie (noun), borrowed from Latin studium. Displaced Old English cneordlæcan.
etymology.native: 承襲自中古英語（studien），來自古法語（estudier），來自名詞（estudie），借自拉丁語（studium）「熱心、學習」。取代了古英語的（cneordlæcan）。

senses.definition: Forming a circle or closed curve containing (something).
Following a path which curves near an object, with the object on the inside of the curve.
Centred upon; surrounding; regarding.
Following the perimeter of a specified area and returning to the starting point.
Near; in the vicinity of; approximately.
At or to various places within or throughout.
So as to avoid something.

examples.text: There has been a lot of controversy around the handling of personal information.
examples.translation: 個人資料的處理方式引起很多爭議。

examples.text: We walked around the football field.
examples.translation: 我們繞著足球場走。

etymology.text: From Middle English around, arounde, from a- (from Old English a- (“on, at”)) + Middle English round (“circle, round”) borrowed from French, equivalent to a- + round. Cognate with Scots aroond, aroon (“around”). Displaced earlier Middle English umbe, embe (“around”) (from Old English ymbe (“around”)).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（around），由字首（a-）「在」加中古英語借自法語的（round）「圓」構成。取代了較早的中古英語（umbe）「周圍」。

senses.definition: Alive; existing.
Present in the vicinity.

examples.text: He pretends to be enthusiastic when his boss is around.
examples.translation: 老闆在的時候他就裝成一副很熱心的樣子。

etymology.text: From Middle English around, arounde, from a- (from Old English a- (“on, at”)) + Middle English round (“circle, round”) borrowed from French, equivalent to a- + round. Cognate with Scots aroond, aroon (“around”). Displaced earlier Middle English umbe, embe (“around”) (from Old English ymbe (“around”)).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（around），由字首（a-）「在」加中古英語借自法語的（round）「圓」構成。取代了較早的中古英語（umbe）「周圍」。

senses.definition: So as to form a circle or trace a circular path, or approximation thereof.
So as to surround or be near.
Nearly; approximately; about.
From place to place.
From one state or condition to an opposite or very different one; with a metaphorical change in direction; bringing about awareness or agreement.
So as to partially or completely rotate; so as to face in the opposite direction.
Used with verbs to indicate repeated or continuous action, or in numerous locations or with numerous people.
Used with certain verbs to suggest unproductive activity.
senses.native: （與某些動詞連用）閒晃；無所事事

examples.text: Can we meet February 28, around 3:00 pm?
examples.translation: 我們可以在二月二十八日三時左右見面嗎？

examples.text: How about February 28th around 3:00 pm?
examples.translation: 2月28號下午3點怎麼樣？

examples.text: Christmas is right around the corner.
examples.translation: 聖誕節快到了。

examples.text: Don't leave your things lying around.
examples.translation: 別把東西亂放。

examples.text: The teacher gathered his students around him.
examples.translation: 老師把他的學生們聚集在他周圍。

examples.text: The fog began to disappear around ten o'clock.
examples.translation: 霧在十時左右開始散了。

etymology.text: From Middle English around, arounde, from a- (from Old English a- (“on, at”)) + Middle English round (“circle, round”) borrowed from French, equivalent to a- + round. Cognate with Scots aroond, aroon (“around”). Displaced earlier Middle English umbe, embe (“around”) (from Old English ymbe (“around”)).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（around），由字首（a-）「在」加中古英語借自法語的（round）「圓」構成。取代了較早的中古英語（umbe）「周圍」。

senses.definition: Continuously during that period of time.
At certain points during that period of time.
senses.native: 在那段期間的某些時候

examples.text: I'd known her only since the previous year, so from/since the moment we got married we’ve quarrelled.
examples.translation: 我從前一年才認識她，所以從結婚那一刻起我們就一直吵架。

etymology.text: From Middle English syns, synnes, contraction of earlier sithens, sithence, from sithen (“after, since”) ( + -s, adverbial genitive suffix), from Old English sīþþan, from the phrase sīþ þǣm (“after/since that (time)”), from sīþ (“since, after”) + þǣm dative singular of þæt. Cognate with Dutch sinds (“since”), German seit (“since”), Danish siden (“since”), Icelandic síðan (“since”) Scots syne (“since”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（syns），是較早的（sithens）的縮略形式，來自（sithen）「之後、自從」加副詞字尾，來自古英語（sīþþan），源於片語「在那之後」（sīþ þǣm）。與荷蘭語（sinds）、德語（seit）同源。

senses.definition: From the time that.
Because.
When or that.

examples.text: It's been ten years since we last met.
examples.translation: 我們離上次見面有十年了。

etymology.text: From Middle English syns, synnes, contraction of earlier sithens, sithence, from sithen (“after, since”) ( + -s, adverbial genitive suffix), from Old English sīþþan, from the phrase sīþ þǣm (“after/since that (time)”), from sīþ (“since, after”) + þǣm dative singular of þæt. Cognate with Dutch sinds (“since”), German seit (“since”), Danish siden (“since”), Icelandic síðan (“since”) Scots syne (“since”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（syns），是較早的（sithens）的縮略形式，來自（sithen）「之後、自從」加副詞字尾，來自古英語（sīþþan），源於片語「在那之後」（sīþ þǣm）。與荷蘭語（sinds）、德語（seit）同源。

senses.definition: Increasing in amount or intensity.

examples.text: Managing your time is increasingly important.
China is increasingly greening its highways.
People are becoming increasingly inhumane.
We feel increasingly alienated from our work.
As a society, we are increasingly overweight.
The situation became increasingly dangerous.

etymology.text: From Middle English encreessingli, equivalent to increasing + -ly.

senses.definition: A shift (scheduled work period) that takes place early in the day.

examples.text: Bob met her grandfather early in the morning.
examples.translation: 清晨，鮑勃遇見了她的祖父。

examples.text: I've always fed my dogs in the early evening.
examples.translation: 每個傍晚我都會餵我的狗狗們。

examples.text: Britain demarcated a semi-autonomous region of Transjordan from Palestine in the early 1920s.
examples.translation: 英國在 1920 年代初期從巴勒斯坦劃出外約旦半自治區。

etymology.text: From Middle English erly, erlich, earlich, from Old English ǣrlīċ (“early”, adjective), equivalent to ere + -ly.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（erly），來自古英語（ǣrlīċ）「早的」，相當於「之前」加字尾（ere + -ly）。

senses.definition: At a time before expected; sooner than usual.
Soon; in good time; seasonably.

examples.text: Tom expected to leave early in the morning, but he overslept.
examples.translation: 湯姆本想早上早點出發，結果卻睡過頭了。

examples.translation: 她到得很早。

etymology.text: From Middle English erly, erlich, earlich, from Old English ǣrlīċ (“early”, adjective), equivalent to ere + -ly.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（erly），來自古英語（ǣrlīċ）「早的」，相當於「之前」加字尾（ere + -ly）。

A set of equations involving the same variables, which are to be solved simultaneously.
A set of staves linked by a brace that indicate instruments or sounds that are to be played simultaneously.
A set of body organs having a particular function.
A set of alters of a person, or the multiple (“an individual with multiple personalities”) who contains them.
A system in which two or more objects are bound to each other by gravity.
A comprehensive and logically organized set of propositions or philosophical beliefs.
The mainstream culture, controlled by the elites or government of a state, or a combination of them, seen as oppressive to the individual.
A set of rules for a tabletop roleplaying game.
senses.native: （桌上角色扮演遊戲的）規則系統

senses.definition: A socioeconomic formation.
A method or way of organizing or planning.

examples.text: What is your favourite operating system?
examples.translation: 你最喜歡的作業系統是哪個？

examples.text: What's your favorite operating system?
examples.translation: 你最喜歡什麼作業系統？

examples.text: Linux is a free operating system; you should try it.
examples.translation: （Linux）是免費的作業系統，你應該試試看。

examples.text: Windows is the most used operating system in the world.
examples.translation: （Windows）是全世界最多人用的作業系統。

examples.translation: 摩天大廈裡的電梯是至關重要的。

examples.translation: 我不喜歡這個作業系統的頁面。

etymology.text: Partly borrowed from Middle French sisteme, systeme, partly directly from its etymon Late Latin systēma (“harmony; musical scale; set of celestial objects; set of troops; system”), from Ancient Greek σύστημα (sústēma, “musical scale; organized body; whole made of several parts or members”), from σῠνίστημῐ (sŭnístēmĭ, “to combine, organize”) + -μᾰ (-mă, resultative suffix). σῠνίστημῐ is from σῠν- (sŭn-, “with, together”) + ἵστημι (hístēmi, “to stand”), from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂- (“to stand
etymology.native: 部分借自中古法語（sisteme），部分直接來自後期拉丁語（systēma）「和諧、音階、天體、部隊、系統」，再來自古希臘語（sústēma）「音階、組織、由多部分組成的整體」，由「一起」（sŭn-）加「站立」（hístēmi）構成，上溯至原始印歐語（*steh₂-）「站」。

senses.definition: At all times; throughout all time; since the beginning.
Constantly during a certain period, or regularly at stated intervals (opposed to sometimes or occasionally).
if necessary, or if there is no better option; in any event.

examples.text: I'm always forgetting people's names.
examples.translation: 我總是忘記別人的名字。

examples.text: Jim's father always comes home late.
examples.translation: 吉姆的父親總是很晚才回家。

examples.text: He always wanted to study Japanese.
examples.translation: 他一直想學日語。

examples.text: Father always says, "Do your best."
examples.translation: 父親總是說「你盡力而為。」

examples.text: Mayuko always aims for perfection.
examples.translation: 麻由子總是追求完美。

examples.text: Life doesn't always go the way we want it to.
examples.translation: 生活並不總是如我們所願。

relations.native: 太陽打西邊出來（不可能的事）

etymology.text: From Middle English alweyes, alwayes, alweys, a variant of Middle English alwey, alway (“always”), from Old English ealneġ, ealne weġ (“always, perpetually”, literally “all the way, all the while, continuously”), from ealne + weġ (accusative case), equivalent to alway + -s. Cognate with Scots always (“always”), Low German allerwegens (“very often”, literally “all ways'”). More at all, way.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（alweyes），是（alwey）「總是」的變體，來自古英語（ealne weġ）「總是」，字面意思是「一路、整段時間」，相當於（alway）加（-s）。

senses.definition: (used of count nouns) each and all of the members of a group considered singly and without exception
each and all of a series of entities or intervals as specified

examples.text: Every child likes music.
examples.translation: 每個孩子都喜歡音樂。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English every, everich, everych, from Old English ǣfre ǣlċ, ǣfre ǣġhwelċ. By surface analysis, ever + each or ever + which.
etymology.native: 承襲自中古英語（every、everich），來自古英語（ǣfre ǣlċ）「永遠每一個」。表面上可拆成「曾經」加「每個」（ever + each）。

senses.definition: To take voluntarily (a child of other parents) to be in the place of, or as, one's own child.
To obtain (a pet) from a shelter or the wild.
To contribute towards the upkeep of (a child or animal), in exchange for occasional stories, pictures, etc.
To take by choice into the scope of one's responsibility.
To take or receive as one's own what is not so naturally.
To select and take or approve.
To beat an opponent ten times in a row.

examples.text: They adopted the little girl.
examples.translation: 他們收養了那個小女孩。

examples.text: We adopted a child.
examples.translation: 我們收養了一個孩子。

examples.text: Adopt his concepts.
examples.translation: 採用他的理念。

examples.text: I think it's better for us to adopt his plan.
examples.translation: 我認為採用他的計劃對我們比較好。

examples.text: If you can't have children, you could always adopt.
examples.translation: 如果你不能有孩子，你總能領養。

examples.text: My wife wants to adopt a child.
examples.translation: 我妻子想收養一個孩子。

etymology.text: From Middle French adopter, from Latin adoptō; ad + optō (“to choose, desire”), equivalent to ad- + opt.

senses.definition: Beneath; below; at or to the bottom of, or the area covered or surmounted by.
Below the surface of.
From one side of to the other, passing beneath.
Less than.
Subject to.
Subordinate to; subject to the control of; in accordance with; in compliance with.
Within the category, classification or heading of.
In the face of; in response to (some attacking force).
Using or adopting (a name, identity, etc.).

examples.text: We found some shade under a tree.
examples.translation: 我們在樹下找到一點陰涼。

etymology.text: From Middle English under, from Old English under, from Proto-West Germanic *undar, from Proto-Germanic *under, from a merger of Proto-Indo-European *(H)n̥dʰér (“under”) and *h₁entér (“inside”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語與古英語（under），經原始日耳曼語（*under），由原始印歐語的（*Hn̥dʰér）「在下」與（*h₁entér）「在內」合併而來。

senses.definition: The amount by which an actual total is less than the expected or required amount.
A bet that a particular sporting statistic, such as points scored in a game, will be below a certain stated value.
Something having a particular property that is low or too low.

etymology.text: From Middle English under, from Old English under, from Proto-West Germanic *undar, from Proto-Germanic *under, from a merger of Proto-Indo-European *(H)n̥dʰér (“under”) and *h₁entér (“inside”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語與古英語（under），經原始日耳曼語（*under），由原始印歐語的（*Hn̥dʰér）「在下」與（*h₁entér）「在內」合併而來。

senses.definition: A condition; a set of circumstances applying at any given time.
A sovereign country or city state with a central government acting as its head and operator; national issues and affairs as opposed to local ones.
A political division of a federation retaining a notable degree of autonomy, as in the United States, Mexico, Nigeria, or India.
A society larger than a tribe. A society large enough to form a state in the sense of a government.
An element of the range of the random variables that define a random process.
The lexical aspect (aktionsart) of verbs or predicates that do not change over time.
A complete description of a system, consisting of parameters that determine all properties of the system.
A mess; disorder; a bad condition or set of circumstances.
The stable condition of a processor during a particular clock cycle.
The set of all parameters relevant to a computation.
The values of all parameters at some point in a computation.
The physical property of matter as solid, liquid, gas or plasma.
Pomp, ceremony, or dignity.
Rank; condition; quality.
Condition of prosperity or grandeur; wealthy or prosperous circumstances; social importance.
A chair with a canopy above it, often standing on a dais; a seat of dignity; also, the canopy itself.
Highest and stationary condition, as that of maturity between growth and decline, or as that of crisis between the increase and the abating of a disease; height; acme.
A great person, a dignitary; a lord or prince.
Estate, possession.
A form of government other than a monarchy.

examples.text: While Caesar was alive the state was safe.
examples.translation: 凱撒在世之時，國家安然無事。

examples.text: The two states now live in peace with one another.
examples.translation: 兩國目前和平共處。

examples.text: Puerto Rico is not a sovereign state.
examples.translation: 波多黎各不是一個主權國家。

examples.text: Do you want Catalonia to become an independent state in the form of a republic?
examples.translation: 你希望加泰羅尼亞成為共和國形式的獨立國家嗎？

examples.text: The patient is in a state of profound stupor.
examples.translation: 患者現在處於深度昏迷狀態。

examples.text: If Tom doesn't take the prescribed medicine, his state of health might deteriorate.
examples.translation: 如果湯姆不服用處方藥，他的健康狀況可能會惡化。

etymology.text: From Middle English stat (as a noun); adopted c. 1200 from both Old French estat and Latin stātus (“manner of standing, attitude, position, carriage, manner, dress, apparel; and other senses”), from stāre (“to stand”). Doublet of estate and status. The sense of "polity" develops in the 14th century. Compare French être, Greek στέω (stéo), Italian stare, Portuguese estar, Romanian sta, and Spanish estar. The verb is first attested around the beginning of the 16th century. Related to English stand

etymology.text: From Middle English stat (as a noun); adopted c. 1200 from both Old French estat and Latin stātus (“manner of standing, attitude, position, carriage, manner, dress, apparel; and other senses”), from stāre (“to stand”). Doublet of estate and status. The sense of "polity" develops in the 14th century. Compare French être, Greek στέω (stéo), Italian stare, Portuguese estar, Romanian sta, and Spanish estar. The verb is first attested around the beginning of the 16th century. Related to English stand

senses.definition: To check a written text for errors in spelling, grammar, syntax, and punctuation.

examples.text: I like proofreading my sentences.
Have you proofread this already?
You should learn to proofread.
I do my best proofreading after I hit 'send'.
You didn't have time to proofread your report.
You should've had someone proofread your essay.

etymology.text: From proof + read.

senses.definition: Beginning; start.

examples.text: Our school begins at eight-thirty.
examples.translation: 我們學校在八點半開始上課。

etymology.text: From Middle English beginnen, from Old English beginnan (“to begin”), from Proto-West Germanic *biginnan, from Proto-Germanic *biginnaną (“to begin”), from be- + base verb *ginnaną also found in Old English onginnan.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（beginnen），來自古英語（beginnan）「開始」，經原始日耳曼語（*biginnaną），由字首（be-）加基礎動詞（*ginnaną）組成，後者也見於古英語（onginnan）。

senses.definition: Not having, containing, characteristic of, etc.
Not doing or not having done something.
Outside of, beyond.

examples.text: Without noticing it I grew old.
examples.translation: 不知不覺我就老了。

etymology.text: From Middle English withoute, withouten, from Old English wiþūtan (literally “against the outside of”). By surface analysis, with- + out. Compare Dutch buiten (“outside of, without”), Danish uden (“without”), Swedish utan (“without”), Norwegian uten (“without”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（withoute），來自古英語（wiþūtan），字面意思是「在外面」。表面上可拆成（with- + out）。比較荷蘭語（buiten）、丹麥語（uden）、瑞典語（utan）。

senses.definition: Someone or something lacking in something.

examples.text: Without water, plants cannot grow or live at all.
examples.translation: 沒有水，植物無法生長或存活。

etymology.text: From Middle English withoute, withouten, from Old English wiþūtan (literally “against the outside of”). By surface analysis, with- + out. Compare Dutch buiten (“outside of, without”), Danish uden (“without”), Swedish utan (“without”), Norwegian uten (“without”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（withoute），來自古英語（wiþūtan），字面意思是「在外面」。表面上可拆成（with- + out）。比較荷蘭語（buiten）、丹麥語（uden）、瑞典語（utan）。

senses.definition: An indefinite, but usually small, number of.
Not many; a small (in comparison with another number stated or implied) but somewhat indefinite number of.
Obscuring one to two oktas (eighths) of the sky.
(US?) Having a 10 percent chance of measurable precipitation (0.01 inch); used interchangeably with isolated.

examples.text: Few Japanese can use English well.
examples.translation: 極少數的日本人可以很好地使用英語。

examples.text: Use interrogative pronouns to rewrite the sentences below; if you need to, you can add or remove a few words.
examples.translation: 用疑問代詞表任指格式改寫下面的句子，根據需要可以增加或者減少一些詞語。

examples.translation: 我還要再待幾個星期。

examples.translation: 幾年前在舊金山，有位年輕女子來找我們諮詢職涯。

etymology.text: From Middle English fewe, from Old English fēaw (“few”), from Proto-West Germanic *fau, from Proto-Germanic *fawaz (“few”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂w- (“few, small”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（fewe），來自古英語（fēaw）「少」，經原始日耳曼語（*fawaz），上溯至原始印歐語（*peh₂w-）「少、小」。

senses.definition: Few people, few things.

examples.translation: 這年代已經沒幾個學生用鉛筆了。

examples.text: He made a few grammatical mistakes.
examples.translation: 他犯了一些文法錯誤。

examples.text: Only a few people understood me.
examples.translation: 只有幾個人才明白過來了我的意思。

examples.text: Few things give us as much pleasure as music.
examples.translation: 很少有東西像音樂一樣帶給我們這麼多的快樂。

examples.text: It's been pouring here for the last few days.
examples.translation: 這裡近幾天都在下大雨。

examples.text: He received quite a few letters this morning.
examples.translation: 今天早上他收到好多信。

etymology.text: From Middle English fewe, from Old English fēaw (“few”), from Proto-West Germanic *fau, from Proto-Germanic *fawaz (“few”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂w- (“few, small”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（fewe），來自古英語（fēaw）「少」，經原始日耳曼語（*fawaz），上溯至原始印歐語（*peh₂w-）「少、小」。

examples.text: Bridges are burning and chances are few.

etymology.text: From Middle English fewe, from Old English fēaw (“few”), from Proto-West Germanic *fau, from Proto-Germanic *fawaz (“few”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂w- (“few, small”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（fewe），來自古英語（fēaw）「少」，經原始日耳曼語（*fawaz），上溯至原始印歐語（*peh₂w-）「少、小」。

senses.definition: The smallest unit of language that has a particular meaning and can be expressed by itself; the smallest discrete, meaningful unit of language. (contrast morpheme.)
A unit of text equivalent to five characters and one space.
A fixed-size group of bits handled as a unit by a machine and which can be stored in or retrieved from a typical register (so that it has the same size as such a register).
Something that someone said; a comment, utterance; speech.
A watchword or rallying cry, a verbal signal (even when consisting of multiple words).
News; tidings.
An order; a request or instruction; an expression of will.
A promise; an oath or guarantee.
A brief discussion or conversation.
A minor reprimand.
The smallest discrete unit of spoken language with a particular meaning, composed of one or more phonemes and one or more morphemes.
The smallest discrete unit of written language with a particular meaning, composed of one or more letters or symbols and one or more morphemes.
A discrete, meaningful unit of language approved by an authority or native speaker (compare non-word).
A sign used in a sign language.
A sequence of letters, characters, or sounds, considered as a discrete entity, though it does not necessarily belong to a language or have a meaning.

With regards to Intel or Intel-compatible hardware and/or in the context of Windows programming, a group of exactly 16 bits regardless of the actual processor capabilities; a fossilized unit referring to the small word size of historical CPUs.
A finite string that is not a command or operator.
A group element, expressed as a product of group elements.
The fact or act of speaking, as opposed to taking action. .
A proverb or motto.

etymology.text: From Middle English word, from Old English word, from Proto-West Germanic *word, from Proto-Germanic *wurdą (“word”), from Proto-Indo-European *werdʰom (“word”), from *werh₁- (“to say, speak”). Doublet of verb, verve, and vort; further related to vrata.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語與古英語（word），經原始日耳曼語（*wurdą）「字」，上溯至原始印歐語（*werdʰom）「字」，再來自（*werh₁-）「說」。與（verb、verve）為雙式詞。

etymology.text: From Middle English word, from Old English word, from Proto-West Germanic *word, from Proto-Germanic *wurdą (“word”), from Proto-Indo-European *werdʰom (“word”), from *werh₁- (“to say, speak”). Doublet of verb, verve, and vort; further related to vrata.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語與古英語（word），經原始日耳曼語（*wurdą）「字」，上溯至原始印歐語（*werdʰom）「字」，再來自（*werh₁-）「說」。與（verb、verve）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: Act of expending or paying out.
The amount expended; expense; outlay.

examples.text: The expenditure totaled 200,000 yen.

To establish a basis for (something).
To form by combining materials or parts.

To be converted into software by compilation, usually with minimal human intervention.

etymology.text: From Middle English bilden, bulden, bylden, from Old English byldan and bytlan, bytlian (“to build”), from Proto-West Germanic *buþlijan (“to build”), from Proto-Germanic *buþlą, *bōþlą (“house, dwelling, farm”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuH- (“to become, grow, thrive, be, live, dwell”). senses.definition: The physique of a human or animal body, or other object; constitution or structure.
Any of various versions of a software product as it is being developed for release to users.
The process or period of constructing a physical object.
A structure, such as a building, statue, pool or forest created by the player.
A configuration of a character's items or skills created by the player.

etymology.text: From Middle English bilden, bulden, bylden, from Old English byldan and bytlan, bytlian (“to build”), from Proto-West Germanic *buþlijan (“to build”), from Proto-Germanic *buþlą, *bōþlą (“house, dwelling, farm”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuH- (“to become, grow, thrive, be, live, dwell”). examples.text: We're going to rebuild this city.

Next to the first in value, power, excellence, dignity, or rank; secondary; subordinate; inferior.
Being of the same kind as one that has preceded; another.

examples.text: Your second button is coming off.

One who fits an item of that size.
A thousand dollars/pounds.

Liberality, generosity.

etymology.text: From Middle English large, from Old French large, from Latin larga, feminine of largus (“abundant, plentiful, copious, large, much”), of uncertain ultimate origin; see there for more. etymology.text: Borrowed from French programme, from Late Latin programma (“a proclamation, edict”), from Ancient Greek πρόγραμμα (prógramma, “a written public notice, an edict”), from προγράφω (prográphō, “to set forth as a public notice”), from πρό (pró, “before”) + γράφω (gráphō, “to write”). Doublet of programma.
etymology.native: 借自法語（programme），來自晚期拉丁語（programma）「公告、敕令」，再源自古希臘語（πρόγραμμα）「書面公告」，由（πρό）「事先」加（γράφω）「寫」組成。與（programma）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: The set of courses, coursework, and content offered at a school or university.
The set of standards schools are required to teach all students.
A racecourse; a place for running.

examples.text: I have an interesting curriculum vitae!

The curriculum needs to be updated.
I completed the whole high school curriculum.
What curriculum does Fadil use to teach Arabic?
How does one write a good curriculum vitae?

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin curriculum (“course”), derived from currō (“run, move quickly”). Doublet of curricle.

senses.definition: The result of multiplying a given number of consecutive integers from 1 to the given number. In equations, it is symbolized by an exclamation mark (!). For example, 5! = 1 × 2 × 3 × 4 × 5 = 120.

examples.text: Tom said that zero factorial (0!) is defined to equal 1.
No factorial of an integer greater than one is a perfect power.

etymology.text: From factor + -ial.

senses.definition: The state of being precise or exact; especially, both exact and accurate.
The ability of a measurement to be reproduced consistently.
The number of significant digits to which a value may be measured reliably.
A bidding system that makes use of many artificial bids to describe a hand quite precisely.

examples.text: Precision is important in math.
examples.translation: 精確性在數學中很重要。

examples.text: Tom always speaks with robotic precision.
This cartographer is famous for the precision in his maps.
examples.translation: 此製圖員出名於其製圖的精準性。

examples.text: He copied his friend's notebook with precision.
Our teacher is someone who likes precision, and always demands precise answers of her students.
examples.translation: 老師性喜精準——她總是要求精確的答案。

examples.text: Precision in measurement is necessary.

etymology.text: From Middle French precision. Equivalent to precise + -ion.

senses.definition: Pertaining to or consisting of objective claims.
True, accurate, corresponding to reality.

examples.text: This is not factual information.
I believe that it's not factual.
It's not factual.
Don't make factual statements without a source.
That book is full of factual errors.
His remark was not intended to be a factual statement.

etymology.text: From fact + -ual, modeled after, and by analogy with, actual.

senses.definition: Any nounal word or phrase which indicates a particular person, place, class, or thing.
A reputation.
An abusive or insulting epithet.
A person (or legal person).
Those of a certain name; a race; a family.
An authority; a behalf.
An identifier, generally a unique string of characters.
An investor in Lloyd's of London bearing unlimited liability.

senses.definition: Any of several types of true yam (Dioscorea) used in Caribbean Spanish cooking.

examples.text: 'Hayastan' is Armenia's name in Armenian.

examples.text: I'm always forgetting people's names.

senses.definition: To determine which disease is causing a sick person's signs and symptoms; to find the diagnosis.
To determine the cause of a problem.

examples.text: Tom was diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis.
She diagnosed me with paranoid delusions.
Schumann was diagnosed with psychotic melancholia.
Tom was diagnosed with ASD when he was three.
Have you ever been diagnosed with hemophilia?
Robert told Sandra what his doctor diagnosed.

etymology.text: Back-formation from diagnosis. Compare also sclerose (verb).

senses.definition: To pay out (money).
To exhaust, to wear out.
To consume, to use up (time).
To bestow; to employ; often with on or upon.
To waste or wear away; to be consumed.
To be diffused; to spread.
To break ground; to continue working.
To squander.
To have an orgasm; to ejaculate sexually.

examples.text: Tom wants to spend more time with his family.
examples.translation: 湯姆想多把時間花在他的家庭上。

etymology.text: From Middle English spenden, from Old English spendan (attested especially in compounds āspendan (“to spend”), forspendan (“to use up, consume”)), from Proto-West Germanic *spendōn (“to spend”), borrowed from Latin expendere (“to weigh out”). Doublet of expend.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（spenden），來自古英語（spendan，多見於複合詞 āspendan「花費」、forspendan「用盡」），再上溯至原始西日耳曼語（*spendōn），借自拉丁語（expendere）「秤出、支付」。與（expend）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: A specific commercial enterprise or establishment.
A person's occupation, work, or trade.
Commercial, industrial, or professional activity.
The volume or amount of commercial trade.
One's dealings; patronage.
Private commercial interests taken collectively.
The management of commercial enterprises, or the study of such management.
A particular situation or activity.
Any activity or objective needing to be dealt with; especially, one of a financial or legal matter.
senses.native: 要處理的事務（尤指財務或法律事務）

senses.definition: Something involving one personally.
Matters that come before a body for deliberation or action.
Business class, the class of seating provided by airlines between first class and coach.
Hollywood, the entertainment industry.
Prostitution.
Something very good; top quality.
The act of defecation, or the excrement itself, particularly that of a non-human animal.
Disruptive shenanigans.
Matters.
A group of ferrets.

examples.text: Everybody's business is nobody's business.

etymology.text: From Middle English busines, busynes, businesse, bisynes, from Old English bisiġnes (“business, busyness”), equivalent to busy + -ness. Doublet of busyness. Sense 17 (something very good, top quality), possibly derives from "the bee's knees"
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（busines），來自古英語（bisiġnes）「事務、忙碌」，相當於「忙碌」加名詞字尾（busy + -ness）。與（busyness）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: Of, to, pertaining to, or used for purposes of conducting trade, commerce, governance, advocacy or other professional purposes.
Professional, businesslike, having concern for good business practice.
Supporting business, conducive to the conduct of business.

examples.translation: 她憑著努力和生意頭腦成了富翁。

examples.translation: 一家種族融合的企業。

etymology.text: From Middle English busines, busynes, businesse, bisynes, from Old English bisiġnes (“business, busyness”), equivalent to busy + -ness. Doublet of busyness. Sense 17 (something very good, top quality), possibly derives from "the bee's knees"
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（busines），來自古英語（bisiġnes）「事務、忙碌」，相當於「忙碌」加名詞字尾（busy + -ness）。與（busyness）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: To cover, fill, or affect with lead.
To guide or conduct with the hand, or by means of some physical contact connection.

To guide or conduct in a certain course, or to a certain place or end, by making the way known; to show the way, especially by going with or going in advance of; to guide somebody somewhere or to bring somebody somewhere by means of instructions.
To direct; to counsel; to instruct.
To conduct or direct with authority; to have direction or charge of; to command, especially a military or business unit.
To draw or direct by influence, whether good or bad; to prevail on; to induce; to entice; to allure.
To influence towards a belief, a conclusion, etc.

To guide or conduct, as by accompanying, going before, showing, influencing, directing with authority, etc.; to have precedence or preeminence; to be first or chief; — used in most of the senses of the transitive verb.
To go or to be in advance of; to precede; hence, to be foremost or chief among.
To proceed in front of others; to go first.
To be more advanced in technology or business than others.
To begin a game, round, or trick, with
To be ahead of others, e.g., in a race.
To have the highest interim score in a game.
To step off base and move towards the next base.
To aim in front of a moving target, in order that the shot may hit the target as it passes.
To lead climb.
To tend or reach in a certain spatial direction, or to a certain place.
To be a cause of.
To place leads between the lines of.

examples.translation: 上場時,隊長先上.

etymology.native: 源自中古英語（led、leed），來自古英語（lēad）「鉛」，再上溯至原始西日耳曼語（*laud），可能借自原始凱爾特語（*ɸloudom），最終來自原始印歐語（*plewd-）「流動」。

Outside the currently selected segment in a segmented memory architecture.

senses.definition: To want (something) to happen, with a sense of expectation that it might [with that (+ clause); or (informal) with clause; or with so or (negative) not].

examples.text: Everyone hoped that she would win.
examples.translation: 每個人都希望她會獲勝。

examples.text: I hope she's not his girlfriend.
examples.translation: 希望她不是他的女朋友。

examples.text: I'm hoping that that'll happen.
examples.translation: 我希望那會發生。

examples.text: Hope that we need not to wait for a long time.
examples.translation: 希望我們不需要等太久。

examples.text: I hope I am not disturbing you.
examples.translation: 我希望沒打擾到你吧？

examples.text: I'm going to get a new car. I hope it will be better than the last one.
examples.translation: 我要買一輛新車，希望會比上一輛好。

etymology.native: 源自中古英語（hopen），來自古英語（hopian）「希望」，再上溯至原始西日耳曼語（*hopōn）；更早的來源不明。

The belief that good will eventually triumph over evil.

I'd love to share your beautiful optimism.

senses.definition: In a hopeful manner.
It is hoped that; I hope; we hope.

examples.text: Hopefully, we'll enjoy our China trip.
examples.translation: 希望我們會喜歡我們的中國之旅。

examples.text: Hopefully, we can all stay healthy.
examples.translation: 希望我們都能保持健康。

examples.text: Hopefully there were no disagreeable incidents.

examples.translation: 帶著希望旅行比達到目的地更為美好。

examples.translation: 明天就要去入學面試了，希望可以透過。

examples.text: Hopefully, Tom will be back on his feet soon.

etymology.text: From hopeful + -ly. The use as a sentence adverb first gained currency in the United States and has been explained as a possible calque of German hoffentlich.

senses.definition: Up to the time of (something happening); pending.
Before (a time).
Up to (a certain place)
Up to the time that the foods or other things available to sell, or tasks which need to be completed, run out.
senses.native: 直到（存貨售完或任務完成）

senses.definition: To; physically towards.

examples.text: Class doesn't begin until eight-thirty.
examples.translation: 八點半開始上課。

examples.text: Can you wait until 2:30 this afternoon?
examples.translation: 你能等到今天下午2:30嗎？

examples.text: It doesn't start until eight thirty.
