etymology.native: 源自中古英語（vntil、until、untill、ontil），可能是中古英語（unto）的北方變體。表面分析為（un）-「朝向、直到」加（till）。

senses.definition: Up to the time that (a condition becomes true).
Before (a condition becoming true).

examples.text: You had better not start until they arrive.
examples.translation: 你最好不要在他們來之前開始。

etymology.text: From Middle English vntil, until, untill, ontil, ontill, perhaps representing a northern variant of Middle English unto (see Modern English unto). By surface analysis, un- (“against; toward; up to”) + till.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（vntil、until、untill、ontil），可能是中古英語（unto）的北方變體。表面分析為（un）-「朝向、直到」加（till）。

senses.definition: The effect upon the judgment or feelings produced by any event, whether witnessed or participated in; personal and direct impressions as contrasted with description or fancies; personal acquaintance; actual enjoyment or suffering.
An activity one has performed.
A collection of events and/or activities from which an individual or group may gather knowledge, opinions, and skills.
The knowledge thus gathered.
A business offering in which a major focus is the way that the customer interacts with the business throughout the transaction, as opposed to only its outcome (the product or service).
Synonym of experience points
Trial; a test or experiment.

examples.text: Please write about your real experience.
examples.translation: 請你把你的真實體驗寫下來。

examples.text: They're young, but they have experience.
examples.translation: 他們還年輕，但他們有經驗。

examples.text: What job experience do you have?
examples.translation: 你有從事什麼工作的經驗?

examples.text: My advice is predicated on my experience.
examples.translation: 我的建議源於我的經驗。

examples.text: Tom has a lot of experience in computers.
examples.translation: 湯姆對電腦有很多經驗。

examples.text: He is fresh from college, so he has no experience.
examples.translation: 他剛剛大學畢業，所以沒什麼經驗。

etymology.text: From Middle English experience, from Old French, from Latin experientia (“a trial, proof, experiment, experimental knowledge, experience”), from experiens, present participle of experiri (“to try, put to the test, undertake, undergo”), from ex (“out”) + peritus (“experienced, expert”), past participle of *periri (“to go through”); see expert and peril. senses.definition: To observe certain events; undergo a certain feeling or process; or perform certain actions that may alter one or contribute to one's knowledge, opinions, or skills.

examples.text: This winter we experienced many rainstorms.
examples.translation: 這個冬天我們經歷了許多場暴風雨。

examples.text: Besides the rain, we experienced heavy winds.
examples.translation: 除了雨之外，我們體驗了強風。

examples.text: Have you experienced the night life here?
examples.translation: 你過過這裡的夜生活嗎？

examples.text: At last, they experienced the joy of victory.
examples.translation: 最後，他們感受到了勝利的喜悅。

examples.text: We have experienced many changes over the last decade.
examples.translation: 我們最近十年經歷了很多變化。

examples.text: When the wound got infected, he experienced a bout of unbearable pain.
examples.translation: 傷口發炎後，他感到難忍無比的劇痛。

etymology.text: From Middle English experience, from Old French, from Latin experientia (“a trial, proof, experiment, experimental knowledge, experience”), from experiens, present participle of experiri (“to try, put to the test, undertake, undergo”), from ex (“out”) + peritus (“experienced, expert”), past participle of *periri (“to go through”); see expert and peril. Displaced native Old English āfandung (“experience”) and āfandian (“to experience”).

etymology.text: Borrowed from French inexpérience, from Late Latin inexperientia.

To cover, as a cost.
To yield as a benefit.

examples.translation: 我一收到錢就馬上還錢給你。

etymology.text: From Middle English payen, from Old French paiier (“pay”), from Medieval Latin pācāre (“to settle, satisfy”) from Latin pācāre (“to pacify”). In this sense, displaced native Old English ġield (“pay”) and ġieldan (“to pay”), whence Modern English yield.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（payen），來自古法語（paiier）「付款」，來自中世紀拉丁語（pācāre）「結清、使滿意」，再來自拉丁語（pācāre）「安撫」。取代了古英語本土詞（ġieldan）「付」，現代英語的（yield）由此而來。

senses.definition: Money given in return for work; salary or wages.
A paying job; a paying concern.

examples.text: I'll pay you the money tomorrow.
examples.translation: 我明天會付錢給你。

examples.text: The majority of his income goes to pay his rent.
examples.translation: 他的大部分收入付了租金。

examples.text: Respect your parents. They pay for the internet.
examples.translation: 尊重你的父母，網錢是他們付的。

examples.text: I'll pay you back once I receive my salary.
examples.translation: 一領到工資就把錢還給你。

examples.text: Hypocrisy is the homage that vice pays to virtue.
examples.translation: 虛偽是惡向善致敬的方式。

examples.text: You pay 10,000 yen a month as an insurance premium.
examples.translation: 你每個月付一萬日圓保險費。

etymology.text: From Middle English payen, from Old French paiier (“pay”), from Medieval Latin pācāre (“to settle, satisfy”) from Latin pācāre (“to pacify”). In this sense, displaced native Old English ġield (“pay”) and ġieldan (“to pay”), whence Modern English yield.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（payen），來自古法語（paiier）「付款」，來自中世紀拉丁語（pācāre）「結清、使滿意」，再來自拉丁語（pācāre）「安撫」。取代了古英語本土詞（ġieldan）「付」，現代英語的（yield）由此而來。

senses.definition: Synonym of pay back in all senses.
To make worthwhile; to yield a result worth the effort; to pay off.
To give in return; requite.
To pay (cover with tar, pitch, etc.) again.

examples.text: Repay your sins with your life.
examples.translation: 納命來贖罪。

examples.text: Algeria repaid its foreign debts.
You have to repay your debts.
Lend money only to such as will repay it.
examples.translation: 只借錢給會還錢的人。

examples.text: I wish there was some way I could repay Tom.
Is there some way I can repay you for this?

etymology.text: From Old French repaier (“to pay back”), from re- + paiier (“to pay”), from Latin pācāre (“to settle, to make peaceful”), from pāx (“peace”) + -ō (forming verbs). Equivalent to re- + pay. Cognate with repacify and French repayer (“to pay again”).

senses.definition: A periodic payment, usually in the form of a paper check, received by an employee from an employer for work performed.

examples.text: He never brings the paycheck home.
examples.translation: 他從不把工資帶回家。

examples.text: She hates living paycheck to paycheck.
We're living paycheck to paycheck.
I can't buy anything until I get my paycheck.
He doesn't want to live paycheck to paycheck.
What will you do with your first paycheck?

etymology.text: From pay (“wages or salary”) + check (“a means of payment”).

senses.definition: To pay too much.
senses.native: 支付得太多、多付、給……的工資過高

senses.definition: To be more than an ample reward for.

examples.text: I think Tom is overpaid.
Tom overpaid Mary.
I think we overpaid for that old car.
Be careful not to overpay when buying second-hand items.
The customer accidentally overpaid and was refunded.

etymology.text: From over- + pay.

senses.definition: Of low quality.
Unfavorable; negative; not good.
Not suitable or fitting.
Not appropriate, of manners etc.
Tricky; stressful; unpleasant.
Evil; wicked.
Faulty; not functional.
Malodorous; foul.
Severe, urgent.
Inaccurate; incorrect
Harmful, especially unhealthy; liable to cause health problems.
Sickly, unhealthy, unwell.
The injured or weak one of a pair of body parts, where the other one is healthy.
senses.native: （成對身體部位中）受傷或較弱的那一邊

senses.definition: Not behaving; behaving badly; misbehaving; mischievous or disobedient.
senses.native: 不乖的；調皮的；不聽話的

senses.definition: Spoiled, rotten, overripe.
False; counterfeit; illegitimate.
Unskilled; of limited ability; not good.
Of poor physical appearance.
Regretful, guilty, or ashamed.
Vulgar, obscene, or blasphemous.

examples.text: Where there's good, there's also bad.
examples.translation: 有好就有壞。

examples.text: These are really, really bad things.
examples.translation: 這是非常，非常不好的東西。

examples.text: The weather was very bad yesterday.
examples.translation: 昨天的天氣壞透了。

examples.text: Talking bad about mother again, eh?
examples.translation: 又再說媽媽的壞話了喔？

examples.text: I was tired and, what is worse, I was sleepy.
examples.translation: 我當時很累，更糟的是我還想睡覺。

examples.text: The situation must be worse than you thought.
examples.translation: 情況比您想的要嚴重。

etymology.text: From Middle English bad, badde (“wicked, evil, depraved”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps a shortening of Old English bæddel (“hermaphrodite”) (for loss of -el compare Middle English muche from Old English myċel, and Middle English wenche from Old English wenċel), or at least related to it and/or to bǣ̆dan (“to defile”), compare Old High German pad (“hermaphrodite”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（bad、badde）「邪惡的、墮落的」，來源不明。可能是古英語（bæddel）「雌雄同體者」的縮略形式，或與之及（bǣdan）「玷汙」相關。比較古高地德語（pad）。

senses.definition: Something that is bad; a harm or evil.
Error; mistake.
An item (or kind of item) of merchandise with negative value; an unwanted good.

etymology.text: From Middle English bad, badde (“wicked, evil, depraved”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps a shortening of Old English bæddel (“hermaphrodite”) (for loss of -el compare Middle English muche from Old English myċel, and Middle English wenche from Old English wenċel), or at least related to it and/or to bǣ̆dan (“to defile”), compare Old High German pad (“hermaphrodite”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（bad、badde）「邪惡的、墮落的」，來源不明。可能是古英語（bæddel）「雌雄同體者」的縮略形式，或與之及（bǣdan）「玷汙」相關。比較古高地德語（pad）。

senses.definition: Used to scold a misbehaving child or pet.

examples.text: Bad! Stop biting my shoe.
examples.translation: 不乖！別再咬我的鞋子了。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Middle English bad, badde (“wicked, evil, depraved”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps a shortening of Old English bæddel (“hermaphrodite”) (for loss of -el compare Middle English muche from Old English myċel, and Middle English wenche from Old English wenċel), or at least related to it and/or to bǣ̆dan (“to defile”), compare Old High German pad (“hermaphrodite”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（bad、badde）「邪惡的、墮落的」，來源不明。可能是古英語（bæddel）「雌雄同體者」的縮略形式，或與之及（bǣdan）「玷汙」相關。比較古高地德語（pad）。

senses.definition: The state of being a member of a group or organization.
The body of members of an organization.
The fact of being a member of a set.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: He has the privileges of membership.
Tom doesn't pay any membership fees.
I applied for membership in the association.
examples.translation: 我申請成為協會會員。

examples.text: There's no membership fee for joining.
examples.translation: 參加不用會員費。

examples.text: She applied for the membership in a golf club.
How much is the membership fee for your gym?

etymology.text: From member + -ship.

senses.definition: To accept as true, particularly without absolute certainty (i.e., as opposed to knowing).
To accept that someone is telling the truth.
To have religious faith; to believe in a greater truth.
To ascribe existence to.
To have been convinced by rational means to accept the truth of a proposition.
senses.native: 經過理性思考而相信（某主張為真）

senses.definition: To have been influenced by arational means (such as emotional experience, the imagination of need, etc.) to accept the truth of a proposition.
senses.native: （因情感、需要等非理性因素）而相信

senses.definition: To opine, think, reckon.
To believe that (something) is right or desirable.
senses.native: 認為（某事）是對的或可取的

senses.definition: To have confidence in the ability or power of.

examples.text: Don't believe everything that you hear.
examples.translation: 不要相信你聽到的每件事。

examples.text: My son believes in Father Christmas.
examples.translation: 我兒子相信聖誕老人。

examples.text: I can't believe you're giving up.
examples.translation: 我不信你要放棄。

examples.text: I know it's difficult to believe.
examples.translation: 我知道，要相信這件事很難。

examples.text: I've always believed in and insisted on this.
examples.translation: 我一直這麼認為並且堅持。

examples.text: Tom said I was the only one who believed him.
examples.translation: 湯姆說我是唯一相信他的人。

etymology.text: From Middle English beleven, bileven, from Old English belīefan (“to believe”), from Proto-West Germanic *bilaubijan (“to believe”), equivalent to be- + leave (“to give leave or permission to, permit, allow, grant”). Cognate with Scots beleve (“to believe”), Old Frisian bilēva (“to permit”), Middle Dutch beloven (“to believe, entrust”), Middle Low German belö̂ven (“to believe”), Middle High German belouben (“to believe”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（beleven、bileven），來自古英語（belīefan）「相信」，再上溯至原始西日耳曼語（*bilaubijan），相當於（be）- 加（leave）「允許」。與蘇格蘭語（beleve）、中古荷蘭語（beloven）、中古高地德語（belouben）同源。

senses.definition: To reside, especially as a boarder or tenant.
To assign to a room; to allocate a room to.

examples.text: Tom and John roomed together at the academy.

etymology.text: From Middle English roum (“room, space”), from Old English rūm (“room, space”), from Proto-West Germanic *rūm (“room”), from Proto-Germanic *rūmą (“room”), from Proto-Indo-European *(H)rewH- (“to root; to rip, tear”), from *Hrew- (“to tear out, open”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（roum）「房間、空間」，來自古英語（rūm），再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*rūmą），最終來自原始印歐語（*Hrew-）「撕開、打開」。

senses.definition: The room where a group of people (especially the board of a company or organization) conducts its meetings
Corporations or corporate management considered as a section of society

examples.text: You're wanted in the boardroom.
The directors meet in boardrooms every Monday.
The meeting with the CEO was in the boardroom.
In boardrooms across the country, executives discussed the new taxes.
The boardroom grew restive when the CEO discussed complex arbitrage strategies no one fully understood.
Though the new law is popular among the general public, it is hated in the boardroom.

etymology.text: From board + room.

senses.definition: Introduces a simple indirect question (without a correlative).
Indicates doubt between possibilities (usually with correlative or).
senses.native: 是否（表示在幾種可能之間的疑問，常與 or 連用）

senses.definition: Introduces a disjunctive adverbial clause qualifying the main clause (with correlative or).
Introduces a direct question between alternatives (often with correlative or).

examples.text: Mary asked whether we were ready.
examples.translation: 瑪莉問我們有沒有準備好。

examples.text: He asked whether he was rich.
examples.translation: 他問他是不是有錢人。

examples.text: Ask Tom whether he can swim.
examples.translation: 問問湯姆會不會游泳。

examples.text: She asked me whether I liked the plan or not.
examples.translation: 她問我喜不喜歡這個計劃。

examples.text: I don't know whether George will come or not.
examples.translation: 我不知道喬治會不會來。

examples.text: Whether you agree or not, I'm going to do it.
examples.translation: 不管你同不同意，我都要做。

relations.native: 經風雨侵蝕，如岩石般磨損
（表示過去該做卻沒做的事）本來可以

etymology.text: From Middle English whether, whather, from Old English hweþer, hwæþer, from Proto-West Germanic *hwaþar, from Proto-Germanic *hwaþeraz, comparative form of *hwaz (“who”). Cognate with North Frisian weđer (“if, whether”), German weder (“neither”), Swedish var (“each, every”), Icelandic hvor (“each of two, which of two”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（whether、whather），來自古英語（hweþer、hwæþer），再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*hwaþeraz），是（*hwaz）「誰」的比較級形式。與北弗里斯語（weđer）「如果、是否」、德語（weder）「既不」同源。

senses.definition: Without doubt, certainly.
Without fail, surely.

examples.text: For somebody who feels rushed all the time, I sure make slow progress.

etymology.text: From Middle English sure, seur, sur, from Middle French sur or Old French seür, from Latin sēcūrus (“secure”, literally “carefree”), from sē- (“apart”) + cūra (“care”) (compare Old English orsorg (“carefree”), from or- (“without”) + sorg (“care”)). See cure. Doublet of secure and the now obsolete or dialectal sicker (“certain, safe”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（sure、seur、sur），來自中古法語（sur）或古法語（seür），再源自拉丁語（sēcūrus）「安全的」，字面意為「無憂的」，由（sē-）「分開」加（cūra）「憂慮」組成；參見（cure）。與（secure）及已廢棄或方言的（sicker）「確定的、安全的」為雙式詞。

senses.definition: Yes; of course.
Yes; I guess; you could say that; a weak or noncommittal positive response.
senses.native: 好啊；應該吧；可以這麼說（勉強或不置可否的肯定）

senses.definition: You're welcome; polite response to being thanked.

examples.text: Make sure you're here before five.
examples.translation: 注意，你們最遲要在五點鐘之前到這兒。

examples.text: I'm not sure, but I think I know where to go.
examples.translation: 我不確定，但我覺得我知道要去哪裡。

examples.text: I think he is going to come, but I'm not sure.
examples.translation: 我覺得他要來了，但是我不確定。

examples.text: I'm not sure how much they are expecting me to donate.
examples.translation: 我不太確定他希望我捐多少。

examples.text: I am sure of his passing the coming entrance examination.
examples.translation: 我確定他會通過即將到來的入學考試。

examples.text: I'm sure you'll be sorry if you give it up halfway through.
examples.translation: 我確定你半途而廢一定會後悔。

relations.native: （表示高興或贊同的呼喊）太好了！耶！

etymology.text: From Middle English sure, seur, sur, from Middle French sur or Old French seür, from Latin sēcūrus (“secure”, literally “carefree”), from sē- (“apart”) + cūra (“care”) (compare Old English orsorg (“carefree”), from or- (“without”) + sorg (“care”)). See cure. Doublet of secure and the now obsolete or dialectal sicker (“certain, safe”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（sure、seur、sur），來自中古法語（sur）或古法語（seür），再源自拉丁語（sēcūrus）「安全的」，字面意為「無憂的」，由（sē-）「分開」加（cūra）「憂慮」組成；參見（cure）。與（secure）及已廢棄或方言的（sicker）「確定的、安全的」為雙式詞。

senses.definition: The act of learning something.

etymology.text: From Middle English lernen (“to learn", also, "to teach"”), from Old English leornian (“to learn", rarely also, "to teach”), from Proto-West Germanic *liʀnōn, from Proto-Germanic *lizaną, from Proto-Indo-European *(le-)lóys-e, stative from the root *leys- (“track, furrow, trace, trail”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（lernen）「學習；也指教」，來自古英語（leornian），再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*lizaną），最終來自原始印歐語詞根（*leys-）「軌跡、溝痕」。

senses.definition: A deep caring for the existence of another.
A profound and caring affection towards someone.
A person who is the object of romantic feelings; a darling, a sweetheart, a beloved.
radiotelephony clear-code word for the letter L.
Affectionate, benevolent concern or care for other people or beings, and for their well-being.
A feeling of intense attraction towards someone.
A deep or abiding liking for something; an enthusiasm for something.
A term of friendly address, regardless of feelings.
A thing, activity, etc. which is the object of one's deep liking or enthusiasm.
Sexual desire; attachment based on sexual attraction.
Sexual activity.
An instance or episode of being in love; a love affair.
Used as the closing, before the signature, of a letter, especially between good friends or family members, or by the young.
A climbing plant, Clematis vitalba.
Zero, no score.
Nothing; no recompense.
A thin silk material.
Charity.

examples.text: Nicholas and Maria love each other.
examples.translation: 尼古拉斯和瑪利亞彼此相愛。

examples.text: He's always looking at you. He must love you.
examples.translation: 他整天盯著你看，肯定是喜歡你了。

examples.text: I love her, but she says we are just friends.
examples.translation: 我喜歡她，但她說我們只是朋友。

examples.text: There are people who go mad for the nostalgic feel and also those who love originality.
examples.translation: 有人為懷舊感瘋狂，也有人喜愛原創性。

etymology.text: From Middle English love, luve, from Old English lufu, from Proto-West Germanic *lubu, from Proto-Germanic *lubō, from Proto-Indo-European *lewbʰ- (“love, care, desire”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（love、luve），來自古英語（lufu），再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*lubō），最終來自原始印歐語（*lewbʰ-）「愛、關心、渴望」。

senses.definition: Used before a noun in the manner of words like some, a bit of, and so on.
Used after a noun.

examples.text: There's enough time for a quick snack.
examples.translation: 有足夠的時間很快地吃一下點心。

etymology.text: From Middle English ynogh, from Old English ġenōg (“enough”), from Proto-Germanic *ganōgaz (“enough”) (compare Scots eneuch, West Frisian genôch, Dutch genoeg, German genug, Low German (ge)noog, Danish nok, Swedish nog, Icelandic nógur), from *ganuganą 'to suffice' (compare Old English ġeneah), or from *ga- + an unattested *nōgaz, probably ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eh₂nó(n)ḱe (“he has reached, attained”), perfective of *h₂neḱ- (“to reach”) (compare Old Irish tánaic (“he arrived”), L
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（ynogh），來自古英語（ġenōg）「足夠」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*ganōgaz），可能最終來自原始印歐語（*h₂neḱ-）「到達」。比較荷蘭語（genoeg）、德語（genug）、瑞典語（nog）。

senses.definition: Sufficiently.
as much as necessary
Fully; quite; used after adjectives to express slight augmentation of the positive degree, and sometimes equivalent to very.
Used after certain adverbs to emphasise that a quality is notable, unexpected, etc.
senses.native: （用於某些副詞後，強調某性質值得注意或出乎意料）

examples.text: I've had enough of your complaints.
examples.translation: 我聽夠你的抱怨了。

examples.text: Is there enough food for everyone?
examples.translation: 有足夠的食物給大家嗎？

examples.text: You're old enough to know better.
examples.translation: 你年齡足夠大了，該瞭解更多。

examples.text: I've had enough of this program.
examples.translation: 我已經受夠了這個計劃。

examples.text: My room is small, but it's big enough for me.
examples.translation: 我的房間很小，但對我來說已經夠大了。

examples.text: Luckily he had enough money to pay the bill.
examples.translation: 幸運的是他有足夠的錢來付賬。

etymology.text: From Middle English ynogh, from Old English ġenōg (“enough”), from Proto-Germanic *ganōgaz (“enough”) (compare Scots eneuch, West Frisian genôch, Dutch genoeg, German genug, Low German (ge)noog, Danish nok, Swedish nog, Icelandic nógur), from *ganuganą 'to suffice' (compare Old English ġeneah), or from *ga- + an unattested *nōgaz, probably ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eh₂nó(n)ḱe (“he has reached, attained”), perfective of *h₂neḱ- (“to reach”) (compare Old Irish tánaic (“he arrived”), L
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（ynogh），來自古英語（ġenōg）「足夠」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*ganōgaz），可能最終來自原始印歐語（*h₂neḱ-）「到達」。比較荷蘭語（genoeg）、德語（genug）、瑞典語（nog）。

senses.definition: A sufficient or adequate number, amount, etc.

examples.text: I explained enough for her to understand the issue: there wasn't enough of an economic surplus.
examples.translation: 我解釋得夠多，足以讓她理解問題所在：經濟盈餘不夠。

etymology.text: From Middle English ynogh, from Old English ġenōg (“enough”), from Proto-Germanic *ganōgaz (“enough”) (compare Scots eneuch, West Frisian genôch, Dutch genoeg, German genug, Low German (ge)noog, Danish nok, Swedish nog, Icelandic nógur), from *ganuganą 'to suffice' (compare Old English ġeneah), or from *ga- + an unattested *nōgaz, probably ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eh₂nó(n)ḱe (“he has reached, attained”), perfective of *h₂neḱ- (“to reach”) (compare Old Irish tánaic (“he arrived”), L
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（ynogh），來自古英語（ġenōg）「足夠」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*ganōgaz），可能最終來自原始印歐語（*h₂neḱ-）「到達」。比較荷蘭語（genoeg）、德語（genug）、瑞典語（nog）。

senses.definition: Stop! Don't do that any more! It is too much!

examples.text: They aren't good enough, are they?
examples.translation: 他們不夠好，對吧？

examples.text: The rope wasn't strong enough to support him.
examples.translation: 繩子不夠牢固，撐不住他。

examples.text: Tom didn't have enough money to pay the rent.
examples.translation: 湯姆沒有足夠的錢付租金。

examples.text: I haven't been getting enough sleep lately.
examples.translation: 我最近一直睡眠不足。

examples.text: Tatoeba: As if the geek invasion wasn't enough.
examples.translation: （Tatoeba）：好像宅宅入侵還不夠似的。

examples.text: You don't have enough faith in yourself.
examples.translation: 你對自己沒有足夠的信心。

etymology.text: From Middle English ynogh, from Old English ġenōg (“enough”), from Proto-Germanic *ganōgaz (“enough”) (compare Scots eneuch, West Frisian genôch, Dutch genoeg, German genug, Low German (ge)noog, Danish nok, Swedish nog, Icelandic nógur), from *ganuganą 'to suffice' (compare Old English ġeneah), or from *ga- + an unattested *nōgaz, probably ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eh₂nó(n)ḱe (“he has reached, attained”), perfective of *h₂neḱ- (“to reach”) (compare Old Irish tánaic (“he arrived”), L
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（ynogh），來自古英語（ġenōg）「足夠」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*ganōgaz），可能最終來自原始印歐語（*h₂neḱ-）「到達」。比較荷蘭語（genoeg）、德語（genug）、瑞典語（nog）。

senses.definition: sufficient for the purpose

examples.text: A word to the wise is enough.

etymology.text: From Middle English ynogh, from Old English ġenōg (“enough”), from Proto-Germanic *ganōgaz (“enough”) (compare Scots eneuch, West Frisian genôch, Dutch genoeg, German genug, Low German (ge)noog, Danish nok, Swedish nog, Icelandic nógur), from *ganuganą 'to suffice' (compare Old English ġeneah), or from *ga- + an unattested *nōgaz, probably ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eh₂nó(n)ḱe (“he has reached, attained”), perfective of *h₂neḱ- (“to reach”) (compare Old Irish tánaic (“he arrived”), L
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（ynogh），來自古英語（ġenōg）「足夠」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*ganōgaz），可能最終來自原始印歐語（*h₂neḱ-）「到達」。比較荷蘭語（genoeg）、德語（genug）、瑞典語（nog）。

senses.definition: In a relative manner; with reference to environment or competition; contextually or comparatively.
Somewhat; fairly.

examples.text: The sales floor was relatively uncrowded.
examples.translation: 銷售區相對來說不算擁擠。

examples.text: This chair is relatively small.
examples.translation: 這把椅子比較小的。

examples.text: She speaks relatively fast.
examples.translation: 她說話相當快。

examples.text: The exam was relatively easy.
examples.translation: 這次考試比較容易。

examples.text: Traveling within Algeria is relatively cheap.
Algeria has a relatively high fertility rate.

etymology.text: From relative + -ly.

senses.definition: In a due, fit, or becoming manner; as it ought to be; suitably; properly.
Regularly; at the proper time.

examples.text: They are now man and wife duly married.
All the tasks have been duly fulfilled.
The above-mentioned mail item has been duly delivered.
I am duly flattered by your proposal.
He's been duly appointed as the assistant director of the program.
Tom is already duly impressed.

etymology.text: From Middle English duely, dewly, dulyche, dueliche, duweliche (“rightly, properly”), equivalent to due + -ly.

senses.definition: To proceed, spring up or rise, as a consequence, from facts, arguments, premises, combination of circumstances, consultation, thought or endeavor.
To return to the proprietor (or heirs) after a reversion.
To have as a consequence; to lead to; to bring about
To leap back; to rebound.

examples.text: Nothing has resulted from his efforts.
examples.translation: 他的努力沒有成果。

examples.text: This policy resulted in a great rise in prices.
examples.translation: 這個政策導致物價大幅度的上升。

examples.text: Many accidents resulted from the icy conditions of the road.
examples.translation: 道路結冰導致了很多起事故。

examples.text: I think a change of ruling party in Hungary will result in WWIII breaking out.
examples.translation: 我認為匈牙利的執政黨輪換將導致三戰爆發。

examples.text: Nothing will result from this meeting.
examples.translation: 這次會議不會有任何結果。

examples.text: I have no intention of telling you the result.
examples.translation: 我並不打算把結果告訴你。

etymology.text: Recorded since 1432 as Middle English resulten, from Medieval Latin resultare, in Classical Latin "to spring forward, rebound", the frequentative of the past participle of resilio (“to rebound”), from re- (“back”) + salio (“to jump, leap”).
etymology.native: 自 1432 年起見於中古英語（resulten），來自中世紀拉丁語（resultare），古典拉丁語意為「彈回」，是（resilio）「彈回」過去分詞的反覆動詞形式，由（re）-「回」加（salio）「跳」組成。

senses.definition: That which results; the conclusion or end to which any course or condition of things leads, or which is obtained by any process or operation; consequence or effect.
The final product, beneficial or tangible effect(s) achieved by effort.
The decision or determination of a council or deliberative assembly; a resolve; a decree.
The final score in a game.
A positive or favourable outcome for someone.
A flying back; resilience.

examples.text: Tom is unsatisfied with the result.
examples.translation: 湯姆對結果不滿。

examples.text: They are happy with the result.
examples.translation: 他們對結果很滿意。

examples.text: The CEO is very disappointed with the result.
examples.translation: 執行長對這個結果非常失望。

examples.text: However you do it, the result will be the same.
examples.translation: 你無論用甚麼方法，結果都是一樣。

examples.text: Please let me know the result by telephone.
examples.translation: 請你打電話把結果告訴我。

examples.text: The prediction was falsified by the result.
examples.translation: 預言被實驗結果推翻了。

etymology.text: Recorded since 1432 as Middle English resulten, from Medieval Latin resultare, in Classical Latin "to spring forward, rebound", the frequentative of the past participle of resilio (“to rebound”), from re- (“back”) + salio (“to jump, leap”).
etymology.native: 自 1432 年起見於中古英語（resulten），來自中世紀拉丁語（resultare），古典拉丁語意為「彈回」，是（resilio）「彈回」過去分詞的反覆動詞形式，由（re）-「回」加（salio）「跳」組成。

senses.definition: A low point or position, literally (as, a depth) or figuratively (as, a nadir, a time when things are at their worst, least, minimum, etc).
The minimum atmospheric temperature recorded at a particular location, especially during one 24-hour period.
A period of depression; a depressed mood or situation.
An area of low pressure; a depression.
The lowest-speed gearing of a power-transmission system, especially of an automotive vehicle.
The lowest trump, usually the deuce; the lowest trump dealt or drawn.
A cheap, cost-efficient, or advantageous price.
A flame; fire; blaze.
Barrow, mound, tumulus.
A hill.

examples.text: Stock prices plunged to a record low.
examples.translation: 股票價格跌至歷史新低。

examples.text: He got the brand new Yankees jersey for the low.
examples.translation: 他用超低價買到了全新的洋基隊球衣。

etymology.text: From Middle English lah, loue, from Old Norse lágr (“low”), from Proto-Germanic *lēgaz (“low; flat”), from *ligjaną (“to lie; to lead”), from Proto-Indo-European *légʰyeti (“to be lying down”), from *legʰ- (“to lie”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（lah、loue），來自古諾斯語（lágr）「低的」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*lēgaz）「低的、平的」，最終來自原始印歐語（*legʰ-）「躺」。

senses.definition: Close to the ground.
Of a pitch, at a lower frequency.
With a low voice or sound; not loudly; gently.
Under the usual price; at a moderate price; cheaply.
In a low mean condition; humbly; meanly.
In a time approaching our own.
In a path near the equator, so that the declination is small, or near the horizon, so that the altitude is small; said of the heavenly bodies with reference to the diurnal revolution.
senses.native: （天體）位置低：接近赤道或地平線

etymology.text: From Middle English lah, loue, from Old Norse lágr (“low”), from Proto-Germanic *lēgaz (“low; flat”), from *ligjaną (“to lie; to lead”), from Proto-Indo-European *légʰyeti (“to be lying down”), from *legʰ- (“to lie”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（lah、loue），來自古諾斯語（lágr）「低的」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*lēgaz）「低的、平的」，最終來自原始印歐語（*legʰ-）「躺」。

senses.definition: Having the necessary powers or the needed resources to accomplish a task.
Free from constraints preventing completion of task; permitted to; not prevented from.
Legally qualified or competent.
Capable of performing all the requisite duties; as an able seaman.
Gifted with skill, intelligence, knowledge, or competence.
Having the physical strength; robust; healthy.
Easy to use.
Suitable; competent.
Liable to.
Rich; well-to-do.

examples.text: Are you able to speak Mandarin?
examples.translation: 你會講普通話嗎？

examples.text: She wasn't able to meet him.
examples.translation: 她不能夠見他。

examples.text: He's able to speak Japanese.
examples.translation: 他會講日語。

examples.text: Is Tom able to speak French?
examples.translation: 湯姆會說法文嗎？

examples.text: We weren't able to find Tom.
examples.translation: 我們找不到湯姆。

examples.text: I was able to succeed because of your advice.
examples.translation: 我因為有你的建議才能成功。

relations.native: 歧視身心障礙者的人；能力歧視的

etymology.text: From Middle English able, from Old Northern French able, variant of Old French abile, habile, from Latin habilis (“easily managed, held, or handled; apt; skillful”). Doublet of habile.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（able），來自古北法語（able），是古法語（abile、habile）的變體，再上溯至拉丁語（habilis）「容易掌握的；靈巧的」。與（habile）為雙式詞。

senses.definition: The nighttime of the current day or date; this night.

examples.text: I hope to be able to finish my book tonight.
examples.translation: 我希望今天晚上我能完成我的書。

examples.text: I don't have the energy for this tonight.
examples.translation: 我今晚沒心力應付這件事。

examples.text: We are going to eat a lot tonight so I hope that you are not on a diet.
examples.translation: 我們今晚會吃很多，所以我希望你沒有在節食。

examples.text: "I'm going to try to make chicken parmesan for my family tonight," said Matthew's sister after trying his recipe.
examples.translation: 馬修的姊姊在試過他的食譜後說道：「我今晚要試著為家人做帕瑪森雞排。」

etymology.text: From Middle English tonyght, to niȝt, from Old English tō niht.

senses.definition: At frequent intervals.
For infinitely many terms of the sequence.

examples.text: She was frequently late for school.
examples.translation: 她經常上學遲到。

examples.text: Tom frequently talks in his sleep.
examples.translation: 湯姆經常說夢話。

examples.text: Indonesia frequently experiences earthquakes.
She frequently gets sugar and salt mixed up.
examples.translation: 她經常把糖和鹽搞錯。

examples.text: How frequently do you check your mail?
examples.translation: 你多久看一次信箱？

examples.text: I have a friend who frequently travels without a ticket.
examples.translation: 我有一個經常不帶票旅行的朋友。

etymology.text: From frequent + -ly.

senses.definition: Done several times or in repetition.

examples.text: Michael was repeatedly ringing the doorbell.
Tom has repeatedly denied those charges.
The ceasefire has repeatedly ruptured.
Tom has been asked repeatedly not to do that.
Flavio was repeatedly knocking on the window.
The word is repeatedly used with that meaning.

etymology.text: From repeated + -ly.

senses.definition: On occasion: at relatively infrequent intervals, from time to time, sometimes.
On an occasion, accidentally, by chance.
On the occasion of something else happening; incidentally, by the way.

examples.text: Tom doesn't mind helping Mary occasionally.
examples.translation: 湯姆不介意偶爾給予瑪麗幫助。

examples.text: That only happens occasionally.
examples.translation: 這只是偶發事件。

examples.text: He occasionally visited me.
examples.translation: 他偶爾會來拜訪我。

examples.text: It happens occasionally.
examples.translation: 它偶爾會發生。

examples.text: The mother occasionally reread her son's letter.
examples.translation: 這位母親偶爾會重溫她的兒子的信件。

examples.text: Occasionally I play golf.
examples.translation: 我偶爾會打高爾夫球。

etymology.text: From Middle English occasionally, occasionaly, occasyoneely, occasyonly, equivalent to occasional + -ly.

senses.definition: At intervals of an hour.

examples.text: Express buses depart hourly.

etymology.text: From hour + -ly.

senses.definition: In a predominant manner. Most commonly or frequently by a large margin.

examples.text: Kabylie is predominantly mountainous.
Berbers are predominantly Caucasian.
Iranians are predominantly Shia.
They live in a predominantly Islamic society.
California is a predominantly blue state.
The audience was predominantly female.

etymology.text: From predominant + -ly.

senses.definition: In a routine manner, in a way that has become common or expected.
Done by rote or habit, as part of a routine, without attention or concern.

examples.text: Prisoners in Guantanamo are routinely abused.
Tobias checked every door and window routinely.
Stefan's school would routinely practice lockdown drills.
Hospitals routinely sterilize their equipment for safety.
We need to change an Internet where women are routinely harassed and threatened when they go online.
Cambodians of Lang Teng’s generation remember routinely living a life that produced little to no waste.

etymology.text: From routine + -ly.

senses.definition: To propose or express one's willingness (to do something).
give something useful or necessary to
present for acceptance or rejection
agree freely
put forward for consideration
offer verbally
make available for sale
propose a payment
produce or introduce on the stage
present as an act of worship
To present in words; to proffer; to make a proposal of; to suggest.
To place at someone’s disposal; to present (something) to be either accepted or turned down.
To present (something) for sale.
To present (something) to God or gods, as a gesture of worship or as a sacrifice.
To present (something) to the sight etc.; to provide for use, consideration etc.
To place (something) in a position where it can be added to an existing mechanical assembly.
To bid, as a price, reward, or wages.
To happen, to present itself.
To put in opposition to; to manifest in an offensive or defensive way; to threaten.
To make an attempt; typically used with at.

examples.text: Do you offer coffee pots in different sizes?
examples.translation: 你們有提供不同尺寸的咖啡壺嗎？

examples.text: How many flights to New York do you offer a day?
examples.translation: 你們一天提供幾班飛往紐約的航班？

examples.text: Do you offer accommodation?
examples.translation: 您提供住宿嗎？

examples.text: I offered to help with the dishes but the hostess would not hear of it.
examples.translation: 我提議幫忙洗碗，但女主人說什麼都不肯。

examples.text: Of course I accepted his offer of support.
examples.translation: 當然我接受了他的支援請求。

examples.text: She turned down the subsidy that I offered.
examples.translation: 她拒絕了我的資助。

etymology.text: From Middle English offer, from Old English offrian (“offer or make a sacrifice”) rather than from Old French offre (“offer”), from offrir (“to offer”), from Latin offerō (“to present, bring before”). Compare North Frisian offer (“sacrifice, donation, fee”), Dutch offer (“offering, sacrifice”), German Opfer (“victim, sacrifice”), Danish offer (“victim, sacrifice”), Icelandic offr (“offering”). See verb below.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（offer），來自古英語（offrian）「獻祭」，而非來自古法語（offre）；兩者最終都源自拉丁語（offerō）「呈獻」。比較荷蘭語（offer）「祭品」、德語（Opfer）「受害者、犧牲」。

senses.definition: Though, even though, in spite of or despite the fact that: introducing a clause that expresses a concession.
But, except.

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: Although we're beginners, we learn quickly.
examples.translation: 雖然我們是初學者，但我們學得很快。

examples.text: Jack was looking well, although tired.
examples.translation: 傑克氣色不錯，雖然有點累。

examples.text: Although she kept protesting, he went.
examples.translation: 雖然她一直抗議，他還是走了。

examples.text: Although he may be clever, he is not wise.
examples.translation: 他只不過是有點小聰明。

examples.text: Although old, he is still very much alive.
examples.translation: 雖然上了年紀，他依舊充滿活力。

examples.text: Although I had ordered tea, he served me coffee.
examples.translation: 雖然我已經點了茶, 他還是給了我一杯咖啡。

etymology.text: From Middle English althagh, from Old English compound of eall (“all (emphatic)”) + þēah (“though”). By surface analysis, al(l) + though.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（althagh），來自古英語由（eall）「全部（強調）」加（þēah）「雖然」組成的複合詞。表面分析為（al）(l) 加（though）。

senses.definition: To obtain (something) in exchange for money or goods.
To obtain, especially by some sacrifice.
To bribe.
To be equivalent to in value.
to accept as true; to believe
To make a purchase or purchases, to treat (for a drink, meal or gift)
senses.native: 購物；請客（請喝飲料、吃飯或送禮）

senses.definition: To make a bluff, usually a large one.
To suffer consequences for (something) through being deprived of something; to pay for (something one has done).

examples.text: I bought this camera for 25,000 yen.
examples.translation: 我用二萬五千円買了這台相機。

examples.text: What she bought was very expensive.
examples.translation: 她買的東西很昂貴。

examples.text: You needn't have bought that book.
examples.translation: 你根本不需要買那書。

examples.text: My mother bought two bottles of orange juice.
examples.translation: 我母親買了兩瓶柳橙汁。

examples.text: I wish I had bought a ticket for the concert.
examples.translation: 我當初要是買音樂會的票就好了。

examples.text: My father bought me a camera for my birthday.
examples.translation: 我爸爸買了個相機作為我的生日禮物。

etymology.text: From Middle English byen, from Old English bycġan (“to buy, pay for, acquire, redeem, ransom, procure, get done, sell”), from Proto-West Germanic *buggjan, from Proto-Germanic *bugjaną (“to buy”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *bʰūgʰ- (“to bend”), or from Proto-Indo-European *bʰewgʰ- (“to take away, deliver”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（byen），來自古英語（bycġan）「購買、支付、取得、贖回」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*bugjaną）「購買」，來源不明，可能源自原始印歐語（*bʰūgʰ-）「彎曲」或（*bʰewgʰ-）「拿走、交付」。

senses.definition: Something which is bought; a purchase.

examples.text: That jacket was a good buy.
examples.translation: 那件外套很划算。

etymology.text: From Middle English byen, from Old English bycġan (“to buy, pay for, acquire, redeem, ransom, procure, get done, sell”), from Proto-West Germanic *buggjan, from Proto-Germanic *bugjaną (“to buy”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *bʰūgʰ- (“to bend”), or from Proto-Indo-European *bʰewgʰ- (“to take away, deliver”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（byen），來自古英語（bycġan）「購買、支付、取得、贖回」，再上溯至原始日耳曼語（*bugjaną）「購買」，來源不明，可能源自原始印歐語（*bʰūgʰ-）「彎曲」或（*bʰewgʰ-）「拿走、交付」。

senses.definition: A person who makes one or more purchases.
A person who purchases items for resale in a retail establishment.
A person who purchases items consumed or used as components in the manufacture of products.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: Tom already has buyers lined up.
You'll find another buyer.
There weren't many buyers.
Tom thinks that he has a buyer for his house.
Most home buyers have very little imagination.
Buyers often have no idea what they're buying.

etymology.text: From buy + -er.

senses.definition: The amount of time that some being has been alive, or that some thing has been in existence, as measured from its birth or origin until the present or until some other given reference point. (Often measured in number of years; alternatively in months, days, hours, etc.; see also the usage notes)
The state of being old; the latter part of life.
Any particular stage of life.
Maturity; especially, the time of life at which one attains full personal rights and capacities.
A particular period of time in history, as distinguished from others.
The shortest geochronologic unit, being a period of thousands to millions of years; a subdivision of an epoch (or sometimes a subepoch).
A long time.
Lifespan, lifetime; the total time that some being is alive from birth to death (or some category of beings, on average).
The entitlement of the player to the left of the dealer to pass the first round in betting, and then to come in last or stay out; also, the player holding this position; the eldest hand.
The time of life at which some particular power or capacity is understood to become vested.
senses.native: 取得某種權利或能力的年紀

senses.definition: The time or era in history when someone or something was alive or flourished.
senses.native: 某人或某物存在或興盛的時代

senses.definition: A great period in the history of the Earth.
senses.native: 地球歷史上的一個重大時期；紀

senses.definition: One of the twelve divisions of a Great Year, equal to roughly 2000 years and governed by one of the zodiacal signs; a Platonic month.
senses.native: 大年的十二分之一，約兩千年，由一個黃道星座主宰；柏拉圖月

senses.definition: A period of one hundred years; a century.
A generation.

pronunciations.attribution: No machine-readable source provided. Own work assumed (based on copyright claims).

examples.text: He's good looking for his age.
examples.translation: 考慮到他的年齡，他看起來挺不錯。

examples.text: They are about the same age.
examples.translation: 他們年齡相仿。

examples.text: I haven't seen you for ages.
examples.translation: 我已經有很長的時間沒有見到你了。

examples.text: At what age did you have your first girlfriend?
examples.translation: 你幾歲交了第一個女朋友？

examples.text: She lived in five different countries by age 25.
examples.translation: 她二十五歲時已經在五個不同的國家住過。

examples.text: The difference in their ages is six years.
examples.translation: 他們差六歲。

relations.native: 有年齡歧視的人；年齡歧視的

etymology.text: From Middle English age, Old French aage, eage, edage, from an assumed Vulgar Latin *aetāticum, derived from Latin aetātem, itself derived from aevum (“lifetime”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eyu- (“vital force”). Compare French âge. Displaced native Old English ieldu.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（age）、古法語（aage、eage、edage），來自推測的通俗拉丁語（*aetāticum），衍生自拉丁語（aetātem），再源自（aevum）「一生」，最終可溯至原始印歐語（*h₂eyu-）「生命力」。比較法語（âge）。取代了古英語原有的（ieldu）。

senses.definition: To grow aged; to become old or older; to show marks of age.
To suffer the passage of time so as to later be viewed or turn out in a certain way.
senses.native: 隨時間推移而顯得或變得（某樣子）

senses.definition: To cause to grow old; to impart the characteristics of age to.
To allow to mature.
To treat or tamper with in order to give a false appearance of age.
To determine the age of (the length of time that something has been alive or in existence).
senses.native: 測定（某物的）年代或年齡

senses.definition: To indicate or reveal that (a person) has been alive for a certain period of time, especially a long one.

etymology.text: From Middle English rather, from Old English hraþor, comparative of hraþe (“soon, early, fast”). More at rathe. etymology.text: From Middle English resoun, reson, from Anglo-Norman raisun (Old French raison), from Latin ratiō, from ratus, past participle of reor (“reckon”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂reh₁- (“to think”), reanalysed root of *h₂er- (“to put together”). Displaced native Middle English reden (found in compounds), from Old English rǣden (“condition, stipulation, calculation, direction”), from the same Proto-Indo-European source (compare West Frisian reden (“reason”), Dutch reden (“reason”)). Double
etymology.native: 源自中古英語（resoun、reson），來自英法語（raisun，古法語 raison），再源自拉丁語（ratiō），來自（reor）「計算」的過去分詞（ratus），最終來自原始印歐語（*h₂reh₁-）「思考」。取代了中古英語原有的（reden），其源自古英語（rǣden）「條件、計算」。比較荷蘭語（reden）「理由」。
